## Build log
### 2026-10-23: The flexure faults: the oceanic carry peaks and the trench floors were one integrator (the surface held an offset over the plate model's height and the plate model's feedback added it back each step), ended by the held offsets (ISO-125); the water load by basin, not by `h ≤ sea` (ISO-126); both and the yield (ISO-120, 380 mGal) on by default under Ben's rule; the solve on the sphere's metric (ISO-127) is right for one solve but its preconditioner does not converge where the rigidity changes along a row near a pole, so it is off (coordinator's task, brief build/coord/briefs/flexure-faults.md; agent worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-a90cfbd93f4cea604, branch worktree-agent-a90cfbd93f4cea604 from master 049c4278; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Trace** (flexure.md "The held offsets"; scattered 1 with the yield, `DEEPTIME_PEAK_TRACE=10000` and the new floor trace `DEEPTIME_FLOOR_TRACE=11000`, surface/floors.rs, measurement only).
  - 17 peak lines, all ocean samples at a ridge 10.0 to 14.7 km high, 9 on the polar rows; 0.2 to 0.99 of their cells in a gap between plates, which handed the sample 0.7 to 2.8 km in the step, what it rose by.
  - 34 floor lines, all on trench rows, 11.0 to 15.5 km under the sea over a plate model at −6.8 to −9.4 km, offsets −1.2 to −7.9 km at the step's start.
  - Cause of both: the surface holds its offset over the plate model's height in a gap (the gap budget's carry) and on a trench row (ISO-097), and the plate model's feedback (ISO-078) read the same offset back each step and added it to the sample: an integrator, up beside gaps, down under trenches.
  - Water: the flexure took every cell at or under the sea level as under the sea, so a closed basin below the sea was loaded with the sea and a lake above it with nothing.
  - The polar metric: see "Why it diverges" below.
- **Fix:**
  - ISO-125 `surface.held_offsets` (params.rs; advect.rs `held_cells`, `held_offset`, the trench carry keeps only the held offset; surface/mod.rs the `offset_held` field; plates/mod.rs the feedback counts a held cell as offset 0 at its full weight; climate/mod.rs its carry reads the same). The first form renormalised over the cells not held and raised a 92 % held collision column 7.6 km in a step; the held cells keep their weight.
  - ISO-126 `surface.flexure.water_by_basin` (surface/lakes.rs, new: the open sea by `pflood::open_sea`, each lake at the level its water balance holds (HYD-050, HYD-057, HYD-100, HYD-101), the rest dry; the flexure's water load and its ρ_m or ρ_m − ρ_w take that level). `h ≤ sea` goes off with it.
  - ISO-127 `surface.flexure.row_metric` (flexure.rs `RowMetric`, `RowSolve`, `Solver::with_metric`, the preconditioner's metric diagonal; `metric_trace` behind `DEEPTIME_FLEX_METRIC_TRACE`, measurement only). Off.
  - ISO-120's default 0 → 380 mGal.
  - Counts in the stage summary (deeptime-cli run.rs): `flexure_yielded_cells`, `flexure_dry_below_sea/wet_above_sea_cells`; the peak trace prints each sample's held share (plates/peaks.rs).
  - Overlapping bodies: the column evaluators, Rust's (deeptime-format column.rs `ColumnWorld::sample`) and Java's (`Columns.sample`, held to Rust's by ColumnParityTest), and deeptime-inspect's strata check (area.rs `body_class`) let the last body by id keep a block; the game (`StrataPass.paintBodies` and `predictedRock`), strata.md and the workbench's slices keep the first. All three now keep the first. The new defaults moved `planet_world_4k`'s bodies so two overlap at block (264, 240), y −103, and the sections test (`rock_at_depth_and_sections_agree_with_the_column_evaluator`) caught the evaluator's hornfels against the slice's diorite.
  - Docs: flexure.md ("The held offsets", "Water by basin", "The solve on the sphere's metric" with "Why it diverges", the yield's section, simplifications, open questions), plates.md ("The polar peaks", "What is left"), ISO-120 amended, ISO-125 to ISO-127 new (ISO-121 to ISO-124 left as a gap), the bibliography (Snyder 1987, Hetényi 1946), claims.md's counts.
- **Measured** (pool, `earthlike_quick_16k`, 1000 Myr, seeds 1 to 4 by both starts, `+DEEPTIME_CRUST_BUDGET=1`; base master bf8477b2 key 7f9d8f115049; `pp-yield380` key 08c9d7d679c0; `ff-held`, `ff-basin`, `ff-metric` key 9bdf6a15219c at 9a46f3c2; medians of 8, Mann-Whitney p against the base):
  - Guard's worst: base 13.84 km, yield 12.92 (p 0.20), yield + held 10.17 (p < 0.001, every run 9.7 to 10.5), yield + basin 13.11 (p 0.38).
  - Largest one-step fall: 9.44, 7.53 (p 0.015), 7.08 (p 0.002), 7.30 (p 0.004). Deepest floor: 9.67, 9.25, 8.94 (p 0.050), 9.88. Most over Airy: 3.85, 3.29, 3.21, 3.57.
  - V1 criteria met per run (the census's criteria at bf8477b2): 3.00, 3.00, 3.75 (p 0.13), 3.12. Land 0.292, 0.296, 0.315, 0.312.
  - Water by basin: 86,900 dry cell-steps under the sea level and 1.34 million wet over it per run (about 174 and 2,700 a step).
  - Yielded cells per run: 13,340 (held), 12,260 (basin).
  - `ff-metric` (yield + metric): 6 of 8 runs stopped by the guard 202 to 942 Myr in, at row 1 or 327, 0.4 to 3.6 thousand km under the sea; the two that finished: guard 25.7 and 234 km. `ff-metric-trace2`: the 80 to 90° rms deflection grew 1.8 to 1.9 times a step.
  - The three defaults together were not run as one arm: `ff-final` (24 runs) was stopped at the coordinator's word before any run finished (pgid 2078181); its staging folders go with `pool.sh gc`.
- **Why it diverges** (probe `probe_the_sphere_solve_where_the_rigidity_varies`, `#[ignore]`): on the 16k raster, single solves to 0.01 m. Block metric with rigidity by x and y: 29 iterations. Sphere's metric, uniform: 1; rigidity by row: 26; rigidity along the rows: 200 unconverged, residual 727 to 1,062 m of mantle at rows 0, 1 and 327 against a ±50 m load; past-pole rows merged: still 200 (the worst moves to rows 2 and 320); couplings capped at 60°: 67, converged. The bank blends uniform-plate solves by each cell's rigidity, right while a load's response stays on plate like its own; along a polar row the flexural length in cells is √a times the equator's (27 to 65 cells for the craton, the blocks' width), so it spans other rigidities. In steps the unfinished part is carried as 1.5 to 8 km of load at the polar rows (5 to 37 m on the block metric); the probe's steps did not grow, so the runs' amplifier (yield, ISO-056's let-go, the surface) is not isolated.
- **Calls** (the agent's, under Ben's rule of 2026-10-23, decisions log): the yield, held offsets and water by basin on by default with no V1 gate; 380 mGal kept, no 300 mGal arm; the metric off; the held cells keep their weight; the lakes' levels are the step's last flood's (game-choice, numerical); the probe stays `#[ignore]` with its findings in its doc. Gap 4's orphaned pool wrappers (pgid 1941565) were killed earlier to free the admission queue (master fixed admit in 319a6045).
- **Tests** (VM, after the merge of master 7c0acb9f, gap 4 on by default): `cargo fmt --all --check` clean, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` 1,250 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored (deeptime-core 939 and 6 ignored, deeptime-cli 59); `./gradlew build test` 492 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 2 skipped (the first run failed ColumnParityTest on the body order until Java's evaluator took the first body too). The only test the defaults broke was the sections test above (the body order); the flexure's one-law fixture (flexure.rs tests `on()`) pins the yield at 0 and water by basin off, so its tests of the plate alone keep their sources' numbers; the surface and plate tests that build on `SurfaceParams::default()` take the new defaults and pass.
- **Next:**
  - The coordinator merges; master's 24-run base afterwards is the first run of the three defaults together.
  - The sphere's metric: a line solve along the rows past 60° (each row's own operator along x, its own rigidity) in the preconditioner, then the probe, the strip test and one 8-run arm (flexure.md, Open questions).
  - The yield's value: a 300 mGal arm on the next base.

### 2026-10-23: V1 item 1 re-sourced as realism checks over Earth's history: the registry's bands for M1, M2, M3 and M7's floor are failed by Earth itself, M4 and M5 are loose and by-rock, M6 needs no glaciation test; proposed bands written, none adopted (docs task, branch worktree-agent-ad41869bac935c82c, Sonnet 5.5)
- **Adopted** by the coordinator on 2026-10-23 (merge 7278c039 and the commit after it): the "fires" bands are now the pool registry's targets (`tools/review/pool/measures.json`) and `v1-item1-table.py`'s criteria: land 0.13 to 0.36, largest at least 0.06, under the sea at most 0.56, above 2 km at most 0.07, coast with high ground at most 0.11, under ice at most 0.32, collisions at most 6 per 100 Myr. The watch lines stay on the page only.
- **What was done:** docs and sourcing only; no cargo, Gradle or simulation, nothing on the VM, `tools/review/pool/measures.json` and `v1-item1-table.py` untouched. New page `docs/science/realism-checks.md` (the seven measures, how each is computed, Earth's range, the proposed band, what a player sees), new ledger `docs/science/ledger/RLC.md` (30 rows), claims.md counts re-run (`python3 tools/review/claims_counts.py --write`), five new bibliography entries (Marcilly2022, ScoteseWright2018, Condie2015, Macdonald2019, WikipediaRealismChecks2026) and RLC ids added to Tozer2019, Cogley1984 and NSIDC-GlacierFacts.
- **New file:** `tools/review/earth-paleodem.py` (`paleodem <folder> [N]`, `relief <grd> [N]`): the census's own helpers (`continents_census.py`) over Scotese and Wright 2018's 1 degree PaleoDEMs (0 to 540 Ma every 5 Myr) with a present-day SRTM15+ control. It changes no existing code. Run on the laptop for a few seconds a map at N = 40,000, one niced core.
- **Finding 1, by rock and by surface:** the census's `elevation` is the ice-free surface, so M4 and M5 are by rock, but their registry values (0.12, 0.15) were set from by-surface Earth figures (0.102 to 0.104). Earth by rock: M4 0.047 (CRUST1.0) to 0.055 (SRTM15+ without ice sheets), M5 0.076.
- **Finding 2, Earth fails four of the registry's bands:** M1 0.26 to 0.32 fails at 15 of 26 Marcilly steps over 0 to 250 Ma (exposed land 0.185 at 80 Ma, 0.131 at 510 Ma, 0.292 today); M2 at least 0.12 fails at 13 of 51 PaleoDEM maps (minimum 0.070 at 80 Ma); M3 at most 0.25 fails at all 26 steps of 0 to 250 Ma by Marcilly's polygon definition, 22 of 26 after the 0.044 offset to the census's 20 km cut (drowned crust 0.258 to 0.528 over 0 to 250 Ma, 0.600 at 510 Ma; Table 1); M7's floor of 2 (Earth had about 0 to 1 in 0 to 100 Ma by the writer's from-memory count). M4 and M5 pass with room (Earth's maxima 0.062 and about 0.10).
- **Proposed bands** (fires / watch; the coordinator decides; band rule RLC-002: the Phanerozoic extreme rounded outward fires, the last 250 Myr or today's like-for-like value is the watch line): M1 outside 0.13 to 0.36 / outside 0.18 to 0.30; M2 below 0.06 / below 0.07; M3 above 0.56 / above 0.48; M4 above 0.07 / above 0.05; M5 above 0.11 / above 0.08; M6 above 0.32 in any state / above 0.11 if not in an ice age; M7 above 6 / above 4, no floor. On the master default (D6 medians from physics-gap-audit.md, not re-run) only M4 (0.271) and M5 (0.411) fire, about four times Earth's maximum.
- **Caveats:** M7 has no source for the model's definition (a terrane of at least 3.64 Mkm2 that ends in a weld; Condie 2015 read as abstract only, its "one to 20 per 100 Myr, average six" is a search extract; Macdonald 2019 counts sutures); the writer's own count is `from-memory`. The PaleoDEMs are a "first draft" (two phases, 1 degree land bridges toggle the largest landmass; 240 Ma jumps 0.07 in land share). Marcilly's table is verified; the PaleoDEM runs are the project's own computation.
- **Next step:** the coordinator decides whether to adopt the proposed bands in `measures.json` (adopt M1, M2, M3 and M7's floor change at least; M4 and M5 are optional; M6 as an unconditional ceiling since the census has no glaciation flag); a geologist or a read of Condie's full text rebuilds M7's Earth count. Open questions are on the page's "Open questions" list, each with a recommendation.

### 2026-10-23: The release's pace: a plate the `Te` law weakens can now take the lower value over the lithosphere's thermal time constant (ISO-099, τ = 62.8 Myr, McKenzie 1978), not in one step; measured on the pool it leaves V1 where it was, gives more closed basins and larger one-step falls, so it is off by default (`--set surface.flexure.te_weakening_myr=62.8`); the surface's sediment fills a basin in a few Myr (coordinator's follow-up to the savanna pit; agent branch worktree-agent-af6976f50d4669c4c-release from master 3fc91491, worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-af6976f50d4669c4c/build/af69-release; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Cause** (the savanna pit, build log 2026-10-23 part B): the law's `Te` (ISO-048 to ISO-053) is a thermal state, but a craton the Andean arc's orogeny reached went from 80 to 5 km in a step and let go of nearly all its held load at once (ISO-056), 4.3 km of floor in 6 Myr.
- **Fix:**
  - `surface/flexure.rs`: `FlexureParams::te_weakening_myr` and `weakened_te_km`. The plate carries the law's `Te` it held (`FlexState::te_law_km`, blended as a logarithm with its crust; NaN on new crust, which takes the law at once). Where the law gives less, the held value relaxes as e^(−dt/τ); where it gives more, at once. The ISO-055 boundary break stays at once. 0 is the old rule and the default.
  - Unit test `a_plate_the_law_weakens_lets_go_as_it_warms` (τ = 62.8 set in the test), on dry ground: with the sea in reach the flexure's water, whose depth kinks at the sea, made the two paths end 172 m apart.
  - The pool's `fill` measure: `tools/review/pool/measure_fill.py`, `measures_fill.json`.
  - Docs: docs/science/flexure.md "The release's pace", ISO-099 (new), ISO-056 (amended), the bibliography (McKenzie 1978, Parsons & Sclater 1977, Hyndman, Currie & Mazzotti 2005, Watts & Zhong 2000, Beaumont 1978, Currie & Hyndman 2006, Currie, Huismans & Beaumont 2008, Horváth & Cloetingh 1996, Horváth et al. 2015), claims.md's counts.
- **Measured** (pool, 12 seeds by two starts, 24 runs an arm, 1,000 Myr; the pace on at key 76b4db9c66ff, `fg-release` on the base's arguments and `fg-release-sheet` on trench-m-rs12e-sheet's, each against the pool's 24 runs of the same arguments; the sheet set is master's default and the pool's `base` since 57558f0a, so its column is the comparison with the new base). Medians, Mann-Whitney p:

  | measure | old base set | sheet set (the new base) |
  |---|---|---|
  | V1 criteria (mean) | 2.33 to 2.54 (p 0.60) | 3.42 to 3.17 (p 0.45) |
  | land share | 0.292 to 0.302 (p 0.63) | 0.306 to 0.309 (p 0.67) |
  | largest landmass | 0.139 to 0.124 (p 0.53) | 0.189 to 0.157 (p 0.16) |
  | closed basins deeper than 10 blocks | 125 to 144 (p 0.27) | 102 to 130 (p 0.018) |
  | of them under sea level | 86 to 97 (p 0.58) | 69 to 86 (p 0.022) |
  | the guard's worst, m | 16,029 to 16,394 (p 0.92) | 16,351 to 15,930 (p 0.84) |
  | largest one-step fall of a cell, m | 11,404 to 13,984 (p 0.003) | 10,649 to 14,363 (p < 0.001) |
  | largest one-step rise of a cell, m | 7,993 to 8,189 (p 0.065) | 6,692 to 7,981 (p < 0.001) |

  - The first four seeds' largest-landmass drop on the base set (0.191 to 0.104, p 0.028) did not hold at twelve.
  - The larger falls are on the polar rows and away from them alike (base set: 8.4 to 10.3 km, p 0.003; 10.9 to 13.9 km, p 0.001).
  - One run at τ = 0 (supercontinent, seed 1) is bit-identical to the base's.
  - The fill: in the 24 base-set runs with the pace on, the median closed basin takes 271 m of sediment a Myr and already holds 4.0 km; room over the last step's deposition is 2.5 Myr and 84 % of the basins would fill within 10 Myr (the sheet set: 2.7 Myr, 85 %). So the surface fills a basin as it opens, far faster than the plate weakens.
  - Why the basins and falls grow was not traced. The hypothesis: a plate that keeps its strength longer holds more load when the boundary break (ISO-055) lets go of it in one step, and a stiffer plate makes broader moats and bulges. The flexure's water on closed dry ground under sea level (wet by `h <= sea`) would deepen the ones under the sea.
- **Calls:**
  - Master 57558f0a (the seven keys on by default; the honest memory estimates) merged in at 03b38887. Two pool checks on the merged head (key 670222000352, supercontinent seed 1): at its default (`fg-release-def`) it made the new base's run again, every field the base dumps byte for byte; with `--set surface.flexure.te_weakening_myr=62.8` (`fg-release-on`) it made `fg-release-sheet`'s run again, every field byte for byte. So the sheet-set column is the merged head's pace against the new base.
  - Off by default: the pace did not move V1 and made the basins and falls worse on the set that becomes the default. The pool's runs at key 76b4db9c66ff are the branch's head with `--set surface.flexure.te_weakening_myr=62.8` (the head's key differs: the default and the test changed).
  - The fill read at the last step only; the base runs predate the deposition field, so there is no before for it beyond the one τ = 0 run.
- **Tests:** with τ = 62.8 as the default (1bdacb76), `cargo test --workspace` on the VM had one failure: `bake::tests::a_planet_run_bakes_every_chunk_time_layer`, L1 cell (159, 11) of the test planet baked a continental heat flow of 33.7 mW/m², under the plate model's floor of 55 (its formula cannot go lower). 33.7 is the sea floor's law at 229 Myr, so most likely a continental sample still holding an oceanic heat flow at the final snapshot (`plates/ridges.rs` keeps the old value when no corner is of the sample's kind); not traced, plates/. A changed history exposes it; the default 0 is master's history. On the merged head (off, 03b38887): fmt and clippy clean, every test passed (deeptime-core 909 passed, 5 ignored).

### 2026-10-22: The quick 16k world fits the default 4 GiB cap again: the amplifier's windows no longer carry the lake surface (AMP-090) (coordinator's task after master facf9356 failed four deeptime-cli tests; agent worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-abffaab214ac9e912, branch worktree-agent-abffaab214ac9e912 from master facf9356; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Cause** (VM, master facf9356). The four tests (editor `edits_land_where_the_core_reads_them`, `a_tuned_code_from_the_game_loads_unchanged`, `a_run_over_its_memory_cap_is_refused_and_a_raised_cap_allows_it`, watch `workbench_queue_editor_and_kept_runs`) fail because the editor refuses pipeline_quick_16k at the default cap: needed (peak + `SERVER_OVERHEAD_BYTES`) 4,389,206,656 B against 4,294,967,296, 94,239,360 B over. The pit merge 9f51d372 added the lake surface twice: `Level::lake_z` (level 21 to 24 B a cell, +6,291,456 B on the world's L2 level) and an f32 copy in every window, `Buf::lake_z` (tile 79 to 83 B a cell, +134,217,728 B on the whole last level). The second is what broke the cap: the amplifier's base estimate (3,852,335,744 B) went over the 3.5 GiB stage cap, so no streaming could fit it either.
- **Fix** (`surface/amplify/`). The window copy goes: `Fine::lake_z` and `Buf::lake_z` removed, `Buf::BYTES_PER_CELL` back to 12 x 4 + 2 + 4 (tile 79 B). The quad rule (the highest lake surface among the cell's 1, 2 or 4 coarse corners) moves into `Level::lake_surface` (resample.rs), which `Level::sample` uses for the lake flag; `LevelSink::put` (tiles.rs) sets the next level's `lake_z` from it for each flagged cell (`LevelTile` hands on the 1-B flags and the coarse level, `from`, in place of the f32s). The flags are never changed after sampling, so every level's `lake_z` is the value the window used to carry. `LEVEL_BYTES_PER_CELL` stays 24: the level does keep 4 B of lake surface. Tests (resample.rs, tests.rs) read the surface through `lake_surface`; `auto_streams_when_whole_is_too_big`'s pinned bytes are the 79-B ones again. The rule itself is unchanged (the savanna-pit lane owns it).
- **Margin** (`session::estimate_for` at the editor's stage cap of 4 GiB less 512 MiB, pipeline_quick_16k, starts random, scattered_continents and supercontinent, 50 to 2,000 Myr; a temporary, uncommitted test with the constants set in the VM copy). A stage's peak is its base plus as much of the recorded history as fits under the cap (the rest spills), so the run is refused only when the amplifier's base passes the stage cap; the margin is the stage cap less the base, the same at every length and start. Before 9f51d372: base 3,711,826,560 B, margin +46,269,824 B. Master: base 3,852,335,744 B, margin -94,239,360 B. This branch: base 3,718,118,016 B, margin +39,978,368 B (38.1 MiB); the 6,291,456 B under the pre-merge margin is the L2 level's lake surface, which the rule needs. (The editor's "needed" is 8,521,088 B under the cap at 50 Myr, where all 31.5 MB of history fits, and exactly the cap at 100 Myr and over, where some spills.) The margin is thin: in the estimate a level byte costs 2,097,152 B (the L2 level, 2048 x 1024 cells) and a window byte 33,554,432 B (the whole last level, 8192 x 4096 cells), so up to 19 B a cell more on the levels fits, or 1 B more on the windows, and 2 B more on the windows refuses the default quick world again.
- **The estimate's slack** (the run's own log line: 729 MiB in use when the amplifier starts, the last level 8192 x 2624 cells, 1,727 MiB at its fullest; the measured peak 2,760 MiB). The estimate's 3,576 MiB is 816 MiB over the measured peak, out of three errors. (1) It counts W x W/2 cells on every level (8192 x 4096 at the last), but the run's grid has `Projection::grid_rows` = 2 Zo / r rows (2,624; `GridDesc::for_planet`): 909 MiB of cells the run never has at the last level, 17 MiB at L2. (2) It leaves out what `whole_last_level_peak` adds (the level the ladder keeps, the preview), about 108 MiB here, as its own comment says. (3) The run allocates about 300 MiB beyond what it held at the start plus its whole-level peak (2,760 against 729 + 1,727 MiB), which neither the estimate nor the run's own `auto` decision counts. An estimate with the real rows and `whole_last_level_peak` alone would come to about 2.88 GB, under the measured 2.89 GB, so (3) has to be found and counted first. Not done here (a separate task; the editor tests' cap scenarios would need checking against it).
- **Honest estimate and unchanged output** (`deeptime bench --preset pipeline_quick_16k --start scattered_continents --length-myr 50 --threads 8 --compute cpu`, default cap, `--work` kept; build/amp-mem-cap/bench.sh, binaries of facf9356 and of this branch). Estimate 3,883,793,024 to 3,749,575,296 B, the allocator's measured peak 3,022,701,968 to 2,893,735,456 B, max RSS 2,953,892 to 2,830,608 kB (both in memory, one tile). World data: 68 of 69 files byte-identical, every raster with them (rasters/elevation.dtr sha256 91ea2164...0dd0, water_level.dtr, detail/amplitude.dtr); manifest.json differs only in timing notes (millis, per-pass ms) and the run's reservation notes (`reserved_peak_bytes` 2,602,919,888 to 2,516,946,720), which follow the estimate.
- **Docs.** young-landscape-and-amplifier.md's Fix paragraph (level 24 B, window 79 B, the surface looked up in the coarse level, and the first version's 83 B that broke the cap); AMP-090's location column names `Level.lake_surface` and `LevelSink`. No ledger row names the byte constants; claims.md counts unchanged.
- **Gates** (VM, build/amp-mem-cap/gates.sh). `cargo test -p deeptime-cli`: ok, 59 passed, the four that failed on master among them; `cargo test -p deeptime-core amplify`: ok, 58 passed; `cargo test -p deeptime-core --test memory_estimate`: ok; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`: ok.
- **Not in the plan / contradictions.** None. Next: the coordinator merges; the savanna-pit lane (worktree-agent-ab776fb45c4db5d44) edits the same lines of `Level::sample`, so its merge takes the rule from `Level::lake_surface`.
### 2026-10-22: River channels cut to the bake's depth and incised, not curbed (HYD-120 to HYD-124) (coordinator's task after Ben found his largest river a block deep at x 6131, z -3022 and a one-block curb along every river; agent worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-a6f4fd175c74d25d4, branch worktree-agent-a6f4fd175c74d25d4 from master 86be5340; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Causes** (lines on 86be5340). (1) The main one: a river column took its water and its bed from the covering segment with the lowest w, ties to the lowest id (`crates/deeptime-format/src/rivers.rs:315` in `sample_among`, Java `worlddata/Rivers.java:267` in `sampleRange`; the bed at `water.rs:227`, `Water.java:166`). A wide river's vertices are 3 to 4 blocks apart against hw 16 to 21, so a dozen capsules cover each column, and the lowest-w one grazes it at d/hw 0.88 to 0.99, a block of bed. (2) Minor: the lake step (`water.rs:206-213`, `Water.java:153-157`) and the sea step (`water.rs:215-219`, `Water.java:159-160`) came before the river with bed = ground (30 sea and 235 lake of 14,176 vertex centre columns on Ben's planet). The coordinator's reading (lake and sea first) holds for that minor share only; the D5 measurement found the same main cause. (3) The curb: `finish` raised every bank beside a river to top + 1 (`water.rs:272`, `Water.java:191`).
- **Fix** (Rust, Java and the far terrain together; FORMAT.md "Rivers" and "Water columns"). `RiverSample`/`Rivers.Sample` gain `deep`, the covering segment with the lowest floor (HYD-120); the bed is ⌊its floor⌋ and the top stays the lowest-w hit's. A sea column a channel covers takes min(ground, channel) and WaterBodies cuts it as a river column with the sea's top (HYD-121). A lake column takes the channel's bed only where the lake water is under a block deep over the surface (HYD-122, `SHALLOW_LAKE`), so a river entering a lake does not trench it. Where the lower ground a block beyond the channel's edges is at or under the top block, water and bed go one block down, never under the sea's top (HYD-123, `INCISION`, `bank_ground`). A bank beside a river is raised only to the water held there, its own top or a higher water neighbour's (HYD-124, `held`; the rule now reads a ring of two: Java Region's hidden margin is 1, deeptime-inspect's rivermap margin 2). `FarColumn.Shape.channel` counts a channel-cut sea or lake column as channel (sand, gravel, soil). Commits 929c1417 (Rust), 7348c723 (Java), 8bbdd5ba (test world and GameTests), 839c0064 (docs, fmt, clippy).
- **Test world and GameTests.** `deeptime synth --kind river-test` (`synth/terrain.rs` `RiverTest`, a game-choice fixture: a river of hw 10 and depth 8 down a slope, across sea-level flats and a block of sea into the sea; a stream of hw 1 on a plain whose surface lies in the plain's ground block); gametest.sh writes it to `world/deeptime-river` (one more synth line), level `deeptime:test_river_depth`; `RiverDepthGameTests.riverBedsReachTheBakeDepth` and `flushStreamHasNoCurb`. - **Where the picture is made, and why in Rust.** The satellite look exists once, in Rust: `deeptime_core::satellite` fed by `deeptime-tiles`' `BakeMap` (the workbench's Final world: the bake's climate, ice, surface rock, lakes and rivers under relief shading), the same code behind the Create World screen's satellite view. A Java port would be a second copy of that look to keep in step, so the dev map asks the natives. New: `BakeMap::zoom_for` (the pyramid zoom nearest a pixel size, by its logarithm) and `BakeMap::render_frame` (a block-space frame with pixel centres, drawn tile by tile by `render` on scoped threads, edge tiles cropped: a frame laid on a tile's pixels is that tile); the JNI `renderWorldMap` (layers `sat` and `elev` only, a direct RGBA buffer, JSON back with the zoom and the time; bad arguments are `IllegalArgumentException`, a folder it cannot read `DeepTimeIoException`) and `nativebridge.NativeWorldMap` around it. The JNI library now depends on `deeptime-tiles` but not on mic-viewer: the tiles crate's new `tile-source` feature (default on; the workspace dependency is `default-features = false`, the CLI asks for it) gates its `TileSource` impl (NOTICE.md says so).
- **Server** (`ServerMaps`). Two pictures per level on one frame (`MapFrame.of`, 2048 pixels across the period), drawn once per server run on the dev map's worker thread: elevation first (`BaseImage` in Java, needs no natives, so a client has a picture early and a server without natives still has one), then satellite (`NativeWorldMap`, 1 to 4 native threads). Each has its own image id and parts; a failure is that picture's note. The info goes out at once, naming a picture still drawing as "rendering on the server", then a fresh info and that picture's parts as each is ready. `MapInfoPayload` carries a list of pictures (layer, id, parts, note); the channel version is 2.
- **Client.** `MapLayer` (SATELLITE, ELEVATION; `DEFAULT` = SATELLITE). `ClientConfig` key `mapLayer` (`config/deeptime_devmap-client.toml`, default SATELLITE) remembers the choice; S on the map screen, or the new button "Satellite (S)" / "Elevation (S)" after "HUD map (H)", switches it for the map, the globe and the HUD minimap. `DevMapState` keeps both pictures; `MapContext` draws the chosen one when it is here, else the other (`MapLayer.shown`), and the readout's new line "Picture (S):" says which and why (for example "elevation for now (satellite: rendering on the server...)"). `MapTextures` keeps a globe picture per layer, so switching back and forth does not rebuild it.

### 2026-10-22: Structures keep to the ground: a trial chamber, ancient city, stronghold or mineshaft that vanilla places at an absolute height is moved down under Deep Time's ground, so Ben's deepslate blob no longer hangs in the deep sea (SCL-200, SCL-201; coordinator's task from Ben's single-player world; agent worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-ab12d96cb47c0d759, branch worktree-agent-ab12d96cb47c0d759 from master 86be5340; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Why.** Ben's world showed a floating deepslate blob over a trench: `minecraft:trial_chambers` (start height absolute -40 to -20, `encapsulate`) was placed for vanilla's ground, and Deep Time's sea floor is a median y -56 (world floor -512, 35 m a block). Reported start: chunk (46, 105), 207 pieces, box x 656 to 766, y -40 to 17, z 1628 to 1732, sea floor near y -149, trench to -303.
- **Design (the science page's last section, docs/science/world-scale-and-bake.md "Structures keep to the ground").** `mixin/StructureBurialMixin` returns from `Structure.generate` (world generation and `/place structure` both pass there, before anything stores the start or reads its box). `worldgen/StructureBurialPass` leaves a start alone unless it is valid, the level's generator is a `GeologicChunkGenerator`, the rule is on and the structure is covered; then it takes H, the least `TerrainSource.height` over the pieces' union box on a grid of at most 16 blocks with edges and corners, and asks `worldgen/StructureBurial.plan` (pure, no Minecraft types) for dy: 0 when the top is already `cover` (8) under H, else the move that puts the top there, or DROP when the bottom would pass `min_y + 8` (the pass returns `StructureStart.INVALID_START`, so the structure set tries its next candidate). A move calls `StructurePiece.move` on each piece, rebuilds every `JigsawJunction` with `sourceGroundY + dy` (absolute, read by the Beardifier, left alone by `move`), checks each box and each `PieceBeardifierModifier` box moved exactly dy (a mismatch is counted and warned), and builds a fresh `StructureStart` from the same pieces (the class is final and caches its box lazily). No random number is drawn, so chunk order and crash recovery give the same start. `-Ddeeptime.buryStructures=false` turns it off (read each call).
- **Which structures (`StructureBurial.covers`, decided once per structure on its encoded JSON).** `minecraft:stronghold` in any step (vanilla registers it in `surface_structures`, so the brief's step list alone would have missed it); in the steps `underground_structures`, `underground_decoration` and `strongholds`, a structure with a `start_height` and no `project_start_to_heightmap`; `minecraft:mineshaft` only for `mineshaft_type` normal (the mesa kind sets itself between sea level and the ground, and buried treasure and trail ruins follow the heightmap).
- **Files.** New: `neoforge/src/main/java/.../worldgen/StructureBurial.java`, `.../worldgen/StructureBurialPass.java`, `.../mixin/StructureBurialMixin.java`, `.../gametest/StructureBurialGameTests.java`, `neoforge/src/test/java/.../worldgen/StructureBurialTest.java`, `tools/smoke/structure_audit.py`. Edited: `neoforge/src/main/resources/deeptime.mixins.json` (one line), `docs/science/ledger/SCL.md` (SCL-200 cover 8, floor margin 8 and grid 16; SCL-201 which structures; both `game-choice`; header recounted), `docs/science/claims.md` (SCL and all rows recounted with `tools/review/claims_counts.py`), `docs/science/world-scale-and-bake.md` (ledger-ids table row, game-choice 78 to 80, the new section), this file.
- **Tests.** Unit `StructureBurialTest` (11): Ben's start (dy = -149 - 8 - 17 = -174, bottom -214), the already-buried and one-block-short boundaries, the drop and the exact floor boundary (ground -439 kept, -440 dropped), overflow on an empty sample, the least ground at a corner and an edge (floor of -80.5 is -81), the grid never wider than its step with both ends kept (a 255-block box is 17 x 17 samples), NaN skipped, `covers` on the JSON of trial chambers, ancient city, a Cataclysm jigsaw, the normal mineshaft, the stronghold in two steps (true) and buried treasure, trail ruins, the mesa mineshaft, a village, Terralith's surface-step sites, an Ice and Fire cave and non-objects (false), and the property switch. GameTests (`StructureBurialGameTests`, `deeptime:test_planet_real`, each makes the start twice from one seed, once with the rule off for this thread only through `StructureBurialPass.withoutBurial`, and compares): `absoluteStructuresAreBuriedUnderTheSea`, `buriedStructuresStayWhereTheyAre`, `buriedChamberStandsUnderTheFloor`.

The GameTest class, docs and the rename that followed (d0378c73) are covered by the run below.

### 2026-10-22: Wrap engine on the cube, E1 and E2: the cube's twelve seams joined from CubeLayout (quarter and half turns, split chunks, the corner keep-out, Toroidal World's slide composed) and block-entity data in the band, still dev-only (coordinator's task, docs/plans/cube-world-plan.md §5 and phase 6, items E1 and E2; agent worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-ab9924d9a8a834409, branch worktree-agent-ab9924d9a8a834409 from master 6ef0e25d; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Design.** docs/design/wrap-engine.md §12 (new): which seams turn and by how much, one geometry (`CubeLayout`) and the topology built from it, the composition with TW's slide, the corners, what the border W3 becomes, E1 to E8 in order with their gates (§12.6), what waits for phase 2 (§12.7), block-entity data in the band (§12.8) and §12.9 as built. Ledger rows SCL-180 to SCL-186; docs/science/seamless-world.md gained "The seams joined" and its Borders bullet now names `WrapEngine.joinedEdges`.
- **E1, the cube topology.** `WrapLayouts.cube(CubeLayout, depth, slides)` builds the topology from phase 0's net in TW's frame (cut pieces named `<edge>@tw`; `cubeCross` stays as an alias). `WrapTopology` gained the nearest-edge fold, split chunks found from a chunk's four corners (`ChunkFold.split()`, `chunkColumns`, `chunkSources`), `nearCorner` (keep-out 2 blocks), the period window and `translated(dx, dz)` for test sites; `BandManager` copies a split chunk column by column with a ticket on each source. `CubeInstall` is pure and decides `TURNS_ONLY`, `WITH_SLIDES` or `REFUSE`; `WrapEngine.installCube` (on `ServerStartedEvent`) installs on the overworld only with `-Ddeeptime.wrapengine=true -Ddeeptime.wrapengine.cube=<s>`, so master's Petroff-Guyou worlds are untouched. `SeamTurns.seamLink` refuses near a corner.
- **E2, block entities in the band** (§12.8). A band chunk's packet lists the stored block entities at their band positions, tags turned (`BandTags`: an end gateway's `exit_portal` moves, a brushable block's `hit_direction` turns); `blockChanged` at a stored position marks its band images; a band holder sends the stored entity's data re-addressed; `Player.canInteractWithBlock` answers through the nearest band image (menus' `stillValid`, the sign editor's keep-alive); the sign editor opens at the image; front or back of a sign is judged through the image (without `SignBlockEntityWrapMixin` a player at the image edits whichever side faces the far stored sign); `BandManager.copy` marks every entity a chunk shows. The access transformer widens `ClientboundLevelChunkPacketData$BlockEntityInfo` and its constructor and `ClientboundBlockEntityDataPacket`'s constructor; those lines apply with the engine off too and only widen access.
- **Tests.** Unit: `WrapTopologyCubeTest` 11 (the engine's fold equals `CubeLayout.fold` in every band for s = 256, 1024 and 3840 in both modes, chunk columns, corners, TW's frame), `CubeLayoutTest` 13, `BandTagsTest` 3. GameTests (namespace `deeptime_wrapengine`) on `cube(CubeLayout.of(256), 16, true)` moved to (49152, 20480): six cube tests (building across a quarter and a half turn, band consistency on a quarter seam and at the TW seam, the slide composed with a turn, the corner refusal) and three E2 tests in `WrapBlockEntityGameTests` (half seam, quarter corner, the cube's quarter seam), six checks each.

Sign-facing cases where vanilla's own answer is wrong: 2 (half), 6 (quarter), 2 (cube), so the test tells the fix apart. 191 s, peak server RSS 4,095 MB.
  - `./gametest.sh` (standalone) at ba016e22: "All 95 required tests passed", exit 0; 606 s on a fully loaded VM (load 32), peak server RSS 7,158 MB.

### 2026-10-22: The full-set Create World hang in the VM dev client was the harness: `vm-client.sh --stage` left the pack's `config/` behind, so Remove Reloading Screen ran on its own default `hideOverlays = "ALL"`, ended the start-up load early, Project Atmosphere's client setup failed and NeoForge stopped mod loading; the walk now carries the stage's `config/` and reaches the world on all 181 mods (coordinator's task after the previous entry's hang; agent worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-a82e9a28279b92829, branch worktree-agent-a82e9a28279b92829 from master fed26937; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Cause**, in order (third-party classes decompiled on the VM for this only, under `/data/ban/deeptime-runs/create-world-hang/decomp`, none of it in the repo):
  1. `vm-client.sh --stage` linked the stage's mods and copied its `kubejs/`, not its `config/` or `defaultconfigs/`, so every mod ran on its own defaults in the dev game dir. Remove Reloading Screen (RRLS 5.0.11) defaults to `hideOverlays = "ALL"`; the pack's `config/rrls.toml` (and Ben's instance, since 2026-10-01) says `"RELOADING"`.
  2. With `ALL` (and `LOADING`: `HideType.forceClose`), RRLS's `MinecraftClientMixin` calls `Minecraft.onResourceLoadFinished` at the end of Minecraft's constructor. NeoForge's `ClientModLoader.completeModLoading` then runs before mod loading is done (no error yet, so the game event bus starts and the title screen comes up), and RRLS first reloads the language on a new resource manager (log: "Creating new resource manager!", "Quick reload listener 'LanguageManager'"), so the language is already an immutable `ClientLanguage` map.
  3. Project Atmosphere 0.9.1.2's client setup (a deferred task, `ClientBootstrap.java:41`) puts a key into `Language.getInstance().getLanguageData()`: `UnsupportedOperationException` from `ImmutableMap.put`, NeoForge's FATAL "Failed to wait for future Sided setup: Deferred Queue, 1 errors found", and with a loading error NeoForge skips the rest of mod loading (IMC, the load-complete event, the network registry lock). No error screen: `completeModLoading` had already run. Under `RELOADING` the deferred task runs before the language is loaded and its `put` goes into a mutable map.
  4. `ScreenshotDriver` opened Create World 40 ticks after the title screen appeared, during that half-loaded start; Create World's data reload (`openFresh`, `managedBlock`) never completed, with every worker idle. Which reload listener never reached its barrier was not pinned down: it is a state a player's game with the pack's config does not reach.
- **KubeJS's spinning thread is a side show.** KubeJS starts its local web server unless `kubejs/config/web_server.json` says `"enabled": false` (`WebServerProperties`' default is `true`; Ben's instance has `false`, the dev game dir `true`). A taken port is handled (it moves to the next of ten: 61424 in the first hang and in the lite walk, 61423 in walk A). The lite walk ran it too (61424) and reached the world. It is off in the walk now.
- **It never passed before.** The only earlier full-pack client walk was `--mods mic --no-create` (2026-10-20); the full set's Create World walk first ran in the previous entry and hung both times. The lite set (no RRLS, no Project Atmosphere) passed.
- **Change** (harness only; no Deep Time game code):
  - `tools/client/vm-client.sh`: `--stage` also copies the stage's `config/` and `defaultconfigs/`, replacing the game dir's own; `write_options` turns KubeJS's web server off whenever a set is linked; the runner stops a pass on NeoForge's "Failed to wait for future" as it does on a crash. The `--stage` help says so.
  - `ScreenshotDriver` (dev-only, `-Ddeeptime.dev.screenshots`): the TITLE step waits until `ClientModLoader.isLoading()` is false, `getOverlay()` is null and the title screen has been up 40 ticks from then (`titleReadyTicks`); on `ModLoader.hasErrors()` it logs `FAILED: mod loading failed (<the error issues>)`, shoots `zz-mod-loading-failed` and quits.
- **Measured** (VM, admitted; the stage `/data/ban/play/831b3847-client/minecraft`, 181 mods; `--no-guidance --prop length=60`; outputs in this worktree copy's `review/out/<name>/`, not committed):
  - **The fix**: `tools/remote/mac.sh -- tools/remote/detach.sh start cwh-full-fixed --kind client:editor tools/client/vm-client.sh --name cwh-full-fixed --stage /data/ban/play/831b3847-client/minecraft --no-guidance --timeout 1800 --prop length=60`: "config/ (23 files) and defaultconfigs/ (2)" copied; TITLE to CREATE_SCREEN, the 60 Myr run to DONE, Play, **in world on a `GeologicChunkGenerator` planet; client exited 0 after 221 s**, 24 PNGs. The rule: world-gen threads run only while the client's average camera speed (`ClientApi.getAvgCameraSpeed()`, client JVM only) is not above 20 blocks a second, the LOD builder is not overloaded, and (with `limitIfServerUnhealthy`) the server's tick health is fine. That matches Ben's 3.3.1 client (generator under 6 s of CPU in 7 minutes, spectator flight well above 20 b/s): the pause rule stalls the generator entirely; turning it off helps but does not restore the still rate.
- **Recommendation.** Deep Time should not try to override the two rules from code: the API cannot reach them, and `Config` is DH-internal (reflection would break on each DH release). Set `pauseIfMovingQuickly = false` and `limitIfServerUnhealthy = false` as the MIC pack's default `config/DistantHorizons.toml` (Deep Time's override runs on DH's own executor and never loads a chunk, so the server-health rule only costs LODs), and do not promise a full fix: a camera that fast still overloads DH's builder. That is a pack config change, the coordinator's and mic-rtsim's call; nothing in this branch depends on it.

Cause: the snow line's rules bind in vanilla (its snowless biomes are vanilla's stony peaks, meadow and windswept hills; the log said `biome rules: [deeptime:snow_line (2 of 2 rules)]` with 0 volcanic biomes), and `VolcanicBiomes.Level.active()` counted any bound rule as the volcanic layer being on; the census's `columns_changed` also counted the snow line's 350 columns, since the plain search leaves every rule out. `geologyGateChangesNothingWithoutThem` had passed only by skipping its check on that same flag (348 columns changed). Fix (branch volcano-fix-inactive-layers): `Level.volcanicActive()` is the volcanic layer's own flag (a kept-out volcanic biome, a role biome or a role rule; false in vanilla), `active()` keeps its meaning (anything to do, the query's fast path); `VolcanicBiomes.byOrdinaryRule` tells an ordinary rule's decision from a role rule's; both censuses report `columns_changed_by_rules` (the volcanic one also `volcanic_active`), and the two vanilla checks require every changed column to be a rule's. So a pack without a volcanic biome keeps the volcanic layer off exactly as before; the snow line stays on in vanilla, as BIO-180 intends (my reading of "and no snowless replacement": vanilla has one). biomes.md notes it. Gates on the VM (build/vfix/gates-fix.sh, 2026-10-22): `./gradlew build test` 431 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped; GameTests all 95 required passed in each of standalone, -PwithMic, -PwithEv, -PwithTerraBlender and -PwithEe (profiles reinstalled first). The vanilla checks now read: standalone and EV changed 350 = by rules 350 (volcanic), 348 = 348 (geology), volcanic layer off; MIC, TerraBlender and EE have volcanic biomes (layer on, logged only). No Rust change.

PLT-242 against its source: at the model's crossing (655 km³ per km and Myr) Stern & Scholl's 50 of deep loss is 7.6 % and 65 with the sediment 9.9 %; the model loses 5 % by the share and 11.9 % in all. ### 2026-10-21: Guaranteed deposits hold ore in the world as generated, and each essential reaches every land region in the world's own frame (DEP-220 to DEP-222, ORE-280; branch worktree-agent-a155838f16eaf3b96 from master 3ecea5b9, masters f58eb30d, f1632cf3, 54c40df4, bd7c8f21 and 44032ad9 merged in; sub-agent of the coordinator's session f981c0d3)
- **The problem.** The essentials guarantee promises one source of each essential in every 8,192-block (lead, zinc, copper, gold) or 4,096-block (iron, coal) land region. On master most guaranteed bodies held no ore in the world (quick planets: iron 10 of 46, lead and zinc 1 of 8), and the regions it counted were the simulation's Lambert ones, not the Petroff-Guyou world's (iron's 8 guarantees fell in 4 or 5 of the world's 8 regions).
- **Causes** (a column probe of master's quick planet, scattered continents 1, with `deeptime inspect-column`: 6 of 8 guaranteed iron bodies under the world's sea, none with ore). (1) The regions were the simulation's; the bake chooses λc later from its final land. (2) Where a region's cells tied (common for iron), the first land cell in index order won, at the region's edge, often a pole or a coast the young landscape redraws; ties of several essentials then took one cell, the later body painting over the earlier one's ore. (3) The body was placed against the deposit stage's ground, and the bake's lift and crest raise (STR-052, STR-053, STR-056) and the projection then moved it with the strata, mostly above the world's ground.
- **Fix** (no world-data format change: one new manifest note, the guarantee event's `region` string names the world's region, the top-up's copies are events of an existing kind; the guaranteed sites are found from the `deeptime:guaranteed_occurrence` events, so no Site flag).
  - DEP-220 (revised after the coordinator's review of 2026-10-21): the projection keeps master's λc rule (SCL-087 on the baked land, `BAKE_SEARCH`), so the cone points are master's. The deposit stage forecasts λc with that rule on its present L1 land at a coarser step (`FORECAST_SEARCH`: 1 degree, rings 0.5 degrees of 72 directions; `notes.deposits.world_frame` with `forecast` true; a preset without essentials keeps the Lambert frame, `why` "no essentials") and counts each essential's regions on that world's index frame (`Regions::in_frame`). After the projection, `anchor::top_up` counts the world's own land regions (a 64-block lattice on the generated terrain) against the sources holding ore in their centre column, natural or guaranteed, and gives each short region a copy of a template source (the essential's first guaranteed site with ore, else its smallest natural one; never a placer or a child site) at the region's inland point (128 blocks of dry lattice around it) nearest the baked spawn, anchored as below, with a new `deeptime:guaranteed_occurrence` caused by the template's. The CLI's `deeptime project` (a Lambert run's folder reprojected) says on stderr that its deposit stage counted on the Lambert frame and how many sources the top-up added.
  - DEP-222: candidates at least 128 world blocks from the present sea first (each cell's distance scaled by its own world blocks per simulation block, `world_scale`, floor 0.25), any land cell when a region has none; ties to the cell nearest the spawn the bake picks (the land nearest the simulation's (0, 0), drawn into the world); a guaranteed body keeps clear of every earlier one by the sum of their radii.
  - DEP-221, ORE-280: `deposits::anchor`, after the projection in `session.rs` (inside the run's thread pool) and the CLI's `project`, reads the finished folder through `ColumnWorld` and moves each guaranteed site's bodies together by whole blocks so the top of its ore (the highest block of the centre column where one of its bodies places ore, not the padded box) lies at the top rock block (ground less 4 blocks of soil on dry land, the bed under water) for iron and coal, and no higher than it for the others. An in-stratum body (MVT) stays in its host while its ore is in rock; otherwise it is read unclipped, moved into the highest limestone or dolostone run within 64 blocks as thick as its ore's span, else the thickest, and clipped there; an exposed essential's in-stratum body is raised as well as lowered (to a host run's top within 8 blocks, else the top rock block). Placers stay where `placer_channels` put them; natural bodies are untouched. The pass writes the events segment and index, then the bodies and sites files; the caller writes the manifest last (`notes.bake.guaranteed`: `topped_up`, `top_up` per essential, `millis`, `top_up_millis`). Run log: "guaranteed deposits: N under the world's ground, N moved (largest B blocks), N with ore in rock at the centre, N under water; N added where the world's regions lacked a source".
  - `deposit-audit`: per essential the sources and guaranteed sources holding ore in the world, the land regions with a source holding ore, the spawn's nearest source holding ore. `tools/review/essentials-table.py --guaranteed` tabulates them.
  - Tests: `deposits::anchor` unit tests (`a_guaranteed_body_moves_its_ore_top_to_the_top_rock_block`, `a_moved_body_holds_ore_at_the_top_rock_block`, `an_in_stratum_body_takes_a_host_that_holds_it`, `an_emptied_in_stratum_body_is_settled_into_rock`, `the_top_up_fills_every_land_region_of_the_world`), `deposits::tests::inland_cells_keep_the_margin_from_every_sea_cell`, `playability::tests::a_petroff_guyou_world_has_regions_of_its_own`, and `bake::tests::guaranteed_deposits_hold_ore_in_the_world` (a baked planet: the forecast recorded, every guaranteed site's ore under the rock, iron's exactly at it, no two guaranteed bodies overlapping, every land region of the world holding each essential with ore, a second anchor pass moving and adding nothing).
  - Docs: deposits.md "The guaranteed deposits in the world as generated" with the measurements, FORMAT.md (the λc forecast, `notes.deposits.world_frame`, the top-up, the rewrite order, `notes.bake.guaranteed`), EVENTS.md (the top-up's copies), ledger DEP-220 to DEP-222 and ORE-280 (Rows by hand: DEP 177, ORE 199), claims.md recounted after the merges (2,663), decisions log (three rows, 2026-10-20, revised 2026-10-21).

### 2026-10-21: Far terrain's sections are the same on every thread again: vanilla's warm-started climate search settled a tie by the thread's history, which the sea bed's per-thread biome cache (BAK-065) exposed; far terrain's searches now start cold (coordinator's task after the gate batch on master 44032ad9 failed `farTerrainSectionsAreCheapAndThreadSafe` standalone, with MIC, EV and TerraBlender; agent worktree agent-ae40153a5590aa6a8, branch worktree-agent-ae40153a5590aa6a8-threads from master 44032ad9; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Cause.** `Climate.RTree.search` starts from the thread's last leaf (`lastResult`, a ThreadLocal) and replaces it only with a strictly nearer one, so at a tie the thread's history picks the entry. Before BAK-065 every thread asked the same searches in a section's order; since it, the sea-bed rule reads biomes through PackSurfaceRule's per-thread quart cache (which outlives a build), so which searches run depends on what the thread built before. The gate's section [384, 128, 8], block (844, 396): sand at y -7 under `minecraft:deep_lukewarm_ocean` alone and `minecraft:deep_ocean` on thread 3, the only differing column (same with MIC). The preliminary-surface scan, the SurfaceRules.Context and the other per-thread caches are pure and were not it.
- **Change.** `climate/ColdBiomeSearch` (a per-thread depth) and `mixin/ClimateRTreeMixin` (at the head of `RTree.search`, inside it, `lastResult.remove()`): every far-terrain biome lookup (`FarTerrain.noiseBiome`, used by `biomeAt` and the pack rule's biome reader) runs inside it, so a tie goes to the first entry in the tree's order on every thread. Real chunks keep vanilla's search. The thread test compares column for column and logs the first 16 differing columns with their ground, block and biome (`threadsafeDiag`). world-scale-and-bake.md "Ties in the biome search". No ledger row (no physical value).
- **Measured** (VM, the GameTest with a scratch warm or cold switch in commit 614bde8e, removed after; `./gametest.sh -PgametestOnly=farterrainsectionsarecheapandthreadsafe` and `-PwithMic`, the VM loaded with an ensemble): warm 1 section of 24 differs on one of 4 threads, cold none, standalone and with MIC. Section cost, best of 3 alternating passes, detail 0 / detail 3: standalone warm 9.09 / 24.89 ms, cold 9.33 / 28.00; MIC warm 9.03 / 26.90, cold 9.33 / 30.36 (the ceiling is 250).
- **Gates** (VM, on the final commit): `./gradlew build test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 426 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped. `./gametest.sh -PgametestOnly=farterrainsectionsarecheapandthreadsafe` PASS (no differing column; 11.9 / 36.9 ms a section at detail 0 / 3, VM at a load of about 30 to 40); with `-PwithMic` and `farterrainseabedsfollowthesurfacerule`: both PASS (thread test 13.4 / 43.9 ms; sea beds warm 48 of 48 and other seas 48 of 48 the same top block and biome as the chunk, none generated further). Commands: `tools/remote/mac.sh -- ./build/ae40/run_final.sh` (gitignored: run_gradle.sh then the two gametest.sh calls).
- **Choices** (mine, undoable): cold searches only for far terrain, not for real chunks (their biomes stay vanilla's); a plain cold start rather than a bounded search (the warm answer's distance as a bound for a first-in-order pass, which would win back the 3 ms at detail 3); the lone build on the server thread, as before.
- **Next step.** The coordinator merges and reruns the gate batch.

### 2026-10-21: The plateau's warmth (the mass-elevation effect): land's ground temperature gets a monthly warmth per metre of base height, fitted to plateau stations against R1's free air (CLM-225 to CLM-231, MOI-085); Earth's Tibet loses its spurious ice cap (glacier share above 3 km 0.64 to 0) and Nagqu's July goes from -2.5 to 8.0 °C (observed 10.0); on the quick planets land under ice falls from 0.231 to 0.156 and the present-day target is met in 5 runs of 6 (0 before); an ice cap already standing on a plateau stays (coordinator's task after the white-patches diagnosis; agent worktree agent-a41fb0102cf16166c, branch worktree-agent-a41fb0102cf16166c from master c790d1f3, masters 54c40df4 and bd9cede0 merged in (viewer and STATUS only); sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **The law** (`climate/lapse.rs`, `climate/snapshot.rs`, GPU mirror in `climate/gpu.rs`): on land, t_sl[m] = the lowland's t_sl + k(q̂_m)·Ẑ, then the lapse rate (GLA-038) as before. Ẑ = max(0, min(z, B(B(z')))), z' the ground's height with the sea and land ice of at least 1 m at 0, B a box blur of half-width 150 km (CLM-225, CLM-228); k = 2.43e-3 K/m × (clamp(q̂, 0.60, 1.42) - 0.792), q̂ the month's daily-mean top-of-atmosphere sunlight over S0/4 from the climate's own insolation (CLM-226, CLM-227). The orographic rain's moisture factor keeps the lowland's temperature. Every reader of the ground temperature inherits it: the ELA, Köppen and aridity, the weathering kernel, the carried anomalies (MOI-052), the bake's `t_sl_c_NN` (lapsed per block by Java's ClimateSample) and the L2 Köppen.
- **Sources** (bibliography "The plateau's warmth"): read in full by a sub-agent, `verified`: Han et al. 2018, 2018b, 2020 (J. Mt. Sci.), Zhao et al. 2015, Yao & Zhang 2013, Pepin & Seidel 2005, Yanai, Li & Song 1992, Flohn 1968, Pan et al. 2021; abstracts only: Yao & Zhang 2015 (CLM-220 now `abstract-only`), He et al. 2016, Han et al. 2012, Zhao et al. 2014; station normals from Wikipedia's copies of the CMA, SENAMHI and NOAA tables and R1's 1991-2020 long-term means (CLM-229, `abstract-only`). Han's MBE law (annual MEE = 0.0019 MBE + 0.584) is not used: its baseline gives 11.5 °C in Tibet's core against about 2 K at Nagqu against R1.
- **The fit** (`tools/validation/mee_station_fit.py`, new, run on the VM on Earth's climate-dem dumps): least squares on 28 station-months of 12 stations, K 2.432e-3, Q0 0.792, rms 1.28 K; mean residuals Tibet -0.10, Altiplano -0.63, Rockies +1.51, Addis Ababa -0.07 K. Footprint sweep 56/111/150/222/333/500 km: rms 1.19/1.20/1.28/1.37/1.52/1.63.
- **Earth** (`deeptime climate-dem`, 280 ppm, five ice feedback snapshots; `build/pw/earth.sh`, scored with `climate_vs_obs.py` and the fit script), before → after: global 14.41 → 14.56 °C (CLM-138's 14.1 ± 0.4: 0.06 K above), land 8.67 → 9.24 °C, glaciated land 0.094 → 0.081, Tibet above 3 km glacier 0.643 → 0, its warmest month p50 -3.5 → 6.0 °C; warmest month at the stations' heights Nagqu -2.5 → 8.0 (10.0), Tingri -0.9 → 7.8 (12.6), Puno 4.1 → 8.2 (11.4), Leadville 3.0 → 6.5 (12.8), Addis Ababa 14.0 → 16.4 (18.8); Greenland 0.497 → 0.483, Antarctica 0.883 → 0.881; cities 21 of 24 (23 at station heights, was 22); Köppen A/B/C/D/E 0.17/0.16/0.24/0.23/0.20 → 0.18/0.17/0.23/0.25/0.18. `KERNEL_EARTH` (CLM-061) re-measured 5.039e7 → 5.147e7.
- **Quick planets** (`earthlike_quick_16k`, 1000 Myr, seeds 1 to 3 × supercontinent and scattered continents, `build/pw/runs.sh`, census `continents_census.py fields`, `build/pw/summary.py` and `series.py`), means before → after: land 0.264 → 0.245, land under ice 0.231 → 0.156 (every run lower), the largest plateau's ice 0.81 → 0.49 (cleared in 3 of 6) and its warmest month -4.6 → 2.4 °C, global mean at the end 17.6 → 16.5 °C, end CO2 median 1,429 → 822 ppm (natural, before the present nudge, 817 → 622), the present-day target (CLM-203) reached 0 → 5 of 6, sea level -22.7 → -3.3 m. Over the last 500 Myr the CO2 rose instead (1,313 → 1,791 ppm mean), with 9 % more degassing and more land above 2 km (0.26 → 0.33): the plate histories part, so neither CO2 change is the law's alone.

### 2026-10-21: The biome bake's land call on the world's ground: the projection pass re-decides every L2 biome node with the column evaluator's own sea rule, so no node keeps a land biome under the sea or an ocean biome on dry ground (BIO-170 to BIO-174, BAK-057 to BAK-059, HYD-106 to HYD-109) (coordinator's task, loose end (1) of the HYD-100 entry below; agent worktree agent-a7e8aa9425fbce4eb, branch worktree-agent-a7e8aa9425fbce4eb from master f1632cf3; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Where the call was.** `bake/biomes.rs` `map` decided land from the simulation's Lambert L2 grid, `elevation > sea level || closed_below_sea` (HYD-104). The game's sea is `ground < sea level - 1 && !closed` on the world's own projected height (step 3 of the column evaluator). Two differences: the last block under sea level (H in (sea - 1, sea], a 35 m band) is dry in the game and ocean in the bake (HYD-107), and the Lambert L2 cell and the world's footprint mean disagree on some nodes, plus HYD-105 opens pockets to the sea that the Lambert hydrology called closed (HYD-108).
- **Change.**
  - The rule is one function per language: `water::sea_covers(ground, sea_level_y, closed)` (and `sea_covers_height`) in `deeptime-format/src/water.rs`, `Water.seaCovers` in Java; `core_with_surface` and `Water.core` read it (HYD-106). A Rust test builds columns around the line and the closed flag.
  - `bake/biomes.rs`: `ContinentAnchors` (the continentalness laws of `map`, one object for the bake and the settle), `is_land_continentalness` (stored edge compared on the layer's 1e-4 quantum), `BiomeCells`, `settle_to_ground`: a node whose continentalness side disagrees with the world's rule takes the continentalness of the land law (distance to the sea) or the sea law (depth) and the record of the nearest stable donor of the new medium (class 31 and no wetland for sea, with the deep sea floor's erosion); every other node is untouched (BIO-171, BIO-172).
  - `bake/project.rs`: the pass holds the seven L2 biome layers (`Held`, `is_biome_layer`) until the world's `elevation` and `closed_basin` exist (L3 is processed after L2), then `settle_biome_layers` decides each node and writes them; note `notes.bake.projection.biome_land` (BAK-057). Lambert presets have no projection pass and keep the old call.
  - Census: `BiomeCensus` counts `sea_call` on the real planet (sea columns on a land biome, dry columns on an ocean biome, columns inland of the coast only); `BiomeGameTests.climateConsistent` asserts at most 1 % each way and at least 40 columns of each (BIO-173). `tools/review/biome_land_census.py` is the offline census (BAK-058).
  - Tests: `the_biome_layers_settle_to_the_worlds_sea_rule` (six x-bands through `project_folder`), `settling_to_the_world_s_ground_moves_only_the_mismatched_nodes`, `a_deep_pocket_takes_the_deep_sea_floor_and_a_far_basin_takes_inland_bands`, `the_stored_edge_is_land`, `the_sea_rule_is_one_function_and_the_column_evaluator_reads_it` (BAK-059).
  - Docs: biomes.md "The land call on the world's ground"; rivers-and-lakes.md "The sea's one rule"; FORMAT.md (projection pass, the sea step); ledger rows BIO-170 to BIO-174, BAK-057 to BAK-059, HYD-106 to HYD-109, HYD-104 and HYD-105 touched; `claims_counts.py --write` and the three "Rows:" headers by hand.
- **Measured** (VM, admitted; `earthlike_quick_16k`, 1000 Myr, 8 threads, supercontinent and scattered seeds 1 and 2; master f1632cf3's binary against this branch's, same simulation; `build/bioland/ens.sh` for the eight bakes, `census.sh` and `tools/review/biome_land_census.py` for the counts, `table.py` for the table, `crcs.py` for the layer CRCs; the rule is read on each world's own `elevation` and `closed_basin` rasters):

| run | L2 nodes before: land biome under sea, ocean biome on dry | after | L3 columns after: land under sea, ocean on dry |
|---|---|---|---|
| supercontinent 1 | 4,110 (1.15 % of the land), 37,475 (10.51 %) | 0, 0 | 21,522 (0.38 %), 60,833 (1.07 %) |
| supercontinent 2 | 2,361 (0.61 %), 21,676 (5.58 %) | 0, 0 | 15,403 (0.25 %), 48,974 (0.79 %) |
| scattered 1 | 4,135 (1.15 %), 18,307 (5.07 %) | 0, 0 | 22,160 (0.38 %), 62,747 (1.09 %) |

- **What changed besides the mismatches.** Nothing: the nodes that differ between before and after are exactly the before-mismatched nodes (41,585 on supercontinent 1 = 4,110 + 37,475; 24,037, 22,442, 24,670 on the others; collateral 0), and 42 of the 49 layers of the world folder are byte-identical (CRC); the seven settled layers differ. 92 % of the ocean-on-dry nodes lay in the 35 m band (34,560 of 37,475), 55 % were more than two nodes from the sea.
- **The remainder** (BIO-174). At the 8-block L3 columns 0.25 to 0.38 % (land biome under the sea) and 0.79 to 1.09 % (ocean biome on dry ground) of the land are still on the wrong side of the rule: the game reads the layers bilinear between nodes 8 blocks apart, so the coast falls where the two node values cross. These columns lie at a median of 2 blocks (90th percentile under 4, at most 10) from the rule's coast; 0 to 2 are further than a node. The call also reads the elevation layer, not the detail term (as HYD-105).
- **Gates** (VM, admitted, `build/bioland/gates.sh` on BASE_HEAD; Rust unchanged after that but for comments): cargo fmt ok, clippy `-D warnings` ok, `cargo test --workspace` all ok (the largest suite 811 passed, 5 ignored, 0 failed), deny ok, `./gradlew build test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL with 424 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped, on e2c09390 (all the Rust and Java code); the comment-only edits since (ledger ids in comments) rechecked at de681cfd with fmt, clippy `--workspace --all-targets`, the format water test and a Java compile. GameTests not run.
- **Choices** (mine, undoable): the rule is read at the node's own block on the world raster (nearest sample), not a footprint; a settled node takes the nearest stable donor's record rather than a recomputed Koppen class (the pass has no monthly climate); sea nodes take class 31 and no wetland, the deep sea floor's erosion floor where the band is under 2; the stored edge counts as land on the 1e-4 quantum; the GameTest ceiling 1 % and the inland-only count (8 blocks on four sides) and its 40-column floor; the one rule as `sea_covers` in both languages; the census' `land` and the volcanic, bedrock and fluid-picker thresholds left alone (HYD-109).
- **Not done, for the coordinator.** (1) Lambert presets (no projection pass) keep the simulation grid's call, including the 35 m band as ocean; a call on the Lambert grid would need `sea_covers_height` in `biomes.rs` `map` itself. (2) The detail term is not read; a column whose detail carries it across the line is not settled; not measured. (3) HYD-109's four thresholds (`VolcanicBiomes.land`, `GeologyGround.sea`, `LavaFluids`, the census' `land`) call the 35 m band sea or compare y; not measured. (4) The GameTest bound (BIO-173) was not run on the 4k planet (`./gametest.sh` is the coordinator's batch): the first run logs the counts, and the ceiling may need setting from them. (5) A world with no sea donor or no land donor keeps a node's own record but for its continentalness.

### 2026-10-21: Closed ground below sea level by its water balance, kept dry in the game: a basin the open sea does not reach takes its own lake, playa or dry floor whatever its height (HYD-100, format 0.6), the game stands no sea there and keeps its caves (HYD-103), and the Petroff–Guyou projection draws the flag again on the world's ground, which closed dry holes of up to 1,519 km2 beside the sea (HYD-105) (coordinator's task, the lakes follow-up part 1; agent worktree agent-ac96e57f36cb99ad4, branch worktree-agent-ac96e57f36cb99ad4 from master 72280b3b, master 406d63b1 merged in at 77c49e74; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Change.**
  - Bake: `hydro/mod.rs` finds the open sea (bodies of 5,000 km2 a block or more under sea level, HYD-012) and the low ground it reaches; `network.rs` keeps HYD-052 only for basins whose lowest cell is reached, so a closed basin takes HYD-050's balance (a lake below sea level, a playa or dry). New u8 layer `closed_basin` on the `water_level` grid with an 8-block halo (BAK-055, HYD-102); water `method` "hyd-100", `stats.below_sea`. The biome bake calls closed ground land (`hydro::closed_below_sea` on L2, HYD-104).
  - Projection (HYD-105): `bake/project.rs` redraws the layer on the world's own ground (`hydro::closed_basin_on_world`, `world_ground`); the note `notes.bake.projection.closed_basin`. ### 2026-10-20: Hot-spring pool water stays open in any biome (GEO-062): `LakeFreeze.keepsOpen` now also answers yes at the surface block of a geothermal pool's water, so vanilla's `freeze_top_layer` (generation) and snowfall (weather) never ice a pool under Biomes O' Plenty's cold hot springs; `hotSpringPoolsSitInTheirBiome` reads every pool surface; `GeothermalTest` holds the rule; branch worktree-agent-a5e9d5bf9f39edb59 (from master 634a9b1c)
- **The bug.** In a `-PwithTerraBlender` GameTest the pool at (558, 257) came out iced (the side finding of the playa task, below). Reproduced first with the new test and no fix, TerraBlender: pools 18, 708 pool columns, 190 with ice on the water (`iced(454,96,246 biomesoplenty:hot_springs)` and 189 more), and the other 518 water surfaces all froze under snowy plains' rule (`coldBiomeFreezes=518 of 518`); the test failed on the ice. Standalone had no ice (no hot-spring biome there).
- **Cause.** `GeothermalPass.placePool` puts plain water down from the site's `level` and nothing kept it open: `LakeFreeze` and `BiomeFreezeMixin` exempted only Deep Time lakes (via `LakeIce`). The hot-spring field's role gives the disc Biomes O' Plenty's `hot_springs` (temperature 0.17), cold enough that vanilla's `Biome.shouldFreeze` says yes at the pool's surface block, once at generation (`freeze_top_layer`, which calls it with the water block's position) and again in weather (`ServerLevel.tickChunk`). GEO-020's 3 degrees C floor keeps pools out of cold fields, but the biome's temperature is not the field's, and the floor never made the biome agree. GEO-020 says pools stay open; nothing enforced it.
- **Fix** (Java only; no world-data format change, no new pass, no change to what the pool pass places).
  - `Geothermal.poolSurface(x, y, z)` (plain Java): true when the winning site by part priority (`claim`) is a POOL, the column is a pool part (`Part.pool()`, folded across the seam by `dx`) and `y` is the site's `level` (the surface block; `placePool` puts water from `level` down). A set of the pools' levels answers most queries without a claim. `POOL_MIN_C`'s javadoc no longer says the floor guards against ice.
  - `LakeFreeze.keepsOpen` (the one hook `BiomeFreezeMixin` asks at the head of `Biome.shouldFreeze`): the lake rule as before, else `poolSurface` on the level's `Geothermal` (`WorldDataTerrain.geothermal`, cached; `GeothermalPass` has built it before any chunk reaches the features). Only the answer "does not freeze" is ever forced, only at a pool's surface; snow on the dry apron is vanilla's and stays.
  - Tests: `GeothermalTest.aPoolsSurfaceWaterIsKeptOpenWhateverTheBiomeAndNothingElseIs` (JUnit: over every site's box, pool columns open at the winner's level, also across the x seam; false one above and below, 12 above, in non-pool columns at all heights, with `NONE`, density 0 and a cold field). `VolcanicBiomeGameTests.hotSpringPoolsSitInTheirBiome` no longer returns early in a pack without a hot-spring biome: its biome half runs only when the pack has one, its water half in every profile. The water half reads the surface block of every pool column (spread over ticks by `ChunkSampling`) and fails on ice, on any surface that snowy plains' freezing rule would ice, and when `LakeFreeze.keepsOpen` is not yes at every surface or is yes one block under. The vanilla probe's liveness is a control: the same rule one block under the surface must say yes.
  - **The MIC probe caveat.** Under `-PwithMic` the control said yes to 0 of 409: Serene Seasons (`MixinBiome`, a `@Redirect` of `Biome.warmEnoughToRain` inside `shouldFreeze` to `SeasonHooks.shouldFreezeWarmEnoughToRainHook`) makes vanilla's freezing seasonal, so snowy plains does not freeze in the season the test runs in. The control assertion therefore holds in the profiles without it; with Serene Seasons loaded the test logs "the cold-biome probe is inconclusive" and rests on the direct `LakeFreeze.keepsOpen` assertions (708 of 708 yes at the surface, 0 of 409 one block under). A pack that stops vanilla's freezing for any other reason fails the control loudly.
  - Docs: geothermal-features.md (never-frozen pool water, model item 6, the GEO-020 row and a new GEO-062 row, the "No ice-covered fields" limit rewritten, an "Open water is a game rule" limit, the game choice and how to undo it), ledger GEO (GEO-062 `game-choice`, the GEO-020 row, "Rows: 62" by hand from claims.md's table: `verified` 4, `game-choice` 55, `uncited` 3), BIO-086 and HYD-072 (a clause about pools), claims.md (`claims_counts.py --write`), the decisions log (2026-10-20). GEO-062 is free on master and on all 225 `worktree-agent-*` branches (a grep of docs/science, neoforge/src and crates for GEO-062 and up found none).
- **Measured** (VM, admitted, `./gametest.sh [-PwithTerraBlender|-PwithMic] -PgametestOnly=hotSpringPoolsSitInTheirBiome,lakeIceAndSaltFollowTheClimate,lakeHolds,geothermalAroundActiveVolcanoes,volcanicBiomesOnlyAtVolcanoes,volcanicBiomesChangeNothingWithoutThem` through `tools/remote/detach.sh`, at ae246c08):
  - TerraBlender: 6 of 6 pass; pools 18, columns 708, `inColdBiome=190`, water 708, iced 0, `coldBiomeFreezes=0 of 708`, control 409 of 409, `keepsOpen` 708 of 708 and 0 of 409.
  - Standalone: 6 of 6 pass; the same 708 columns, all water, iced 0, control 409 of 409, `inColdBiome=0` (no hot-spring biome, so the role half has nothing to read).
  - MIC: 6 of 6 pass; iced 0, `keepsOpen` 708 of 708 and 0 of 409, the vanilla probe inconclusive (above).
  - No mutation run beyond the baseline: the TerraBlender run without the fix (above) is the failing case.
- **Gates** (VM, admitted, `build/geo/gates.sh` on the branch after the docs commit): cargo fmt clean; clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; `cargo test --workspace` 1,064 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored; cargo deny licenses and bans ok; `./gradlew build test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL, JUnit tests=424 failures=0 errors=0 skipped=2.
- **Choices** (mine, undoable; decisions log 2026-10-20): keep the water open by the lake mechanism rather than changing the role biome's temperature or choosing role biomes by temperature (the biome keeps its look and the apron its snow); the 3 degrees C floor of GEO-020 left as Ben's game choice, no longer carrying the ice guarantee; the rule covers pool water only (rims, terraces and vents are not water); GEO-062 as a `game-choice` row; the MIC control made conditional on Serene Seasons rather than weakening the liveness check in the other profiles. Undone by removing the pool line in `LakeFreeze.keepsOpen`.
- **Next.** No full GameTest batch (the coordinator's). Seasonal behaviour is untouched: Serene Seasons changes when snow falls and pool water ignores it by this rule. The exact pool of master 05be7359's planet (558, 257) was not re-read; the 18 pools of this branch's test planet stand in for it.
