### 2026-10-20: The live map: the Create World map follows the run between keyframes (Ben's report "the map seems to update every ~50 mil years instead of in real time"): the layer the player views drawn natively after a step into one reusable frame, not kept, paced to 2 % of the run (measured 1.3 to 1.8 % added wall time, a frame every 5 to 6 s); the keyframe grid, stops, epoch picks and scrubber unchanged, the world byte-identical with or without it (coordinator's task; agent worktree agent-a1668b971da4ec7fa, branch worktree-agent-a1668b971da4ec7fa from master d9bd2b65; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Cause.** The map showed only keyframes, which the quick presets draw every 50 Myr (Ben, 2026-10-06). On a 1,000-Myr quick run that is a new picture every 20 s or so, up to 50 Myr behind the status line.
- **Design** (decisions log 2026-10-20, two rows).
  - Core: `deeptime_core::live` (`LiveMap`, `LivePacing`, `LiveFrame`, `LiveStats`). `Session::advance` calls `draw_live` after each step: when the screen has asked within 2 s and a frame is due, it renders the one layer with `keyframes::render` (the keyframes' own code, full keyframe size) into one frame that replaces the last (an `Arc` swap). Only layers of the stage group now running are drawn; a keyframe drawn at the same step stands in. Pacing: the next frame waits 49 times the last frame's drawing time and at least 250 ms (2 % of the run); a layer change draws at once. The pending P1-19 follower is never settled for it; its time stays out of the stage timings and is logged per stage ("live map during plates+...: 96 frames, 74 ms each on average ...").
  - JNI: `watchLive(session, layer)` (null stops; returns the newest frame's number) and `copyLiveFrame(session, direct buffer)` (JSON seq, t, stage, layer, w, h; "" before the first). Neither waits on a step. `copyKeyframe` now shares the direct-buffer helper `with_direct_bytes`.
  - Java: `SimSession.watchLive` and `copyLiveFrame`; `RunHandle.LiveFrame`; `TimelapseModel` renews the request on every poll while it follows the newest frame, fetches a newer live frame on its loader thread and shows it while its layer matches and it is newer than the newest keyframe. `index`, `current`, the stop and the epoch stay on keyframes; `mapTime()` is the shown picture's time. `GenerationPage`: the badge "● Live map", the scrubber's label at the live frame's time, the stop tooltip (`deeptime.gen.stop_here.hint_live`); the scrubber's tooltip rewritten.
  - CLI: `deeptime run --live <layer> [--live-every-step]`; every run prints `deeptime run: live layer= frames= live_ms= mean_ms= max_ms= share_of_steps= stepped_s=`.
  - Client walk: the ScreenshotDriver's LIVE step shoots `04c-live-map-a` and `04d-live-map-b`, one new live frame apart, and logs each picture's time beside the newest keyframe's.
- **Tests.** `live.rs` (4 unit tests: lease, pacing, stand-in, replace and copy); session test `the_live_map_draws_the_watched_layer_between_keyframes`; `crates/deeptime-core/tests/live_map.rs` (the overlap test's small planet run unwatched and with the satellite view drawn after every step: the same world byte for byte (sites, bodies, events, notes without times, history, postcard bytes), the same keyframes and pixels, the same files; at least 10 live frames at times no keyframe has); `TimelapseModelTest.showsTheLiveFrameBetweenKeyframesWhileFollowing`; `NativeLinkTest.liveFramesCrossTheBoundary`.
- **Measured** (`earthlike_quick_16k`, supercontinent, 1000 Myr, 8 threads, release build, the VM loaded by other agents; `build/live-map/bench.sh`, not committed: `deeptime run --preset earthlike_quick_16k --start supercontinent --length-myr 1000 --threads 8 --out <dir> [--live satellite [--live-every-step]]`, pairs started together):

| run | wall s (on / off) | added wall | live frames | ms each (mean / max) | drawing share of the stepping | a frame every |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| every step (frame cost) | 440.9 | | 482 | 68.7 / 177.9 | 7.9 % | |
| pair 1, same binary | 619.05 / 610.91 | +1.33 % | 94 | 94.7 / 140.3 | 1.50 % | 6.3 s |
| pair 2, same binary | 537.82 / 528.28 | +1.81 % | 82 | 88.1 / 188.9 | 1.40 % | 6.3 s |
| pair 3, against master d9bd2b65 | 374.33 / 369.22 | +1.38 % | 75 | 71.6 / 113.3 | 1.54 % | 4.7 s |

  User CPU time: +1.5 %, +0.9 % and 0.0 %. A full-size frame is cheap enough, so no reduced size: the satellite view's cost is per grid (the water view, the box filters), not per pixel.
- **Evidence** (the real client on the VM, `tools/remote/mac.sh -- tools/remote/detach.sh start lm-client --kind client:editor tools/client/vm-client.sh --name live-map --no-guidance --no-create --prop start=supercontinent --prop length=1000 --prop cancel=false --prop customize=false`; 7 sim threads; https://spacesheep.dev/@benmac/deeptime-live-map-walk, private): `live map a: 898 million years ago (t -898 Myr), newest keyframe 900 million years ago (t -900 Myr), 3 keyframes`, then 5 s later `live map b: 884 million years ago (t -884 Myr), newest keyframe 900 million years ago ..., the same newest keyframe as shot a`; the shots show "● Live map", "Map: 898" and "Map: 884 million years ago" under a status line 2 Myr ahead, and the rift between the two continents visibly wider. The layer shots (plates, Köppen) show the live map too. The run: 462 s for 1000 Myr; live map during the coupled group 96 frames, 74 ms each, 7.1 s in all.
- **Gates** (VM, admitted, at 8be711c7; the later commits are documents): cargo fmt clean; clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo test --workspace 1,045 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored; cargo deny licenses and bans ok; `./gradlew build test` successful, JUnit 421 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped. No GameTest batch (the coordinator's).
- **Overlap with Faster Create World** (P1-24, worktree-agent-af885b010222cb104, not merged here; no commits past master c947b996 yet, its design is docs/design/faster-create-world.md in that worktree): kf100 (express: a keyframe every 100 Myr) would make the old map move every 100 Myr; with the live map the keyframe interval no longer sets how often the map moves while a run goes. Express's 4-Myr step: at most one live frame per step, so frames at least 4 Myr apart, and its coarser L1 (l1r32) makes a frame cheaper, which the pacing turns into more frames by itself. The planet pool: a run in the background has nobody watching, so nothing is drawn and it costs nothing; a pooled planet's timelapse is its keyframes. Expected conflicts only in text (STATUS, the decisions log, the plan).
- **Choices** (mine, undoable; decisions log 2026-10-20): the live map as a frame that is not a keyframe; the 2 % share with a 250 ms floor and the 2 s lease; full keyframe size; only the running group's layers; Stop here and Pick this epoch stay on keyframes with a tooltip that says so; the texts ("● Live map", the stop hint, the scrubber's tooltip). Docs: create-world-ux.md (the map), playability-steering.md (design and science page: the live map is not a stop), the plan §6.1 (the natives, the live map) and §7 (run page, P1-11). No ledger row: no physical value.

### 2026-10-20: Crust templates and the relief lift: each crust kind draws its own rock (ocean crust is Penrose's lavas over sheeted dikes over gabbro, 6.6 km), rock pools no longer blend across crust kinds, the transition's granite under the sea traced and put behind a switch for Ben (PLT-294, off), and the rock now rises with the amplified terrain instead of the top unit filling it (coordinator's task, the external review's D1 and D2, then the coordinator's Opus review of 6e406395, findings 1 to 8; agent worktree agent-a8d769d9446780ad7, branch worktree-agent-a8d769d9446780ad7 from master d54c7f0f, masters bc2e5472 (the continents fix), 49f5f543 (the sea-floor fix), f9da262a, 5e0615b9 (REV-2), 45b09c52 (P1-11d), 5dc06974 (the Petroff forward fix, devmap) and 9d6758bb (land shape and the high ground) merged in; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Causes.**
  - `plates/ridges.rs` `interpolate` and `plates/l1.rs` `sample_with` blended every rock pool over all three corners whatever their crust kind. Each resampling put a share of a continent's granite, gneiss and platform cover into the ocean samples beside it, and spread arc and margin rock a little further across the basins.
  - `structure/columns.rs` drew every crust kind's pools with the continental classes and order (granite, gneiss, rhyolite under the sea). `structure/bake_horizons.rs` smoothed one kind's basement into the other's across the coast.
  - `plates/transition.rs` (the sink loop of `step`) gives the oceanic samples within W/2 of a margin the continent's own rock; on the quick planet that is nearly all of the ocean. Switching the transition off (on d54c7f0f) took the ocean-basin cells holding felsic plutonic rock from 0.83 to 0.35: the main source.
  - Island arcs (`plates/subduction.rs`, PLT-043 to PLT-046) add felsic rock to oceanic samples along fronts about 8.6 times Earth's length (125,000 km against 14,500 at 500 Myr: plates.md "The crust budget on sourced rates", plate task 8, 2026-10-17, inferred from the fronts' km x Myr; not re-measured here).
  - D2: `bake/strata.rs` stored the stack against the history's coarse surface, so any terrain the amplifier raised above it was filled by the top unit.
- **Changes.**
  - PLT-293: blend within one kind; ocean crust's felsic and metamorphic pools stay the nearest corner's at a resampling.
  - RCK-095 and RCK-096 (first numbered RCK-091 and RCK-092; REV-2 took RCK-091 on master, so they moved, RCK-092 to RCK-094 left free): ocean crust is basalt over 1.2 km of sheeted dikes drawn as greenstone over gabbro; its felsic rock andesite, diorite under an arc, granodiorite elsewhere, its metamorphic rock schist; never granite, rhyolite or gneiss.
  - STR-054: the bake smooths within one crust kind.
  - STR-052 and STR-053: every horizon of a cell lifts by its node relief where positive (over the L3 cells of the four L1 squares round the cell's node, the mean of the final elevation less the history's surface at the same point), capped at max_y; crests are filled by the thickest rock unit within 16 blocks.
  - STR-056: bodies and deposit sites rise by how far the raise moved the column's height of the stratigraphic key their rock has (`key_shift`), so a site keeps its host stratum (lift and crest raise together). REV-2's aureole slabs and stock roots are bodies and move with them.
  - STR-055: the structure file keeps the history's heights; the new layer `strata/lift` carries each cell's lift and both deformed column rules (Rust `Structure::deformed_stack`, Java `Structure.deformedStack`) read every source stack through its own lift, so a fault's plane and an intrusion's body rise with the rock of each column they cut.
  - STR-057: the bake's surface census (`notes.bake.strata.surface_census`): valley floors, lifted ground, the horizon at the ground, `surface/class_top` against the drawn class.
  - PLT-294, `tectonics.transition_ocean_crust` (off by default; on, an oceanic sink takes the same volume as lavas and gabbro).
  - Tools: `inspect-column --points`, `notes.bake.strata.mountain_fill`, `tools/review/geo-template.sh`, `geo_template.py`, `geo_template_fields.py`.
  - REV-2's `meta/crust_type` is sampled from the same `plates/crust_type` field the column's class choice reads; no second crust-kind layer was added.
- **The review of 6e406395** (each checked against the code before fixing; all eight stood, 6 and 8 in part). 1, the lift measured curvature: it set the window's mean elevation against the cell's own first top, so a valley cell beside high ground rose by the coarse surface's own curvature; now the pointwise relief above. 2, structures rose by the lift at their window's centre: measured over the after runs (`notes.bake.strata.structure_lift`, a 9 x 9 lattice of each window), faults p90 2.2 to 3.0 blocks and p99 12 to 13, intrusions p90 0.7 to 1.2, so over the review's 2 to 3 block bar; hence STR-055. 3, `Lift::sites` moved a site by the lift, not by its host rock: `key_shift`, test `a_site_keeps_its_host_stratum_across_the_lift`. 4, `surface/class_top` was unchecked: STR-057. 5, STR-051 measured another window than the lift and only the first horizon: now the lift's node window, and the first rock horizon beside it. 6, citations, in part: the arcs' 8.6 times Earth's front length traced to plate task 8 (inferred there, not re-measured); the volcanic-margin reading behind RCK-096 and PLT-294 was from memory and is now marked so; RCK-095 says the dikes are a 1.2 km cap, not a share. 7, the Noddy plane guard is the caller's (unit tests 1e-6, the stage's check 1e-4). 8, `l1.rs`'s same-kind weights were already non-negative; clamped at 0 anyway.
- **Outside the brief's area, needed by the gates.** PLT-293 changes every planet, so three plate tests that rest on one seed's history were reseeded after a sweep (`plates/tests.rs`: the weld tests on scattered continents seed 19 and supercontinent seed 1, the recording test on scattered seed 19). The dense-structures test then failed on a side flip 5.3e-6 of a block from a fault plane in a 740-event column: the Noddy check's plane guard is now 1e-4 of a block, the agreement the tests ask (`structure/deform/lattice.rs`, CRE-034). After master 9d6758bb was merged, the recording test met the land-shape task's new per-step bound (the boundary mix's subducting fronts never above the plates' fronts) on this branch's seed 19: step 16 over by 1.0 % (24,489 km against 24,236), the only step of 138. The bound is not an invariant: the mix judges the motion across the boundary's normal (PLT-310, PLT-311), the plates' fronts (`subduction::fronts_begin`) by single lattice edges, so a sample whose boundary converges while each of its edges parts is a front in the mix only. The test now asks at most 3 % a step (three times the measured worst) and, over the run, no more than the plates' fronts and over half of them (measured 0.72); `classify_boundary` is unchanged, so the land-shape task's boundary tables stand.
- **Not touched: trench width and hadal area.** The work changes which rock the pools carry and how a column draws and lifts it; it does not change the trench code, so the one-sample trenches the sea-floor fix met are a separate task.

### 2026-10-20: Petroff's forward projection fixed on its degenerate lines: exact inputs on the square's diagonals (the world's equator and the meridians λc and λc + 180°) and at the cone points land where they were asked, in Rust, Java and the pages; the dev map's nudge retries dropped; REV-2's site-15 lat/lon mismatch traced to the deposits overlay's simulation-frame x and z, and the site card now gives the world's block (coordinator's task; agent worktree agent-a8b68c5b73883ce80, branch worktree-agent-a8b68c5b73883ce80 from master ccdced0b, masters 5e0615b9 and 45b09c52 merged in; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **What was wrong.** The forward's last step puts P′ in a flat triangle: U′ on V′W′ at the distance `up` from V′, P′ on C′U′ at the fraction `xpxpyp` from C′, and P′'s angle at V′ (`alphap`) from the triangle V′U′P′'s three sides by the law of cosines. When P′ lies on that triangle's side V′U′ (`yp` near 0) or U′C′ (`up` near 0), the triangle is flat and the angle is rounding noise. That is every exact input on the square's diagonals: the world's equator and the meridians λc and λc + 180° (`up` is noise from a tile's centre to its 67.5° vertex, `yp` from there to the edge). At the cone points `up` is exactly 0, and the fallback angle ξ′ − π/6 is sub-triangle 2's, while the cone points lie in sub-triangles 0 and 1. Petroff's `new_projection.py` (Zenodo 4661351, re-read today at its `alphaprime` lines) has the same fallback. On the play planet (b 6656, λc 146°), 180 of 4,341 exact inputs (0.25° steps) came back more than 1e-5° off: the equator up to 1.61°, the meridians λc and λc + 180° up to 1.13° and 1.35°, and the cone points 10.49° ((45° N, 236°) clamped to (616, -3328)). The other three worlds tried had 152 to 161 misses each. Random inputs never land on a line, so the old round-trip tests had not seen it.
- **The fix** (`petroff.rs`, `Petroff.java`, `projection.js`: the same operations in all three). When `up` or `yp` is at most `NEAR_SIDE` = 1e-6 local units (about 0.002 blocks at b 6656), P′ is placed by coordinates: V′ at the origin, U′ = (up, 0), C′ = cp (cos gp, sin gp), P′ = C′ + xpxpyp (U′ − C′). `rp` is then √(px² + py²) and `alphap` is atan2(py, px). It is the same point, without the cancellation. Elsewhere the code is unchanged, operation for operation. Ledger SCL-083 and SCL-086 updated, `docs/science/seamless-world.md` has a new section, "The forward on the diagonals and at the cone points", and the bibliography's Petroff2021 entry records today's re-read. The fix is checked numerically, not against the paper (marked so on the page).
- **The coordinator's calls** (all undoable):
  - `NEAR_SIDE` 1e-6, not 1e-5 or 1e-4. A sweep of inputs 10⁻² to 10⁻¹⁵ degrees off the lines (5 longitudes on the equator, 3 latitudes on λc), against a 50-digit mpmath evaluation of the construction, put the law of cosines' error just above the switch at 1.5e-7 blocks at most. A larger switch would only change more outputs.
  - `PlanetGeometry.blockOf` keeps the inverse check, and a miss over 1e-5° now throws `IllegalStateException` instead of retrying from nudged inputs. A broken forward shows at once.
  - No before/after bake. The parity fixture shows that nothing else moved (below).
- **Measured.**
  - The sweep and the reference: `tools/remote/mac.sh -- 'node sweep.js 6656 146 1e-6 | python3 mpref.py'` (scratch scripts, not committed; mpmath through `nix shell --impure --expr "with import (builtins.getFlake \"nixpkgs\") {}; python3.withPackages (ps: [ps.mpmath])"`). On 1,850 exact inputs the new forward was within 1.43e-7 blocks of the reference and the old one was 616.5 blocks off at worst. On 112 near-line inputs the worst was 1.53e-7 blocks for both, the same on the old and new paths at 1e-3° to 1e-5° off. Below 1e-6° the new path was under 1e-9 blocks.
  - Exact inputs, the scratch JS twin of the three forwards on 4 worlds ((6656, 146), (6656, 31.25), (1536, 0), (13056, 200)): 0 misses after the fix (152 to 180 before). The worst cone point was 4e-14°.
  - Random inputs: 0 of 200,000 per world changed a bit (`node explore.js 1e-6`, the same scratch twin, checked bit for bit against `DTPetroffGuyou.blockOf` first).
- **Nothing else moves.** `DEEPTIME_WRITE_PARITY=1 cargo test -p deeptime-format parity_fixture` rewrote `projection_parity.json`. A JSON comparison with master's file finds every existing row identical: math 240, petroff 200 (inverse and forward), and per world 200 points and 200 `inverse` (`block_of`) rows. The file gains an `exact` section per world: 444 exact inputs at 2.5° steps (`diagonal_inputs`), read bit for bit by `ProjectionParityTest` and `tools/viewer/projection-check.js`. The inverse is not touched.
- **Tests** (new; all fail on master's forward, below):

The round trip must be under 1e-7 rad (worst 7.5e-9 rad, the inverse's), the q = 0 meridian must lie on x = −y to 1e-12, and the corners on the diamond's.

- **REV-2's site-15 mismatch** (the coordinator's follow-up). Neither the inspector's lat/lon nor the site's record is wrong, and the forward is not involved.

### 2026-10-20: Ice spikes 6 to 40 times the packs' own: no rarity is dropped; the frozen, driest land is 8 to 40 times the packs' and near-inland ground bypassed the flats rule; EF held mid-inland (BIO-161) and the census bounds the ice cap's ice spikes on steep ground and flats (BIO-162) (coordinator's task from Ben's report; agent worktree agent-afb2f6d841f45452e, branch worktree-agent-afb2f6d841f45452e from master db1844e6, masters bc2e5472, c83f445e, ccdced0b and 74a8768a merged in; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Ben's report.** "I've also noticed like 20x more ice spike biomes than I'd usually see, might be indicative of biome rarities being ignored." Play world bake be17a7cf (earthlike_quick_16k, supercontinent, seed 1).
- **The chain** (docs/science/biomes.md, "Ice spikes and the rare variants", with file and line): the bake's five vanilla-unit rasters (`bake/biomes.rs` `map`, `Placement::place`), the router's `deeptime:raster` reads and the world's climate mapping, `minecraft:multi_noise` with the pack's parameter list (nearest slot), `VolcanicBiomeSourceMixin` and the biome rules, then `IcePass`. No step weights by rarity: a biome's share is how often the baked inputs fall in its slots.
- **The cause.**
  - The frozen, driest cell (T0, H0, "the corner") is 10.7 % of land on the play world, 23.5 % on the 2026-10-20 master's supercontinent and 33.5 % on its scattered continents, against 1.28 % (MIC) and 0.83 % (vanilla) in the packs' own worlds: a colder planet (Köppen E 16.8 %, 29.2 %, 44.9 % of land against Earth's 12.8 %; not retuned) and the ice cap in the driest band on purpose (BIO-078).
  - Inside it, near-inland ground got past BIO-077's flats rule: Terralith 2.6.2 draws ice spikes on the corner's near-inland flats on both signs of weirdness (66 to 71 % of the flats against MIC's own 34.5 %), and vanilla's builder gives near-inland steep ground on positive weirdness (which EF's steep ground always has) the middle biome, ice spikes. 72 to 78 % of these planets' land is near-inland against 22 to 27 % in the packs' worlds.
- **Target** (coordinator's call): ice spikes as a share of the corner's flats (erosion E2 and up) at BIO-077's fifth, never above the pack's own; more cold, dry land rightly has more ice spikes.
- **The fix.** `placement.json` `classes.EF.continentalness {"min": 0.1}` (an existing key; the class clamp at band 4 and up): EF inland of the beach strip is mid-inland, out of both near-inland slots. Bake test `bake::biomes::tests::ef_land_is_held_mid_inland_off_terraliths_near_inland_ice_spikes`.
- **Before and after** (ice spikes, % of land with times the pack's own; of the corner's flats; of the ice cap), the game's pipeline emulated on the bakes (`ice_spikes.py emulate`, agreeing with the game's census on 98.5 % MIC and 99.3 % vanilla of the play world's land):

  - 2026-10-20 master, supercontinent, MIC: 6.03 (18.3x), 65.9 %, 25.4 % to 1.73 (5.3x), 19.0 %, 7.1 %; vanilla: 3.66 (10.3x), 6.4 %, 15.3 % to 0.84 (2.4x), 6.4 %, 3.4 %.
  - same, scattered continents, MIC: 12.98 (39.5x), 71.1 %, 38.2 % to 3.76 (11.4x), 20.7 %, 10.8 %; vanilla: 8.99 (25.3x), 34.5 %, 26.5 % to 6.57 (18.5x), 34.5 %, 19.3 %.
  - The GameTests' 4k planet has no ice cap to speak of (3 to 4 census columns), so nothing moves there.
  - After the fix MIC's ice cap draws ice spikes only from Terralith's mid-inland slot (erosion 0.05 to 0.33 after the mapping: 94 to 100 % of mid-inland E4) and the unclamped beach strip; vanilla's from the flats rule's positive branch (6.4 to 34.5 % of the flats: the rule's noise is not a fifth on every world) and a few valley columns.

The supercontinent baked with the fix (the before bake's own binary without the patch, `nm-super-fix`: the same 81,607 land columns) gives 1.84 % (5.6x) with MIC and 1.08 % (3.0x) with vanilla, flats 20.1 % and 6.8 %: the emulation ran 0.1 to 0.25 points of land low, because the bilinear resampling onto the world grid (`bake/project.rs`) leaves a ring of near-inland values between the unclamped beach strip and the first clamped cells (4 % of the ice cap), where Terralith's near-inland slot and vanilla's low-slice middle biome still draw ice spikes. ### 2026-10-20: The internal developer map, a separate mod (deeptime_devmap): the planet in block space and on a globe with the player, the other players, the seam, the poles, the edges and the cone points, a readout that matches F3, an operator's click-teleport and a HUD minimap; and a bug in Deep Time's Petroff forward projection found on the way (coordinator's task from Ben's request; agent worktree agent-a6dc06e49a5c3b213, branch worktree-agent-a6dc06e49a5c3b213 from master db1844e6; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Ben's request.** "Also, for dev purposes develop an internal use map mod that can show both the players location on a globe / on whatever projection is currently getting used by the world."
- **The coordinator's calls** (all undoable; built to them):
  - a separate mod, id `deeptime_devmap`, LGPL-3.0-or-later, a Gradle subproject `devmap/` beside `neoforge/` (`neoforge/settings.gradle` includes it), compiled against Deep Time (`compileOnly project(':')`) so it reuses Deep Time's projection and world-data code; never in Deep Time's jar or the MIC pack;
  - singleplayer and Ben's dedicated play server; the server sends the projection's parameters and one downsampled base image, and the channels are optional both ways;
  - a keybind opens the map; a block-space map and an orthographic globe with the same image, graticule and markers; a readout; Deep Time's own rendering, no second renderer; operator-only click-teleport landing at a safe height; a toggleable HUD minimap; "no Deep Time planet in this dimension" elsewhere;
  - correctness over looks: Deep Time's Java projection, JUnit round trips, the marker checked against F3 and the play world's geography;
  - opt-in deploy flags on the play scripts, no deploy.
- **What it is** (`devmap/src/main/java/.../devmap/`):
  - `model/`: `PlanetGeometry` (F3 latitude and longitude conventions, seam and edge distances, the poles' block images, the cone points, the nearest pole by block distance and by arc, a checked forward projection, below), `Graticule` (meridians and parallels swept through the projection and cut where Petroff-Guyou turns them back at an edge), `ViewTransform` (pan, zoom about the mouse, the x wrap), `MapFrame`, `BaseImage`, `ImageCodec`.
  - `net/`: four optional payloads (`MapInfoPayload`, `MapImagePayload` in 256 KiB deflated parts, `PlayersPayload` once a second, `TeleportPayload`); a client without the mod, or a server without it, connects as before.
  - `server/ServerMaps`: the base image is rendered once per dimension on a background thread from the world data's height and water through Deep Time's own elevation and water ramps (`Ramps`), 2048 pixels across the period (6.5 blocks a pixel on the play planet, 1850 KiB in 8 parts, 1.4 s), with a private 64 MiB tile cache. Teleport needs permission level 2; it lands on the highest motion-blocking block (leaves skipped) at the canonical point (x wrapped, z folded and kept 4 blocks inside the border inset; Lambert: short of the pole stop); a creative or spectator player is set flying so they stay there. Toroidal World's client then shows the copy of x nearest where the player was (9984.5 for -3327.5 after the seam place, its F3 "Unwrapped" line). Each teleport logs the surface block against the world data's H, water level and sea level (AGREE or DIFFER). A permission change re-sends the info on the next tick, so an op granted after login gets the teleport.
  - `client/`: `DevMapScreen` (Map, Globe, Centre (C), HUD map (H); Tab switches; drag pans or turns; the wheel zooms; right-click teleports), `HudMinimap` (top right, or bottom right while F3 is open; north up, 512 blocks across by default), `ClientConfig` (HUD on or off, its span and size), `ShotDriver` (the real-client check, below). The globe is Deep Time's `GlobeProjection.render` of a 1024-wide latitude/longitude picture built from the base image; the client's projection is `ClientPlanetState`, the same object as the F3 line. Without the dev map on the server: the graticule and markers on a plain background, no other players, no teleport.
- **Keys.** Comma opens the map, period toggles the HUD minimap. M is taken in MIC (Antique Atlas, Simple Voice Chat, Cobblemon). Both are rebindable under "Deep Time dev map" in Controls.
- **Found: Deep Time's Petroff forward projection is wrong on some exact inputs** (`worlddata/Petroff.forward`, and the Rust twin `deeptime_format::petroff::forward`, same bits). On the square's diagonals between its centre and the 67.5° vertex, `up` is rounding noise and the branch on `up * rp` picks an arbitrary `alphap`. On the play planet (b 6656, λc 146°) `blockOf` misses 254 of 4,318 exact diagonal inputs by more than 1e-5°: latitude exactly 0 at simulation longitudes about 127..168° and 304..338° lands up to 75 blocks off the equator (1.6°), and the cone points themselves come back 616 blocks along the edge ((45° N, 236°) to (616, -3328), which is 53.13° N). The inverse (`latLon`, what F3 and the terrain use) is right. The bake calls `block_of`/`point_of_unit` (`bake/project.rs`), so an exact diagonal input there would land wrong. Not fixed here (Deep Time's projection, three twins and the parity fixtures); the dev map works around it with `PlanetGeometry.blockOf`, which checks each forward result by the inverse and retries inputs nudged by 1e-9°, 1e-7° and 1e-5° when it misses by more than 1e-5°.
- **Tests** (`devmap/src/test`, 18): block to lat/lon to block on Petroff-Guyou (a 218 x 139 grid, worst under 1e-4 blocks) and Lambert, lat/lon to block to lat/lon on both (worst under 1e-5°), points outside the domain fold back, the seam and the wrap, the poles and the cone points against the play manifest, the nearest pole, the F3 longitude conventions, the checked forward on the exact diagonals, the view transform, the image codec, the base image's sampling, the globe picture against the block image, and the graticule on its latitude or longitude with no jumps.
- **Gates** (VM): `cd neoforge && ./gradlew build test` green: 370 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped (Deep Time) and 18, 0 failures (dev map). No Rust changed.
- **Real-client check** (`tools/client/devmap-shots.sh`, new: a server job of the admission tool with this checkout's Deep Time and dev map jars and Toroidal World on a copy of the play world's data, keyframes linked through `allowed_symlinks.txt`; a portablemc client on the job's Xvfb with llvmpipe; `-Ddeeptime_devmap.shots=true` drives it). The player is opped over RCON, right-clicks the map at three places, and at each the driver checks the readout's latitude and longitude against Deep Time's F3 line, reads the map marker and the globe marker (turned 0° and 35°) back through the view and the projection's inverse, and takes the HUD (F3 on), the map and the globe. Result: 10 shots, 0 failed checks, 3 teleports, 3 AGREE:
  - spawn (-9.5, 12.5): 0.178° S 124.310° W, F3 the same; map marker 0.0 blocks off, globe 1e-10 and 1e-10; grass at y 78, world data H 77.2, land;
  - beside the seam (6630.5, 0.5), 26 blocks from x = 6656: 0.007° S 55.168° E, F3 the same; markers 0.0, 7e-9, 2e-10; water at 63, H -21.2, sea;
  - beside the north pole (-3327.5, -3267.5), 61 blocks from the pole by block distance (1.975° of arc, 92 blocks, 27 km): 88.025° N 146.207° E, F3 the same; markers 0.0, 3e-9, 4e-9; water at 63, H -26.4, sea.
  The PNGs are in review/out/devmap-shots/ (not committed; index.html is a contact sheet with the driver's and the server's lines). A first walk passed the same checks; after looking at it the HUD button's label was made to fit, the seam labels moved to the top of the view (they sat under the player's name), the readout shows x wrapped as TW's F3 XYZ line does (the raw x beside it), and a teleported creative player flies (that walk sank through 84 blocks of sea). The second walk, on the gate's jar, is the one above. Its first walk also showed the harness had read the launcher's output, which stops when FML hands logging to log4j: it reads the game's latest.log now and fails without the driver's "done after" line.
- **Deploy** (not done): `play-stage.sh --devmap` (and `--extra-mod JAR`, repeatable) put the dev map jar in the play folder's mods; `--mods-only --hash H` adds it to an existing play folder (then restart deeptime-play). `play-client-stage.sh --devmap` takes the play folder's jar into the client stage, `--mods-only` for an existing stage; `play-client-apply.py --devmap` copies the play folder's jar into Ben's instance after the mods mirror (`--extra-mod JAR` for a local jar). Without the flags nothing changes, and a plain apply removes the jar again.
- **Tooling.** `tools/remote/mac.sh` no longer deletes `devmap/build/` on every sync.
- **Next.** The coordinator merges; a fix for `Petroff.forward` at `up` near 0 (Java, Rust and the pages' twin, with the parity fixtures) is its own task.

### 2026-10-20: Sea-floor spikes: the tail was not realistic (2 to 9 times the share of deep sea floor steeper than 20 degrees of Earth's roughest 15-degree tiles), from the plate model's walls with nothing relaxing them under the sea; the sea floor now fails to its own 15 degrees in the young landscape (YNG-022, YNG-023) and the amplifier (AMP-074); most of the on-screen look is the 8.4x vertical scale, Ben's (coordinator's task from Ben's report; agent worktree agent-a178044f2a1370861, branch worktree-agent-a178044f2a1370861 from master db1844e6, masters 8f4408a8 and c83f445e merged in; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Ben's report.** The sea bed looks "very 'spiky' / like a sin wave. If this is realistic, great. If not, make sure it gets fixed."
- **Verdict.** Measured in real metres (each block's own size on the Petroff-Guyou map, `deeptime heightmap --scale`), the play world's deep sea floor (more than 210 m down) has an Earth-like body (median 2.0 degrees, 90th percentile 6.7) and a tail Earth does not: steeper than 20 / 30 degrees on 2.3 / 0.75 % of it, against 0.26 to 1.32 / 0.029 to 0.15 % in ETOPO 2022's five rough 15 arc-second tiles and 0.088 / 0.0036 % over the whole ocean at 60 arc-seconds; p99.9 40.8 degrees against 24.6 to 31.8. Earth's grids are a lower bound (80 % predicted from gravity); multibeam on the Kermadec trench gives single scarps of 10 to 40 degrees, 150 to 1,200 m high, but not 2 to 5 km walls. The look on screen is mostly the vertical scale (35 m up, about 296 m across: 6.8 degrees real is 45 on screen): Earth's rough tiles drawn this way are steeper than 45 degrees on 4.0 to 16.5 % of their area, the play world on 11.6 %, and that does not change with the fix.
- **Root cause (bake, not play time).** The detail noise is 7.8 m of the 195 m RMS of the high-passed terrain. The walls are already in the plate model's elevation (L1, 4.8 km: 2.0 / 0.68 % steeper than 20 / 30 degrees; one-sample trenches toward 10 km, interleaved crust strips 2 to 5 km tall over 5 to 9 km), and nothing relaxed them under the sea: marine diffusion stops at the wave base, the submarine slope failure (ERO-168) moved sediment only, and the amplifier's thermal pass held the sea floor at the land's 31 degrees (AMP-034). The L2-to-L3 interpolation draws each step as an S over two or three cells: the "sine wave".
- **What changed.**
  - `surface/young.rs`: `fail_sea_floor` runs `marine::slope_failure` on every open-sea L2 cell before the young steps, with rock as well as sediment, to `young.sea_floor_slope_deg` 15 (YNG-022), 300 iterations (YNG-023); `sea_floor_failed_km3` in `young_final`.
  - `surface/amplify.rs`, `amplify/kernels.rs` (`tmult_fill`): the thermal pass holds sea cells at `amplify.submarine_slope` 0.268 (tan 15 degrees, AMP-074), with the same noise and drama; a sea cell under more than 60 m of glacier ice (a fjord) keeps the land's slope. AMP-034's row says so.
  - `deeptime heightmap --scale`: each sample's ground metres east-west and north-south, latitude and longitude (real slopes on a Petroff-Guyou world).
  - Tests: `surface::young::tests::the_plate_model_sea_floor_fails_to_its_critical_slope` (its world is over 50 degrees before the failure runs, at most 15 degrees + 3 % after, matter kept, land untouched, the trench still deeper than 5.5 km) and `surface::amplify::tests::the_sea_floor_keeps_its_own_critical_slope` (the multiplier cell by cell, the fjord exception, 700 m knolls one L2 cell across: 22 degrees against 36 at the land's angle).
  - Tools: `tools/review/seafloor/` (survey.py, earth_stats.py, earth.sh, stages.py, relax.py, calib.sh, compare.py, boxes.sh, closeup.py).
  - Science: `docs/science/young-landscape-and-amplifier.md` "Sea-floor walls"; ledger YNG-022 and AMP-074 (`calibrated`), YNG-023 (`game-choice`), AMP-034; claims.md recounted; bibliography: StewartJamieson2018, GoffSmithMarks2004, Sandwell2022, WesselSandwellKim2010, BeckerSandwell2008 (abstract), GoffJordan1988, Goff1991, SmithJordan1988, Wessel2001 (abstracts), Smith1988 (not read; its ratio from memory).
- **Calibration** on the play world's own planet (run-s1: earthlike_quick_16k, supercontinent, 1000 Myr, default seed, master of the morning; its young and amplify stages rerun from the deposits checkpoint with the fix off bake the play world's terrain to the block), λc pinned at 146 (left free it moved to 193.25 or 13.5 when a few coastal cells changed). Deep sea floor at 2 blocks (in brackets 6), steeper than 20 / 30 degrees: off 2.29 (1.67) / 0.75 (0.40) %; young step only 1.10 (0.66) / 0.21 (0.079) %; amplifier step only 1.07 (0.78) / 0.16 (0.10) % (each alone leaves the 30-degree share above Earth's range); 10 degrees 0.25 (0.16) / 0.044 (0.020) %; **15 degrees 0.50 (0.35) / 0.096 (0.053) %**; 20 degrees 1.42 (0.86) / 0.16 (0.096) %. p99.9 40.8 to 29.7 degrees; tile relief RMS p99 618 to 391 m (Earth's rough tiles 244 to 331). The rule (coordinator's call): the steepest slope that puts both shares inside Earth's rough range; 15 does, 20 is just past its top.
- **What else moved** (15 against off, `compare.py`): mean sea depth 2,870 m both; shelf 7.63 to 7.53 % of the sea; hadal 1.60 to 1.36 % (Earth about 0.22 %: StewartJamieson2018's "over 800,000 km²" over an ocean of about 361 million km², from memory); deepest 9,944 to 9,889 m; 0.08 % of samples land to sea, 0.04 % sea to land; land changed by more than 2 blocks on 2.6 % of its samples, 94 % of them within 64 blocks of the sea, none beyond 256; the glacial pass carved 2.7 % more volume over 15 % more cells (not traced); the share steeper than 45 degrees on screen 11.6 to 12.3 %.
- **Today's planet.** A fresh earthlike_quick_16k run (supercontinent, 1000 Myr, default seed) on this branch merged with master c83f445e (continents keep their land), run-m1, its young and amplify stages again with the fix off and at 15 degrees, λc pinned at the 113.25 its bake chose: steeper than 20 / 30 degrees off 1.37 (0.83) / 0.37 (0.15) %, fixed 0.36 (0.21) / 0.061 (0.029) %; p99.9 36.2 to 26.9 degrees; tile relief RMS p99 495 to 341 m. The new plate model's tail is smaller than the play world's, but its 30-degree share is still 2.5 times the top of Earth's rough range; fixed, both shares sit in the lower half. Sea 76 % of the planet, hadal 0.51 to 0.42 % of the sea, on screen steeper than 45 degrees 7.6 to 8.1 %. **The deepest point falls from 9,112 to 7,833 m** (55 m on run-s1): the failure gives 1.3 km of the deepest trench's floor to its walls; Earth's deepest is about 10.9 km (from memory).
- **Commands** (all on the VM; scripts in `tools/review/seafloor/`): `deeptime run --preset earthlike_quick_16k --start supercontinent --length-myr 1000 --checkpoints --threads 8` (run-s1); `calib.sh <tag> <deg> <sub> [λc [run [binary]]]` (young and amplify again, bake, `heightmap --scale --step 2` over the whole world, `survey.py --coarsen 1` and `3`); `earth.sh` (ETOPO 2022 60 and 15 arc-second grids, downloaded by hand into their own folders, `earth_stats.py`); `deeptime dump-fields` and `stages.py` (the stage table); `relax.py` (the iteration count); `compare.py` (heightmap differences); `boxes.sh` and `closeup.py` (the 384-block renders). Study folder `/data/ban/deeptime-runs/seafloor/` (delete when this lands).
- **Gates** (VM): on the merge of master c83f445e (713f11e9; no Rust changed after it): `cargo fmt --all --check` ok; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test --workspace` 1,008 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored (before the merge, 1,002); `cargo deny check licenses bans` ok; `./gradlew build test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 400 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped. No GameTests (the coordinator's batch).
- **Review page** (private): https://spacesheep.dev/@benmac/deeptime-seafloor-spikes (the before tables, the stage table, the calibration against Earth, the play world's close-up C and boxes P, Q, R and S before and after).
- **Coordinator's calls (undoable).** 15 degrees for both steps by the rule above; the failure on L2 in the young stage (the only grid where a 2 to 5 km step's 8 to 19 km ramp fits) plus the amplifier's own slope, rather than a change in the plate model; 300 iterations; the fjord exception at the glaciers' `min_ice_m`; the planet held to Earth's rough tiles rather than to the whole ocean (a lower bound, and a 4.8 km plate grid draws trenches and fracture zones more often than abyssal plains); λc pinned in the calibration runs only.
- **Not checked.** The half-turn edge rows (box S keeps steep walls; the map is most anisotropic there and the survey takes one size per sample); the square shelf steps along L1 cells (boxes P and Q, both runs); the floating stone shelf and contour terraces; the Lambert grid's cos φ anisotropy in the failure; carbonate platform walls; why the glacial pass carves more.
- **For Ben.** The vertical scale (35 m a block, about 8.4x) is most of the "spiky" look and is his. The plate model draws trenches one sample wide and a hadal area about six times Earth's share: a source fix belongs to the plates and ocean-crust work (agent a8d769d9446780ad7's area); this fix relaxes what reaches the young landscape, and on today's planet costs the deepest trench 1.3 km (9.1 to 7.8 km). A wider trench at the source would keep its depth.

### 2026-10-20: Dirt walls around water: the router's near-surface cave entrances opened dry pits beside the water and the water pass built every bank and bed up from their floors in dirt; a cave shield beside water (HYD-078) and soil over rock in the fills (HYD-079) (coordinator's task from Ben's play-world screenshots; agent worktree agent-ae0943ce7b7cc6d77, branch worktree-agent-ae0943ce7b7cc6d77 from master b438d47a; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Ben's report.** Play world (bake be17a7cf, run 1a1578fa5d2, earthlike_quick_16k, supercontinent, seed 1), screenshots at x -343 z 268 and x -393 z 225, then a fresh singleplayer world: "it seems generally bodies of water just have these dirt walls around them, extremely unprofessional". Copies of the region files, never the server's folder: `/data/ban/deeptime-runs/ben-shots/world`; views in `/data/ban/deeptime-runs/ben-shots/out/` (`build/bs/look1.sh`, `look2.sh`, `cols.sh`).
- **The cause (ours).**
  - `planet.json`'s router: `range_choice(terrain final < 1.5625, min(terrain, ratio · 5 · entrances))` reaches about 12.5 blocks under H at k = 8, and its cave entrances open pits to the sky.
  - The vanilla aquifer floods a pit only when a sampled preliminary surface + 8 is under sea level (the largest multiple of 8 strictly below H, so H at most 56), at its grid points up to a cell away. Beside a river at H 60 to 70 the pits stay dry.
  - `WaterBodies` then filled the RIVER channel, raised and sealed the BANK and laid the SEA bed from the pit floor up, all in dirt: the 10 to 27 block dirt walls, and the floating sea at (-393, 257..290).
  - Every water GameTest ran on `planet_nocaves`, so none saw it.
- **The fix.**
  - `deeptime:water_shield` (`WaterShieldDensity`, `WaterCaveShield`): 1 within 8 blocks of the water's edge, smoothstep to 0 at 16. Edges: a river's `Rivers.edgeDistance` (centreline distance minus the half-width), a wet `water_level` cell minus the shore reach 4, an `elevation` cell with E − A at most the top minus SEA_REACH 8.5 (a sea column lies within 4√2 + 2√2 of one). The sea counts fully where the column's ground H is at least top − 8 and not at all under top − 14, so the deep sea floor keeps vanilla's cave mouths. Cells that cannot be sea (E − 255/16 over the top) are skipped.
  - `planet.json`'s band argument is now `ratio · 5 · entrances + 16 · flat_cache(water_shield)`: at shield 1 the band equals terrain and the ground stays at H. Caves under the band and the carvers are unchanged.
  - `WaterBodies`' fills (RIVER fill and plug, LAKE plug, BANK raise and seal): 3 blocks of soil (a channel's sand or gravel) at the top, then the column's own rock (the first block under the ground within 16 that is not open, skin or fluid, else stone). The SEA bed is unchanged.
  - Ledger HYD-078, HYD-079 (game-choice), HYD-074 updated; `docs/science/rivers-and-lakes.md`; decisions log 2026-10-20.
- **Tests.** JUnit `WaterCaveShieldTest` (planet4k): every river, lake and shallow-sea column and its ring of 7 has shield 1 (102 river, 110 lake, 9,366 shallow sea columns, 140,024 shore columns checked); 560 samples: 410 unshielded, 150 shielded (26.8 %), none without a water column within 26 blocks; 9.96 µs a column, 0.25 ms a chunk. GameTest `WaterShoreGameTests.shoresHaveNoDirtWalls` on `test_planet_caves` (the real router with caves): beside shielded water at most 1 % pits (ground more than 3 under the expected top, or air within 3 under it) and no exposed dirt face over 10 blocks, on at least 100 water columns. Not run here (the coordinator's batch).
- **Gates** (VM): `./gradlew build test` green, 370 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped. No Rust changed (fmt, clippy, cargo test and the parity fixtures not touched).
- **Validation on Ben's seed.** A preview of the screenshots' box (x -432..-320, z 200..312, 12,544 columns, all full) with this branch's jar on the play world's data and seed (`build/bs/fix.sh`: `preview.py run --profile standalone --size 13312 --world-data /data/ban/deeptime-runs/ben-shots/wd --box -432,200,-320,312 --seed 54324317120568257 --keep-world`), read against the play copy by `build/bs/lookfix.sh`, `wc.sh` and `walls.py` (in this worktree's gitignored build/; deeptime-inspect heights, compare, section, column, water-check):
  - dry columns within 7 blocks of water whose top is more than 3 blocks under that water: 1,141 of 2,271 (50.2 %) on the play world, 10 (0.44 %) fixed; the 10 sit at the world data's own low ground (the generated top at H);
  - columns that compare excludes as pits: 3,886 to 890; within 1 block of H: 0.9982 to 0.9994 of the compared;
  - the same 345 water columns; water-check counts no floating water, leaks or steps on either side (it looks for water over air, and the play world's perched sea rests on one dirt block);
  - (-393, 270): water on one dirt block over 15 blocks of air on the play world, water on sand, sand, then stone fixed; sections `build/bs/out-play/sec/` against `build/bs/out-fix/sec/` (x -393, z 268: the 15-block dirt wall and the slot canyon are gone).
- **Also from the screenshots.**
  - The straight channel: D8 routing, the open follow-up "Rivers and valleys: route by a direction not bound to eight" (grid-artifact audit, "What is left" (2); P1-23).
  - Staircase slopes and terraced pits: the voxelised isosurfaces of the same noise caves; beside water the shield removes them, elsewhere they are vanilla's caves.
- **Tooling gap.** `preview.py --install` runs `install.sh --size <spec size>`, and install.sh takes only 16384 or 32768, so a 13312 preview needs `install.sh standalone --size 16384` first and then preview.py without `--install` (`build/bs/fix.sh`).
- **Next.** The coordinator merges and runs the GameTest batch, which now includes `shoresHaveNoDirtWalls`. Only newly generated chunks change: Ben's play world keeps its walls where chunks exist (a new world, or deleting the affected regions, shows the fix).

### 2026-10-19: GPU compute phase 3: the diffusion solve's multigrid V-cycle and the submarine slope failure run on the GPU; the slope failure 3.1 times faster per 100 Myr on the laptop's Radeon (4.8 times over 1000 Myr, two pairs), the solve 1.2 times per 100 Myr and even over 1000; the cycle gives the CPU's heights to the bit on lavapipe; land is higher on the GPU, settled (13 of 15 seeds, +0.007 of the area), and +0.005 above three physically null CPU controls, which lean up less (coordinator's Phase 3 task; agent worktree agent-a1265f3344b19b0c1, branch `gpu-phase3` from master 3e7edd49, masters be17a7cf and c88c2eb5 merged in; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Design note:** `docs/design/gpu-compute.md` sections 15 (the cycle) and 16 (the slope failure), section 10's Phase 3 measurements, section 4's memory, section 12's order (items 2 and 3 ported). Science: `docs/science/erosion-and-sediment.md` "On a GPU", and the "where" of ERO-169 and ERO-183 name the GPU files. No law, constant or threshold changed, so no ledger value moved.
- **What changed.**
  - `surface/diffusion/multigrid/gpu.rs` (new): the V-cycle on the device (the smoother, the residual, the restriction and the prolongation as WGSL kernels in the CPU cycle's order of operations, all levels in one submission); `multigrid.rs` picks the preconditioner per solve (`Pre::Cpu(Hierarchy)` or `Pre::Device(Box<DeviceCycle>)`), and the conjugate gradients with their f64 vectors and sums stay on the CPU, sending the residual up and reading the correction back each iteration. The device's buffers live in the session slot (`Ambient::kept`) and are rebuilt when a grid of another size comes.
  - `surface/marine/gpu.rs` (new): the slope failure as two kernels a pass (SHARE: each wet cell with sediment works out its give over the lower wet neighbours beyond the critical drop and the scale that keeps it within its sediment; CHANGE: each cell gathers its gains and losses), all 40 passes in one submission and one read-back; heights carried as `base + acc` in f32. `marine.rs` dispatches to it and keeps the CPU's sparse worklist as the fallback and the reference.
  - `compute.rs`: `device(mode, log, kernel)` and `ambient_device(kernel)` take the kernel's name; `DEEPTIME_GPU_KERNELS` (comma list of prefixes, read once a process) keeps any kernel group on the CPU, which the bisection below used. `deeptime-gpu`: `Gpu::readback` and `Gpu::submit_and_read`. Both ports run at `--compute auto` from 2^17 cells (`DEVICE_MIN_CELLS`), so on L1 and in the young stage's L2 steps.
  - Tests: `the_gpu_cycle_matches_the_cpu_cycle` (z and the sum of r times z equal to the bit in all 21 cycles on lavapipe), `the_gpu_cycle_solve_meets_its_tolerance_and_keeps_the_mass` (all 30 solves equal to the bit, error at most 0.055 of the bound), `the_gpu_slope_failure_matches_the_cpu` (40 passes: heights within 4.2e-4 m, sediment 1.5e-3 m, moved 4.1e-8 relative, matter 4.4e-3 m-cells; 400 passes 3.6e-3 m, 9.3e-3 m, 3.0e-7, 6.1e-2; grids one and two cells wide move nothing on either path).
  - The early stop of the slope failure was **not** taken: P1-19 found that no tolerance stops a call early, and on the device a stop test costs a read-back a pass.
- **Same state on both, full 16k, 100 Myr, seed 1** (VM, lavapipe; a temporary harness, not committed, ran every surface step's solve and slope failure twice from the same state). The solve, 50 solves on L1: the same heights to the bit in every cell, 17.64 iterations a solve on both. The slope failure, 50 calls: metres moved 8.230063e8 on both (1.5e-8 relative), heights device less CPU -1.0e-7 to +1.3e-8 m per call on average, RMS at most 2.5e-5 m, largest 1.5e-3 m, no cell land on one path and sea on the other; the device's f32 matter round-off is -1.52 m-cells over the 50 calls (1e-6 m over L1).
- **Whole histories, the land lean** (VM, lavapipe, 8 threads; `deeptime stage volcanoes --preset earthlike_full_16k --start scattered_continents --length-myr 100 --threads 8 --set seed=N --compute cpu|gpu`, seeds 6 to 15). Land, the area above the sea, each world less the CPU's: every kernel on the GPU up in 9, down in 1, +0.0069 (sign p 0.021); `DEEPTIME_GPU_KERNELS=surface:` 7 / 2 / 1, +0.0060; `plates:` 6 / 4, +0.0053; `climate:` 9 / 0 / 1, +0.0100. With Phase 2's seeds 1 to 5: higher on the GPU in 13 of 15, equal in 1, lower in 1 (p 0.002), +0.007, a quarter of the spread between seeds. **Three CPU controls** (`--compute cpu`, changes that do nothing physical): the submarine critical slope 1e-10 relative higher (`--set surface.submarine_slope_deg=2.50000000025`): 7 / 2 / 1, +0.0034; 1e-10 lower: 4 / 5 / 1, -0.0007; f32-sized changes on every cell every step (`surface.kd_land_m2_yr`, `surface.kd_marine_m2_yr`, `surface.k_spl` and `climate.diffusivity_w_m2_k` each 1e-7 relative higher): 8 / 2, +0.0031. Pooled 19 up, 9 down, 2 equal, +0.0019 (p 0.09). The GPU sets sit +0.005 above the controls (labels shuffled within seed: one-sided p 0.0014). The worlds that move further from the CPU's lean further (mean distance 0.007 to 0.010 for the GPU sets, 0.003 to 0.006 for the controls), so part of the lean is the model's answer to any perturbation; whether the rest is the GPU's larger perturbation or a small bias of the kernels these seeds do not tell (against the f32-sized control alone +0.004, one-sided p 0.06). No kernel leans on the same state. In practice: about 0.7 % of the planet's area more land than the CPU's world of the same seed (0.5 % more than the controls'), against 2.4 % between seeds. ### 2026-10-20: Distant Horizons far terrain to multiplayer clients: DH 3.3.1 switches its generator off on every client that has Chunky installed, so Ben's client never asked the play server for a section; Deep Time now lifts that override on a planet (coordinator's task; agent worktree agent-aedfeb2853b0d9bb3, branch worktree-agent-aedfeb2853b0d9bb3 from master b438d47a; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **The cause** (DH 3.3.1 decompiled with CFR on the VM, `libs/decomp/`).
  - `AbstractModInitializer.logIncompatibilityWarnings()` runs from `onInitializeClient()` only. When `org.popcraft.chunky.api.ChunkyAPI` loads, it logs "Partially Incompatible Distant Horizons mod detected: [Chunky]" and sets `generatorPlan = DISABLED` (and `disableUnchangedChunkCheck = true`) on the API override layer.
  - `ConfigEntry.get()` prefers the API value to the file's, so the client's `DistantHorizons.toml` and its config screen still say SURFACE_THEN_CHUNKS.
  - `SessionConfig`'s rule gives DISABLED when either side is DISABLED. `DhClientLevel.shouldDoWorldGen` is then false, `LodRequestModule` never starts its queue (no "Set world gen queue for level" in the log), and nothing is requested. Singleplayer is the same: the integrated server reads the same config.
  - Chunky is `side = "both"` in the pack (`mic/pack/mods/chunky.pw.toml`), so Ben's client has it (`Chunky-NeoForge-1.4.23.jar`). His client's latest.log has the Chunky line (05:05:43) and no "Set world gen queue"; his F3 showed "World Gen/Import Tasks: 0".
  - The 2026-10-03 client check had Chunky on its client too (the set's jars), which is why its client asked for nothing.
  - No other pack mod sets `generatorPlan` or `readOnly` (VM jar scan, client-only jars included). The server is not the cause: its plan is SURFACE_THEN_CHUNKS and a client without Chunky gets far terrain from the same set (run D).
  - DH 3.3.3 (Modrinth `9w34y8ai`, 2026-09-29; changelog "Only disable DH world gen when Chunky world gen is active") replaced the rule: `AbstractChunkyAccessor` sets DISABLED only while Chunky's generation-progress events arrive and clears it 2 s after. So no upstream report is needed; the draft was dropped.
- **The fix.**
  - `compat/dh/DhGenerationGate` (plain Java, tested) and `client/DhGenerationClient` (checked once a second on the client tick). On a Deep Time planet, with Chunky installed and DH 3.3.2 or older, it clears the DISABLED from the API layer, so the player's own file decides. Off the planet it puts the value back.
  - Left alone and logged: an override set again after the lift, a DISABLED without Chunky (another mod's), the player's own DISABLED, and DH 3.3.3's while-Chunky-runs override. `-Ddeeptime.dhGenerationGate=false` switches the gate off (the control).
  - `DhApiBinding.generationEnabled()` reaches `DhApi.Delayed.configs.worldGenerator().enableDistantWorldGeneration()` by name.
  - `tools/client/dh-client-check.sh` gained:
    - `DHCC_CLIENT_JVM_ARGS` and `DHCC_CLIENT_DROP`;
    - the client log's DH facts (the Chunky line, the gate's line, "Set world gen queue");
    - empty client and server DH databases on every run (below).
- **Measured** (`tools/client/dh-client-check.sh dh` on the VM; the `dh` set on synth wrap-test, C = 16384; DH 3.3.1 on both sides; Chunky on the server in every run):
  - A, gate on, Chunky on the client: "Set world gen queue" once; 333 sections asked at the spawn and 1,580 beside the seam; 1,627 far sections in the client's database (west of the seam 336, east 358). PASS.
  - C (the control), gate off, Chunky on the client: the Chunky line, no "Set world gen queue", 0 sections asked at either place. FAIL.
  - D, gate off, Chunky removed from the client: "Set world gen queue" once; 1,907 and 5,326 asked. PASS. A client without Chunky joins a server that has it (Chunky registers no network payload).
  - C's and D's database counts are void (44,043 sections in both). The client kept A's database, and C's client built new rows from it between 07:29 and 07:32. Its only traffic was sync-on-login for sections it already held, and the server's generator ran 0 times. Now each run starts with an empty client database (fd9d092b).
  - Reruns on the head's jar (2c46153f code), each with an empty client database:
    - C2, gate off: the Chunky line, no "Set world gen queue", 0 sections asked, 0 sections in the client's database. The control: a client that holds nothing gets nothing, even from a server whose database is full.
    - A2, gate on: the gate's line at the join (08:23:45, 5 s after DH bound), "Set world gen queue" once, 24,126 far sections in the client's database (3,916 and 3,970 in the 2,048 blocks either side of the seam).
    - A2's verdict was FAIL only because the server's generator ran 5 times. The set's world is linked into every run, so the server answered from its own DH database, which the earlier runs had filled. The check now clears that database too (a4f69890).
    - A3, gate on, both databases empty (a4f69890 check, head's jar): the gate's line, "Set world gen queue" once; 804 sections asked at the spawn and 1,508 beside the seam; 2,462 far sections in the client's database (812 west of the seam, 902 east). PASS.

  - The default world type: `mixin.client.CreateWorldScreenMixin` (`@ModifyArg` on `openFresh`'s `setScreen`, `@Inject` at the head of `onCreate`), `CreateWorldScreenInvoker`, `screen.CreateWorldFlow`. The client setting `defaultWorldType` (on) turns it off; the vanilla types stay in the World tab; without the natives the game's own default stays.
  - Create on a Deep Time world without world data opens `PlanetEditorScreen.generate(parent)`, which starts the run at once with `EditorModel`'s defaults (earthlike_quick 16k, supercontinent, 1,000 Myr, 4 GiB). Play is `accept()` and then the real `onCreate`.
  - The generation page: `screen.GenerationPage` and `screen.PanelList` replace RunPage and EventTicker. The plain-Java models: `model.GenerationStatus` (state, sentence, fraction, time left), `model.Phrase` (one time convention), `model.Milestones` (time windows, grouped and counted rows), `model.Legend` (every ramp in ramps.json, via `Ramps.names`). Details/F3 holds the developer's line.
  - Customize: `screen.CustomizePage` replaces SetupPage; `model.CustomizeTopics` sorts `EditorFields` (the workbench's editor_fields.json, 281 settings) into Planet, Plates, Climate, Surface, Rocks and Advanced; `EditorModel.edited`, `editCount`, `resetField`, `presetText`, `resetAll` and the start/length/cap edits and resets.
  - `ScreenshotDriver` walks the new flow (Create World fresh and on Deep Time, the four Customize topics, the generation page live with its tabs, details, layers and globe, done, the epoch, review, Play into the world).
  - `tools/client/vm-client.sh`: `--gui-scale`, `--mods`, and the GLX fix below.
- **A trap: "GLX: No GLXFBConfigs returned" on the VM's Xvfb.** vm-client.sh took Mesa from the registry's nixpkgs (26.2.4) while the client's JDK and the libraries the JVM had already loaded by soname (libstdc++, zlib, ...) come from the flake's pinned nixpkgs. Mesa's driver then failed to load inside the JVM, GLFW found no FBConfigs, and `glxinfo` on the same display worked. Fix: resolve mesa, libglvnd, xorg-server and pulseaudio with `nix build --inputs-from "$REPO" nixpkgs#<pkg>`, and give Xvfb `LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH` too (nixpkgs' xorg-server carries no DRI drivers). `tools/client/dh-client-check.sh` has the same registry pattern and was not changed.
- **Gates (test VM).** `cd neoforge && ./gradlew build test` (in a separate build directory, `-I` an init script setting `build/gate`, so a queued walk keeps its classes): BUILD SUCCESSFUL, `junit-summary.py` tests=387 failures=0 errors=0 skipped=2 (CustomizeTopicsTest 5, EditorModelTest 18, MilestonesTest 3, LegendTest 5, PhraseTest 5, ScreenSourcesTest 2), on c324d3f1 and again on 8b39e9f8 after the walk fixes. No Rust change, no GameTest run (the coordinator's batch).
- **Walks (test VM, `tools/client/vm-client.sh --prop length=300`, `ScreenshotDriver`).** Shots in review/out/create-world-ux/ (not committed):
  - before-2000x1500 and before-1920x1080: the VM's older build ("World Type: Default", the developer's line, one row per event).
  - after-2000x1500 (GUI scale 3, with the guidance pass; 26 PNGs, on 8b39e9f8) and after-1920x1080 (GUI scale auto, 4; 24 PNGs, on e5c90929). Both: the fresh type is `deeptime:planet`; Create is blocked (NOT_SIMULATED) and the generation page opens with the run started; Cancel stops it and its staging folder goes; Create again; the 300 Myr run took about 3 min; Play goes into the world (`GeologicChunkGenerator`). The guidance pass (natives missing) keeps `minecraft:normal` and shows the panel.
  - MIC (`--mods mic`: the 157 jars in /data/ban/mic/mods/deep-time/smoke/mic/server/mods, refreshed 2026-10-19; 1920x1080, `--no-create`): after-mic-1920x1080, 24 PNGs. The default holds with the pack: the fresh type is `deeptime:planet` (another mod's "World Shape: Normal" sits under it), Create opens the generation page, the run finishes and the review binds it. The first try stopped at Distant Horizons' "update available" screen over the title screen; `vm-client.sh` now turns DH's updater off as `dh-client-check.sh` does, and the driver closes any other mod's screen it finds there (and logs which).

### 2026-10-20: Mountains eat the world: the continents kept their area but drowned (land 0.30 to 0.16 to 0.18 in 1000 Myr, the dry share of the continental crust 0.71 to 0.32 to 0.39); a lower-crustal flow (PLT-300, PLT-301) and a settling of every continental column to its isostatic height on the mantle's 4 kyr (ISO-078) hold the land at 0.31 and the dry share at 0.66; the archipelago shape remains (coast p50 130 to 170 km against Earth's 433)
- **The ask.** Ben, earthlike_quick_16k, supercontinent, 1000 Myr: "mountains will 'eat' the world and delete most of the continents and leave things as a stringy mess of 'islands.'"
- **The budget** (`DEEPTIME_CRUST_BUDGET=1`, `plates/crust_budget.rs`, PLT-302; `DEEPTIME_CRUST_BUDGET_MAPS=<dir>` writes the visible samples; read with `tools/review/continent-budget.py`): the stocks every 50 Myr booked to the plate step's processes. Measurement only (test `the_crust_budget_changes_nothing`).
  - The continental area holds (0.42 at the start, 0.39 to 0.47 at the end); the land and the freeboard go. Every thickness band stands 1.1 to 1.9 km under its Airy height.
  - The cause, on master c88c2eb5: nothing returns a column to its isostatic height (`collapse::toward`, collapse.rs:205, and every process's own height line); arcs turn continental "whatever its height" at the ocean's line (`finish_samples`, mod.rs:1076: 0.58 of the planet over a run at -3,219 m on 19.6 km of crust); and thickened crust keeps its root, since the collapse releases only quiet crust (collapse.rs:241 to 252) into room thinner than normal (collapse.rs:328 to 351): 4.1 of 33 km³ a year moves.
  - Earth: 0.41 continental, 0.71 of it dry (Cogley 1984, HYP-012); coast p50 433 km (HYP-035, new, `tools/review/earth-coast.py` on SRTM15+ 15', at the quick presets' 100,000 points).
- **The fix.**
  - `plates/flow.rs` (PLT-300, PLT-301): continental crust thicker than 50 km diffuses its thickness into the crust around it on its plate, K = K0 (h/15 km)^3, h = T - 50 km capped at 30 km, K0 `crust_channel_km2_myr` 1,500 km²/Myr (Rey, Teyssier & Whitney 2010's 150 km in 15 Myr). Volume kept to a millionth (test).
  - `plates/settle.rs` (ISO-078): every visible continental column moves to z_A above the sea, s + (z_A - s) x 1.454 below it, plus the flexure, with `isostasy_relax_myr` 0.004 Myr (Wieczerkowski, Mitrovica & Wolf 1999, abstract, 3 to 5 kyr): complete each step. Tried and dropped: McKenzie 1978's 62.8 Myr (land 0.24), 10 Myr (0.27), 0.5 Myr (0.34; it and 4 kyr differ within a run's chaos).
  - Both run after the collapse and before the rate limits; set in the default and the twelve earthlike, pipeline and plates presets.
  - The settling's and the collapse's held sums are now in sample order: a parallel float sum changed the globals' last bits from run to run (test "the worlds differ").
  - Tests: the weld tests' seed 3 no longer welds in 300 Myr; seed 14 does (14 of seeds 3 to 24 weld). New flow test.
  - Ledger ids PLT-300 to PLT-302: renumbered from PLT-293 to PLT-295, which the ocean-crust agent took.
- **Measured** (VM, `env T=8 tools/review/force-balance-ensemble.sh <out> <bin> 1000 <seeds> <start> hyps <label> +DEEPTIME_CRUST_BUDGET=1 [+DEEPTIME_CRUST_BUDGET_MAPS=<dir>]`, master = c88c2eb5 with the budget; end of run, mean of seeds 1 to 3):

  | | land | continental crust under the sea | above 2 km, of land | coast p50 km | continental crust | T, degC |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | quick, supercontinent, master | 0.178 | 0.61 | 0.251 | 169 | 0.417 | 16.7 |
  | quick, supercontinent, fix | 0.310 | 0.34 | 0.285 | 166 | 0.432 | 15.6 |
  | quick, scattered, master | 0.155 | 0.68 | 0.282 | 162 | 0.426 | 19.5 |
  | quick, scattered, fix | 0.305 | 0.33 | 0.354 | 148 | 0.408 | 16.6 |
  | full 16k, scattered 1, master | 0.221 | 0.46 | 0.400 | 163 | 0.386 | 19.3 |
  | full 16k, scattered 1, fix | 0.317 | 0.35 | 0.350 | 129 | 0.442 | 15.0 |
  | Earth | 0.289 | 0.29 | 0.102 | 433 | 0.41 | |

  - Climate: colder on six of seven pairs (2.2 to 4.3 degC), natural CO2 lower on five (full: 1,461 to 810 ppm). Köppen E share of land 0.23 to 0.33 (supercontinent), 0.28 to 0.40 (scattered), 0.41 to 0.33 (full).
  - Sea floor: the drowned continental crust is shallower (median 1.2 to 0.4 to 0.6 km) and smoother; the shallowest tenth of the ocean floor rises (p90 -1.3 to -1.9 km to -0.5 to -0.9 km); neighbour relief between sea samples shows no consistent change.
  - Gates (VM): fmt, clippy, `cargo test --workspace` (deeptime-core lib 743 passed), `cargo deny check licenses bans`, `./gradlew build test` (365 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped). No fixture regenerated (the parity worlds come from `deeptime synth` at test time).
- **Not done, and next.** The shape: the land is still belts and island strings, coast p50 130 to 170 km against 433 (409 at 250,000 points), and the land above 2 km is 0.29 to 0.35 of land against 0.10. Next: measure the three leads one by one (collisions turning area into thickness, 18 km³ a year kept; island-arc crust on thin strings, 4.1 km³ a year against Earth's 1.5; the resampling filling continental gaps with ocean floor, 15.9 of the planet's worth of samples over a run), then the width of the thickness distribution under the Airy line. The transition's width (PLT-262) is Ben's and was not changed. `editor_fields.json` does not list the two new parameters.
### 2026-10-19: The present-day nudge's cap: the 1000 Myr hothouse ends (10,011 ppm on master) were the temperate nudge multiplying the natural CO2 by up to x12.6, not the carbon cycle; a temperate present now raises CO2 by at most x1.75, and full 16k's 1000 Myr ends fall from a median 8,867 to 1,510 ppm (24.7 to 18.5 degC); the Köppen floors are tested by a 99 % Wilson bound (coordinator's task; agent worktree agent-ae6030c66af57f107, branch worktree-agent-ae6030c66af57f107 from master 26ce664e; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **The cause.**
  - The end CO2 is the temperate present's factor times the natural CO2 (CLM-148 to CLM-151):
    - master 26ce664e, `earthlike_full_16k`, 1000 Myr, scattered start, seeds 1 to 4: factor 6.86, 1.58, 9.73 and 12.65 on natural 1,460, 315, 794 and 932 ppm;
    - seed 1's 10,011 ppm is the GPU agent's CPU run.
  - The carbon cycle holds:
    - weathering equals degassing within 0.2 % at every 100 Myr point before the last step;
    - the natural CO2 falls from 3,800 to 4,600 ppm at -998 Myr (fainter sun) to 360 to 960 ppm at -100 Myr;
    - T stays 9 to 16 degC throughout;
    - over the last 500 Myr the natural CO2 is 267 to 3,209 ppm, inside the Phanerozoic's 1 to 25 PAL. It leaves that range only through the nudge, in the last 100 kyr.
  - The nudge needed so much because of the ice sheets on high ground:
    - land above 2 km grows from 0 to 0.20 to 0.41 of the land;
    - 0.68 to 0.88 of the land above 3 km is under sheets in the natural end;
    - x1.75 clears 5 to 14 % of it (`sheets_by_height`, new).
  - A bisect of the merges 25ae6723..26ce664e (quick, 500 Myr, scattered, seeds 1 and 2):
    - the worlds change only at 32589362, fb38204f and 7d60fc4a;
    - each moves the factor, and none moves the natural CO2 out of the spread between seeds.
    - The old master had the same hothouse on other seeds: scattered seed 4 x5.27, 7,832 ppm.
  - The land share (0.12 to 0.23) and the high ground are the plates' output; the climate takes them as given.
- **The fix.** `climate.present_co2_factor_max` = 1.75 (CLM-206), from Lüthi et al. 2008's 172 to 300 ppmv (abstract read on OSTI).
  - It applies to temperate only, and is set in the default and the eight earthlike and pipeline presets.
  - A present that needs more ends at the cap with `reached` false.
  - `ice_age` and `snowball` are unlimited.
  - The search is now a pure function, `present_search`; the bracket below the cap is unchanged, and the cap is its last step.
  - With the cap at 10,000 the runs equal master's to every printed digit.
  - The note gains `co2_factor_max`, `trial_rows` (every trial's factor, sheets, land ice, sea ice and T) and `sheets_by_height` / `sheets_by_latitude`.
  - Tests:
    - new `the_present_search_stops_at_its_cap` (pure: no cap, the cap, inside the cap, cap 0, cooling, a trivial target);
    - `the_present_climate_setting_governs_only_the_present` extended with the new fields.
- **Measured** (VM, `tools/review/co2-driver.sh 3 <tasks>` driving `tools/review/co2-ensemble.sh`, read with `tools/review/co2-table.py`; median [min, max]):

  | | runs | end CO2, ppm | factor | natural CO2 | T, degC | land | above 2 km | under sheets | reached |

  | old master 25ae6723, quick 500 Myr | 8 | 881 [477, 7,832] | 1.46 [1.00, 5.27] | 653 | 17.2 [14.8, 23.7] | 0.189 | 0.254 | 0.148 | 8 |
  | master 26ce664e, quick 500 Myr | 8 | 2,030 [474, 15,463] | 1.67 [1.00, 8.91] | 1,019 | 19.2 [15.6, 28.2] | 0.180 | 0.274 | 0.148 | 8 |
  | fixed, quick 500 Myr | 8 | 1,764 [474, 3,036] | 1.66 [1.00, 1.75] | 1,019 | 18.7 [15.6, 21.4] | 0.180 | 0.274 | 0.150 [0.117, 0.257] | 5 |

  - The quick runs are `earthlike_quick_16k`, 2 threads, seeds 1 to 4, both starts. The full runs are `earthlike_full_16k`, 8 threads, scattered start, seeds 1 to 4.
  - The fixed runs' clock series equal master's at every 100 Myr point.
  - The fixed 1000 Myr ends are 1.8 to 9.1 PAL. Master's were 1.8 to 42, three of the four above the Phanerozoic's 25.
  - The quick scattered seed 1 at 4 threads equals its 2-thread run.

  - Its land ice from -760 Myr on, and the tropical ice at 4.1 km and -9 degC, are the natural climate, which the cap does not change.

- **Science.**
  - climate.md: "The present-day nudge's cap" and the ledger-ids table.

  - the Wilson bound at 99 % rather than 95 % (about 65 comparisons a batch);
  - the cap as the bracket's last step.

  - its natural CO2 at 1000 Myr is 1.1 to 5.2 PAL, and three of the four runs have 0.27 to 0.33 of the land under sheets on high ground;
  - it ends with 0.24 to 0.29 of the land under sheets where the cap stops the nudge (Earth 0.10).
  - The high ground and the small land share are for the plates (P4 relief); the dry-ice extent rule is for the climate.

- **Cause.** The arc band (weight above 0.3) is d 134 to 266 km behind the slab front, 132 km wide; 5,000 samples on the plate model's Earth-radius sphere are about 320 km apart, so the distance field's first ring lies beyond it. Volcano stage: `flux_valid = plates.resample_step != plates.step` (VOL-011); `VolcanoState.last_flagged` removed. ### 2026-10-19: GPU compute phase 2: the plates' L1 relink and the climate snapshot's cells run on the GPU; `write_l1` 1.6 times faster and the cells 4 times on the laptop's Radeon; no lean in any layer or climate field from the same state; the ported kernels take 72 to 86 s off a 1000 Myr full 16k run on the laptop (3 to 3.6 %) (coordinator's Phase 2 task; agent worktree agent-a1265f3344b19b0c1, branch `gpu-phase2` from master b337fa73, the climate sub-agent's branch and masters fb38204f, 7d60fc4a and 26ce664e merged in; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Design note:** `docs/design/gpu-compute.md` sections 13 (the relink) and 14 (the cells), section 10's Phase 2 measurements, section 4's memory, section 12's order. Science pages: `docs/science/plates.md` "L1 sampling on a GPU" and `docs/science/per-cell-climate.md` "Down to L1 on a GPU", each with a whole-planet paragraph. No law, constant or threshold changed, so no ledger row.
- **What changed.**
  - `plates/l1.rs`: one dispatch point. `sample` asks `compute::ambient_device` for the session's device and runs `plates/l1/gpu.rs`'s relink beside the k-d tree's build; a cell the device settled takes its link, every other cell runs the CPU code. WGSL: a latitude-band bucket grid for the nearest visible sample within 1.2 spacings, the walk (at most 48 steps) to the group's triangle, the corner test, the barycentric weights; 5 words a cell back, `u32::MAX` for a cell left to the CPU. The 30 layers stay on the CPU. `compute.rs`: `Ambient` (the session's mode and log on every pool worker, since the plates get no stage context), `ambient_device`, `Ambient::kept` (a session-scoped slot that keeps the pipeline and the grown buffers) and the compute gauge. `session.rs` puts the ambient context on its pool's workers; `sphere/coupling.rs` takes the device's links in `Coupling::relink`. CLI: the bench's timings line gains `compute[...]` (the compute gauge: the relink's device, CPU part, tree and layer laps, and the counts of cells).
  - The climate cells (sub-agent's commit bd25536b, merged as 61efa322): `snapshot::CellsDevice` called from `compute_on(.., dev)`; `climate/gpu.rs` runs step 5 of a snapshot per cell in chunks of 2^18 cells; the sums that feed weathering and the ice cover stay in f64 on the CPU in their order; `snapshot:ebm2d` stays on the CPU (section 12 item 6).
  - Tests: `plates::l1::gpu::tests::the_gpu_relink_matches_the_cpu_but_at_ties` (lavapipe: 125,952 cells, 11.6 % left to the CPU, no link different, weights within 1.6e-5, NaN equal to NaN in the layer comparison) and `climate::tests::the_gpu_cells_stay_within_their_error_budget_of_the_cpu`.
