### 2026-10-20: Build-level speed-ups for the natives measured: mimalloc under the counting allocator and PGO each change a full 16k run by less than the pair noise (about 4 %), so neither ships; both stay as opt-in tooling (coordinator's task; agent worktree agent-a43d3ff144b13ae85, branch worktree-agent-a43d3ff144b13ae85 from master 3e7edd49; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Question.** Can the allocator (mimalloc or jemalloc, inside `CountingAlloc`) or profile-guided optimisation make the 1000 Myr full 16k run (the 900 s target on an average gaming rig) faster by a build switch alone? Ben: performance over determinism, so worlds need not match byte for byte.
- **Allocator** (`crates/deeptime-core/src/alloc.rs`, feature `mimalloc`, off by default; `deeptime-cli` and `deeptime-jni` forward it, the jni's as `mimalloc-dyn-tls` so a `dlopen`ed library gets thread-local storage the JVM can load). `CountingAlloc` stays the global allocator and keeps its own layers (mmap'd blocks from 1 MiB with the 2 GiB kept-block cache, the per-thread park of 4 small blocks); only the small blocks that used to go to glibc come from mimalloc, counted by `mi_usable_size` where the glibc build counts `small_footprint`, and `trim_system` calls `mi_collect(true)` for `malloc_trim`. `libmimalloc-sys` 0.1.49's own `extended` feature (and its `cty` dependency) is not used: `mi_usable_size` and `mi_collect` are declared by hand. New dependencies `mimalloc`, `libmimalloc-sys` (MIT; `cargo deny check licenses bans` passes).
  - Exactness: the new `crates/deeptime-core/tests/alloc_exact.rs` churns small blocks through many size classes (grow, shrink, zeroed, freed out of order) on one thread and on four, and asserts the counter returns to where it began; it passes with glibc and with `--features mimalloc` (its four-thread half allows up to the 4 slots of 4 KiB per exited thread: the park has no destructor, so a thread's last freed blocks after its final `unpark_thread` stay counted). `memory_estimate` and `history_cap` pass with glibc; with mimalloc `history_cap` passes and `memory_estimate` fails on the young stage, 66.2 against its 63.1 MiB estimate (+5 %), because mimalloc's size classes round small blocks up more than the glibc footprint the estimates were fitted to: a second reason not to switch it on without refitting.
  - Cross-builds (`cargo zigbuild` / `cargo xwin`, `--features mimalloc` on `deeptime-jni`): the other six native targets build (x86-64 and aarch64 Linux on gnu glibc 2.17 and musl, Windows x86-64 and arm64); the two macOS targets do not: mimalloc v3's C source includes CommonCrypto, which zig's macOS stubs lack (the `mimalloc-v2` feature avoids it; untested). Not needed while nothing ships. jemalloc was not tried: the measurement below says the small-block allocator is not the limit, and `tikv-jemalloc-sys` brings an autoconf build per target.
- **PGO tooling** (all opt-in; `build-natives.sh` is unchanged). `tools/natives/pgo-profile.sh <out>` builds an instrumented `deeptime` (`ship` plus `-C profile-generate`), runs `deeptime bench` of `earthlike_quick_16k` for 6 Myr on 1 thread (the defaults), and merges with the rustc-matching `llvm-profdata` (the `llvm-tools` rustup component, added to `rust-toolchain.toml` and the dev shell: rustc's LLVM is 22.1.8, the dev shell's own `llvmPackages.llvm` 21.1.8). `tools/natives/gate-bins.sh <out> --pgo <profile> [--features F]` builds the gate's two binaries from it, each in its own target dir; `ship.sh`'s `pgo_cargo_args` passes `-C profile-use` and `-C llvm-args=-pgo-warn-missing-function` through `--config target.<triple>.rustflags`, which merges with `.cargo/config.toml`'s flags as the v3 flag does. Traps found: (1) training must be 1 to 2 threads: the instrumented binary's counters are shared atomics and 8 threads ran 10 to 30 times slower (the full 16k at 8 threads did not finish in an hour); (2) a profile finds its functions by symbol name, which carries the crate id, which cargo derives from the build's roots and target: the CLI's profile on the library build (or the library's on the CLI) had about 13,000 functions without data, so the instrumented and the optimised build must select the same packages (`-p deeptime-cli`); (3) `-pgo-warn-missing-function` makes a profile that does not fit loud (the same-package build has 0 such warnings).
- **Does one x86-64 Linux profile serve the other targets?** No, measured: the profile made by the `-p deeptime-cli -p deeptime-jni` instrumented build (host triple) left 15,772 workspace functions without data on `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.17`, 15,837 on musl and 13,856 on Windows x86-64 (its run was cut short; aarch64 and macOS were not run once the first three showed it), where the CLI's profile on the CLI's own build gives 0 (the gnu run is the same triple as the instrumented build, so what differs there is the `.2.17` glibc suffix, or the second package; the cause was not separated further). The target is part of the crate id, as far as these runs show, so each target needs its own instrumented build and training run, and the aarch64 ones cannot run on the x86-64 VM at all (and the Windows and macOS ones would train under emulation or on other hardware). Nothing in the tree builds the library for a triple with the CLI beside it either (`deeptime-cli` does not link for glibc 2.17: it calls `mallinfo2`). arm64, macOS and Windows would ship without PGO even if x86-64 Linux did; `--pgo` was therefore left out of `build-natives.sh`.
- **Measured** (VM, 8 pinned Zen 5 cores per arm, 8 threads, `earthlike_full_16k` from `scattered_continents`, 100 Myr, `tools/review/p1-19-pair.sh`: the two arms side by side on the two core sets, then swapped; box load 12 to 23 other busy CPUs by turns, so the two orders differ by up to 27 % between them and only the within-order difference means anything; 0 of the 66 output files differ between the two arms in every pair). Wall seconds, CPU seconds (user plus system) as the mean of the two orders, plain against the variant:

  | Variant | wall, plain to variant | change | CPU, plain to variant | change | other |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | mimalloc | 250.9 to 250.9 | 0.0 % | 1,025.8 to 1,027.0 | +0.1 % | peak RSS 4.41 to 4.57 GB (+3.6 %) |
  | PGO, short quick profile (training 372 s) | 245.8 to 243.3 | -1.0 % | 1,010.1 to 992.7 | -1.7 % | binary 24.8 to 22.1 MB |
  | PGO, 40 Myr quick profile | 208.2 to 210.7 | +1.2 % | 904.5 to 872.0 | -3.6 % | training 1,142 s |
  | PGO (short profile) and mimalloc | 234.7 to 232.2 | -1.1 % | 973.4 to 955.4 | -1.8 % | |

  Stage times (plates, climate, surface, young, amplify, finalize) move together with the load and in no consistent direction; the two orders of one pair disagree on the sign (wall, variant against plain, first order then second: mimalloc +2.3 and -1.8 %, PGO 0.0 and -2.1 %, the 40 Myr PGO 0.0 and +3.2 %, PGO and mimalloc +2.3 and -4.2 %), so the noise is about 4 %, larger than every wall gain here. The counted peak (4,273 MiB plain, 4,276 MiB with mimalloc) is the same: the counting allocator's mmap layer, not the small-block allocator, holds the memory. The 100 Myr full run is the stand-in for 1000 Myr here: no variant gained beyond the pair noise, so no 1000 Myr pair was run for any (the rule: one full pair per change kept; none was kept).
- **Cost of PGO**, were it kept: the instrumented build 412 to 496 s, the training 290 s (6 Myr, quick preset, 1 thread) to 1,142 s (40 Myr), the optimised build 313 to 342 s (the plain ship build 270 to 373 s on the same loaded box). 12 to 25 minutes per profile, per target, repeated whenever the code changes enough to change function control flow (`-pgo-warn-missing-function` says when).
- **Why so little.** `CountingAlloc` already takes the allocator out of the hot path: the big arrays (the run's memory) are mmap'd and cached, and the 4-block park serves the small allocations of the inner loops, so a faster `malloc` has almost nothing to speed up. PGO's usual wins are in branchy, pointer-chasing code; the hot code here is wide array loops the compiler already vectorises, with fat LTO and one codegen unit already on, so the profile moves the layout and little else (the binary shrinks 11 %, the CPU time 1.3 to 3.6 %, the wall time not at all).
- **Gates** (VM, admitted, `tools/dev/gates.sh`): `cargo fmt --check` ok; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (after one `is_multiple_of` fix in the new test, rerun clean); `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 997 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored (core lib 737; the one more than before is `alloc_exact`); `cargo deny check licenses bans` ok; `./gradlew build test` successful, 363 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped. No gametest.sh, per the task.
- **Coordinator's calls (undoable).** `mimalloc` stays a feature, default off, nothing in the natives enables it. PGO tooling stays, `build-natives.sh` untouched. The profile's training is 1 thread on the quick preset (the full preset at 8 threads is unusable). 1000 Myr pairs not run, for the reason above. jemalloc not tried. If Ben wants either shipped anyway, the allocator is one feature flag on `deeptime-jni` (the macOS cross-build needs `mimalloc-v2` or a CommonCrypto-free build of v3), PGO needs a per-triple instrumented build and training in `build-natives.sh`.

On 7d60fc4a's planet there is no active volcano, so the test logs that and reads nothing.

A column counts as a pool when `Geothermal`'s site part there is a pool and the water's top is the pool's level, logged as `hotSpringPoolColumns`. On fb38204f: outside 0/0, pools 3/3. On 7d60fc4a (the parallel flood): outside 0/0, pools 0/0, five other sites.

On fb38204f, with the band then at 7/8 of the Lambert pole z (427; the planet is Petroff-Guyou, its edges at 768): rows 183, 311, 327, 343, 167, -9; west 76 and east 24 dry columns, all within a block. On 7d60fc4a the west of the seam is sea to 7/8 of the edges (0 dry columns in the band, east 69): rows 103, 119, 167, 23; the west compares its sea bed (123 of 128 within a block), the east 26 dry columns, all within a block. ### 2026-10-19: P1-19 surface numerics: a multigrid-preconditioned diffusion solve (ERO-183) and a parallel depression flood (ERO-184) cut their timers by 58 % and 57 %, 32 s of a 150-Myr full 16k run's 516 s; the slope failure cannot stop early, so its stopping rule was not landed (coordinator's #25, #26, #28; agent worktree agent-ac143b395160ae3ed, branch worktree-agent-ac143b395160ae3ed from f221b3d3; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Settings.** `surface.numerics.diffusion_solver` (`multigrid`, the default, or `jacobi`), `surface.numerics.diffusion_tol_m` (10⁻⁵ m, ERO-183) and `surface.numerics.flood` (`parallel`, the default, or `serial`, ERO-184). With `--set surface.numerics.diffusion_solver=jacobi --set surface.numerics.flood=serial` the branch gave master's six ensemble worlds figure for figure. New files: `surface/diffusion/multigrid.rs` (+ `multigrid/tests.rs`), `surface/pflood/parallel.rs` (+ `parallel/tests.rs`). The Jacobi solve and its `step()` stay (spread.rs uses `step()`).
- **#25, the diffusion solve.** Conjugate gradients preconditioned by one geometric multigrid V-cycle: 2 × 2 aggregation, piecewise-constant transfer, coarse couplings half the Galerkin sum (Braess 1995), damped Jacobi ω 0.8 with two sweeps a side, a coarsest level of at most 64 cells with 16 sweeps; the cycle in f32, the conjugate gradients in f64; the same split first guess and mass put-back. The audit (`DEEPTIME_DIFFUSION_AUDIT=1`, `earthlike_full_16k`, 100 Myr, 54 solves, each also run by the Jacobi solve and to 10⁻⁹ m): 127.2 iterations a solve to 17.2; against the old solve 0.68 mm largest, 1.5 × 10⁻⁶ m RMS; error against the tight solve 0.67 mm largest, 1.5 × 10⁻⁶ m RMS, against the Jacobi solve's own 0.024 mm and 3.0 × 10⁻⁷ m. The stage stores f32 elevations, whose step is 0.49 mm from 4 to 8 km.
- **#28, the flood.** Barnes 2016's parallel Priority-Flood (strips with watershed labels, a graph of the strips' edges) for the ε = 0 fill, then an exact Priority-Flood+ε over each group of cells the first phase cannot settle, the groups in parallel. It is the unique least fixed point of the ε relaxation, so it does not depend on the thread count or the order (proof in `pflood/parallel.rs`); it differs from the serial flood in ulps (168 of 250 steps of a 500-Myr `pipeline_quick_16k` run, about 170 of ~13,000 raised cells a step).
- **#26, the slope failure's stopping rule: not landed.** A trace of every call (`earthlike_full_16k`, 100 Myr, 54 calls) found that no tolerance from 0.005 to 0.5 critical drops stops any call before its 40 iterations: the largest residual falls from 65.8 to 8.9 critical drops (0.95³⁹ = 0.135, a rate-limited relaxation) and about 200,000 cells move every iteration. A second form that also skipped settled pairs cut the movers by a quarter but was not faster (22.8 s against master's 18.8 s in one pair) and moved the planet outside master's runs (land above 2 km 0.241, land median 838 m, CO₂ 3,237 ppm with one run at 14,177; two plate checks failed). `marine.rs` is back to the base.
- **Time** (`tools/review/bench-quiet.py`, `earthlike_full_16k`, scattered continents, 150 Myr, 8 threads; master on CPU set A against the branch on B, then swapped; a loaded VM, load up to 93): `diffusion_solve` 48.4 → 20.5 s (27.9 s saved, 58 %), `pflood` 7.8 → 3.4 s (4.5 s, 57 %), `slope_failure` 31.9 → 27.3 s (the same code: load), the young stage's diffusion 8.7 → 6.7 s, the surface stage 180.4 → 131.9 s, the run 515.9 → 465.4 s (means of the two pairs). Scaled by those fractions, the full gate run's `diffusion_solve` 109.3 s and `pflood` 32.7 s would give about 63 s and 19 s (inferred; the gate was not rerun).
- **Planet** (`tools/review/force-balance-ensemble.sh`, `earthlike_quick_16k`, seeds 1 to 3, both starts, 500 Myr; `p1-17-hyps.py`, `erosion-recal.py`): every surface figure inside master's runs but the continental crust mean (0.423 against master's largest 0.418, one run at 0.507); plate checks 29 → 28 of 45, the pass/fail changes all inside master's runs; erosion RMS log error against Montgomery & Brandon 0.19 → 0.21; high ground's flat part 139.0 → 145.2 m/Myr; conjugate-gradient iterations a step 62.2 → 9.5. Several plate figures with no target moved outside master's runs (largest plate's median share 0.18 → 0.25, supercontinent steps 28.6 → 49.9 %, the large plate's in-plane stress 2.07 → 0.62 MPa; eleven in all, inside their targets where they have one). A control ensemble with the multigrid solve only (`--set surface.numerics.flood=serial`) also kept every surface figure inside master's runs (27 plate checks, erosion RMS 0.20) and pushed eleven plate figures outside master's runs too, mostly others (plate speed median 33.7 → 38.3 mm/yr, collision length's 90th percentile 119 → 173 Myr): read as the spread any perturbation makes in a chaotic run, not an effect of the flood (inferred). The all-old-settings control gave master's worlds exactly.
- **Memory estimate.** The multigrid hierarchy raised the young stage's counted peak (`DEEPTIME_MEM_TRACE`, scattered continents, 500 Myr, 8 threads, the 4 GiB cap, `DEEPTIME_LARGE_CACHE=0`; `build/p119s/memyoung.sh`, scratch): quick 16k 1,322.8 → 1,376.5 MiB (master against the branch), 42 B a cell; full 16k 4,311 MiB on the branch (P1-17 measured 4,143). Own arrays 448 B a cell on quick, 445 B on full. So `young::OWN_BYTES_PER_L2_CELL` 460 → 500 (`no_stage_holds_more_than_its_estimate` had failed, young 74.4 > 74.3 MiB), and the pinned holds of `young::tests::the_estimate_covers_the_measured_hold_closely` 1,105 → 1,162 MiB (quick) and 4,143 → 4,311 MiB (full), with a note in the test; master's quick run gave 1,108.6, so the method matches P1-17's. Full 16k's young stage now peaks 215 MiB over a 4 GiB cap (47 before); the editor refuses full at 4 GiB as before.
- **Tests.** No test asserted identical output across thread counts in a way the changes broke, so none became a tolerance test: the flood's tests compare the parallel flood with a plain Priority-Flood+ε bit for bit, which holds because the parallel flood is order-free; the multigrid tests use tolerances (`the_multigrid_and_jacobi_solves_agree_within_their_tolerance`).
- **Gates** (VM, admitted): fmt, clippy -D warnings, `cargo deny check licenses bans` and `./gradlew build test` (354 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped) passed on the branch before the estimate fix; `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` with 500: every test binary passed but `young::tests::the_estimate_covers_the_measured_hold_closely` (quick listed 1,291 MiB against the 1,105 then pinned), which with the re-measured holds passes (`cargo test -p deeptime-core --lib surface::young::tests`: 2 passed), as do `--test memory_estimate`, fmt and clippy -D warnings again.
- **Science.** ERO-183 (game-choice: the tolerance, with the audit) and ERO-184 (verified: Barnes 2016); bibliography (Barnes 2016, Briggs, Henson & McCormick 2000, Tatebe 1993, Braess 1995); `erosion-and-sediment.md` "Surface numerics" (the solve, the flood, the stopping rule, time, the planet); `claims_counts.py --write` (ERO 173 rows).
- **Shared with the other surface agent.** `surface/mod.rs`, `surface/young.rs`, `surface/diffusion.rs`, `surface/pflood.rs`, `surface/params.rs`; `surface/marine.rs` unchanged against the base. ERO-183 and ERO-184 are new ids and may collide with the other agent's.
- **Choices** (mine, undoable): multigrid-preconditioned CG over plain multigrid; 2 × 2 aggregation with a coarse scale 0.5; two sweeps; ω 0.8; coarsest 64 cells and 16 sweeps; f32 cycle; tolerance 10⁻⁵ m over 10⁻⁶ m (17.2 against 27.4 iterations, error about one f32 step); the order-free two-phase flood over an order-dependent one; both new methods default; the stopping rule not landed; the second b2 timing pair cancelled once its ensemble failed; the estimate 500 B.
- **Next.** The slope failure at a rate of 1/16 with 32 iterations (the same relaxation a step, 0.127 against 0.129) would save about a fifth of its time but changes its path and needs its own ensemble. The multigrid solve's setup and first guess are now a large part of its time.

### 2026-10-19: P1-19 plates part 2: feedback, flexure, belts and fronts, and the neighbour queries of write_l1, detect and stats_margins. The plate stage is 1.25× faster side by side (15 s per 200 Myr) and the worlds are identical (profile items #3, #5; agent worktree agent-ad646ba0bbca1e26b, branch worktree-agent-ad646ba0bbca1e26b from master be80c6c1, master 32589362 merged before the measurements; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **What changed** (every change identical: same files, byte for byte).
  - **#3, feedback and flexure** (`plates/mod.rs`). The feedback's serial scatter stays. The flexure's sample (`flexure_of`) runs beside it in a `rayon::join`, since both only read the last sampling's links. The `flexure_sample` lap is now only the fallback for a step without feedback.
    - A parallel gather over the links turned round (`FanIn`, a counting-sort transposition, each sample's additions in the serial order) was built twice and dropped. It lost to the serial scatter under the follower stage's load: feedback +2.35 s per 200 Myr (v1) and +1.9 s (v2, `pairs-fanin`).
  - **#3, belts** (`plates/belts.rs`). `stack` runs every front's two distance fields at once. Each is plates part 1's `dijkstra_sparse`, sorted by vertex (`geometry::dijkstra_sorted`), so the sums run in the old order. The loops run over the reached set, not every sample. A front stacked after another cuts its field back to the shorter reach, which is exact (see `dijkstra_sorted`), or runs it again.
  - **#3, fronts** (`plates/subduction.rs`). Split into begin, reach and finish. The read-only reach runs beside `belts::stack`, so the `belts` lap now holds it. The arcs' search from every front runs per rigid group (`geometry::dijkstra_parts`, each group's `dijkstra_sparse` on its own thread, exact because no allowed edge joins two groups).
  - **#5, write_l1** (`plates/l1.rs`, `sphere/coupling.rs`).
    - One nearest query finds the nearest visible sample's group first. The six-nearest search runs only where that fails.
    - The 30 output layers are written in one pass.
    - Each cell's row is interpolated inside the block loop; before, every cell's row was collected first (about 150 MB a step on full 16k).
    - The coupling keeps its cells' unit vectors per row and column.
  - **#5, detect** (`plates/subduction.rs`). Samples whose 5×5×5 block of cubes holds only their own plate are skipped (`Voxels`). This is exact because √3·h < 2h.
  - **#5, stats_margins** (`plates/stats.rs`). One 8-nearest query per sample serves both the margins and the landmass links.
  - **Tests.** `sorted_and_split_dijkstras_match_the_dense_one` (dense against sorted, per part and a shorter reach, bit for bit), `voxels_skip_only_samples_whose_nearest_share_their_plate` and `kept_unit_vectors_are_the_frames`.
  - **Tooling.** `tools/review/p1-19-pair.sh` runs two builds side by side on the VM's sets A and B, then swapped, and compares each pair's worlds.
- **Merge with plates part 1** (master 32589362): `geometry.rs` takes master's `dijkstra_sparse`. This branch's own kept-scratch search (`Reach`, `dijkstra_reached`) is gone, as the coordinator asked.
- **Seconds.**
  - **Setup.** The shipped x86-64-v3 builds (`tools/natives/gate-bins.sh <out> --only x86-64-v3`) of master 32589362 and of this branch, run with `tools/review/p1-19-pair.sh <master bin> master <branch bin> branch <out> earthlike_full_16k scattered_continents 200 8 ab,ba`. Lap timers are from `deeptime bench` through `bench-quiet.py`. The VM was loaded by other agents: others' busy CPUs averaged 14 to 19, load1 peaked at 91 in ba.

  | Lap | ab: master A → branch B | ba: master B → branch A | Saved per 200 Myr (mean) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | feedback + flexure_sample | 8.2 → 4.3 | 10.5 → 9.3 | 2.6 |
  | belts + fronts | 6.7 → 3.3 | 7.9 → 5.3 | 3.0 |
  | detect | 5.3 → 3.4 | 9.1 → 9.1 | 1.0 |
  | stats_margins | 2.0 → 1.5 | 2.8 → 2.6 | 0.35 |
  | write_l1 | 29.6 → 19.5 | 48.9 → 40.5 | 9.25 |
  | plates stage | 69.4 → 48.8 | 103.1 → 93.4 | 15.2 (1.25×, geometric mean) |

  - The wall times swing with the CPU set, not the build. Set B ran 4.84 and 3.24 CPUs busy against set A's 4.15 and 2.79, and the stages after the plates (amplify, finalize), which this branch does not touch, moved by 17 to 25 s with the set.

- **cmp** (`tools/review/p1-17-cmp.py` per pair): 68 of 68 files are byte-identical in both orders. Before the merge, against be80c6c1, both earlier pairs and the FanIn pair also gave 68 of 68.
- **Tolerance tests.** None needed: every change is identical, and `tests/overlap.rs` (1 thread against 3, byte for byte) passes.

### 2026-10-18: Natives: a baseline and an x86-64-v3 build for each x86-64 platform, picked at runtime by a CPU probe, and the `ship` profile (fat LTO, one codegen unit) for everything that ships and for the gate. At 100 Myr on full 16k, ship v3 is 1.08× faster than plain `release` (CPU time 1.10×). Ship baseline matches it in wall time (1.00×) and is 1.03× by CPU time. The worlds are the same files (coordinator's task, Ben's decision of 2026-10-18 "Both, picked at runtime"; agent worktree agent-aa3973505c3dc829a, branch worktree-agent-aa3973505c3dc829a from master f221b3d3; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **What ships.** A release jar holds 16 native files, up from 8:
  - the eight platforms' baseline `deeptime_jni`;
  - an x86-64-v3 `deeptime_jni` for linux-x86_64-gnu, linux-x86_64-musl, windows-x86_64 and macos-x86_64;
  - a `deeptime_cpuprobe` for the same four.

  The aarch64 platforms stay single. `natives.json` is schema 2: each library carries `variant` (`baseline` or `x86-64-v3`), and the probes have their own array. Jar paths are `natives/deeptime/<platform>/<variant>/<file>` and `.../<platform>/probe/<file>`. Each file extracts to its own `<version>-<sha12>/` directory (plan §6.4, §6.5).
- **The probe** is a new crate, `crates/deeptime-cpuprobe`. It has no dependencies and one JNI function, `CpuProbe.probe()`, which returns `ABI << 32 | mask`. The mask covers the 16 features of x86-64-v3: `is_x86_feature_detected!`, which uses CPUID and checks XGETBV for the AVX family, plus CPUID 8000_0001h for LAHF/SAHF.
  - **Why a library of its own:** the JVM binds a class's natives to the first library that exports them. If the baseline `deeptime_jni` answered the question, every later `DeepTimeNative` call would go to it, so the loader could never load v3.
  - **Tests:** a Rust test holds Java's feature list to the Rust one.
  - **Sizes:** 118 kB on Windows, 344 to 347 kB on Linux, 1.26 MB on macOS (the plan said "a few kB"; corrected).
- **The loader** (`NativeLoader`, plan §6.5 step 6):
  - **The choice.** It runs the probe from its own directory, once per JVM, and loads v3 only when every feature is present. Otherwise it loads the baseline.
  - **The log.** The summary line logs the build and the reason, for example `build=x86-64-v3 ... (x86-64-v3: the CPU has every x86-64-v3 feature)` or `(baseline: the CPU lacks avx2, fma of x86-64-v3)`.
  - **The override.** `-Ddeeptime.natives.variant` or `DEEPTIME_NATIVES_VARIANT` takes `baseline`, `x86-64-v3`/`v3` or `auto`; the property wins.
    - A forced baseline skips the probe.
    - A forced v3 is refused with a WARN on a CPU the probe says lacks the level. It is taken on trust only when the probe cannot run.
  - **The fallback.** If v3 fails to link or answer, the loader logs it and loads the baseline.
  - **Test hooks.** `-Ddeeptime.natives.forceFail=v3_link` exercises the fallback, and `-Ddeeptime.natives.testCpuFeatures=<mask>` stands in for the probe's answer.
  - **GameTests.** The native GameTest's log line adds `build=`.
  - **CI.** The x86-64 rows of `natives.yml` run `NativeSmoke` a second time with the baseline forced.
- **Building.**
  - **How v3 is built.** `-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3` goes in through `--config 'target.<triple>.rustflags=[...]'`, which merges with `.cargo/config.toml` (`RUSTFLAGS` would replace it, so the scripts refuse to run with it set). Each build names `--target`, so build scripts stay on the baseline CPU, and uses its own target dir, `target/x86-64-v3`. The shared settings are in `tools/natives/ship.sh`.
  - **Checks on every v3 file.** Its version string must read `cpu=x86-64-v3`, and it must have at least 500 BMI1/BMI2 instructions (SHLX, SHRX, SARX, RORX, ANDN, MULX, BZHI) and more than four times the baseline's count.
    - The first check counted FMA/AVX2 instructions. It gave 1,402 and 1,468 for the two builds, because runtime-dispatched dependencies carry those instructions in the baseline too.
    - The BMI count gives 0 in every baseline build. The v3 builds measured 1,638 on Linux, 1,597 on Windows and 2,962 on macOS.
  - **macOS install names.** They moved from `.cargo/config.toml` to each library's `build.rs`, so the probe does not claim `libdeeptime_jni.dylib`.
  - **Gradle.** `hostNatives` builds the probe and the v3 build for an x86-64 host (`-PbaselineNativeOnly` skips v3). The dev jar on the VM held baseline, v3 and probe.
- **The `ship` profile** (`Cargo.toml`) is `release` plus `lto = "fat"` and `codegen-units = 1`. Two things use it:
  - `build-natives.sh`;
  - `tools/natives/gate-bins.sh <out> [--plain]`, which builds `deeptime-baseline` and `deeptime-x86-64-v3` for the gate.

  `p1-17-profile.sh` profiles the ship build (`P117_CPU=x86-64-v3` for v3). Everyday builds, Gradle's host native and the tests stay on `release`. The gate doc's new section "Running the gate: the shipped builds" has the commands and asks for both numbers.
- **Measured: plain release against ship baseline and ship v3.**
  - **Setup.** `earthlike_full_16k`, scattered continents, 100 Myr, 8 threads, `tools/review/bench-quiet.py`. Each pair ran side by side on sets A (0,16,2,18,4,20,6,22) and B (8,24,10,26,12,28,14,30), then the other way round. Plain is `release` built from this branch, whose core is master f221b3d3's. The VM was busy throughout: others' busy CPUs 14 to 25, siblings 33 to 88 % busy.
  - **Speed-ups** (geometric mean of the two orders):

    | build | over | wall | (each order) | CPU time |
    |---|---|---:|---|---:|
    | ship v3 | plain | **1.08×** | 1.085, 1.079 | 1.10× |
    | ship baseline | plain | **1.00×** (second round) | 0.985, 1.019 | **1.03×** |
    | ship v3 | ship baseline | 1.10× | 1.148, 1.048 | 1.06× |

    The plain and baseline pair ran twice. The first round's orders gave 1.047 and 1.246, because set B was held back in one run (3.57 against 4.26 CPUs busy). The second, quieter round (siblings 14 to 23 % busy) gave 0.985 and 1.019. CPU time was 1.022 to 1.036 in all four pairs.

    So fat LTO is worth about 3 % of the CPU time and v3 about 6 % more. By CPU time they compound: 1.027 × 1.060 = 1.089, against the 1.097 measured directly.
  - **The worlds.** `p1-17-cmp.py` on every pair: 66 of 66 files equal. At 100 Myr, plain, ship baseline and ship v3 build the same world. Nothing requires it (Ben, 2026-10-18).
  - **Tables:** docs/design/p1-17-benchmark-gate.md, "Running the gate: the shipped builds".
- **Build cost** (measured; `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, fresh target dirs, VM load 22 to 77):

  | build | release | ship | ship v3 |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | CLI, cold | 81 s | 274 s | 289 s |
  | `deeptime_jni`, dependencies built | 75 s | 194 s | 259 s |
  | CLI after a core change | 72 s | 323 s | 305 s |
  | `deeptime_jni` after a core change | 65 s | 190 s | 245 s |

  So ship costs 2.6 to 4.5× the build time.
  - **The full cross-build.** `build-natives.sh` built the 16 files in 2,594 s on the loaded VM: 2.5 to 4.1 min per library.
  - **CI.** The 2026-09-28 run of 8 release builds took 25 min. `natives.yml`'s build job timeout goes from 30 to 180 min; about 100 min is the 2-core runner estimate (inferred).
- **Sizes.**
  - **linux-x86_64-gnu `deeptime_jni`** (unstripped `cargo build`): release 19,692,808 B, ship 15,252,816 B (−22.5 %), deflated 5,101,915 → 4,666,210 B (−8.5 %).
  - **The 16 shipped files** (bytes): Linux gnu 11,952,704 baseline and 11,960,992 v3; musl 11,948,480 and 11,955,984; Windows 15,407,616 and 15,433,216; macOS x86_64 19,665,336 and 19,651,184; aarch64 9.4 / 9.4 / 11.6 / 15.3 MB.
  - **The release jar** is 57,690,314 B. Its natives deflate to 55.8 MB: baseline 35.5, v3 19.4, probes 0.9. The jar with master's 8 release-profile libraries is estimated at about 40.7 MB, so it grows by about 17 MB (1.42×; inferred, since there is no recent master jar).
- **Gates** (test VM):
  - `cargo fmt --check` passes.
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` passes.
  - `cargo test --workspace`: 966 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored.
  - `cargo deny check licenses bans`: ok.
  - `./gradlew build test`: tests=361, failures=0, errors=0, skipped=2. These include the three new variant tests, each in its own JVM:
    - `NativeVariantTest` loaded v3 and checked the probe against `/proc/cpuinfo`;
    - `NativeVariantBaselineTest` saw `forced by -Ddeeptime.natives.variant=baseline`;
    - `NativeVariantFallbackTest` saw the `v3_link` fallback.
  - `NativeLoaderTest` covers the choice on a CPU without the level (a forced v3 is refused) and the override's order.
  - `build-natives.sh`: 16 files, all checks passed (glibc floor 2.17, musl, PE, Mach-O install names, cpu level, BMI counts).
  - No GameTests (the coordinator's).
- **Choices made here** (all undoable):
  - the probe is its own crate and library;
  - schema 2 with a `variant` per library and a `probes` array;
  - a forced v3 is refused on a CPU without the level;
  - `-PbaselineNativeOnly`;
  - the `testCpuFeatures` and `forceFail=v3_link` hooks;
  - the BMI count as the v3 check, at ≥ 500 and > 4× the baseline;
  - ship only for shipping and gate builds;
  - the CI timeout of 180 min;
  - the build-time job stopped after one incremental round to free the VM.
- **PGO (#24, not done; what it would take, inferred):**
  1. An instrumented ship build per variant: `-Cprofile-generate` through the same `--config` rustflags route, because `RUSTFLAGS` is refused.
  2. Training runs of the CLI on the presets players use (quick and full 16k, both starts, 100 to 200 Myr each), on x86-64 only, so the Windows and macOS builds would reuse the Linux profile.
  3. `llvm-profdata merge` from rustc's own LLVM (rustup's `llvm-tools`).
  4. The real build with `-Cprofile-use`.

  Costs and limits:
  - The profiles go stale with every core change, so it is a per-release CI step: one instrumented build plus training, perhaps 30 to 60 runner minutes more.
  - aarch64 has no hardware here to train on.
  - BOLT on top is Linux-only.
- **GPU (wgpu) later:**
  - **Fits as is.** The CPU choice stays CPU-only: wgpu picks its adapter at runtime inside Rust. On Linux and Windows the libraries load Vulkan dynamically, and cargo-xwin's SDK has the DX12 import libraries.
  - **macOS is the awkward one.** The Metal backend links `Metal.framework` and `QuartzCore.framework` at link time. cargo-zigbuild has no Apple SDK, so the Linux cross-build cannot link it. That needs either an SDK on the build host (Apple's licence: Ben's call) or a macOS CI runner (about 10× the minutes; the free plan's 2,000 a month).
  - **Size.** wgpu inside `deeptime_jni` is carried twice on each x86-64 platform. A separate GPU library would need its own JNI class, as the probe has, or a C ABI that `deeptime_jni` opens.
- **Scratch:** `/data/ban/deeptime-runs/natives-v3/`, deleted.
- **Next:**
  1. The coordinator merges this branch, runs the GameTests, and dispatches `natives.yml` once to see the real CI time and the OS matrix with both builds.
  2. A 1000 Myr gate run of both ship builds with the commands in the gate doc.
  3. Add `crates/deeptime-cpuprobe` to CLAUDE.md's Layout list (not edited here).
### 2026-10-19: P1-19 plates part 1: the plate step's transition, record, collision and collapse in parallel, and resamplings without a new hull (profile items #2, #13, #19; agent worktree agent-a0c387a36d940833e from master be80c6c1)
- **What changed.**
  - **Commit 8faa692c (identical).**
    - `transition.rs`: the plate, eligibility and boundary scans run in parallel. Seeds come from a cube grid (`Near`) instead of a scan of all seeds. Each side's reach is a sparse multi-source Dijkstra (`geometry::dijkstra_sparse`, a thread-local scratch reset only where it was touched), and the two sides run in a `rayon::join`.
    - `collapse.rs`: the per-plate plans run in parallel and are applied in plate order.
    - `collision.rs`: the plate lookup is lazy and the flood stops once the terrane welds.
    - `rifting.rs`: `heal`'s fastest-pair scan is a parallel fold and reduce.
    - `dynamics.rs`: `record_step`'s tallies, pieces and ocean ages run in parallel.
    - `ridges::resample` takes the motion lap's all-sample tree.
    - `deeptime bench` reads `DEEPTIME_BENCH_NO_OVERLAP` (a measurement knob: the structure step after the plates' instead of beside them).
  - **Commit 6db4f51b (world-changing, bit level).**
    - Every lattice is the Fibonacci sphere turned. `Geo::build` triangulates the unturned sphere and turns it, and a resampling's lattice is `Geo::turned` from the old one (`SphereMesh::turned`). The serial hull runs once per run, not at every resampling.
    - Triangle and adjacency order follow the sphere's build, and edge lengths come from the unturned points. Only cocircular ties could flip a diagonal, and either diagonal is Delaunay.
    - New tests: `a_turned_triangulation_is_the_turned_points_own` (1,000 to 100,000 points, three rotations each, outward and locally Delaunay on the turned points), `a_turned_lattice_is_the_built_one` and `the_sparse_dijkstra_matches_the_dense_one`. Science page: plates.md "The new lattice's triangulation".
- **Seconds** (plate lap timers, `deeptime bench --preset earthlike_full_16k --start scattered_continents --length-myr 100 --threads 8` through `tools/review/bench-quiet.py`, side by side on CPU sets A and B, then swapped, on a VM loaded by other agents):

The deposit stage's cover and the bake's strata pass take them when the fingerprint matches and bake their own otherwise. Not in checkpoints. The packed horizons (30.9 MiB at 100 Myr, 39.6 MiB at 200 Myr) wait in an anonymous file in the run's folder, made like the history's spill file: in memory they sent the amplifier's last level into tiles at 100 Myr (below).

  - **#23 history spill** (deposits/recorded.rs, spill.rs, FORMAT.md): fields added to a frame already on disk are appended as a record of their own; the frame's head says which record holds each field. A checkpoint still gets each frame as one record in field order.

### 2026-10-19: P1-19 exit item 1, the climate stage takes a fifth less time (1.28x), bit-identically (coordinator's task; agent worktree agent-a9596de4877bee11c, branch worktree-agent-a9596de4877bee11c from master be80c6c1; Sonnet 5.5)
- **What changed** (all in `crates/deeptime-core/src/climate/`; Ben's 2026-10-18 rule allowed bit changes with a 100 Myr proof, but every change below came out **identical**, so no ensemble or hyps proof was needed; the two row-subtotal sums I first wrote, in `land_terms` and `snapshot::ice_cover`, changed the last bits, so I put them back to the serial order).
  - **#10, the 2-D energy balance** (`ebm2d.rs`, `ocean2d.rs`; identical). One rayon region per step instead of many: each block of rows runs the step's local terms, the atmosphere's and the slab's row sweeps and its share of the column sweeps; the two column sweeps run side by side (`rayon::join`); the ocean's sub-steps run in groups of at most `MAX_GROUP` = 4 on blocks that recompute their halo rows (`OceanTransport::sub_steps` / `substep_rows`, `SubstepRows`); the next step's local terms are fused into the last sweep; `northward` sums four edges at a time. Block size `h.div_ceil(2 * threads)`. Same expressions on the same inputs, so the bits do not move (`the_factored_solves_give_the_old_loop_bit_for_bit` now also runs a monthly-steps, multi-group case).
  - **#16, the climate ice** (`mod.rs`; identical). `land_terms` finds each land cell's runoff, kernel at its temperature and kernel at its sea-level temperature once (the kernel and the notes' loop each found them before), rows side by side, then adds in cell order. `Geometry::volume_km3`, `area_where`, `sheet_cells`, `band_share` and the tail maps run in parallel (row sums collected, added in row order; the counts are whole numbers).
  - **#14, the climate snapshot** (`snapshot.rs`, `percell.rs`, `coarse.rs`; identical). The fields only the land mask decides (land and sea nearby, basins, the continental share, each row's monthly sunlight) run in `rayon::join` beside the per-cell model and its flux fit; the orographic regimes run side by side and beside the winds' march; the march's eight blurs run side by side. The row loop finds each cell's coarse neighbours once (`CellTaps`, `MaskedTaps`: the corners and weights of `masked_at`, the same sums in the same order), each row's onshore share once per month, each cell's plateau factor once, and the sea-ice logistic's end values once (`Sharpen`). The four anomaly fields and the land sort run in parallel.
  - **#18, the climate clock** (`ice.rs`, `mod.rs`; identical). `BandMargins::new` splits the margins in 64k-cell chunks, joins each band's and sorts bands side by side (`total_cmp` is a total order, so the lists are the serial pass's). The ice sheet's inputs (`bed_fine`, the coarse bed, snow line and precipitation; the old default `500 / 1000` became `vec![0.5; n]`) are built only when `ice_dynamics` is on (off in this preset).
  - **Timers:** the snapshot's land fields now run beside the per-cell climate, and the orographic precipitation beside the winds' march, so those timers overlap and no longer add up to the snapshot's. The march has its own timer (`march`; it was inside `cells`).
- **Measured** (VM, `tools/review/bench-quiet.py`, `deeptime bench --preset earthlike_full_16k --start scattered_continents --length-myr 100 --threads 8`, master binary against this branch's, side by side on set A (0,16,2,18,4,20,6,22) and set B (8,24,10,26,12,28,14,30), then swapped; two such pairs = four master and four branch runs; climate timers from `work/t8/manifest.json` `/notes/climate/millis`). **The VM was never quiet**: others' busy CPUs averaged 12 to 22 (the quiet baseline `base100-A` had 2.1) and the runs' SMT siblings were 14 to 73 % busy, so the absolute seconds are loaded ones; only the ratios between sides of one pair are comparable. The first branch binary, with those two sums, had differed in 63 of 66 files after 100 Myr (global mean 15.0 C against 14.9, CO2 570 ppm against 551, sea level 30 m against 32 m): the carbon cycle amplifies a last-bit change in the weathering sum, which is why I put them back rather than argue it is noise. ### 2026-10-18: Resampling lumps: crust a collision had taken came back at a resampling and stacked on one column; each volume is now counted once, the belt stacks only on continental crust, and ocean floor as thick as a continent turns continental (PLT-289 to PLT-292): the loss to the mantle falls from 5.5 to 2.1 km³/yr at 500 Myr and from 8.3 to 3.0 at 1000 Myr, the rate limit's part by a factor of eight (coordinator's follow-up to the plate spikes; agent worktree agent-afb3c8f2d4d681610, branch worktree-agent-afb3c8f2d4d681610 from master 9091c163, origin/master 19cb11e0 and then 991354a4 (the polar holes) merged before the measurements; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Which process.** Not many footprints on one column. A temporary trace (not committed) sorted every resampling's accretion by what lay under the column, and by whether the column took more than 10 km at once, on the plate spikes' two traced runs (`earthlike_quick_16k`, 500 Myr, scattered seed 2 and supercontinent seed 1, master 9091c163). Of 13.8 and 9.5 × 10⁹ km³ accreted, 6.7 and 4.3 came in lumps of more than 10 km on one column. The largest parts: crust of hidden ocean floor (8.6 and 5.7, of it 3.4 and 2.0 in lumps), visible continental crust of a plate going under (2.1 and 1.8; 1.5 and 1.3 in lumps), visible ocean floor of a plate going under (1.8 and 1.2). One covered sample carried a lump: at −372 Myr on the scattered run a hidden sample labelled ocean floor held 128 km of rock (32 km metamorphic, 85 km felsic plutonic) and raised the continental column above it from 600 m to 17.9 km. Four ways put a continent's worth of crust where the accretion counted it again:
  1. The belt stacked on ocean floor. Its receivers were every sample of the overriding plate behind the front; ocean floor among them (beside a narrow continent, or an island arc) took up to 60 km of metamorphic rock, kept its room because the dampening pulled its surface back down, then subducted as ocean floor and came back at a resampling.
  2. Continental crust of the plate going under, still visible inside the overriding plate's footprint, had crossed the front and been counted by the belt; the resampling added it to the column on top as well.
  3. `stacked` (PLT-276) was cleared every step, and a terrane transfer or a weld unhid the terrane's crust, so crust that had gone under came back as the receiving plate's crust beneath its own and the next resampling accreted it.
  4. Crust stacked under the oceanic label by earlier accretions subducted as ocean floor and came back in one lump.
- **Fix** (`plates/{belts.rs, ridges.rs, subduction.rs, collision.rs, state.rs, stats.rs}`, commit 75b62645).
  - The belt's receivers are the overriding plate's continental samples only (PLT-290). PLT-243's profile and area floor are unchanged, so behind a narrow continent more of the stack goes down with the slab.
  - At a resampling, visible continental crust of a plate colliding under the column's plate is consumed, as the hidden crust of PLT-276 is, and counted with it in `resample_stacked_km3` (PLT-292).
  - `stacked` stays while the sample stays hidden; a transfer moves, and a weld unhides, only the terrane's crust that has not gone under (PLT-291).
  - Ocean floor at a contact whose crystalline crust is at least a normal continental column's (T_n, 33 km, PLT-261) turns continental before the overlaps are resolved, and then collides or moves as a terrane (PLT-289; the summary's `buoyant`). Cloos (1993) puts the buoyancy that jams a subduction zone above about 15 km of crust; at 15 km the two traced runs turned about ten times as many samples, the transition's ocean side (up to about 20 km, ocean floor by design) turned with them, and continental crust ended at 0.478 and 0.464 (master 0.394 and 0.415). So the threshold is T_n.
  - The rate limits (PLT-287, PLT-288) stay as the guard.

  The loss to the mantle falls by more than half and the six runs' ranges no longer overlap; the rate limit's part falls by a factor of about eight, the founder's is unchanged within the spread. Crust still passes the step ceilings at about half master's volume, but most of it now finds room within reach. Each crossed volume is counted once: the crust a resampling consumes as a collision's (15.6 and 21.2 km³/yr) matches what crossed a front (16.6 and 21.9), where master consumed 11.5 of 15.5 and 13.8 of 18.9 and accreted the rest again. Continental crust, land, the highest cell and the guard are the same within the spread. Against Earth (PLT-258): the founder and the rate limit lose three to four times the 0.7 km³/yr of collision zones (one and a half to two times the 1.4 at today's length); with the slab's share, about what Earth loses at all subduction zones (3.2).
- **Plate checks.** At 500 Myr the continental crust's lowest step passes (0.37 to 0.38); the collisions' median length fails (38.7 to 54.5 Myr; its runs span 27 to 85, and at 1000 Myr it passes, 36.2 to 40.7); the oceanic arc cells above sea fail (10.2 to 8.6 %; at 1000 Myr 12.9 to 10.6 %, a pass). At 1000 Myr the most land gained in one step passes (1.53 to 1.35 %) and so do the collisions per 100 Myr (1.73 to 2.17): thick island arcs and stacked ocean floor now collide instead of going under, and more plates die by welding (5.3 to 7.0 a run at 500 Myr, 17.3 to 21.7 at 1000). The continental arcs' median stands lower (941 to 709 m, 1,014 to 817 m; a fail on both sides; not traced).
- **The collision wedge's 0 km.** It comes with the rate limits, not with this change: master with the limits gives 0 km in all six runs at 500 and at 1000 Myr, and master before them gave 13 and 54 km. The fix gives 0 km in eleven of twelve runs and 94 km in one (supercontinent seed 1, 500 Myr), against 100 to 350 km on Earth (PLT-244's target). The width is the farthest incoming continental sample still below the wedge's 1.5° profile from the front (`belts.rs` `stack_front`), so it comes in steps of one sample (about 70 km on the model sphere), and a one-sample wedge needs the front to stand about 1.9 km above the incoming crust. With the uplift held to 3.5 mm/yr the front seldom does. Not fixed here: the rule is the wedge's (PLT-244), not the accretion's; a follow-up.
- **The guard's outlier, before the polar holes' fix.** On this branch before 991354a4 was merged, supercontinent seed 3 at 500 Myr met the guard at 129,576 m and spent 67 steps beyond one Earth relief. A traced rerun (a temporary print of the farthest cell, its neighbours and the plates' uplift, not committed) put every one of them on rows 323 to 326 of the 328-row surface grid: a hole of two cells deepened to 129.6 km and moved along the row while the plates' uplift there stayed between −5.9 and +3.5 mm/yr. It was the surface stage's polar-row excursion; after the merge the same run's worst is 13,602 m and no run on either side passes one relief.
- **The source behind PLT-258.** Scholl & von Huene 2009 (Geol. Soc. London Spec. Publ. 318:105, abstract read through Crossref; the paper is paywalled). The 0.7 km³/yr is the paper's figure for crust-suturing (collision) zones: c. 115 km³ Ma⁻¹ km⁻¹, "assessed far less securely", times an assumed past mean length of 6,000 km, "one-half that under way since the early Tertiary". At today's length it would be about 1.4 km³/yr (my arithmetic). The loss at all subduction zones is c. 3.2 km³/yr (2.5 of it at ocean margins, most by subduction erosion, which the plate model does not have), against 2.7 added. So the row cited the figure correctly; it now quotes the abstract and says what the 0.7 covers. Status stays `cited-unverified`, the paper `abstract-only`.

### 2026-10-18: P1-19 exit item 1, the stages of one step side by side: the structure step now runs beside the next plate step; full 16k 1.039× side by side at low load (1.010× under load), quiet 1,290.1 s, worlds identical (coordinator's task, Ben's decision of 2026-10-18; agent worktree agent-a429a6a924e26ae78, branch worktree-agent-a429a6a924e26ae78 from master 0729e267, origin/master 991354a4 merged before the measurements; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Design first** (docs/design/p1-17-benchmark-gate.md, "P1-19 exit item 1: the stages of one step side by side", committed before the code): the dependency map of a coupled step (plates, climate, surface, volcanoes, impacts, structure). Every step of the chain needs the one before it; the plate step k + 1 needs the surface's, volcanoes' and impacts' feedback of step k. The only free edge is structure k beside plates k + 1: the plate step reads neither the surface state nor the history, writes the L1 fields anew, and takes or reads only the material and the flexure of what structure reads. Also mapped, not done: deposits beside young and amplify (10 to 20 s, estimated), a keyframe beside the next step (about 10 s), the deposit stage folding in frames beside the group (up to most of its 82 s; one stage beside another, so outside this task); the climate step beside structure gains little (structure is shorter than the plate step it hides behind); the bake overlaps nothing.
- **Implementation.** `Stage` gains `steps_beside_lead`, `detach`, `step_detached` and `attach` (stage.rs). The session (session.rs) puts a follower's step off (`Stepper::pending`) and runs it at the lead's next step in a `rayon::join` inside the session's pool (`step_beside`); detach and attach run in the pool too, since they copy and pack grids in parallel (the first version ran them on the caller and `session_pool` caught it). It runs the step on the world instead where anything reads the world in between: a keyframe or epoch due after the step, `with_world`, `checkpoint`, `write_checkpoint`, the group's end (`settle_now`). The step loop's room-making, context and single step are split into `make_room`, `context` and `step_one`. `stage_sets` gives a group the lead's set plus each beside-follower's own when that is larger. `Session::set_overlap(bool)` (on by default) turns it off. `StageTiming::beside_millis`: the timings line gains `beside[structure=X.Xs]` after the `name=X.Xs/Nsteps` tokens (`tools/review/p1-24-profile.sh`'s pattern unchanged), bench.json's stages `beside_millis`; the follower's time beside is inside the lead's `millis`. The structure stage (structure/mod.rs): its step split into `step_on` (metamorphism, plutons, deformation and the history's frame fields, on what it is given), `publish` (the frame fields into the history) and `finish` (the last step's structure, bodies, events, note); its reservation moved to the start of the step, so a refusal changes nothing and the session reruns it after the join; `detach` moves out the 18 fields of `MOVED` and the pool fields, copies the material and the flexure (`alloc::copied`), takes the surface state with its strata log, and refuses the last step and the keyframe steps. Its fold and fault causes (structure/deform/mod.rs) are a `Causes` cache filled in emission order up to the events seen at detach, so the plate step's new events are not read; results equal the old scan over the world's events.
- **Test** (new crates/deeptime-core/tests/overlap.rs): the history test's planet at L1 64, 60 Myr, a frame every 6 Myr, run with the overlap off on 1 thread and on on 3 with 1 ms budgets and `with_world` every fifth call; sites, bodies, events, notes without times, the recorded history and the world's postcard bytes equal; the structure stepped beside the plates. `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo deny check licenses bans` clean on the VM after the merge of 991354a4. `memory_estimate` (dev profile): plates held 51.2 MiB against 72.8, run peak 95.6 against 97.5, resident 101.0 MiB against the 121.1 MiB bound.
- **Measured** (`tools/review/bench-quiet.py`; full 16k, scattered continents, 1000 Myr, 8 threads; master 991354a4 and the branch at cb270657 built on the VM; set A = 0,16,2,18,4,20,6,22, set B = 8,24,10,26,12,28,14,30; each pair one `deeptime-admit run --kind sim:earthlike_full_16k:16t` job, the quiet run `--kind sim:earthlike_full_16k:8t` after three minutes under load 6). Master on A, branch on B, others' load 14.6: 1,883.5 → 1,864.7 s (1.010×). Branch on A, master on B, others' load 4.8: 1,485.8 → **1,430.5 s (1.039×)**. Plates plus structure fell 49 and 60 s (estimated 45 to 65 s); the structure step spent 74 to 101 s beside the plates, and its 20 keyframe steps on the world 48 to 57 s. **Quiet, set A: 1,290.1 s** (others' load 0.0; CPU 6,111 + 337 s, 4.98 cores). Worlds: **84 of 84 files equal** in both pairs and the quiet run (`tools/review/p1-17-cmp.py`). Memory: estimate (4.86 GiB) and counted peak (4,198 MiB) unchanged; peak resident 4,239 to 4,245 → 4,495 to 4,529 MiB (+6.6 %, by inference the allocator's arenas with two stages allocating at once; still under the estimate).
- **Against the plan.** The 900 s gate stays out of reach: 1.43× quiet, 390 s left. The overlaps left (B, C, D above) are at most about 110 s at their estimates. The rest needs less work per step (Ben's call) or the one-core items inside `plates/`, `surface/` and `climate/`.
- **Coordinator's calls (undoable).** The overlap is on by default with `Session::set_overlap` to turn it off, and no CLI flag. Keyframe and last steps are not put off. The structure stage reserves before it steps, and a refused reservation beside the plates is retried after the join. The timings line's `beside[...]` token and bench.json's `beside_millis`. The `Causes` cache in deform. The overlap test's planet (L1 64, 60 Myr). The memory estimate's lead-plus-follower term. Only piece A was built; B, C and D are documented with their estimates.
- **Next step.** The coordinator merges this branch (GameTests with the batch). If the plate accretion fix lands first, merge it and re-run `tools/review/p1-17-cmp.py` on one pair. Then, for the gate, Ben's call on less work per step, or B (deposits beside young and amplify) if 10 to 20 s is worth a session mechanism for stages outside a group.
### 2026-10-18: the ice cover lies on the climate's own extent, closed on each body's balance, and is EF under it; one cover rule (nearest extent) for every reader; the -PwithEe D census miss was an untagged EE taiga (coordinator's task; agent worktree agent-a24d995879bff43ce, branch worktree-agent-a24d995879bff43ce, master 991354a4 merged, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c)
- **The two faults.** (1) The bake laid the climate's L1 ice thickness on L2 by a bilinear resample read as "ice where at least 1 m", which spread each iced L1 cell half a cell onto every bare neighbour, and the game read the layer bilinear and rounded, which spread it again (planet_world_4k: 22 % of the cover over ground whose L1 cell is warmer than 0 °C mean annual, 8 world cells at 10 °C or more). (2) L2 cells under an L1 sheet kept their own lapsed class: 189 of the 4k planet's 190 covered world cells were not EF (BWk 57, Cfb 47, BSk 42, ET 42), 21,962 of earthlike_quick_16k's 42,047.
- **Fix** (`bake/ice.rs` `downscale`, `climate::ice::surface_balance`, `bake/biomes.rs`, `deeptime_format::raster::cover_of`, Java `RasterSampler.cover`/`coverOf`, `IceCover`, `bake/project.rs` `Kind::Cover`, the workbench's map). The candidates are the L2 land cells whose nearest L1 cell holds at least 1 m of ice (BIO-082); the thickness is blended over the iced corners only, the ELA and precipitation over the finite ones. Each 4-connected body's surface balance on its own L2 ground (the climate's law, `surface_balance`, now called by the climate's published balance, the sheet model and the bake: GLA-069, GLA-070) must reach min(0, the balance of the same ice at its L1 cells' mean ground); its most negative cells are given up until it does (BIO-157). A tongue below the line stays where its body's higher cells pay for it, the way an accumulation area feeds an outlet glacier (Meier and Post 1962, Porter 1975, Osmaston 2005, Cuffey and Paterson 2010: all from memory, not read); a lagged sheet the climate already has in deficit keeps that deficit. The old ELA fallback is gone. A covered L2 cell is glaciated EF, an uncovered one keeps its own class and is not glaciated (BIO-158). The cover rule (BIO-159), one function in Rust and its arithmetic in Java: covered where the nearest cell is (as the Köppen class is read), at the weighted mean of the covered cells of the bilinear blend; the projection takes the same nearest Lambert cell `Kind::Categorical` reads for `climate/koppen_l2` and the footprint's covered samples for the depth. A first version of the rule (covered where the covered samples hold half the bilinear weight) left 646 covered world cells of another class on earthlike_quick_16k and 9 on the 4k planet (cell corners, footprint edges), so the nearest cell decides. The workbench's own ELA smoothstep and blur are gone; its nearest read breaks a tie to the later cell, as `RasterRead::nearest` does.
- **Measured** (world grid, `scratch` measure script over `deeptime run` outputs: planet_world_4k with `--placement-patch .../packs/terralith.json`; earthlike_quick_16k `--start scattered_continents --length-myr 500`; both `--threads 8`, base = master 991354a4 built from the same copy with this branch's Rust diff reversed, after = this branch with 991354a4 merged):

### 2026-10-18: The polar holes: a plate that weakened let go of its bending moment, and along a plate boundary one cell wide the moment's curvature made forces of several times the load held; it now lets go of its share of the load it held (ISO-056), and its rigidity is carried as a logarithm (ISO-075). The guard's worst over six 500 Myr runs fell from 30.8 to 15.5 km, the largest from 59.6 to 18.1 km (coordinator's task; agent worktree agent-a2d3dcd7f6d245dc3, branch worktree-agent-a2d3dcd7f6d245dc3 from master 9091c163, origin/master 19cb11e0 merged before the measurements; sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Which process.** A per-process trace of the surface stage (temporary, `DEEPTIME_PTRACE`, not committed) printed each step's largest rise and fall per process and latitude band (0, 45, 60, 70, 80°), plus the polar picks with their parts. It ran on master 9091c163 with the step records added, over the six runs below. The polar picks were the flexure's, and within it the released moment. Example: supercontinent seed 2, −290 Myr, cell (505, 9) at 70°, a craton cell that a plate boundary brought to the Te floor (5 km), released 17.2 km in one step. The other bands had the same on a smaller scale: the step records' "rest" reached 25.5 km in a step.
- **Why.** The plate carried `M = D ∇²w` and released `L((1 − r)·M)` where `D` fell to `r·D`. For a plate in balance `L(M)` is the load held from local isostasy, so where `r` is uniform the release is that share of the load. Along a boundary `r` jumps from cell to cell: a craton cell keeps (5/80)³ of its rigidity, its neighbours all of theirs. There the Laplacian of the released moment is several times the load held, with opposite signs in neighbouring cells. The polar rows get more of it, for three reasons:
  - poleward of 60° a row is taller on the planet than the plate model's samples are apart (about 71 km), so boundaries step from row to row;
  - plates carry crust about ten cells a step east to west there;
  - the linear carry of `D` read a weak cell beside a stiff one as nearly as stiff, so the next step found it weaker.
- **Fix** (`surface/flexure.rs`).
  - Where `D` fell, the force is `(1 − r) ρ_m (Q + ice − w − unsolved)` per cell (`held`, `let_go`). It equals the old release where `r` is uniform and is bounded by the cell's departure from local isostasy, the Airy limit a viscoelastic plate relaxes to (Eshagh & Tenzer 2021, Buoninfante et al. 2023: full text; Beaumont 1978: abstract).
  - `FlexState::moment` is removed. This changes the checkpoint; no compatibility kept, as the rules say.
  - The carry blends `ln D` (ISO-075).
  - `StepOut::released_m` reports the load let go.
  - Measurement only: `surface/guard.rs` `POLAR_FROM_DEG` (60°, ISO-074), `STEP_GLOBALS` and `step_extremes` (ISO-074, ISO-076); `surface/mod.rs` records them; `deeptime-cli/src/run.rs` prints `step_rise/fall_polar_m` and `step_rise/fall_rest_m` in the summary's surface line.
- **Tried** (first 110 Myr of scattered seed 1 and supercontinent seed 2, through the trace). Largest per-step total below 45°, up and down: the departure rule 4.7/4.6 and 5.2/4.5 km; with the log carry as well 4.5/4.4 and 4.8/4.6 km; no release at all (a bound) 3.7/4.4 and 4.8/4.6 km. The polar bands came to the same size. Kept: the departure rule with the log carry.
- **Test.** `a_plate_that_weakens_settles_towards_local_isostasy`: a plate bent by a disc load, then a boundary stepping between rows across it for ten steps. It asserts that no step moves the ground by more than 1.05 times the most held, that nothing goes more than a quarter of that past local isostasy, and that something is let go. The old rule fails it at step 3 (11.2 km against 8.0 km; 4.2 km past against 1.9 km). `a_moving_margin_bends_smoothly` now leaves out of its deflection check the cells where the load itself zigzags by more than 10 m (17 m at the margin's trough with the log carry). The flexure field stays checked everywhere.
- **Measured.** `earthlike_quick_16k`, 500 Myr, seeds 1 to 3, both starts; mean [min, max] over six runs. Before: 9091c163 with the step records (and the trace, which changes nothing: the guard's worst is the task's 59,631 m). After: a0b3f2f9. - **Against Earth's rates** (ISO-076, values read in the fetched texts). The fastest measured rates are exhumation 9 to 13 mm/yr (Guevara et al. 2022), denudation 8 to more than 30 mm/yr (Deng et al. 2021, abstract), rebound 11 mm/yr (Lidberg et al. 2010) and subsidence 9 to 12 mm/yr (Brothers et al. 2009). Over millions of years the surface moves more slowly: the Altiplano rose 0.4 to 0.9 mm/yr (Garzione et al. 2008), and a basin's tectonic subsidence totals 3 to 4 km (Xie & Heller 2009). Before the fix a cell rose 39 km in a step, 20 mm/yr held for 2 Myr. After it the largest change is 9.7 km a step (4.9 mm/yr), and nothing stood farther from the sea than 18.1 km.

### 2026-10-18: the admission tool measured nested jobs at 0.0 cores and 0.0 GiB (coordinator's follow-up; agent worktree agent-acb1f30bcb635c94e, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c)
- **Cause** (`tools/remote/vm/admit.py`, `Sampler.attributed`). Each job's sampler took off the trees of every other admitted job (`exclude_roots` = their admit.py pids). When a script run through admission starts sims through admission with `env -u DEEPTIME_ADMIT_JOB` (force-balance-ensemble.sh, margin-runs.sh, `full.sh`), the inner job's ancestor is the outer job's admit.py, so "take off the outer's whole tree" took off the inner job's own tree: `run:earthlike_quick_16k:4t` finished with 0.00 cores and 0.02 GiB (the 0.02 is the first sample, taken before any exclusion), 20 runs each; the estimate became 0.0 and the kind started whatever the load. The same hit a launcher that takes over a server job's slot (`smoke:*`, `gametest:*` inside `mac.sh --server`): its host's admit.py was its ancestor. The outer job was wrong the other way: the final sample passed no exclusions, and when an inner job ended, its whole life reached the outer's shell as cutime, so `shell:full.sh` read 13 cores mean with p90 0.0 and peak 32 (double counted).
- **Fix, design choice: the outer job does not count the inner job's processes, and the inner job counts its own.** The sampler takes off only the jobs that are not its ancestors (ancestry recorded while the root lives, with start times, so a reused pid takes nothing off); the final sample uses the same exclusions as the loop; and an inner job's processes that end are taken off the outer's CPU delta (their reaper, the outer's shell, carries their life in cutime). Chosen over "the outer counts everything and the inner counts nothing" because each kind has to learn its own load: the sim estimate is what gates the next sim, and the wrapper's estimate is what gates the next wrapper. Known residue: what an inner job did after the outer's last look at it (one `SAMPLE_S`) still reaches the outer as one blip (a few core-seconds per inner job; in the VM check below, 3 inner jobs of 2 cores at SAMPLE_S 2 gave the outer a 6-core peak sample, 0.48 mean over 25 s; negligible over a 15-minute outer).
- **Implausible measurements are not recorded.** A run of 60 s or more with a mean under 0.05 cores and a peak RSS under 0.05 GiB (`IMPLAUSIBLE_S`, `IMPLAUSIBLE_CORES`, `IMPLAUSIBLE_GIB`) is not recorded; the stderr line and the `finished` log line say "cannot be right, the measurement lost the job's processes". 0.05 GiB and not 0.0, because the broken runs showed 0.02 GiB from the first sample; a bare interpreter is ~0.005, so a real job is far above. Side effect: a genuinely idle waiter job over a minute (shell:... that only sleeps) is not recorded either and keeps its seed (1 core, 1 GiB), the safe side.
- **Tests** (`tools/remote/vm/test_admit.py`, 46 tests, 0 failed; the five new or strengthened ones fail on the old admit.py with `0.0 not greater than 0.6`): a nested job measured on its own processes with the outer not counting it; attribution skips outer jobs, takes off inner ones and ignores a stale pid; the nested server launcher's record has CPU and RSS; implausible runs are not recorded and the log says so; an idle run end to end.
- **Verified on the VM** from the synced copy with a scratch state directory (`DEEPTIME_ADMIT_CACHE`/`DEEPTIME_ADMIT_DIR`), not the installed tool: an outer admitted script running three admitted 2-process busy loops of 20 s: inner jobs 1.60 to 1.61 cores mean, 2.0 peak, 0.04 GiB; outer 0.48 mean. Not installed on the VM: the coordinator installs after the merge (`tools/remote/vm/install.sh`). The kinds already forgotten stay empty until new runs record.
### 2026-10-18: a leached cap holds no copper, and `-PwithEv` passes again (coordinator's follow-up to the gossan task; agent worktree agent-a3957099ec4d835ad, branch worktree-gossan-cap-holds-no-ore from master 20272e83, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c)
- **The failure.** `-PwithEv` failed 88 of 90 since the gossan merge (27f44a4e): `evVariantWhenInstalled` and `bodyHasOre` (132 blocks). `GossanSkin` paints the ironstone cap (fallback `minecraft:red_sandstone`) onto the ground over the porphyry; `DepositFeature` took the painted block as host rock and placed Excavated Variants' red-sandstone copper; `StrataPass.predictedRock` did not know the skin. Only EV has a copper block per host rock, so standalone could not see it.
- **The rule** (coordinator's call, decisions log 2026-10-18; ledger DEP-212): a leached cap holds none of the porphyry's ore. SIR 2010-5070-B p. 67 and p. 120 put the copper in the blanket at the top of the water table, not in the cap above it; Cook and Porter 2005 PDF p. 14 give Silver Bell's 30 m remnant leached capping as "averaged 300 ppm Cu" (about 0.03 % against the median 0.44 % Cu of DEP-002). The sources say depleted; the game reads it as none (`game-choice`). The gossan's own gold zone (`gossan_gold`, density 0.02) and a placer's gold stay: leaching removes copper, and a placer's gravel is not the cap.
- **How the cap is named** (DEP-213, `game-choice`). The ore step cannot read the skin back: carvers and earlier features have changed the column. `GossanSkin.Caps` is a pure window of the column, `ground + 3` down to `ground - thickness - 2`, from the ground the terrain model gives (`Water.topBlock(Water.cellSurface(...))`); the skin hangs its cap from the ground it finds clamped to the model's ground plus or minus 3 (`GROUND_MARGIN`), so every repainted block is inside the window. In the test world the clamp held 0 of 1,631 capped columns (the model agrees with the generated ground to within 3 blocks there), and `gossanCapHoldsNoOre` fails if it holds more than a quarter. `DepositFeature` skips `caps.holdsNoOre` cells for every body that is not loose rock (a placer) and not a gossan.

- **Which process.** The gap budget now keeps a spike record (`plates/gap_budget.rs`, PLT-283): for every bracketed process of a plate step, the largest rise and thickening one visible column took from it, and how many column-steps fell in the bands 5, 10, 20 and 30 km. A temporary per-step print (`DEEPTIME_SPIKE_TRACE`, not committed) gave the step and cell. Runs: `earthlike_quick_16k`, 500 Myr, scattered seed 2 and supercontinent seed 1, master's binary with only the reports added (`build/spikes/trace.sh`, scratch, each sim admitted on its own, `deeptime stage volcanoes` with `DEEPTIME_GAP_BUDGET=1`).

  | Process | Largest rise in one step | Largest thickening in one step | Column-steps rising over 10 km |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | A resampling's accretion (PLT-284) | 35.8 km, 33.2 km | 526 km, 566 km | 2,697, 1,272 |
  | Collision belts and wedge | 13.1 km, 9.9 km | 94 km, 77 km | 5, 0 |
  | Founder (its receivers) | 5.8 km, 6.0 km | 42 km, 42 km | 0 |
  | Collapse (its receivers) | 4.3 km, 4.3 km | 30 km, 30 km | 0 |
  | Hotspots, arcs, transition, the rest | 1.2 km or less | 3.7 km or less | 0 |

  Every step whose largest rise passed 20 km (21 and 16 of 250) was a resampling. So was each run's final peak (29,181 and 26,984 m): the run ends with a forced resampling, and two steps before it the highest cell stood at 5.6 km. The accretion hands one column the crust of every footprint under it at once. The surface's flexure then turns the lift into the 50 to 100 km the guard met (ISO-072).
- **Physical?** None of the large spikes. On Earth crust thickens at dH/dt = u·H/W (Garzione et al. 2006, EPSL 241:543, eq. 2, full text read): about 1.7 mm/yr for the Altiplano. Southern Tibet thickened by about 40 km at about 1.3 mm/yr between 60 and 30 Ma (Sundell et al. 2021, GSA Today 31(6), full text read). The fastest surface uplift Garzione et al. report is 2.5 to 3.5 km in 1 to 4 Myr (0.6 to 3.5 mm/yr), and it needed the removal of eclogitic lower crust. The accretion's 36 km in a step is 18 mm/yr of uplift, and its 566 km is seven times the thickest crust on Earth. The wedge's 94 km is 47 mm/yr of thickening, about 35 times Tibet's. The belt's 13 km is 6.5 mm/yr of uplift. The founder's and collapse's rises (2.9 and 2.2 mm/yr) are within Garzione's range, but their receivers thickened by up to 21 mm/yr.
- **Fix** (`plates/rate.rs`, new; `collapse.rs` `spread`, `sink`, `held`; `ridges.rs` carries the limits across the resampling; `mod.rs` calls `rate::begin`, `limit` and `end`).
  - When a step begins, every sample keeps T₀ and z₀. Its ceiling is T₀ + `thickening_max_mm_yr` (5) × δt (PLT-287, `game-choice`: about three times the regional rates, for one lattice column over one step). Its top is z₀ + `uplift_max_mm_yr` (3.5) × δt (PLT-288, `verified`: Garzione's fastest).
  - After the thickening processes, and again after a resampling's accretion (limits blended with the column's own resampling weights), a visible column above its ceiling moves the excess to the nearest room on its plate within `collapse_reach_km`. Continental crust fills up to `crust_max_km` and ocean floor up to the normal column, each under its own ceiling. What finds no room goes from the bottom of the column to the mantle (`collapse::sink`, as PLT-258).
  - A column that releases crust sinks by its Airy change, never below z₀. No visible column ends higher than its top: one lifted faster is left below its Airy height and rises the rest in later steps.
  - The collapse's and the founder's receivers fill only up to their ceilings.
  - Counted as the gap budget's `rate` part and in the run summary's `rate_capped_km3`, `rate_lost_km3` and `rate_held_km3`. 0 for either parameter turns that limit off.
  - The surface guard now also counts steps beyond 1, 2, 3 and 6 Earth reliefs and the worst it met (`surface/guard.rs`, ISO-073; the summary's `guard_worst_m` and `guard_steps_over_1/2/3/6_reliefs`).
- **Measured.** `earthlike_quick_16k`, seeds 1 to 3, both starts, master (m0: 10c92fe4 with only the reports) against the fix (f2); mean [min, max] over six runs. Ensembles: `tools/remote/detach.sh start ens-<tag>-<len> tools/review/force-balance-ensemble.sh <dir> <bin> <500|1000> 1,2,3 scattered_continents,supercontinent ck <tag>`, then `tools/review/p1-17-hyps.py <dir> <len> "1 2 3" "scattered_continents supercontinent" <tag>`. The young-stage and amplifier peaks come from full `deeptime run`s (`build/spikes/full.sh`, scratch, each run admitted on its own).

  At 500 Myr the fix's CO₂ is lower because the present-day nudge raised it less (its factor 5.31 on master, 1.24 with the fix); why master's runs needed more was not traced. At 1000 Myr the two are inside the spread.
- **Plate checks.**
  - At 500 Myr the fix passes four that master fails: rift-born plates welded back within 50 Myr (10.8 to 6.6 %), the collisions' median length (57 to 45 Myr), speed against plate area (rho −0.41 to −0.38) and oceanic arc cells above sea level (9.7 to 10.3 %). It fails two that master passes: the collisions' 90th percentile length (91 to 132 Myr) and supercontinent tenure (103 to 98 Myr).
  - At 1000 Myr the only verdict that changes is the most land gained in one step: 1.12 to 1.64 % of the planet, against at most 1.5. Not traced; a likely reading is that crust a resampling used to pile on one column now spreads over its ring and lifts more cells above the sea at once.
  - The wedge's width is 0 km in every fixed run (master 13 and 54 km, both far below the 100 to 350 km target), probably because its thickening, up to 94 km a step on master, is now held to 10 km.
- **What is left.**
  - More crust goes to the mantle. Where no room is within reach (about one ring of samples at 16k), the excess sinks. The total loss rose from 4.1 to 6.1 km³/yr (500 Myr) and from 6.6 to 8.5 (1000 Myr), against about 0.7 at Earth's collision zones (PLT-258, Scholl & von Huene 2009 as cited there). Continental crust ends 0.013 and 0.028 lower. Follow-up: a wider reach for the release, or a resampling accretion that does not stack every footprint on one column.
  - The surface stage's own excursions are untouched. A polar row of L1 rose 20 to 40 km over a few steps with plate uplift of 2.2 km or less, on master and with the fix. The fixed run with the largest worst (supercontinent seed 2, 500 Myr, 59,631 m) was traced again with the deepest cell printed (`build/spikes/trace.sh` on a binary with a temporary print, not committed): the worst was a hole, not a peak. Two neighbouring cells of one row near the pole (rows 8 to 15) went from 17.1 km below the sea at −290 Myr (beside a cell at +17.3 km) to 59.7 km below at −274, and back to 18.7 km below by −264, moving east along the row. The plates raised those cells by 0.3 to 2.0 km a step, and from −288 on the highest cell anywhere stayed between 5.9 and 10.5 km, with no plate step lifting a cell more than 5.8 km. So it is the surface stage on its polar rows, both up and down (a follow-up, outside the plate model).

Jobs of those kinds now start whatever the load. The cause, in `admit.py`'s measurement of nested jobs, was not traced.
