### 2026-10-18: The conveyor sank 30 Sv on one coarse cell: a sinking region now carries only what its open sea can cool, which ends the 634 m/yr of runoff and the weathering kernel at 1.3e8 times Earth's on `earthlike_quick_16k` (coordinator's task, found by the erosion-recalibration agent; agent worktree agent-a49de89b4df643387, branch worktree-agent-a49de89b4df643387 from master 80f72bb0, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; origin/master 8b2cfb83 merged; not merged)
- **The bug, reproduced** on master 80f72bb0: the report's figure comes out exactly in the 500-Myr run (supercontinent, seed 1): at −50 Myr the land's mean runoff 633.9 m/yr and the kernel 1.32e8 × `KERNEL_EARTH` (CLM-061), then CO₂ 574 → 126 ppm in one step. The 1000-Myr run blows up at other times (up to 3,710 m/yr at −552 Myr). The supply limit (CLM-152 to CLM-157) caps the weathering, so CO₂ looked plausible.
- **Cause, with evidence.** `ocean2d.rs` sank the whole conveyor (30 Sv, CLM-131) in the narrowest polar-connected basin (CLM-132), whatever the size of its sinking region (its ice-free sea poleward of 50°). A narrow inlet reaching just past 50° won with 1 to 20 coarse cells, and those cells took the heat of cooling 30 Sv (about 1 PW): their sea tiles went to 90–800 °C, the coast blend carried it to the land, and the belts' e^(0.07 ΔSST) rain (MOI-063) and the kernel's e^(0.09 (T − 15)) did the rest. Temporary diagnostics (removed) per step and snapshot: in master's 1000-Myr run every snapshot with a blown-up cell sank on 1 to 20 cells, its hottest sea tile in or beside the sinking region; the others sank on 27 to 339 cells with their hottest sea tropical and at most about 38 °C. Over six 500-Myr master runs: regions of 1–9 cells overheated (a sea tile over 45 °C) in 16 of 17 snapshots, 10–19 in 11 of 15, 20–29 in 6 of 10, 30–38 in 4 of 13, 39–49 in 0 of 10, 50 or more in 1 of 263.
- **Fix** (`ocean2d.rs`: `SINK_RATE_M_S` 8e-6 m/s, CLM-204; `Sinking.sea_km2`, also in the snapshot's sinking note). By Walin's (1982, from memory) water-mass transformation a region of open sea A sinks at most A w_max; only basins that can carry all of Ψ compete for the narrowest, and when none can, the roomiest sinks what it carries. 8e-6 m/s is about 260 W/m² cooling the water by 8 K; Earth's North Atlantic sinks its 30 Sv at 4.7e-6 (it could carry 51 Sv), and 30 Sv needs about 39 quick-planet coarse cells, the size below which master's regions overheated.
- **Tests.** `ocean2d::tests::a_sinking_region_carries_only_what_its_sea_can_cool` (the rule and its fallback on a test sea); `climate::tests::a_narrow_inlet_past_the_sinking_latitude_keeps_the_climate_physical` (the idealised planet with an inlet to 56° N, belts and upwind rain: every cell's annual rain and runoff under 15 m/yr and annual mean under 45 °C, CLM-205). On master's `ocean2d.rs` it fails (the conveyor sinks 30 Sv on the inlet's two cells at 51° N; 258 °C, 3.5e10 mm a year); with the fix it passes. `the_climate_runs_in_the_coupled_pipeline_and_resumes` now holds every series row's land runoff under 15 m/yr and kernel under 100 × Earth's. The ceilings: the WMO records table (as of 31 July 2025; Mawsynram 11.872 m a year over 38 years, read), 45 °C over Dallol's ~35 (from memory), 100 × a test bound.
- **Measured** (`deeptime stage volcanoes --preset earthlike_quick_16k --start <s> --length-myr <L> --threads 8 --set seed=<n> --climate-json …` through `detach.sh`, admitted `sim:earthlike_quick_16k:8t`; master = the same tree with master's `ocean2d.rs` and `snapshot.rs`). On 80f72bb0, six 500-Myr runs (supercontinent and scattered continents, seeds 1 to 3), master / fix: steps with a cell over 15 m/yr or 45 °C 84 of 1,500 in five runs / 0; worst cell rain 8.2e9 / 10,610 mm a year; worst cell T 234 / 39.2 °C; highest land runoff 634 / 0.66 m/yr; highest kernel 1.6e11 / 1.93. With the fix no snapshot fell back below 30 Sv (0 of 318), the smallest region was 41 cells and the hottest sea 43.6 °C. The 1000-Myr report case: 33 of 500 steps / 0, worst cell 3.2e11 mm and 286 °C / 9,174 mm and 32.8 °C. On today's master 8b2cfb83 it is worse: 23 of 500 steps with a land-mean runoff over 15 m/yr or a kernel over 100 ×, up to 2.7e6 m/yr and 8.0e17, CO₂ down to 7 ppm and five snowballs (−378 to −304 Myr) straight after such steps; with the fix 0 steps, at most 0.72 m/yr and 3.2 ×, CO₂ at least 599 ppm, no snowball.

Where two classes meet, the mean of their code indices names a class neither has (BSk 7 beside Cfa 14 passes through Csa 8, Csb 9, Csc 10). The census, the families, the forbidden lists and the biome rules' `koppen` conditions (Expanded Ecosphere's rule file) all read this layer. A diagnostic dump of the 383 Cs columns (not committed) showed 118 of them Csc, a class the bake barely places, and the shrubland misses with the humidity of the class next door (raw vegetation median -0.09, where the Mediterranean squeeze gives -0.94 to -0.61). Of the 137, 45 lie under the ice cover and 2 of them are on the table's biomes: the bake holds glaciated land in the frozen band whatever its class (BIO-035) and the ice pass covers it, so the table's Cs rule never places them (26 carry the bake's frozen cap: L2 cells lapsed to their own ground at 490 to 1,630 m, Csa or Csb, under L1 cells at a mean annual -18 to +3 °C, median -11 °C, whose ice keeps them cold; the other 19 are the cover's fringe). The pack checks now leave the ground under the ice cover out (`left_out_glaciated` in the JSON), as the forbidden families already split it: Cs 74 of 92 (0.804) on the dump. Not (c): no single merge did it; the averaging is as old as the layer, and the CLM-203 planet's class borders put more columns on the invented classes.

Expanded Ecosphere's `wythers:ice_cap` surface rule paints ice over packed ice (column (136,152): 74 ice, 71 to 73 packed ice, stone below), and vanilla's frozen peaks paint ice patches on stone, so a pack's glacier biome lost the cover; the new planet put one of the test's columns there. The test's own message hid it: with no snow near the top it walked six blocks down and reported the stone. Fix: ice is a lake's only with water under it or where the lake ice rule names the block as a frozen lake's top (`LakeIce.ices`, the rule `WaterBodies` ices by, which also covers a lake a block deep whose ice lies on its bed); `IcePass.apply(chunk, wd, reach)` passes that rule from the generator, the two-argument form none. The test reports the top when no snow is near it, counts a frozen lake's ice the same way, and names the biome in its message; `icePassLaysTheCover` gained the two cases (the pack's ice on packed ice takes the cover; a lake a block deep keeps its ice); `LakeIceTest` checks `ices` in a world without the rule. ### 2026-10-18: The surface divergence on large planets: the plateau spreading's root no longer bends the plate (ISO-070), and a guard stops a diverged surface at twelve Earth reliefs from the sea (ISO-071, ISO-072) (coordinator's task; agent worktree agent-ad323cd80f2e3f576, branch worktree-agent-ad323cd80f2e3f576 from master 27f44a4e, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Cause.** The surface step splits the plateau spreading (implicit diffusion above the strength height h_s, about 5.1 km, D = D₀ min(x, 2)³, in the map's metres) from the flexure (Earth-normalized lengths). The spreading's root went into `bend_part`, the root that bends the plate. On a stiff plate the flexure holds a thickening up as T = u / (1 − k), about 7u, so a mode the spreading lowers by λ/(1 + λ) is then amplified: the per-mode gain is 1 − Fλ/(1 + λ), unstable above λ ≈ 0.4. λ for a checkerboard grows with the cell's size in metres. At 1:100 the spreading holds plateaus at h_s, where D is nearly nil. On the Earth-sized planet (1,222.5 m a block, 39 km cells) the spreading is 144 times weaker per cell, the plate model lifts cells far above h_s (D up to 8 D₀), and λ for a checkerboard reaches about 2.5. Traced with a temporary per-phase print (not committed) on `earthlike_quick_32k` at 1,222.5 m a block, scattered start, 100 Myr. It starts with a plate-model spike (one cell to 9.2 km, 4.6 mm/yr) 40 Myr in. Then, 30 to 50 Myr in, a craton (Te 80 km, no uplift) holds a checkerboard in which the spreading lowers a peak by 8.7 km and raises its neighbour by 12.8 km, and the flexure turns these into −47 and +56 km. The solve converges in 12 to 14 iterations: the coupling is what is unstable. With the spreading off, the same planet stays near 14 km; with the flexure off, 6.6 km. 1:300 has the milder form: the median step's highest cell after the flexure was 11.6 km (6.0 after the fix), against 6.7 km at 1:100 (5.8 after).
- **Fix** (`surface/flexure.rs`, ISO-070). `bend_part` is now only the binomially filtered `plate_root`. The spreading's load and root still enter the plate's load (they cancel in the residual) and the gap budget, but its root stays locally compensated. The spreading's thin-channel law is itself the locally compensated answer of the lower crust's flow (from memory of Clark & Royden 2000, not read). Substepping the spreading was not used: it would only move the threshold.
- **Guard** (`surface/guard.rs`, new; called in `surface/mod.rs` after the flexure, every step). A cell that is not finite, or stands farther from the sea than 12 × (Everest 8,848.86 m + the Challenger Deep 10,925 m) × max(1, g_E / g), stops the run. That is 237,286 m at 1 g and 624,438 m at 0.38 g. The error names the time, the cell, its height, the bound and the science page. It is a stop, not a clamp. ISO-071 is `verified`: Dangol et al. 2020 and Stewart & Jamieson 2019, both read in full; bibliography Dangol2020 and StewartJamieson2019. ISO-072 is a game choice (the margin). Five Earth reliefs was tried first. It stopped a shipped bake on a plate-model transient (`earthlike_quick_16k`, scattered, seed 2, −272 Myr, 105,755 m), hence twelve.
- **Demo.** With the old coupling and the guard, the Earth-sized planet's 500 Myr bake stops after 92 s, at −388 Myr, at cell (797, 120), 263,824 m, exit 1. Unguarded, that bake ran 3.56 h to 3.3 × 10²⁹ m.
- **Measured, the three scales** (`earthlike_quick_32k`, 500 Myr, scattered start, the preset's seed). Each run was made with `build/diverge/trace-run.sh <m_per_block> 500 <tag>` (scratch: the preset with `scale.m_per_block_h` set, run through `deeptime run`) through `detach.sh`.

  | Scale | Before: land, peak, above 2 km | After: land, peak, above 2 km |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1:1221 | diverged (3.3 × 10²⁹ m, 3.56 h, one 146 min step in `marine::fill`) | 0.265, 23,507 m, 0.345 (p90 5,231 m); 738 s |
  | 1:300 | 0.231, 26,950 m, 0.228 | 0.278, 36,813 m, 0.181 |
  | 1:100 | 0.177, 23,319 m, 0.284 | 0.200, 14,428 m, 0.334 |

  Single runs differ more than the fix. The surface feeds the plates, so each run is a different planet, and the shipped scale was compared on an ensemble.
- **Measured, `earthlike_quick_16k`** (the shipped preset, 1:300): `T=2 tools/review/force-balance-ensemble.sh <dir> <bin> 500 1,2,3 scattered_continents,supercontinent hyps <b|f> +DEEPTIME_GAP_BUDGET=1`, then `tools/review/p1-17-hyps.py`. Six runs each; means, ranges in brackets.

  | | Land | Median height | p90 | Above 2 km | Peak mean (max) | CO₂ |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Master | 0.195 [0.174, 0.212] | 792 m | 3,720 m | 0.249 [0.201, 0.300] | 26,560 m (34,130) | 2,372 ppm |
  | Fix | 0.188 [0.148, 0.214] | 720 m | 3,477 m | 0.225 [0.155, 0.368] | 26,395 m (33,858) | 3,081 ppm |

  The differences are inside the run-to-run spread. Master matches the recalibration's numbers (0.194, 796 m, 0.251).
- **What is left.** The plate model now and then lifts a patch by tens of km in one step: up to 16.5 mm/yr, 33 km a step over hundreds of cells, against its 30 km ceiling (ISO-025). The flexure then holds part of the root up for a step or two. These spikes are scale-independent and there before and after the fix. The highest cell after the flexure, in four traced 500 Myr runs (`build/diverge/spikes.py` over the traces), was 112 km (1:300) and 66 km (1:100) before the fix, 69 and 92 km after; steps over 30 km at 1:300 went from 20 to 6. The 237 km bound sits above them and above the about 210 km a sound step could reach (7 × the 30 km ceiling). Which plate process makes the spikes was not traced.
- **`marine::fill`.** The 146 min step is gone; it came from the diverged heights. At 1:1221, `marine_fill` still takes 83.9 s of the surface's 268.9 s over 250 steps, against 1.7 to 3.2 s at 1:300 and 1:100. That cost tracks volume: 3.5 × 10⁹ km³ to the sea against 1.6 × 10⁸ (22 ×), and 13,084 basins against 743. Left to the surface-speed work; nothing changed here.
- **Tests.** `surface::flexure::tests::the_spreading_on_a_stiff_plate_does_not_grow_a_checkerboard`: 39 km cells, a plateau at three times h_s with a ±300 m checkerboard. It now flattens; on the old code the plateau's range leaves 13,188 to 16,812 m in the first step. `surface::tests::a_planet_of_large_cells_keeps_its_surface_physical`: the small coupled planet, seed 11, 1,221 m a block, 100 Myr, 30 s. Every cell must stay within twice Earth's relief of the sea; it ends at 4.0 km, and the old code fails at "the surface spans -21741 to 29927 m from the sea". `surface::guard::tests::a_surface_past_any_planets_relief_stops_the_run`. Both new tests fail on the old coupling: `build/diverge/gates.sh` puts the old line back on the VM copy.
- **Science.** flexure.md: the ISO-070 to ISO-072 rows, "Why it exists", "The surface guard", "What is left, and why the margin is wide", and an open question on the spikes. The design doc flexure.md §14 holds the full trace. Ledger ISO-070 (`game-choice` numerics, its physical reading `from-memory`), ISO-071 (`verified`), ISO-072 (`game-choice`); bibliography Dangol2020 and StewartJamieson2019, and ClarkRoyden2000 now cites ISO-070. Ran `claims_counts.py --write` (2,542 active rows, 295 verified).
- **Files touched.** `crates/deeptime-core/src/surface/flexure.rs`, `surface/guard.rs` (new), `surface/mod.rs` (two lines), `surface/tests.rs` (one test appended), `docs/science/flexure.md`, `docs/design/flexure.md`, `docs/science/ledger/ISO.md`, `docs/science/claims.md`, `docs/science/bibliography.md`, STATUS.md. No surface module other than `flexure.rs` changed, and nothing in `marine`, the stream power or the spreading itself.

Both will refine as real runs come in, or their history can be dropped from the admission tool's store.
- **Choices made without asking (all can be undone; the coordinator's call).**
  - The spreading's root kept local rather than substepping the spreading.
  - The guard as a stop after the flexure, not a clamp, in a new module.
  - Twelve Earth reliefs (five tripped a shipped bake).

### 2026-10-18: The temperate present counts ice sheets: the present-day nudge's land-ice target reads land under bodies of at least 50,000 km² (Cogley et al. 2011), mountain ice left out (coordinator's task; agent worktree agent-a4f01237ab69a22b1, branch worktree-agent-a4f01237ab69a22b1, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; on the erosion recalibration e81b4946 with origin/master 80f72bb0 merged for the decision; not merged: it lands with plate task 8 and the recalibration)
- **Decision** (the coordinator's call, decisions log 2026-10-18): CLM-150's temperate 0.15 and ice-age 0.25 count ice sheets only, as Earth's ~0.10 does; mountain ice is defined from a source, not a height cut.
- **The definition (CLM-203, `verified`).** Cogley et al. 2011, the glossary of glacier mass balance, p. 53, "Ice sheet": "An ice body that covers an area of continental size, generally defined as covering 50 000 km2 or more" (NSIDC the same). In the code (`climate::ICE_SHEET_MIN_KM2`, `Geometry::sheet_cells`): a body is the land cells with at least 1 m of ice (ICE_MIN_M) joined by shared edges, the rows wrapping east to west; a body of 50,000 km² or more (Earth-normalized; about 33 L1 cells on `earthlike_quick_16k`) is a sheet, the rest mountain ice. Earth's figures, read: NSIDC 10 % of the land under glacial ice today, about 32 % at the last glacial maximum; Antarctica almost 14 million km², Greenland 1.7 million; the RGI (which "excludes the ice sheets of Greenland and Antarctica") about 706,000 km² (6.0 and 7.0 terminus-type rows summed), about 0.5 % of the land (the land's 149 million km² from memory).
- **Code.** The present's trials (`climate/mod.rs`) read the sheet share from the trial's own ice (`IceRun` now keeps `in_window` and the band lines: in the window the ice thickness, outside it the land above the shifted line), band-weighted on the window's starting land like the total; `reach` uses it for both Temperate (at most) and IceAge (at least). The clock's physics (albedo, weathering, the ice load) still use all of the land ice; nothing before the last 100 kyr changes. ### 2026-10-17: Plate task 8: the crust budget on sourced rates, with the gap budget's recommendations 1, 3 and 6 (coordinator's task; agent worktree agent-aae15c33270dffe0b, branch worktree-agent-aae15c33270dffe0b, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; base master 7827e9f0; not merged: it lands only together with the erosion recalibration, which goes on top of this branch)
- **What.** (1) *Island arcs* at Stern & Scholl's 100 km³ per km of arc and Myr (PLT-045), times the convergence factor, over the arc band (940 m a Myr at the axis at full convergence), standing up on the ocean's height line by the crust they add; only an oceanic slab makes an arc; they turn continental at 15 km of crust (Cloos 1993, PLT-047), not after 20 Myr. (2) *Continental arcs* at 35 km³ per km and Myr (PLT-285, new knob `continental_arc_km3_per_km_myr`, editor field `continental_arc`), standing up by their Airy change towards the column's Airy height. Into the pools: continental arcs 1 in 8 felsic volcanic (7:1), island arcs 1 in 6 volcanic (5:1, two thirds of it mafic), the rest felsic plutonic (PLT-046). (3) *The cordillera by shortening* (PLT-048 to PLT-050, HYP-018): pure shear at `cordillera_shortening_mm_yr` (6 in the earthlike and pipeline presets and `planet_world_4k`; 0 in the plates presets and the default), its volume taken pool by pool from the same plate's continental crust 440 to 800 km behind the front, so moved, not made; the root from an uplift (PLT-051, merged into PLT-048) and both height-only arc uplifts (HYP-017, PLT-044) are gone. (4) *Cones are rock* (PLT-286): the volcano stage's stratovolcanoes, silicic centres and ignimbrites hand felsic volcanic rock to the pools, shields and flood basalts mafic volcanic (`surface/volcanoes` hands them over through the plate model's cones), counted inside the arc and hotspot rates (once per contact and per hotspot), and MV joins the erosion order. (5) *Accretion stands up* (PLT-284): a visible continental column that receives crust at a resampling rises by the Airy change of the crust added, capped at its Airy height, handed to the surface as uplift; `ACCRETED_GLOBAL` counted in the crust budget. (6) *A held ocean floor* (PLT-264): oceanic samples cool towards the floor their own crust holds up on the ocean's line, capped at 20 km of crystalline crust (about −2,540 m). New run-summary globals: `cordillera_shortened_km3`, `resample_accreted_visible_km3`, `resample_accreted_rise_km3`, `hotspot_magma_km3`, `cone_felsic_km3`, `cone_mafic_km3`, `arc_front_continental_km_myr`, `arc_front_oceanic_km_myr`; `tools/review/crust-budget.py` prints them as rates. Science: `docs/science/plates.md` "The crust budget on sourced rates"; ledger PLT-284 to PLT-286 and HNT-125 to HNT-127 new, PLT-044 to PLT-051, PLT-264, HYP-017, HYP-018, PRS-015 to PRS-017, PRS-038, PRS-039 changed; `docs/design/plate-force-balance.md` task 8.

### 2026-10-17: The land's gap budget: which process takes a continental column's height and leaves its crust (coordinator's follow-up "Measure which process lowers a continental column's surface faster than it thins it"; agent worktree agent-a1c34919ad14af84e, branch worktree-agent-a1c34919ad14af84e, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; master 68d95f44 merged, then 2c448f9e and f6703ee0; not merged)
- **What.** A measurement, no physics changed. `plates/gap_budget.rs` (PLT-283, on with `DEEPTIME_GAP_BUDGET=1`) keeps each sample's gap, its elevation less the Airy height of its own column (`collapse::iso_height`), split into 27 parts by the process that changed it: every process of a plate step, the surface's feedback (erosion and deposition, their local rebound, the local answer to the sea water and ice, the flexure's regional answer to those loads, the flexure's bending of the plate model's roots, its answer to the moment a weakened plate releases, the rest of the flexure, the spreading, what the volcano stage and the impacts add after the surface stage (`surface/gap_later_m`), the carry) and a resampling's blend and accretion; each part keeps what of it was made on the ocean floor. The run summary prints a stock and a rate (gap, elevation, Airy height) per thickness band every 50 Myr; `tools/review/gap-budget.py` makes the tables. The loads', roots' and released moment's parts of the flexure are three extra solves of the same operator (`flexure::StepIn::parts`, at a tenth of the step's tolerance), only with the variable set. The parts add up to the gap in every run (worst residual 0.0 m, no restarts) and the budget changes nothing (`the_gap_budget_changes_nothing_and_adds_up`; the split runs' land equals the plain runs'). Science page: plates.md, "Which process holds the gap (the gap budget, 2026-10-17)".
- **Measured** (`earthlike_quick_16k`, `tools/review/force-balance-ensemble.sh <out> <bin> <500|1000> <seeds> scattered_continents,supercontinent hyps gb +DEEPTIME_GAP_BUDGET=1` through `tools/remote/detach.sh`, then `python3 tools/review/gap-budget.py --t 0 <summaries>`). 40–55 km crust, a third of the continental samples, 500 Myr, six runs (seeds 1 to 3, both starts), on the merged code with the rain at 773 mm: gap −2,326 m (−388 of it made on the ocean floor). Parts: a resampling's accretion −4,046 (crust stacked under a column with no height; `pools::accrete`), the plate model's ocean-floor step −2,142 (all on the ocean floor: `pools::surface_step` damps oceanic samples to −5,600 m whatever their thickness), the flexure with the water's local answer −2,086, the transition −420, erosion net of its local rebound −401 (−13,450 and +13,049); arcs +3,071, founder +1,786, carry +1,383 (the volcano stage's cones in it), collapse +441. 30–40 km: −930; 55–70 km: −3,254, with the same order (accretion −8,420 there). At 1000 Myr (four runs) 40–55 km: −2,709, accretion −6,809, ocean-floor step −3,700, flexure with the water −3,215. Before the rain (four runs, 500 Myr): −2,333 with the same parts; the rain raised erosion's part of the gap rate by 31 % (−47.0 to −61.4 m/Myr) and the rebound with it, and lowered the 1000 Myr land (0.189 to 0.174) by thinning the thickest crust (share of continental samples at 55–70 km 0.33 to 0.27), not by widening the gap. Sea level −16 to −25 m at 500 Myr, about −60 at 1000.
- **The flexure, split** (four 500 Myr runs, seeds 1 and 2, both starts, binary built at 1034f1df with `DEEPTIME_GAP_BUDGET=1`; same land as the plain runs; 40–55 km crust, gap −2,382): regional answer to erosion, deposition and water −420, bending of the plate model's roots +44, released moment −104, the rest −1,216; the water's local answer −350; the volcano stage's cones and the impacts +1,270; the carry +60. The rest is the flexure's answer to the cones (+54 m net); net of them the flexure and water hold −830 m, a third of the gap. The water's −350 m is the sea's weight on columns already flooded (the Airy height is a dry column's): it follows the gap. 30–40 km: −223, +67, −47, −543, −372, +552, +156; 55–70 km: −670, +99, −414, −1,816, −273, +1,888, −60.
- **Erosion is not the maker.** Its net is 3 % of the depth it removes: the surface gives back 0.8 of it (ISO-001), the Airy height falls by 1/7.0 of it (PLT-281), 0.058 of the depth.
- **Bookkeeping.** One fix, in the budget's own split, none in the model: under the sea the split booked the roots' answer to their whole crust (−705 m on the 40–55 km crust) and the water's answer to the water their crust pushed aside (+416 m) apart; the water pushed aside now goes with the roots (roots +44, water −350; sum −289 before, −306 after; test `under_the_sea_a_root_with_nothing_to_bend_answers_nothing`). One hand-off finding, not fixed: the volcano stage hands its cones to the plate model as elevation only (`surface/feedback_m`), while the pools change only by the surface stage's `surface/material_m`; a cone's rock never joins the column, yet its erosion is stripped from the column (`pools::strip`) and laid down downstream. On the gap it nets about +54 m; on the crust it is a sink at arcs and hotspots of up to about 1.3 km of the 40–55 km band mean over 500 Myr (inferred upper bound: the part counts every rebuild). Where the cones' rock belongs is the crust budget's question (arc crust is 7.0 times an uplift, PLT-048/051), so it is recommendation 6, not a fix. The accretion's missing height is documented design ("thickens a column without raising it", collapse.rs): recommendation 1.
- **What-if, not in the code: accreted crust given its Airy height** (capped at the column's Airy height, handed to the surface as uplift; four runs at 500 Myr against the same four plain): gap of 40–55 km crust −2,382 to −1,256 m, its elevation −73 to +988 m, land 0.175 to 0.201, continental crust dry 0.53 to 0.67, median land 760 to 1,244 m (Earth 427), land above 2 km 0.20 to 0.34 of the land (Earth 0.10), continental crust 0.31 to 0.27 of the planet (volume −17 %), eroded rock +32 %. Half the thick crust's gap closes, the land share barely moves: the raised crust is high and erodes.
- **Recommendations (each can be undone; for Ben or the coordinator to take):**
  1. *Give a resampling's accretion its Airy height* (Recommended), capped at the column's Airy height, through the surface's uplift as the collapse raises its receivers. Land it together with plate task 8 (sourced crust rates) and the erosion recalibration, not alone: alone it doubles the high ground and erodes away a sixth of the continental crust. Alternative: keep accretion heightless and count it as the reason the land sits low.
  2. *The flexure:* leave it (Recommended). Split, its own parts are small (roots +44, regional −420, released −104); its large rest answers the cones, and the water's −350 is the sea on columns the gap already flooded.
  3. *The ocean-floor step:* leave it (Recommended). Its −2.1 km on later continental crust comes back as the arcs' height-only uplift and the carry. If task 8 makes arcs grow height from thickness, give oceanic samples a floor held by their thickness at the same time, or the arcs' compensation goes and the gap widens by about 2 km.
  4. *The erosion recalibration:* go ahead on its own terms (Recommended); erosion holds a few per cent of the gap, so recalibrating it will not raise the land by itself, but once accretion has its height it sets the land and the high ground.
  5. *The transition* (heights on 4.24 m of crust per metre against the Airy 7.0): leave it (Recommended); −420 m.
  6. *The volcano stage's cones* (Recommended: with task 8): hand a cone's growth to the plate pools as volcanic rock (felsic volcanic for stratovolcanoes and silicic centres, mafic volcanic for shields and flood basalts) and count it in the sourced arc and hotspot rates, so arc magma is counted once, as crust that erodes. Alternative: leave it; it moves crust from arcs to basins and the sea and nets nothing on the gap.
  For task 8: the arcs' height-only uplift (+1,600 m on the 40–55 km continent, +1,471 m on the ocean floor) is the largest positive part; sourcing the arc rates removes it unless recommendation 1 lands first. Count `ACCRETED_GLOBAL` in the crust budget.
- **Choices made without asking (all can be undone).** The 27 parts and their names; the split solves only with the variable set, at a tenth of the tolerance and four times the iterations; the water the roots' crust pushes aside booked with the roots; the volcano hand-off reported, not fixed (it changes crust thickness and depends on task 8's arc rates); the bands; the stock as the band mean of each sample's own cumulative parts; the rate over the last 50 Myr. The what-if patch was built and run, then reverted.

### 2026-10-17: `memory_estimate`'s resident check: the session threads' glibc arenas carried freed blocks into the bake; `alloc::release_cache` now trims them (the coordinator's task; agent worktree agent-a6726a524e4c6fb75, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; master 1aeb7e4e merged, with P1-17's session-pool fix; not merged)
- **The question:** does the estimate undercount, or does the measurement leak? The check that failed (line 175) compares the resident peak with the counted peak; the count was right and the same in every run (91.5 MiB on master 1aeb7e4e), so the measurement leaked. Two causes. The first, Rayon's global pool (37 threads and their arenas on the 32-vCPU VM), was found and fixed by P1-17 (`tests/session_pool.rs`) and is not redone here. The second is fixed here: blocks under 1 MiB go to glibc, which keeps the ones freed in each thread's arena. That memory is resident but outside the count, and the session's threads carried 11 to 15 MiB of it from the stages into the bake, more on a busier VM.
- **Measured** (`cargo test -p deeptime-core --test memory_estimate -- --nocapture` on the test VM, one at a time, and a temporary diagnostic copy of the test, not committed, printing each phase's count, `VmHWM`, `RssAnon`/`RssFile`, `mallinfo2` and threads; MiB above the start; the bound is the count + 16 + a tenth = 116.7):
  - master 1aeb7e4e alone, VM load 25 to 37: resident peaks 114.9, 111.2, 119.2, 118.4, 124.9, so 3 of 5 failed. At load 10 to 18: 110 to 113.5.
  - with `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1`: 101 to 102. With `malloc_trim(0)` where the session releases: 95 to 101.
  - with transparent huge pages off for the process (`prctl`, THP is `always` on the VM): no material change. Ruled out.
  - `RssFile` (the code paged in) grows by about 3.7 MiB, inside the bound's fixed 16 MiB.
- **Fix:** `alloc::release_cache` also returns the arenas' free memory to the OS (`alloc::trim_system`, glibc's `malloc_trim(0)`; a no-op off glibc). The session calls `MemoryGauge::release` when a stage group ends and before the bake's projection pass. The CLI, JNI and test gauges all go through `release_cache`, so the game trims too. Cost on the test planet: 5 calls, 21.9 ms in all, the longest 5.7 ms (diagnostic). Under a memory cap, the pressure paths also call `release` and so trim too: the reservation in `stage.rs`, the room made before a step, and `trim_history`. Their cost at 16k was not measured. The test's bound is unchanged, and its comment now names both causes. It prints the bound. No ledger rows: a test tolerance, unchanged.
- **Estimate against held, per stage** (master 1aeb7e4e, with the fix, MiB; the count is deterministic): plates 51.0 / 72.8 (from the earlier base; P1-17 changed it little), climate 58.3 / 72.8, surface 55.4 / 72.8, volcanoes 44.4 / 72.8, impacts 44.3 / 72.8, structure 53.8 / 72.8, deposits 59.1 / 83.9, young 71.8 / 74.3, amplify 72.2 / 97.5, run 91.5 / 97.5. The bake holds 91.5 against its `bake_bytes` of 76.0 (projection pass 18.0). That row is not asserted, by design (P1-17's design page): `estimate_for` counts only the finished world and the projection pass, and the run's estimate covers the bake by 6.0 MiB (6 %).
- **Passes with the fix:** alone 5 of 5, resident 98.7, 98.8, 98.7, 99.7, 97.1 (load 19 to 22; margin 17.0 to 19.6 MiB). Inside `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast -- --show-output`, serially, 3 of 3: 924 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored each time, resident 96.8, 98.0, 100.2 (load 12 to 20).
- **Gates** (`tools/remote/mac.sh`): `cargo fmt --all --check` ok; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` ok; `cargo deny check licenses bans` ok; the workspace tests above (924 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored). Gradle not run: no Java changed.
- **Still weak, with numbers:** the bake's own row, 91.5 against 76.0 (20 % under), is covered only through the run's peak. A bake change that adds 6 MiB on the test planet fails the run check, which is the guard. The young stage's estimate is 3 % above its held 71.8. The resident check's margin is now 16.5 to 19.6 MiB in these eight runs. What is left of its load dependence is how glibc's arenas behave under contention (inferred, not measured).
- **Next:** the coordinator merges. If the bake's estimate is ever wanted on its own, it needs a measured 16k bake peak first (P1-17's page).

### 2026-10-17: `placerBarHoldsPannedGold`, second MIC failure: the test read a chunk saved in full below full status; the world keeps the gold (coordinator's follow-up to the entry "Placer gold opts out of Lootr" below; agent worktree agent-a11da4e0e0cecad9b, sub-agent of the Deep Time coordinator; branch worktree-agent-a11da4e0e0cecad9b at master 8da33444; not merged)
- **The failure (the coordinator's gate batch on master 5bc63aa5, `-PwithMic`):** `PlacerScan[due=285, panned=50, filled=13, ...]`, the other 37 suspicious blocks "block entity null (ImposterProtoChunk minecraft:full)", all in chunk -90, 0 of `test_deposits`.
- **Cause, with evidence.** A full `./gametest.sh -PwithMic` with temporary diagnostics (since removed: mixins at the head of `LevelChunk.removeBlockEntity`, `LevelChunk.clearAllBlockEntities` and `ProtoChunk.removeBlockEntity`, and listeners on `ChunkEvent.Load` and `Unload` and `ChunkDataEvent.Save` and `Load`, for the bar's 25 chunks) failed the same way, 37 cells in chunk -90, 0, and showed the chunk's history. 09:07:43: `coePicksSiteVein` (MIC only: with COE installed it reads COE's state through `level.getChunk` at each vein site's best chunk, and -90, 0 is the best chunk of both placer site 1 and porphyry site 0) loads the chunk in full: 37 suspicious blocks, 37 brushable block entities, 37 holding their gold. 09:08:11, during `vanillaOreBlock`'s scan: C2ME's chunk system saves it (`ChunkDataEvent.Save`, status full, 37 brushable block entities in the NBT, 37 with an `item`), unloads it (`clearAllBlockEntities`, as on any unload) and reads it back. 09:08:40: the placer scan asks for it at `FEATURES` and gets a `LevelChunk` inside an `ImposterProtoChunk`, read from disk (`ChunkDataEvent.Load`: 37 of 37 in the NBT) with no block entity object and no pending tag, `loaded=false`, its `postLoad` a `ChunkSerializer` lambda, and `getChunkNow` null. `ChunkSerializer.read` keeps the block entities of a chunk saved in full inside the post-load processor of `postLoadChunk`, which `ChunkStatusTasks.full` runs only when the chunk is made full again. Nothing removed a block entity of the bar (no `removeBlockEntity` on it), and the chunk was not written again below full (`ImposterProtoChunk.isUnsaved` is false; `ChunkMap.save` returns early). Of the coordinator's candidates: Lootr's ticker and `BrushableBlock`'s scheduled tick changed no bar block; the save and promote path keeps the data and restores it on promotion; the batch order matters only because `coePicksSiteVein` (batch 0) made the chunk full first. Standalone has no COE, and the lone MIC runs had no `coePicksSiteVein` before them, so neither saw it. The first fix (`getBlockEntityNbtForSaving`, entry below) covered a `ProtoChunk` read back from disk, not a chunk saved in full.
- **The world keeps the gold.** With the fix and the diagnostics in the same batch, the chunk is read back from disk with no block entity (09:13:50), and once the scan makes it full it holds 37 of 37 again (`ChunkEvent.Load`, `new=false`, 09:13:51); it is saved at the end with 37 of 37. A player's chunk is always made full, so this is the path a world takes. No worldgen or block change.

The expiry warning ("Generation for section ... has expired!") never appeared (0 lines in 222 s, the cross run of row 4), and no error or warning about the pregeneration appeared; the last `PregenManager` line was `Generated radius: 23.07 / 32 chunks (132 cps, 52%)`. - **Cause confirmed by reading 1.0.0** (CFR on the VM through `mac.sh`, never the laptop). `GeneratedFullDataSourceProviderMixin.toroidal$retrieveTheOneSection`, a `@WrapMethod` on `queuePositionForRetrieval(Long)`, is the 0.19.3 method unchanged: it calls the original with `DhKeys.foldSection(DhRepoLevel.latticeOf(repo), genPos)` and returns the original's future as it is, so `DataSourceRetrievalResult.pos` is the folded key. `AbstractDhRepoMixin.toroidal$answerTheAskedKey` still reseats `getByKey` results under the asked key (`DhKeys.reseat`); the retrieval result gets no such treatment. Distant Horizons 3.3.3's `PregenManager$PregenState` is the 3.3.1 logic: `pendingGenerations.put(rawSectionPos)`, `invalidate(result.pos)` (or `fullDataSource.getPos()` for an already generated section), the removal listener refills, 2-minute `expireAfterWrite`. `DataSourceRetrievalResult` in 3.3.3 still has `final long pos` and `CreateSuccess(long, FullDataSourceV2)`. ### 2026-10-16: Plateau erosion and the hillslope diffusion's map scale: the scaling is consistent; plateaus are worn by the stream power as calibrated (coordinator task after the erosion audit; agent worktree agent-a0a3b643ccd2cf4ec, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c, continued after the VM rebuild; master merged at 4e6b0022, then 9eef053e and 85c9cfe2; not merged)
- **Diagnosis: no scaling error.** The surface stage uses one length, the map's real metres (decisions file, "Tectonics scaling"): a 4.8-km L1 cell on the 16k quick planet (ERO-084), drainage area in m² of those cells, slopes in metres per metre. Drawn 8.15 times narrower than Earth, stream power with m = 1, n = 2 is unchanged (A as L², S² as 1/L²), linear diffusion is 66 times stronger (κ Δt / Δx²) and the critical slope S_c, a fixed gradient, bites more. The controlled plateau (ERO-176, `surface/plateau_check.rs`: 4 km high, a 2-cell escarpment, 10 Myr of the stage's own kernels; interior gross lowering by stream power, diffusion and net, m/Myr) shows it: without κ and S_c stream power is the same at both widths (305.1 on the map and at Earth's width); with κ 2 the map's edge diffuses 13.3 against 0.2 at Earth's width, but diffusion protects the interior rather than wearing it (stream power 118.4, net 124.6, against 305.1 without κ; at Earth's width 308.5 net); κ 0.0036 on the map gives 301.7 net; the critical slope cuts nothing in any controlled case (the escarpment's rivers keep the slope below 0.35). A terminal lake at the plateau's centre: 132.4 net (no help); a rim range 500 m higher whose closed interior spills over it: 145.7, the same ending in a terminal lake: 121.1 (the rim's own rivers cut through it within the 10 Myr); a dry plateau at a tenth of the runoff: 10.1. So the width does not set the rate, the stream power's K 3e-9 with n = 2 does, and only less runoff slows it.
- **The planet** (quick 16k, scattered, preset seed, 500 Myr; new per-step split by process and 1-km band, ERO-175, `land_erosion_by_band_m_myr` in the surface notes and `land_erosion_by_process_m_myr` in `deeptime erosion-audit`): above 2 km stream power is 63 to 76 % of the gross lowering and diffusion 21 to 33 %; the critical-slope cut grows with height (9.6 m/Myr at 2 to 3 km, 110 of the 123 m/Myr of stream power above 4 km). Flat high ground (a quarter of it, under 500 m of 3 x 3 relief) wears at 63 m/Myr net (stream power 37, diffusion 26), six times southern Tibet's plateau surface (under 10, ERO-174, a reference line); steep high ground at 199.
- **κ at the measured value** (Roering, Kirchner & Dietrich 1999 read in full from the author's reprint: 0.0036 m²/yr on hillslopes, ERO-177; eSCAPE's coarse-mesh 0.01 to 0.1 is a model's choice, ERO-178): a bake with κ = 0.0036, all else the same. Net lowering 2 to 3 / 3 to 4 / above 4 km 159 / 171 / 190 → 145 / 163 / 141 m/Myr; flat high ground 63 → 46 (stream power 37 → 45: it takes over the slopes diffusion rounded); land 0.158 → 0.198 (HYP-001 0.29), land median 583 → 284 m (HYP-002 427, range 430 to 640), above 2 km 0.124 → 0.066 (HYP-004 0.102, range 0.10 to 0.13), highest point 4,123 → 5,476 m, Köppen B 0.30 → 0.43, land rain 697 → 619 mm, no snowball in either, mass residual -7.2e-4 and 1.7e-4 km³. So the measured κ does not fix the plateaus and moves two calibrated targets out of range.
- **The cause.** The stream power as calibrated: K 3e-9 with n = 2 (ERO-004, ERO-007) was fitted to the hypsometry with κ = 2, not to measured rates, and wears any plateau that sheds water at range rates whatever its width. With n = 2 a knickpoint's celerity 2 K A S is large for the large area an escarpment's rivers collect, and the escarpment's knickpoint crosses the controlled plateau within a 2-Myr step at either width. The routing is not the lever: the priority flood routes every closed basin over its rim (ERO-080), but a terminal lake in the same place saves little (121 against 146 m/Myr behind a rim). On the planet's steep ground above 3 km the cut at S_c 0.35 (uncited, ERO-013) does most of the stream power's work.
- **Changed.** Diagnostics and docs only; no physics, default or preset changed: `surface/erosion_bands.rs` (ERO-175) and its totals in the surface notes; `surface/plateau_check.rs` (ERO-176, fourteen cases; asserts the width invariance of stream power, the map's far stronger diffusion, that diffusion protects the interior, that a dry plateau wears slowly and that a terminal lake behind a rim does not save it); `deeptime erosion-audit` reports `land_erosion_by_process_m_myr`; `tools/review/erosion-audit.sh` takes `BIN=<tag>` to bake a preset variant with an earlier bake's build; `erosion-audit-summary.py` prints the split; ledger comments on S_c and κ (ERO-013, ERO-023, both rows annotated); ERO-175 to ERO-178; Roering1999 updated and Salles2019 added in the bibliography; `docs/science/erosion-and-sediment.md` "Plateaus and the hillslope diffusivity"; claims counts.
- **Erosion and burial depths against the targets** (500 Myr, shipped κ): porphyry sites 22 (counted 14 against the target 25.04; formation capped at 20 per survivor, 22.5 expected), site centre depth median 24.7, p90 136.1, max 388.5 blocks, 3 sites deeper than 100 blocks (3.5 km); burial since formation over all 483 porphyries median 0.5 km, p90 4.9 km; eroded 461, buried 13, truncated 9. With κ 0.0036 (not shipped): 27 sites (13 against 14.5), depth median 38.6, p90 222.0, max 434.8 blocks, 10 deeper than 100 blocks, burial p90 8.5 km: deeper, not shallower.
- **Gates** (test VM, `tools/dev/gates.sh` detached through `tools/remote/detach.sh`, admitted, 2026-10-17, branch at ee51bd72 with master 85c9cfe2 merged): `GATES fmt=0 clippy=0 test=0 deny=0 gradle=0`; cargo test --workspace all ok (core 646 passed, 3 ignored, `plateau_erosion_by_process_and_scale` among them); deny bans ok, licenses ok; `./gradlew build test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL, JUnit tests=338 failures=0 errors=0 skipped=2. No GameTests (branch rule). The first Gradle run on the branch failed resolving Toroidal World by its old Modrinth slug; master's b61afa40 fixed it and came in with the merge.
- **Decided (coordinator's call under Ben's rule, decisions log 2026-10-16):** κ stays 2 m²/yr and S_c 0.35; follow-ups listed.
- **Question for Ben** (Pending questions, 2026-10-16 "Plateau erosion"): calibrate K, n, κ and S_c together against measured erosion rates instead of the hypsometry; recommended after plate tasks 7 and 8.

### 2026-10-16: Plate task 7 continued: the eclogite root and whole-column isostasy (Ben, decisions log 2026-10-06, "Fix isostasy first, then land (Recommended)"; agent worktree agent-a4232de5edf71e65c, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c, resumed 2026-10-16 after the pause and again after the laptop crash of 2026-10-17; master 85c9cfe2 merged; not merged)
- **What.** (1) Whole-column isostasy: where a column's thickness changes as a whole (belts, collapse, foundering, cordillera roots) its height changes at the continental crust's mean density, 2,830 kg/m³ (Christensen & Mooney 1995; Hyndman & Currie 2011 measure 131 to 141 m/km, the model now 142), 7.0 m of crust per m of height instead of 5.5; erosion from the top keeps 5.5 (PLT-281, ISO-043). (2) The eclogite root: mafic pools deeper than 1.5 GPa (54 km) are 30 % eclogite at 3,450 kg/m³ (Wittlinger et al. 2009, Shi F. et al. 2018, Shi D. et al. 2020; PLT-278 to PLT-280, rule PLT-282). (3) The surface flexure infers the crust behind a plate uplift at the same density (ISO-046). (4) Run-summary globals `plates/arc_continental_km3`, `plates/arc_oceanic_km3`, `plates/continental_volume_km3` for the crust budget. Science page: plates.md, "The eclogite root and whole-column isostasy"; design doc §13.
- **The Urals target is not met, and was not tuned for.** A 50 km column has no root (the eclogite depth is 54 km) and stands about 2.7 km (3.2 before); a 70 km column stands about 5.0 km, its root pulling 0.5 km. The sources put the Urals' 0.5 to 0.8 km on a dense lower crust that is not eclogite and a cold lithosphere (Hyndman & Currie 2011: about 1,600 m at equal thickness); the model carries neither.
- **Measured: hypsometry at 500 Myr** (`earthlike_quick_16k`, seeds 1–3, both starts, `force-balance-variants.sh … final.txt 500 1,2,3 … hyps`, `p1-17-hyps.py`; reported against Earth, not tuned; mean [lowest, highest]): land 0.191 [0.145, 0.214] (Earth 0.289; 0.18–0.30 over the Phanerozoic), median land height 745 m [509, 1,058] (Earth 427), 90th percentile 2,907 m (Earth 2,022), land above 2 km 0.187 [0.103, 0.274] of the land (Earth 0.102), continental crust 0.307 of the planet (Earth about 0.41), 0.58 of it dry (Earth about 0.70). Before the root (2026-10-05): 0.183, 900 m, 0.25, 0.299. Master 2026-10-05: 0.184, 414 m, 0.083, 0.382. The surface flexure feeds back into the plates, so each row is a different planet; the spread between runs is as large as the change.
- **Measured: plate-check at 1000 Myr** (seeds 1–4, both starts, `… final.txt 1000 1,2,3,4 … ck`): 31 of 45 (30 on 2026-10-05); the 14 fails are the ones of before (collision rate 0.89 per 100 Myr, lowest crust 0.25, active margin 0.46, slab ratio 1.82 and rank correlation 0.45, rotation 90th pct 25.2 %, old floor 3.55 %, supercontinent tenure and period, subducting boundary 52.6 %, oceanic arc crest 1,107 m, wedge, foredeep). Pooled supercontinent episodes: 2.5 a run, tenure 48 Myr, period 267 Myr (2026-10-05: 2.1, 46, 213). At 1000 Myr: land 0.192 [0.170, 0.221], median land height 1,004 m, above 2 km 0.265 of the land, continental crust 0.317.
- **The land share: height has fallen behind thickness** (`crust_bins`, plate-model elevation; plates.md, "The land share: height has fallen behind thickness"). At 500 Myr crust 30–40 km thick stands at a median of −72 to +51 m and 40–55 km at −71 to +763 m, where the model's own Airy height (`collapse::iso_height`) is about 510 m and 2,300 m; at 1000 Myr 40–55 km stands at −191 to +61 m. So most continental crust is near sea level and half flooded; at its Airy height the land would be near the crust's 0.31. Which process lowers a column's surface faster than it thins it was not measured (candidates: the surface stage's erosion, which gives height back only through the flexure; deposits fed back at sea level; the transition, trench and thermal subsidence). Land above 2 km is about 0.036 of the planet against Earth's 0.029: its excess as a share of the land is mostly the small land.
- **The crust budget against Stern & Scholl 2010** (new run-summary globals, 500 Myr mean of six runs): continental arcs with the cordillera roots add 8.5 km³ a year (Earth about 1.0), island arcs 0.14 (Earth about 1.5), 7.0 km³ a year founders beyond the thickest column (Earth's collision zones lose about 0.7), collapse moves 4.7; 7.3 billion km³ at the end, a mean of about 47 km over 0.31 of the planet. Not too little crust; neither rate is sourced. At 1000 Myr: 11.2, 0.18, 12.4, 7.9; 8.4 billion km³.

### 2026-10-17: Placer gold opts out of Lootr; the MIC failure of `placerBarHoldsPannedGold` was the test reading reloaded chunks (coordinator's call, decisions log 2026-10-17; agent worktree agent-a11da4e0e0cecad9b, sub-agent of the Deep Time coordinator; branch worktree-agent-a11da4e0e0cecad9b from master 85c9cfe2; not merged)
- **The failure (master gate, `-PwithMic` only):** `PlacerScan[due=285, panned=50, withTable=0, ...]`, every suspicious block "has no brushable block entity". **Not Lootr.** Diagnostic runs (MIC and standalone, since removed) read the same cells 1200 ticks after a first scan: the chunks were `ProtoChunk`s at status `minecraft:spawn`, read back from disk, holding the block entities only as their saved tags (`{LootTable:"deeptime:archaeology/placer_gold",LootTableSeed:...,id:"minecraft:brushable_block"}`), while the level chunk of the same position held a `BrushableBlockEntity` with the table. The data was intact; the scan asked `chunk.getBlockEntity(p)`, which a `ProtoChunk` answers only for block entity objects. Only the MIC batch showed it because of timing: there the porphyry scan of `bodyHasOre` generated those chunks 36 s before the placer test (7 s standalone), long enough for them to be saved and dropped. Fix: `scanPlacer` reads `getBlockEntityNbtForSaving(pos, registries)`, which returns the object's save or the pending tag.
- **What Lootr does (1.21.1-1.11.38.125 from MIC's server set, decompiled with CFR on the VM):** `MixinLevelChunk` on `LevelChunk.updateBlockEntityTicker` hands every block entity of a level chunk to `BlockEntityTicker.addEntity`, which admits it without looking at its loot table (out only if Lootr is off, the dimension blocked, the type in `#lootr:convert/blacklist` or it is Lootr's own). Each server tick an entry whose chunk and the 5 by 5 around it are in `LoadedChunks` (chunks whose `ChunkEvent.Load` came at full status) is processed: skipped when its loot table is null, a structure rule excludes it, the table is in the config's blacklists or the block has no replacement (`#lootr:convert/gravels` = suspicious gravel, `/sands` = suspicious sand); otherwise the vanilla table is cleared and the block becomes Lootr's, per player. So the old placer blocks (a table and a seed) would have become per-player loot in any MIC world. No inter-mod message handler, no exemption API.
- **Mechanism (the coordinator's call: one brushing, for whoever gets there first; the how is mine):** `PlacerPanning.fill` rolls the table when `DepositFeature` places the block (`roll`: the same table, the position's `panSeed`, vanilla's brushing parameters, CHEST with the block centre as origin, the first stack) and stores the nuggets as the block entity's `item` with no loot table (`loadCustomOnly` with an `item` tag). Lootr skips a brushable block entity without a table, in any pack, with no config. A cell where no block entity or no gold comes back keeps the plain gravel or sand. Rejected: Lootr's `loot_table_blacklist` (a pack config file, world-level serverconfig; holds only where a pack sets it), `#lootr:convert/blacklist` or emptying the convert tags (would exempt every suspicious block, vanilla's archaeology too, and puts Deep Time data in Lootr's namespace), the feature pack `lootr_no_suspicious_blocks` (the same, and it is the world's choice), reflection into Lootr (a supported route exists). Cost: the roll is `getRandomItemsRaw`, without NeoForge's global loot modifiers (it runs on a world-generation thread, before the block is a block of the level), so a pack modifier that adds to archaeology loot does not reach placer gold; 400 seeds show the roll equals vanilla's `getRandomItems` for this table.
- **The GameTest server cannot show Lootr converting a suspicious block:** `GameTestServer.create` selects every available pack, so Lootr's opt-in feature pack `lootr_no_suspicious_blocks` is on there and both convert tags are empty. My first control (a suspicious gravel with the old table) therefore never converted (`Lootr has not replaced the control at -1435, 638, 10`, 8594 ms). The check now uses a chest with a vanilla loot table as the control (Lootr must turn it into `lootr:lootr_chest`, or the check sees nothing), adds the suspicious control only where the server's tags convert suspicious blocks, logs when they do not, and then rescans: no bar cell converted, the same 50 suspicious blocks, each still holding its roll. The opt-out itself is checked as `filled == panned` (no loot table, the rolled item). A MIC world has the feature pack off: it is registered as `PackSource.FEATURE`, not required, and MIC's pack (branch `deep-time`) has no Lootr config and enables it nowhere.
- **Files:** `ore/PlacerPanning.java` (`setLoot` replaced by `fill`, `roll`, `setItem`), `worldgen/DepositFeature.java` (calls `fill`, falls back to the plain block; diagnostic code removed), `ore/OreBlockResolver.java`, `worldgen/OreDraws.java` (javadoc), `gametest/DepositGameTests.java` (`placerGoldLootTable`: 400 seeds against vanilla's unpacking, then a real block brushed 10 strokes by a mock survival player drops exactly the roll and leaves gravel; `scanPlacer` reads the saved tag and counts `filled` and `converted`; `placerBarHoldsPannedGold` and `lootrLeavesPlacerGold` as above), `test/.../PlacerGoldTableTest.java` (header); docs: decisions log 2026-10-17 (the coordinator's call and reason), `docs/science/deposits.md`, ledger ORE-269 (ORE-267 and ORE-268 unchanged: the table and its count are as they were), `docs/science/bibliography.md` (sources read again, Lootr section, `GameTestServer.create`), plan line on the placer block entity. Pack repos: no change.
- **Gates (VM, admitted, 2026-10-17; pack dc49fe7 with Ben's uncommitted change, as `install.sh mic` read it):** `tools/smoke/install.sh mic` exit 0, 157 mods (11 excluded: Cobblemon's dependencies), Lootr `lootr-neoforge-1.21.1-1.11.38.125.jar` in it, no Excavated Variants. `./gametest.sh -PwithMic -PgametestOnly=placerbarholdspannedgold` PASS required=true 5505 ms, `PlacerScan[due=285, panned=50, filled=50, ore=98, unsupported=0, missed=0, hanging=0, converted=0, other=137, problems=[]]`, then "81 chunks loaded in full (81 forced here); 22 ticks after placing, chest control became lootr:lootr_chest; suspicious control left out ...; bar cells converted=0 panned before=50 after=50 filled after=50"; "All 1 required tests passed". The same test standalone: PASS required=true 2275 ms (first run 1856 ms), the same scan, "Lootr is not loaded; nothing to check". The whole deposit class under MIC (`-PgametestOnly=bodyHasOre,placerGoldBlockRules,placerGoldLootTable,placerBarHoldsPannedGold,vanillaOreBlock,evVariantWhenInstalled,depositsDeterministic,siteApiAndProbes,backgroundScatterPlaces`): "All 9 required tests passed", `placerGoldLootTable` 71 ms (the 400-seed equality with vanilla's `getRandomItems` holds with MIC's loot modifiers loaded), `placerBarHoldsPannedGold` 6071 ms with the same scan and Lootr line. `cd neoforge && ./gradlew build test`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 2m 7s, junit-summary tests=338 failures=0 errors=0 skipped=2 (as master: no JUnit test added or removed).
- **Contradicts the plan or earlier notes:** the master failure was not Lootr; MIC's master pack pins no Excavated Variants today, so MIC pans (the test's and the page's "with Excavated Variants (MIC)" holds only for MIC's `deep-time` branch); the GameTest server runs with Lootr's no-suspicious-blocks pack on, unlike any world.
- **Next step:** the coordinator merges this branch and runs the gate batch (`./gametest.sh`, `./gametest.sh -PwithMic`); `placerBarHoldsPannedGold` should pass under both. Rust untouched: no cargo checks. VM scratch `deeptime-runs/lootr-placer/` removed.

### 2026-10-16: Placer gold as panning, suspicious gravel and sand with a gold-nugget loot table (Ben, decisions log 2026-10-16; agent worktree agent-a6df0e7b2d44da705, sub-agent of the Deep Time coordinator; branch worktree-agent-a6df0e7b2d44da705 from master b46e2ee0; not merged)
- **Asked and decided (Ben, 2026-10-16: "Could we use suspicious gravel w/ a loot table set to a gold nugget?"):** in a pack without Excavated Variants (EV) a placer's gold cell in a gravel host is `minecraft:suspicious_gravel` and in a sand host `minecraft:suspicious_sand`; the block entity's loot table is a new Deep Time table of gold nuggets and brushing it is the panning. Deep Time ships no block of its own. With EV (MIC) nothing changes: the EV gravel gold ore stays. A placer cell whose block is not gravel or sand (soil over the gravel, a rock bench) keeps today's ore block (a stone `gold_ore`).
- **Built, file by file.** `neoforge/src/main/resources/data/deeptime/loot_table/archaeology/placer_gold.json` (type `minecraft:archaeology`, one pool, one roll, one entry `minecraft:gold_nugget` with `set_count` uniform 2 to 5). `ore/PlacerPanning.java` (new: `GOLD_TABLE`, `tableOf`, `suspiciousFor` via `#c:gravels` and `#c:sands`, `supported` = not `FallingBlock.isFree`, `setLoot`). `ore/OreBlockResolver.java` (`madeFor` split out of `compute`: EV variant, then the host's own `#c:ores_in_ground/<host>` for hosts other than stone and deepslate; new `panned(material, cell, host)` with its cache: null unless the material has a table, the cell is gravel or sand and `madeFor` finds no gold ore for the body's own rock). `worldgen/DepositFeature.java` (in a loose body, after the raw-ore draw, a due cell with a `panned` block is written as that block and its loot table and seed are set, only where the block below holds it; the cell is then done either way). `worldgen/OreDraws.java` (`panSeed(worldSeed, c, x, y, z)`: a SplitMix64 chain of the canonical x, y, z, the salt `PAN!` and the world seed, never 0, same on both sides of the seam). `gametest/DepositGameTests.java` (`scan` accepts panned blocks and counts an unsupported plain cell as not-host; new `placerGoldBlockRules`, `placerGoldLootTable`, `placerBarHoldsPannedGold`). Tests: `OreDrawsTest` (panSeed), new `ore/PlacerGoldTableTest` (the JSON). Docs: plan 7.6 ("Placer gold as panning"), `docs/science/deposits.md` (new section "Placer gold as panning" with the compatibility notes for packs without EV, constants table, game choices), ledger ORE-267 (`from-memory`: placer gold is washed out of gravel as flakes and small nuggets, no source read), ORE-268 (`game-choice`: the count), ORE-269 (`game-choice`: the block rule, the support rule, gold only), ORE-233 and ORE-234 reworded, bibliography entry for the 1.21.1 sources read, `claims.md` recounted (`tools/review/claims_counts.py --write`: ORE 191 to 194 rows).
- **The loot table's count (ORE-268, a game choice):** one stack, uniform integer 2 to 5 gold nuggets, mean 3.5 (about 0.39 of an ingot at 9 to the ingot). A median placer holds about 150 ore blocks (build log 2026-10-02), so about 500 nuggets, about 55 ingots, if every block is brushed. Ben may want it lower or higher: it is one number in the JSON, and a pack's datapack can override the table.
- **A cell without support.** Suspicious gravel and sand fall like their plain blocks (`FallingBlock.isFree` of the block below: air, fire, a liquid or a replaceable plant), and `WorldGenRegion.setBlock` does not schedule the fall, so one placed over air would hang until a neighbour update. `DepositFeature` therefore checks `level.getBlockState(pos.below())` (the same chunk column, so already generated) and where it is free leaves the cell as the plain host block with no gold and no other ore (it `continue`s). The bar's overhanging edge or a bar over a cave holds less gold than the draw said; ORE-269 and deposits.md say so, and the GameTests count such cells apart from cells that should have been panned.
- **Mechanics checked in the 1.21.1 sources** (`libs/neoforge-src`): `WorldGenRegion.setBlock` leaves a `DUMMY` block-entity tag in a proto chunk and `getBlockEntity` makes the real `BrushableBlockEntity` from it (so `setLoot` is called after `setBlock`, as vanilla's desert well does); `BrushableBlockEntity.unpackLootTable` rolls with the CHEST parameter set and keeps the first stack; `LootContext.Builder.withOptionalRandomSeed` ignores a 0 seed (the level's sequence would be used), hence the non-zero seed; `RandomSource.create(seed)` is the legacy generator, so consecutive small seeds roll alike and the seed is a hash.
- **Choices made without asking (all can be undone):** the count 2 to 5; only gold is panned (silver, the placer's by-product zone, keeps `silver_ore`); a gravel or sand cell is decided by the cell's actual block (`#c:gravels`, `#c:sands`, so red sand pans too) while the host (the body's own rock) decides whether a pack ore exists; the raw-ore draw still wins; the panned seed is a function of the world seed and position (the same nuggets for the same brush on any machine); no `setChanged` (vanilla's desert well does not call it); the loot table name `deeptime:archaeology/placer_gold`.
- **Left as it was:** soil cells inside a bar still get `gold_ore` (the decision covers gravel and sand); silver is unchanged; `deeptime-inspect` counts ore blocks and does not count suspicious blocks as ore, so its placer census undercounts in a pack without EV (a follow-up if the census matters). The "Follow-ups from decided questions" row for this decision (`Placer gold in packs without Excavated Variants`) is done and can be removed by the coordinator.
- **World-level GameTest, what the 4k fixture holds.** a dump of the fixture world's deposit records (`deposits_world_4k.json`, read with a short Python query on the VM): 14 `placer_au` sites, each with a `channel` ore body of rock class gravel and a gold zone of density 0.25; bodies 2 to 166 blocks wide (all but site 16 are within the GameTests' 96-block limit), almost all flat (0 or 1 block thick) and clipped to the ground (y 65 to 119). Flat benches on the ground may come out as the soil the surface rules put there, because `StrataPass.paintBodies` paints a body's gravel only into stone, deepslate or horizon rock and leaves soil, sand, water and surface-rule blocks, so I could not tell without running it whether the fixture's gold cells are gravel. `placerBarHoldsPannedGold` therefore scans up to four placer bodies (at least 30 gold cells each) for the first with a gold cell that is gravel or sand, checks that body (every suspicious block has the table and its position's seed; at most 2 % of gravel or sand cells left plain over solid ground or suspicious blocks over a free block, for drift between the feature and the finished chunk; with a pack gravel gold ore, no suspicious block), and when none has one logs `none of N placer bodies has a gold cell that is gravel or sand; nothing to check` and passes. If the coordinator's GameTest batch prints that line, the panned path was not seen in a world; `placerGoldBlockRules` and `placerGoldLootTable` still cover the block rule and the loot table.
- **Gates (rebuilt VM, admitted, 2026-10-16, branch merged with master 9eef053e):** `./gradlew build test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 5m 35s (job admitted after 913 s in the queue), 338 JUnit tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 2 skipped: master's 334 plus 4 of mine (`PlacerGoldTableTest` 2, `OreDrawsTest` now 5 with the panSeed tests). The GameTests are in the main source set, so the build compiled `DepositGameTests` and `PlacerPanning`; none was run (the coordinator's batch). Rust untouched: no cargo checks. VM scratch `deeptime-runs/placer-gold/` removed.

### 2026-10-05: Force balance task 7 (the switch) and a first pass of task 8 (agent worktree agent-a4232de5edf71e65c, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; continued three times after stops; master 6489d4a5 merged; not merged)
- **What.** The plates move by the force balance (docs/design/plate-force-balance.md §13, "Tasks 7 and 8"): motion relaxes towards the balance (`motion_relax_myr` 6), guard on a plate's own fastest point (250 mm/yr, counted), plates start at rest with the earlier motion's slabs hanging (PLT-273, PLT-274), slabs survive contact flicker and hang (PLT-271), initiation plants a slab (PLT-270), rifts keep the parent's motion and heal (PLT-272), collision resistance = belt energy + buoyancy (`collision_buoyancy` 1, Cloos 1993; FRC-028–030, PLT-275), drag floor 1 mm/yr (FRC-011). Removed: `plate_speed_mm_yr`, `continental_speed_factor`, the four `slab_pull_*` speed-law keys, `motion_jitter_per_sqrt_myr`, `rift_speed_mm_yr`, `subduction_initiation_speed_mm_yr`, `collision_resistance_mm_yr` (the old 200 mm/yr resistance does not exist under the balance). New: `initiation_slab_km`, `collision_buoyancy`, `convergence_ref_mm_yr` (Cortial's v_0, no longer a cap; editor field and lang key).
- **Crust budget** (Ben 2026-10-05 "raise crust in 7–8" and the validation policy: physics from sources, land reported not tuned; the coordinator's answers of that night): (1) a collision's hidden crust is not accreted a second time at resampling (PLT-276); (2) `collision_stacking_share` 0.95 everywhere (was 0.8 / 0.5) from Stern & Scholl 2010's suture recycling, ~115 km³/km/Myr of ~1,600 crossing (PLT-242); (3) crust beyond `crust_max_km` spreads to continental crust up to `collapse_thickness_km` and ocean up to the normal column before any founders (PLT-277; filling neighbours to the 70 km limit was measured and dropped: every long collision became a 70 km plateau, 0.35 of land above 2 km at 500 Myr); (4) `collapse_thickness_km` 55 → 50 (Mooney et al.'s figure; PLT-256). New run-summary globals: `collision_crossed_km3`, `collision_kept_km3`, `resample_accreted_km3` (+ `_continent`, `_visible`), `resample_stacked_km3`.
- **Measured: plate-check, 1000 Myr, seeds 1–4, both starts** (`tools/review/force-balance-variants.sh … final.txt 1000 1,2,3,4 … ck`; master 2e07d954 via `tools/review/force-balance-baseline.sh`): 30 of 45 on both. ### 2026-10-05 — The erosion and burial audit: the cause was the deposit bookkeeping, not the rates (Ben's "Investigate and fix (Recommended)", decisions log 2026-10-05; agent worktree agent-ae138b964521cc5ad, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c, continued after two usage-limit stops; master 6489d4a5 merged; not merged)
- **Root cause (three bookkeeping faults; the stream-power, diffusion and isostasy physics are unchanged).** (1) The surface stage summed every step's deposit fields at fixed L1 cells, while the deposit ledger reads frame k where each deposit's crust is at the frame's end: crust moves 7 to 18 cells in a 10-Myr frame on the 16k map (the 200 km arc distance is 5 cells), so an arc's frames carried the trench's fill and the forearc's stripping. `FrameAcc::compose_back` now carries the sums with the crust (`surface/fields.rs`, test `frame_sums_follow_the_crust`). (2) The fate used the net z_f + B − E only, so a body the surface went through and that was buried again counted as whole (porphyries with 16 to 22 km of erosion and as much burial "survived" at 1 to 6 km). The fate now follows the most net erosion at any time since formation (`Ledger::exhumed_max_m`, `ColumnNet::low_after`, survival integral exact per frame; a cut-then-covered body is clipped at its old erosion surface; tests `eroded_then_buried_is_gone`, `documented_cases`, `survives_agrees_with_the_ledger`). (3) "Eroded porphyries lost 19 to 35 km" is all the erosion to today on the `deposit_exhumation` event, hundreds of Myr of it; the body was gone after about 2 km (EVENTS.md now says so).
- **Measured** (`tools/review/erosion-audit.sh bake|report <tag> 500 1000`, new `deeptime erosion-audit`, summaries by `tools/review/erosion-audit-summary.py`; quick 16k, scattered, preset seed; before = master + the ledger recorded on the events): porphyry sites 500 Myr 7 → 27 (counted 5/6.2 → 21/25.0), centre depth median / p90 / max 16 / 81 / 318 → 23 / 51 / 166 blocks; 1000 Myr 25 → 28 sites (counted 7/15.5 → 17/61.5, capped at 20 formed per survivor), depth 81 / 475 / 507 → 26 / 133 / 369 blocks, sites deeper than 100 blocks 11 → 5; burial since formation over all porphyries (1000 Myr) median 9.5 → 2.5 km, p90 30.5 → 15.8 km. The deepest left are old porphyries under thick basin fill (site 91: formed 337 Ma, cut 1.9 km down, then 15 km of sediment). Placers 35 → 154 (500 Myr; more porphyries form and erode); coal, MVT, petroleum, BIF and impact counts move by the usual few. Rates per region type (frames, 500 Myr): orogens 135 m/Myr mean (median 73, p90 365), shields 17 (median 7), basins 1 eroded / 8.5 deposited, shelves 44 deposited: inside Earth's reference lines (Portenga & Bierman 2011 ERO-171: outcrops 12, basins 218, active basins 367; Montgomery & Brandon 2002 ERO-172), so no rate was changed (decisions log 2026-10-05: emergent outputs are reported, not tuned). Parcel totals over the run: orogens 20 km (500 Myr) and 28 km (1000 Myr), shields 11 and 19 km (much of it while they were orogens).
- **Hypsometry, reference line** (final deep-time surface, identical in every run: the fixes do not touch the terrain): 500 Myr land 0.150, land median 613 m, p90 2,054 m, 11.2 % above 2 km; 1000 Myr land 0.128, median 410 m, 7.8 % above 2 km. Lakes and river chains identical in every bake.
- **Docs.** `docs/science/erosion-and-sediment.md` "The erosion and burial audit"; `deposits.md` step 4; DEP-168 changed; ERO-171 to ERO-173 added; Portenga2011 and Montgomery2002 in the bibliography; EVENTS.md (`eroded_m`, `buried_m`, `exhumed_max_m` on `deposit_formation`; `eroded_m` of `deposit_exhumation` explained).
- **Gates** (VM, master 6489d4a5 merged): `cargo fmt --check` clean, clippy -D warnings clean, `cargo deny check licenses bans` ok, `cargo test --workspace` all pass (core 619) except `tests/memory_estimate.rs` (bake peak 101.6 > estimate 98.7 MiB), which fails the same way on master 6489d4a5 alone (101.2 > 98.7; checked by running it on master's tree): not this branch's; `./gradlew build test` tests=321 failures=0 errors=0 skipped=2; `./gametest.sh` All 82 required tests passed; `./gametest.sh -PwithMic` All 82 required tests passed (MIC set reinstalled). One MIC run before the clip fix failed `lakeIceAndSaltFollowTheClimate` (a shallow sandstone-uranium body drawn with `size_mult_v` broke through a salt flat on the 4k test planet once the deposit layout changed): a body the ledger buries is now kept a block under the ground (`geometry::bodies_for`, test `bodies_hold_the_zones_and_clip`).
- **High ground (for plate task 7's plateau rule).** Land erosion by the frame's elevation band (final runs, `land_erosion_by_elevation_m`): 0 to 1 km 36 m/Myr mean (median 6), 1 to 2 km 146 to 155 (median 77 to 92), above 2 km 116 to 144 (median 49 to 69). Earth's plateau interior: southern Tibet exhumed below 0.01 km/Myr since 12 to 11 Ma, cosmogenic rates mostly under 100 m/Myr (Tremblay et al. 2015, ERO-174). The surface stage wears high ground at range rates whether it is a range or a plateau, five to ten times a plateau interior's; a plateau held up by the plate model is not slowed by erosion here. Candidate cause, not checked: hillslope diffusion scales with curvature, so on a map drawn 8.1 times narrower than Earth it acts about 66 times stronger for the same relief (stream power with m = 1, n = 2 is unchanged by that scaling).
- **Next.** Merge (VM scratch /Volumes/Graphide/ban/deeptime-runs/erosion-audit kept for the coordinator; `erosion-audit.sh clean` deletes it). Then: the plateau erosion rate (the diffusion scaling above) with plate task 7; the next reference line to source, how much stable cratons are exhumed per Gyr on Earth, against the shields' 11 to 19 km of parcel erosion here; the memory estimate on master.

### 2026-10-05 — Playability tools: pick the epoch, continue, stop early, end-weighted nudges (Ben, decisions log 2026-10-05; agent worktree agent-a11baf88f3be4e4ec, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; master 6489d4a5 merged; not merged)
- **Design:** docs/design/playability-steering.md. One mechanism: a run's stop is part of its preset (`timeline.stop_myr`, Myr after the start; default the planned length). Picking an epoch, stopping and continuing all resume the same run from an **epoch checkpoint** taken before the new stop's **tail** (the last plate step, the climate's 3-Myr ice-age window, the steering's ramp) and step to the new stop; the world equals a run planned to that stop, file for file (tested). World time stays absolute (a continued run ends after the present; a stopped one before it). The ice-age window and the orbit are now measured from the run's end (`ClimateParams::run_end_years`; 0 for a run to its planned length, so default runs are unchanged).
- **Core:** `params.rs` (`dt_myr`, `run_myr`, `t_end_years`, `step_depends_on_end`, `last_free_step`, `with_stop`), `preset.rs` (`Timeline::stop_myr`, `with_stop`), `epochs.rs` (plan, preset key without the tail-only keys, index, chain), `checkpoint.rs` (`write_from`/`read_chain`: each epoch checkpoint holds only the history frames since the previous one), `session.rs` (`set_epochs`, at most about ten checkpoints a run; `resume_epoch`; `Resumed` in `notes.run.resumed`), `keyframes.rs` (`adopt`), `steering.rs` + climate stage (the nudges), `deeptime run --stop-myr --epochs`, `deeptime resume`. JNI `createWith(…, flags)` (1 epochs, 2 resume). Checkpoint schema 13.
- **Nudges:** `steering` section (on in the four Earth-like built-ins and the pipeline presets; absent or `enabled: false` = unsteered, bit for bit): over the last `tail_fraction` (0.1) a smoothstep weight drives (a) a sea-level offset as ocean water drawn into or given back from the mantle (2 m/Myr at full weight and 5 points of land error, at most 200 m; reported as Earth-equivalent water volume through Airy hydro-isostasy 0.688) toward a land band, and (b) a factor on volcanic outgassing (0.2 of ln per Myr at 5 K error, within ×2/÷2) toward a temperature band. Targets temperate/warm/cool/custom. Dead band, saturating rate; report in `notes.climate.steering`.
- **UI:** Create World run page: **Stop here** (running) / **Play this epoch** (done) at the scrubbed frame, **Continue to [N]** (done); a superseded run's staging folder is kept; the staging mover deletes `epochs/`. Editor fields (playability: toggle, target, tail, shape, custom bands; adv_climate: rates and limits) and lang keys. Workbench: epoch checkpoints every 25 Myr and **Stop / continue** on a finished run (`POST /api/runs/<id>/resume`, hard-links the source's checkpoints and frames).
- **Bug fixed in passing:** the Andean orogeny event's end time was written in Myr, not years (`plates/subduction.rs`); a run continued past the present made the event end before it began (refused by the validator). It changes master's event log, nothing else.
- **Measured** (test VM, quick 16k, scattered, 500 Myr, 4 threads; `tools/review/steering-measure.sh` + `steering-report.py`; scratch /Volumes/Graphide/ban/deeptime-runs/steering, deleted): steering off vs master's binary (seeds 1, 2): 24 of 27 listed files byte-identical, the rest `preset.json` and the event log (the fix above). Epoch store: 10 checkpoints, 2.6–2.9 GiB, 11–13 s of writing in a 650-s run. Nudge cost: none measurable (655 vs 662 s). Pick at 250 Myr 119 s (13 of 125 steps), stop at 120 Myr 116 s (15 of 60), continue to 700 Myr 302 s (125 of 350; a planned 700 would be ~900 s). Default nudges: sea −52/−41 m, land 0.151→0.160 and 0.176→0.183 (band 0.25–0.35 not reached: the planets lose land through their last 50–100 Myr); strong (10 m/Myr, 600 m, 20 %): −473/−269 m, land 0.211/0.217, 12–21 % of an Earth ocean. Temperature: all ended 14–17 °C (in band, outgassing untouched); warm target 17.3→18.7 °C (×1.36), cool 17.3→13.7 °C (÷2 limit). No control reversed direction in any run; largest sea step 4 m (default), 18 m (strong) per 2-Myr step.
- **Client walk** (VM, `tools/client/vm-client.sh --name playability --prop length=200 --prop epochs=true --prop continue=50`): review/out/playability/ (06-run-done shows Play this epoch and Continue; 07a the frame picked, 07b the 150-Myr epoch baked (7 frames, 78 s), 07c continued to 200 Myr (96 s; 8 frames and 1,202 events, as the original 200-Myr run), then review, accept, in-world).
