### 2026-10-05 — `memory_estimate` fixed after the memory-accounting and Petroff–Guyou merges (agent worktree agent-a9a0f9863380efa66, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; master 6489d4a5 merged; not merged)
- **Cause.** On the test planet the bake phase peaked at 101.2 MiB against the run's estimate of 98.7. The estimate had no bake in it (the bake had stayed under the biggest stage by luck), and the projection pass added 7.5 MiB over the Lambert bake's 93.8: its `resample_grid` kept every resampled layer twice (the zeroed output arrays and the per-row buffers of all rows, copied into them at the end), the horizon stacks were cloned for the top raise, the Lambert elevation and amplitude were loaded a second time as sources of their grid, and the bake's freed blocks sat in the allocator's keep-for-reuse count beside the pass's arrays (they are the wrong sizes for them).
- **Fix.** `resample_grid` copies rows out in bands of 64 (no second copy of the output); the stacks move instead of being cloned; the elevation and amplitude layers are shared (`Arc`) with their grid's sources; `finalize_write` gives the kept blocks back (`MemoryGauge::release`) before the pass. `estimate_for` gained `bake_bytes` (the world the amplification leaves + the projection pass's working set, `bake::project::estimate_bytes`; `bake_projection_bytes` alone), which counts in `peak_bytes`; `amplify::world_bytes` is the world the estimate uses. Bytes per cell of each grid's layers (L1 288, L2 16, L3 8) are constants in `bake/project.rs`; `bake::tests::the_projection_estimate_covers_the_baked_layers` fails if the bake outgrows them. The test's tolerance is unchanged.
- **Measured** (`cargo test -p deeptime-core --test memory_estimate -- --nocapture`, test VM, the test planet): bake phase 101.2 → 93.8 MiB, which is now the Lambert bake's own peak (the projection pass stays under it: about 87 MiB counted, 18.0 MiB in the estimate); run peak 101.2 → 93.8 against 98.7 estimated; resident peak 114.0 MiB against a limit of 119.1. Keeping the bake's freed blocks under its estimate (`keep_below`) was tried and dropped: it cut the count to 82.0 MiB but left the resident peak (set earlier, in the young stage) only 1.8 MiB inside the test's tolerance.
- **Not modelled.** The Lambert bake itself (strata, climate, water: about 33 MiB of live memory over the world on the test planet, 47 with the allocator's kept blocks) is not in `bake_bytes` (75.3 MiB here, so the bake phase holds more than it); only the run's peak, which the stages cover, is checked. A model needs its bytes per L1 cell measured at two resolutions.
- **Next.** Coordinator: merge the branch.

### 2026-10-05 — Memory accounting matches the process (P1-24 question 3 (a), "fix it now"; agent worktree agent-a49cb06509c2f140f, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c, continued after two stops; master 2e07d954 merged; not merged)
- **Where the memory went.** (1) glibc kept freed memory the count never saw: every grid-sized array freed by a stage raised malloc's mmap threshold (up to 32 MiB), after which the next arrays came from the threads' arena heaps and stayed there fragmented after being freed: 0.5–1.6 GiB on quick, up to 2.2 GiB on full. (2) The count added only the requested size (no page or chunk rounding). (3) The per-stage estimates of deposits, structure, volcanoes and impacts listed only their own working set, not the world they run beside (deposits: 178 MiB listed while the run held 1.4 GiB). (4) The keyframe ring held 16 raw frames (26 layers × 1024 × 326 RGBA, 35 MiB each: up to 550 MiB). (5) Allocations a stage did not reserve went over the cap with nothing making room for them.
- **What changed.** `deeptime_core::alloc` (new) is the one counting allocator (the CLI, the JNI library and the core's tests declare it): on Linux a block of 1 MiB or more is its own anonymous mapping (munmap on free, mremap to grow), so freed grids leave the process; a large block counts its pages and a small one its malloc chunk. Mapping every grid afresh cost +27 % CPU on quick, so up to 1 GiB of freed large blocks is kept for reuse by the next block of the same size (counted as in use; measured +5 % CPU at 1 GiB, +16 % at 256 MiB). `MemoryGauge` gained `phase`, `phase_peak`, `release`, `keep_below` and `reserved`: before each step the session sets a ceiling (the stage's estimate + the history the cap leaves in memory) above which kept blocks go back to the OS (also when small blocks or growth in place pass it), releases them at every stage's end and before the history spills, and spills history frames so the stage's estimated working set and what its last step held fit under the cap. `estimate_for` adds the world the stages before them left to the four own-only stages and gives a coupled group its members' most; each stage now also lists `own_bytes` (its own figure, what the estimate used before). The keyframe ring holds frames LZ4-packed (~4 MiB a frame); `copyKeyframe` unpacks only the layer asked for. CLI: `deeptime run` prints the estimate beside the measured peak; `DEEPTIME_MEM_TRACE=<file>` traces each phase (count peak, VmHWM reset per phase, glibc's held/free), `DEEPTIME_LARGE_ALLOC`/`DEEPTIME_LARGE_CACHE` for experiments. Tools: `tools/review/memacct-table.py` (the per-phase table), `p1-24-profile.sh` takes `P124_BIN`/`P124_ENV`.
- **Measured** (test VM, mid6 profile of `tools/review/p1-24-profile.sh`: 12 CPUs, 11 threads, `--mem-cap 4294967296`, scattered_continents 500 Myr; before = master 2e07d954's binary for the run, the per-phase before = master of 2026-10-04 with only the tracer added (runs b-glibc, b-full), since master has no tracer; after = this branch's head; `python3 tools/review/memacct-table.py /Volumes/Graphide/ban/deeptime-runs/memacct/{f-quick,f-full}`). ### 2026-10-05 — SW-1 the seamless world: Petroff–Guyou in the format, the bake and every reader (Ben, decisions log 2026-10-04, "We'll proceed w/ Petroff–Guyou" and "Engine only; pause IP"; agent worktree agent-a857faf5aead2df37, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c, continued after two stops; master 2e07d954 merged; not merged)
- **What changed.** Format 0.5. `deeptime_format::projection::PetroffGuyou` (Petroff 2021's equal-area square map in Guyou's aspect, two hemisphere squares of side b = 256·round(C/(256√(2π))): 13,312 × 6,656 at 16k, 26,112 × 13,056 at 32k) on portable trigonometry (`portable_math`), with bit-identical twins in Java (`worlddata/PortableMath`, `Petroff`, `PetroffGuyou`, `WorldProjection`, `WorldLayout`) and JS (`crates/deeptime-viewer/assets/projection.js`: `DTMath`, `DTPetroff`, `DTPetroffGuyou`). Every manifest carries the layout block `projection` (FORMAT.md "The world's layout", `layout_version` 1, the wrap engine's Phase 2 contract): kind, b, λc, the fundamental domain, the four edges with their `CellIsometry` `[k, tx, tz]`, pivot and owner (west/east slides by ±2b, `toroidal_world`; north/south half-turns `[2, 0, ∓b]` about (0, ∓b/2), `wrap_engine`), the cone points and pole images, and the temporary `edge_stop` border. The bake's last step (`bake::project`) rewrites the Lambert folder in the world's projection: λc chosen per planet (0.25° candidates, the cone points farthest from land), every raster resampled from the sphere through a footprint isotropic on the planet and, new today, widened along the parallels poleward of ~59° (`polar_widening`: (0.52/cos φ)⁴, at most 8; SCL-090), categories (now including `climate/wetland` and any `flag` layer) from the nearest cell, edge rows self-glued, and rivers, structure, bodies, sites, volcanoes, craters and spawn candidates carried through the projection and its Jacobian. Readers: Java grids fold through the half-turns, detail noise folds and blends at the edges, FarTerrain/DH, rivers, structure, the climate API (version 4: `latitudeDeg(level, x, z)`, `longitudeDeg`, `projectionKind`), F3, planet info, spawn; the workbench, world-map and preview tools. Toroidal World keeps the x slide (level types' circumference 2b). `wrap/EdgeBorder` stops players, their vehicles and Sable ships 1 block inside the north/south edges (warning 24 blocks before; spectators pass; off on Lambert levels; no pole cap on this world). Lambert stays a setting: `scale.projection` `lambert` (editor "World map"), level types `deeptime:planet_lambert`, `planet_lambert_32k`. New dev command `deeptime project --world-data <lambert bake> --out <dir> [--set …]` re-runs the pass on a Lambert bake (tuning without a new history).
- **Today (the restart).** Merged master 2e07d954 (conflicts in claims.md counts and STATUS only); master's new wetland flag resampled as a category (it was averaged: 0 and 2 made 1, swamp); master's new real-planet editor GameTest moved to the world projection; the sections test's first column fixed; rustfmt. The polar streaks were not gone: the isotropic footprint left the tangential-over-radial slope ratio at 80–88° at 13.4 (point sample 47.4; mid-latitudes 1.32), because the simulation's solvers work in Lambert blocks and its polar terrain has the grid's shape. Swept on the earlier evidence bake with `deeptime project` (`DEEPTIME_POLAR_WIDEN=cos0,max,power`): (0.5,·,2) 1→13.4/10.3 (80–88°/70–80°), 4→3.70, 8→1.39/4.84, 16→0.83/4.84; (0.34,16,2) 1.80/7.81; (0.52,8,4) 1.39/3.21; (0.52,12,4) 0.86/2.82; (0.6,8,4) 1.39/3.13. Kept (0.52, 8, 4): the poles match the mid-latitudes, the subpolar band drops from 10.3 to 3.2, the pass costs ~2 s more. A broad fan of ridges at 65–80° remains on some planets (the simulation's own grid-shaped valleys; the Lambert world shows them as north–south striation); see the question below. The first GameTests on the merged branch then found three faults of the pass, fixed: (1) the climate's band coordinates (`vanilla_param`: temperature, vegetation, continents, erosion, ridges, set per Köppen class) were footprint means, so near the poles they mixed neighbouring classes (Dfc and Dfd columns of the 4k test planet drew forest, Dsub 0.000 against its floor 0.38): now read bilinear at the point, as the Lambert world's game read them; (2) the stacks (nearest cell) could sit under the footprint-mean terrain (`a_planet_run_bakes_every_chunk_time_layer`, "top horizon under the terrain's top block"): the pass now raises every world stack's first horizon by the bake's top rule over the world's own terrain (`notes.bake.projection.top_raise`); (3) the 4k test planet's eight unranked spawn candidates lay on the Lambert rows past the south pole (z 682–698 > R 652) and all became the south pole (-768, 768), under the sea: candidates past the pole are dropped, and unranked ones are picked again on the world's grids, clear of the edges by 64 blocks (POL-024).

### 2026-10-04 — Expanded Ecosphere as a first-class target beside Terralith; Deep Time's biome rules (Ben's "Build out support for both so if I install EE it works or if I go w/ terralith it also works"; agent worktree agent-a8709dc1408faa573, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; master d894c2df merged; not merged)
- **What EE's override did.** EE 3.4.7 (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; downloaded to the VM for testing only, `smoke/ee`, never shipped or edited) registers the built-in datapack `ee_default` through Cristel Lib in its default mode: `data/minecraft/dimension/overworld.json` (vanilla noise generator, inline multi-noise list of 4,589 entries, 240 biomes) and its own `minecraft:overworld` noise settings. Vanilla's `WorldDimensions.bake` takes a datapack dimension ahead of the preset (and of level.dat), so a `deeptime:planet` world with EE was a plain EE world: on the 16k planet below, master's jar booted, Toroidal World still looped it at 1,024 chunks, and `/deeptime probe biomes` answered "minecraft:overworld is not a Deep Time level on world data".
- **Fix** (Java `worldgen/OverworldOverride`, from `mixin/WorldDimensionsShapeMixin` before the planet shape): in a Deep Time world the datapack overworld is set aside, Deep Time's generator stays and takes that dimension's biome source in place of `preset: minecraft:overworld`; every other Deep Time level on the overworld preset does too (the GameTest server's levels, through `GameTestServerMixin`); a vanilla-preset world keeps EE's override. The adopted list is saved in level.dat. Log line `[deeptime] overworld: ...`.
- **A second EE trap found by the GameTests**: EE's surface rule paints smooth basalt below y −55 (an absolute vertical gradient, a layer for vanilla's 384-block world). Through `deeptime:delegate` it stood down to the planet's floor and replaced every rock class below −55 (`everyClassInTheWorld` 961 wrong, parity 59 of 144 samples). `DelegatingRuleSource` now leaves out a pack's top-level world-depth layers (absolute gradients of a block other than stone, deepslate, bedrock; BIO-131); vanilla's deepslate gradient and the bedrock floor stay. AT entries for four `SurfaceRules` records.
- **Biome rules** (Java `climate/BiomeRuleSet` format + matching, `climate/BiomeRules` binding/facts/search, `climate/RuleCensus`; consulted in `VolcanicBiomes.find`): data files `data/<ns>/deeptime/biome_rules/*.json`, active when the source can place a `requires` biome; the first rule whose conditions hold (Köppen class or prefix, t_mean/t_warm/t_cold °C, p_mm, elevation, wetland any/warm/cold/none, ice cover, playa, volcanic zone, top rock class, the plain answer in/not in a list) runs the pack's own R-tree search over that rule's candidates only; `exclusive` keeps candidates out of the climate search elsewhere; `role` rules pick among a volcanic role's biomes before the role tag. Shipped: `deeptime:peatland` (cold wetland → `#deeptime:peatland`, a new tag: EE fen, berry_bog, snowy_bog, snowy_fen; BOP bog, muskeg; RU fen; CliffTree bog; for every pack) and `deeptime:expanded_ecosphere` (19 rules: icy/tropical volcano, thermal taiga/mud pools, glacial cliffs, ice cap, salt lakes on playas, tsingy on tropical carbonate, black beach ×2, Tibesti, hot desert, low/high-arctic tundra, polar desert, dry tropical forest, temperate rainforest, Mediterranean scrub, cold steppe). Volcanic role tags gain EE's volcano, volcanic crater, thermal taigas, mud pools, basaltic incursions, volcanic chamber (after Terralith's and BOP's). FORMAT.md "Biome rules"; docs/science/biomes.md "Expanded Ecosphere and the biome rules"; ledger BIO-115 to BIO-131 (13 game-choice + BIO-131, 3 from-memory: BIO-124 CAVM, BIO-126 Holdridge, BIO-127 Alaback); bibliography Walker2005, Alaback1991.
- **Evidence** (one `earthlike_quick_16k` planet, scattered continents, 500 Myr, seed 1, this branch's CLI, `tools/review/ee-biomes.sh run ee16`; census `tools/review/ee-biomes.sh census <ee|mic|standalone> ee16`, shares `tools/review/profile_shares.py`; 93,727 land columns): before (master's jar + EE) no Deep Time overworld. After with EE: rules decided 36,891 of 94,657 census land columns, roles 107; not-candidate 0, wrong-class 0, exclusive leaked 0; cold wetland on peatland 94 of 97. Distinct biomes on land EE 141 / Terralith 88 / vanilla 40; share on the mod's own biomes 0.69 / 0.42 / 0. Per class (EE | Terralith | vanilla): Aw dry_tropical_forest 60 % | arid_highlands 43 % | savanna 76 %; Am tropical_rainforest 71 % | shrubland+brushland 50 % | jungle 74 %; Csa chaparral 87 % | plains 46 % | plains 70 %; BSk cold_plains 50 % | plains 57 % | plains 82 %; ET tundra 58 % + snowy_tundra 8 % | cold_shrubland 24 % | snowy_plains 67 %; EF ice_cap 88 % | frozen_peaks 34 % | snowy_slopes 51 %; Dfc taiga 61 % | taiga 36 % | taiga 50 %. Gaps EE closes: peatland, summer tundra, ice sheet biome, tropical dry forest, Mediterranean scrub, cold steppe, salt lakes (41 columns), tsingy (128), temperate rainforest (68), black beach (56), volcano and hot-spring climate variants. Never reached on this planet: berry_bog, snowy_fen, salt_lakes_pink. Two rules came from the first census: hot desert (EE's own list made 40 % of BWh chaparral) and temperate rainforest exclusive (28 % of Dfc was temperate rainforest). MIC and vanilla censuses: no rule file active, no override line.
- **Tests:** JUnit `BiomeRuleSetTest` (5: the shipped files parse, columns select their rules, peatland cold only, bad files refused with reasons, ranges and wetland states). GameTests `BiomeRuleGameTests` (every profile; EE checks only with `-Ddeeptime.ee.expected`, set by build.gradle from the set): `overworldOverrideKeepsDeepTimesGenerator`, `deepTimeLevelsTakeTheOverridingBiomes`, `expandedEcosphereRulesAreLive` (every named id registered and placeable, every rule bound, roles resolve to wythers), `mappedBiomesAreReachable`, `expandedEcosphereBiomesFollowTheirRules` (census on test_planet_real).

- **State.** Built on branch `worktree-agent-a1d2d85d0bfeddcc8` (on the ice branch `worktree-agent-a1c432fc38faa9742`, master 7c14e4ab merged in): T1–T4 (earlier), T5 snapshot integration and Köppen on L2, T6 clock coupling, T7 satellite view (sea ice per cell, temperature unblurred; keyframes carry `climate/sea_ice_{max,min}`), T8 editor settings (16 fields, presets, lang, `AdvancedSettingsTest`, HNT-101 to HNT-116; HNT-098 to HNT-113 before the ice branch landed), T9 calibration on Earth's relief (part), T11 docs (science page `docs/science/per-cell-climate.md` rewritten as built, CLM-119 to CLM-146 rewritten as coded, CLM-167 to CLM-179 added, FORMAT/EVENTS/plan notes). The design's §11 "As built" records every deviation. Left: T9's rest (ice reference, observed-grid metrics, the rain budget) and T10 (downstream checks).
- **T6, the zonal clock's correction** (`percell::fit_flux`). A flux per band alone could not hold the zonal model on the 2-D zonal means (it hit any cap up to 80 W/m² at the poles and stalled at 0.7 K RMS): the zonal model's uniform D carries far more heat poleward than the 2-D model. The fit now gives every face between bands its own diffusivity from the 2-D model's heat transport and gradient, then a flux per band **and tile** (land, sea), from the 2-D model's zonal state, cap 60 W/m² (the design's 15 was too small for the land–sea split of mostly-sea bands). Triggered snapshots (3 K or 0.15 of sea ice against the last snapshot); every snowball's escape CO₂ in the run's notes; `deeptime run` prints a `climate_cell` line. Checkpoint schema 12. Tests: the corrected zonal model meets the 2-D zonal means (synthetic Earth: 0.29 K RMS, 2.3 K worst on Lambert's grid; 0.13/0.75 K on equal-angle rows); on a tropical supercontinent at 0.94 of the sun it freezes at 56 ppm where the 2-D model does at 36 and both thaw at 71,054 ppm (inside Hoffman et al.'s 10⁴–10⁵ ppm).
- **T9 on Earth's relief** (GMT `earth_relief_30m_p` resampled onto Lambert's grid, 720 × 240, `deeptime climate-dem --dump` + `tools/validation/climate_vs_obs.py`; banded in brackets): global mean **13.8 °C** (15.3; Ben's target 14.1 ± 0.4); winter along-row spread of land T at 30–70° 4.53 K (2.25; target ≥ 5.0), annual 1.92 K (0.64; ≥ 2.0); southern ice-edge std 2.5° (0°; ≥ 2°); Brest − Vladivostok January 20.6 K (7.1; ≥ 12, Earth 20.1); Yakutsk January −29.0 °C (−15.8; ≤ −28, Earth −39); cities in the right main group 19 of 24 (18; ≥ 21; misses Mumbai, Buenos Aires (rain), Denver, Lhasa (height), Anchorage); Köppen A 0.14 B 0.29 C 0.14 D 0.22 E 0.21. New defaults: `overturning_sv` 15 → 30, `atmosphere_diffusivity_scale` 1 → 1.3, `wind_heat_transport` 0.5 → 0.2, `zonal_diffusivity_ratio` 0.5 → 0.2, `ebm_warm_years` 6 → 12 (at 6 a supercontinent's last snapshot ended 0.21 W/m² out of balance), `KERNEL_EARTH` 2.845·10⁷ → 2.475·10⁷ (1° relief). The 30 Sv conveyor is a compensating choice: the January North Atlantic at 55° N was −3.7 °C at 15 Sv (Earth about +9), and the ocean's northern heat transport now peaks at 3.1 PW (Earth 1.5–2) while the atmosphere's is 3.6 PW (Earth 5.0). The budget rain (`rain_model = budget`) is not ready: Earth's land gets 1,416 mm (belts 528, Earth about 750), Dhaka 24 mm, the Atacama 2,649 mm; `belts` stays the default (§3.8).
- **Lambert's projection** (master 7c14e4ab) gives the climate grid tall high-latitude rows (144 × 48 on Earth's 720-cell relief, the polar row 73–90°). It joined the North Atlantic and Pacific through the Arctic into one conveyor basin (fixed: a row is in the basin's band only when its poleward edge is inside 70°), cooled Yakutsk by 9 K less than the equal-angle grid did, and loosened the correction's fit (0.25 K RMS, up to 3.5 K worst at polar rows). `climate-dem` read its equirectangular DEM as W/π rows on master; it reads W/2 now.

### 2026-10-04 — Terralith-side biome fixes: a pack placement table and the geology gate (Ben's "Deep Time-side fixes (Recommended)", "Keep them", "Doesn't apply, carry on"; agent worktree agent-ac7952b1a5cb7de8c, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c, continued after three restarts; master 6489d4a5 merged; not merged)
- **Asked (decisions log 2026-10-04):** the survey's fixes 2, 3 and 10 (research note biome-mods-survey.md §7–9), no Deep Time biomes, no fantasy veto, all changes in Deep Time's own data (Terralith's licence forbids overriding its files).
- **Pack placement tables (shared mechanism, its own early commit f0d78942).** `crates/deeptime-core/data/climate_mapping/packs/<id>.json`: `{schema, id, requires_biomes, priority, patch}`, `patch` a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386) on `placement.json`. The game keeps a table when every `requires_biomes` id is registered (Java `climate/PlacementPacks`, `ClimatePlacement.packs/chosen/jarPacks`): a dedicated server's first start from its resources (a datapack may add or replace one), the Create World editor from the jar against the screen's data-pack registries (`EditorModel.Deps.game(…, content)`); content-bundle key `climate_placement_patches`; the core merges them over the base table (`Placement::with_packs`) and records `notes.bake.climate.placement.patches` and `class_rule_cells`; `deeptime run --placement-patch <file>`. The table gains `class_rules` (first rule of a class whose conditions on t_mean/t_warm/t_cold/aridity/abs_lat_deg/height_m all hold replaces its temperature, humidity, erosion, continentalness; not on glaciated land), a `continentalness` limit (inland of the beach strip), and switches on the new inputs. Biomes O' Plenty or Expanded Ecosphere get theirs by dropping a file with their own `requires_biomes`. FORMAT.md "Pack placement tables", "Class rules".
- **Terralith's table** (`packs/terralith.json`, ledger BIO-140 to BIO-146, tuned with an offline copy of the game's search, `tools/review/terralith_emulate.py`, 98.8 % agreement with the in-game census): Am humidity ≥ 4.05; Csa/Csb/Csc humidity squeezed into 0.1–0.6; BSk the same and erosion 0.12–0.4 (MIC's mapping turns it into about 0.12–0.33, inside Terralith's steppe slot); ET on the positive variant branch (humidity 1.5, the survey's proposal, measured and changing nothing); class rule `cloud_forest`: Cfb/Cwb/Cfc/Cwc below 25°, above 1,000 m, P/PET > 1 → cold band (ramp `montane`), humidity ≥ 3.05, erosion ≥ 0.62, continentalness ≥ 0.35. 1,000 m read in Scatena et al. 2010 (BIO-145 verified); 25° from-memory (BIO-144).
- **Geology gate, now a biome rule file** (first built as its own keep-out metric in `climate/VolcanicBiomes`, 870e9d21; on merging master's Expanded Ecosphere biome rules, d75b9c7c, it became one of them and the parallel metric is gone). The rule format gains two conditions: `ground` (role ids of `worldgen/GeologyGround`; the column's ground has one) and `in_slot` (the source's own search with nothing kept out gives one of the rule's candidates). `data/deeptime/deeptime/biome_rules/rock_named.json` (requires `#deeptime:geology`) has one rule per role: `{"biomes": ["#deeptime:geology/<role>"], "ground": "<role>", "in_slot": true, "exclusive": true}`, so a rock-named biome is kept out of the climate search and given back its own slot only on its ground (the gate still never adds a biome). Its id sorts after `deeptime:peatland`, so a rule placing another biome comes first. Basalt Cliffs: at volcanoes by the lava-field role, on basalt coasts by the rule. The land-never-turns-to-water retry (c05bc8ca: where a kept-out answer on land is ocean or river and there is no tree under the source, search again without water leaves) now covers every kept-out biome in `keptSearch`, Expanded Ecosphere's exclusives included. Unlike the first version, rule-kept biomes are kept out below the surface layer and under the sea too (rules apply only at the surface on land), as every exclusive candidate is. `worldgen/GeologyGround`: roles shield (province class), granite (bedrock intrusive+felsic), carbonate/granite/basalt coast (sea within 32 blocks, bedrock of the coast within 48), dry_sedimentary (sedimentary bedrock, Köppen B), humid_karst (carbonate, A/C/D). Bedrock = the surface class, or under loose cover (saprolite and laterite are 68 % of the land surface) the first consolidated horizon within 8 blocks. ### 2026-10-04 — Cold wet lowland: taiga, or the pack's peatland (Ben, decisions log 2026-10-03 "Taiga instead, peatland if present"; worktree agent-a009e0a755a3d1c2a, session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c)
- **Rule.** Wet, flat, low, thawed land (BIO-066) of Dfc, Dfd, Dsc, Dsd, Dwc, Dwd (`classes.<code>.cold_wetland` in `placement.json`) is cold wetland: no longer vanilla's swamp band E6; it keeps the class's temperature and humidity with erosion held under E5, so without a mod it is taiga. Dfa, Dfb and the C classes keep the swamp. The bake writes `climate/wetland` (0 none, 1 swamp band, 2 cold). Ledger BIO-133 to BIO-137 (BIO-066 row amended), `docs/science/biomes.md` "Cold wetland", bibliography Xu2018 (PEATMAP: northern peatland 3.21 of 4.23 million km2; the paper itself could not be fetched, status `cited-unverified`).
- **Peatland where the pack has one, found not named.** `Peatland` / `PeatlandProbe` (Java): the first time a flagged column is sampled the game asks the level's biome source, per TerraBlender region of the province table (one answer for a pack without regions), what it puts at the swamp row of the cold band (450 climates through the world's mapping); a peatland biome is one in the shared tag `#deeptime:peatland` (master's tag of the EE, BOP, Regions Unexplored and CliffTree bogs and fens, every entry optional; no second list here) or, for a pack nobody listed, one tagged `c:is_swamp` and (`c:is_cold/overworld` or `c:is_snowy`); a region that answers with one at half the points or more has its flagged ground raised to the middle of E6 (`WorldDataTerrain.raster`). The verdict is stored in `climate_mapping.json` (`peatland`). BOP: `biomesoplenty:overworld_secondary` only (bog; its primary region's swamp row is `wetland`, not cold); MIC and standalone: none, so taiga.
- **Dropped on the way:** the first design (the previous agent's) used a temperature threshold `biomes.wetland_cold_below` (2): it took all of Dfb (the table puts every D class on the boreal ramp: 936 of 2,391 cold wetland cells were Dfb), against Ben's list. Replaced by the class flag; no preset field, editor field or lang key remains.
- **Census.** `BiomeCensus` counts the flagged columns apart (`cold_wetland`: layer present, columns, on a peatland biome, on taiga, on a swamp that is not peatland) over every land column, mod biomes included; E6 land is still set aside from the Köppen families. `climateConsistent` asserts the layer was baked and that at most 5 % of cold wetland is on a non-peatland swamp (old bake: no layer; old rule: all swamp).
- **Tests that fail on the old behaviour.** Rust `cold_wetland_is_taiga_or_peatland_not_swamp` (a wet Dfc plain: flag 2, erosion under E5; an Af plain stays swamp, flag 1, E6; the table's flag decides) and a placement parse check; JUnit `PeatlandTest` (7: peatland region verdict, none for vanilla/Terralith swamps, frozen- or temperate-band-only bogs do not count, under half the points does not, probe grid, JSON round trip); GameTest `climateConsistent` (layer baked, no plain swamp on cold wetland).
- **Measured** (after master's plate/35 m/EE merges; `earthlike_quick_16k`, scattered continents, 500 Myr, seed 1, `tools/review/peat-runs.sh`, `peat-biomes.sh`; the old rule is the same planet baked with the placement table minus `cold_wetland`, which is exactly the old rule; each planet probed through standalone, MIC, BOP (TerraBlender) and EE with `/deeptime probe biomes 16`): the six subarctic classes are 6,979 sampled land columns (Dfc 6,335, Dfb 5,157, unchanged); 97 columns (0.1 % of 94,659 land columns) are flagged. Columns of the six classes on a wetland biome, old rule -> new rule: standalone swamp 30 -> 0; MIC swamp 65 -> 0 (ice marsh 561 both: a frozen-band biome); BOP wetland 25 + swamp 5 -> 0; EE fen 40 -> 68 (fen 95 of the 97 flagged columns, through master's `deeptime:peatland` rule). Dfc taiga standalone 50.4 -> 50.7 %, MIC 36.2 -> 36.6 %, EE 61.6 -> 61.3 %. Flagged columns end on: standalone taiga 36, old growth spruce 25, beach 36; MIC old growth spruce 45, taiga 42, beach 10; BOP field 46, gravel beach 20, beach 16, old growth spruce 13, taiga 2 (none in a BOP secondary province, so no bog this planet: the probe's verdict is `biomesoplenty:overworld_secondary` -> bog); EE fen 95, cold ocean 2. Census `cold_wetland`: on a swamp that is not a peatland 0 on every profile. Full table in `docs/science/biomes.md`. (This planet has fewer flagged columns than the first measurement on an older master, 336; the cause was not investigated.)

The merge of master auto-merged `BiomeCensus.java` into a duplicate local (`coldWet`); the first Gradle run caught it and the rule census's flag is now `ruleColdWet`.

### 2026-10-04 — Create across the wrap engine's turning seams: kinetics and fluids adapters, refusals, train and contraption assessment (Ben's "If it can be done in parallel, do it now, otherwise defer. But we should be doing it."; agent worktree agent-a9fc837518e2419c1, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; dev-only behind `-Ddeeptime.wrapengine=true`, not merged)

**Docs.** The design is `docs/design/wrap-engine.md` §11, "Create across turning seams"; the §4.8
Create rows point at it. The adapters were built first on the spike's fold, then moved onto Phase 1's
API (§9) once master 01d63213 landed.

**Create 6.0.10**, the MIC pin (code MIT, assets all rights reserved):
- compileOnly, with the Ponder, Flywheel and Registrate jars it nests extracted for javac
  (`create_version` and `create_nested_jars` in `gradle.properties`);
- nothing copied; NOTICE.md lists it under "APIs called".

**The rule** (§11.1). A turn carries a speed s about +a to s about R(+a):
- a half-turn flips x and z speeds and keeps y;
- a quarter-turn swaps x and z and flips one of them;
- a face handed between block entities turns with the state.

`SeamTurns` holds the rule and `SeamTurnsTest` checks it (5 tests). On a half-turn seam, Guyou,
Peirce, a quarter-turn corner and the cube cross:
- a seam link is accepted from both ends or refused from both;
- the two turns of an accepted link cancel;
- refusals stay under 10 %.

The test found a cube-corner diagonal that is seen through the seam from one end only. Hence three
rules:
- a seam link must hold from both ends (`SeamTurns.seamLink`);
- pairs adjacent in stored space connect only directly;
- no self-links at turn points.

**Kinetics.**
- `KineticSeams` with `RotationPropagatorSeamMixin` re-runs Create's own `getRotationSpeedModifier`
  with the far block entity shown at its band position, its state turned back and faces turned. The
  result is multiplied by the axis sign.
- Create's answer is never used for a pair that is not adjacent in stored space: its axis rule ignores
  distance.
- `DirectionalShaftHalvesSeamMixin` gives a gearbox the face its source is seen through.
- Belts, chain conveyors and gantries are refused as custom connections.

**Fluids.**
- Faces are turned into the target's frame at 9 places: `FluidPropagator` (3), `PumpBlockEntity` (3),
  `FlowSource` (2) and `FluidNetwork`.
- `PipeConnection.determineSource` folds a band position.

**Refused, with a message and never a crash** (`SeamRefusals`: one log line per place and kind, plus an
action-bar message within 16 blocks):
- belts and chain conveyors whose span touches the band;
- track within a block of a seam: the track tool goes through Create's own placement message, and any
  other track block is broken one tick after it is placed;
- contraption assembly that reaches beyond a seam, through Create's `AssemblyException`, which shows on
  the goggles.

Contraption entities are also left out of the engine's carry: the adapters cancel `WrapCrossingEvent`
for them.

**Edits outside the compat package (small):**
- `DeepTimeMixinPlugin`: a `mixin.wrapengine.compat.<modid>` mixin needs the flag and the mod. Two dev
  switches leave adapters out: `-PwrapNoCompat` (all) and `-PwrapCompatSkip=…` (by name).
- `WrapEngine.init` wires the Create adapters at server start. Doing it during mod construction loaded
  Create's classes early and broke Registrate.
- `WrapEngineGameTests.TOPOLOGY` includes the Create sites.

**Evidence** (`./gametest.sh -PwithMic -PwrapEngine`, test VM, 2026-10-04). All 4 Create tests passed:
- **Half-turn kinetics:**
  - z shafts: far stored speed +16 at (24574, 20480…20482), against the control's −16;
  - y cogs keep their sign; x cogs flip;
  - breaking the shaft next to the motor stops all 7 shafts, the far side included.
- **Quarter-turn kinetics:** z shafts land as an x line at (25600…25602, 22534), +16 against −16.
- **Fluids:** the far tank holds 112 mB of water after 120 ticks, the same as the control.
- **Refusals:**
  - a belt across the seam is refused, while one on this side connects;
  - a bearing across the seam is refused, while one on this side assembles;
  - track at the seam is broken, while track 5 blocks away stays.
- **Control without the adapters** (`-PwrapNoCompat`): the far shafts stand at 0 rpm, the far tank
  stays at 0 mB, and the belt is not refused.

**Found: 6 of Phase 1's own tests fail under MIC** (`-PwithMic -PwrapEngine`). The same 6 fail
without the adapters:
- `redstoneAcross*`: 13, then 0 beyond the seam. The likely cause is Alternate Current [not read].
- `playerCrosses*`: a KubeJS payload sent to the fake player.
- `bandReload*`: a band chunk is not re-copied in time.

**Found: an intermittent boot failure with the engine and MIC.** Registrate reports "Found unused
register callbacks", and the server fails to start:
- with the adapters, 4 of 16 boots, none of the 8 since the merge onto Phase 1;
- without them, 1 of 12 boots.

§11.7 records this.

**Gates:**
- `./gradlew build test`: tests=292, failures=0, skipped=2.
- `./gametest.sh -PwrapEngine`: all 19 passed (the Create tests are skipped without Create).
- `tools/smoke/install.sh mic` (157 mods), then `./gametest.sh -PwithMic`: all 74 passed.
- `./gametest.sh -PwithMic -PwrapEngine`:
  - the 4 Create tests pass;
  - 6 of Phase 1's tests fail, as above.

**Blocked on later phases** (§11.7):
- band block-entity data on the client: the turned Create tags (`Speed` times the sign, `Source` moved,
  pipe faces re-keyed);
- whole-world topologies.

**Assessed, not built:**
- trains across a half-turn: 13–22 days, through a same-dimension portal edge on Create's portal-track
  machinery, with "dimension" generalised to "frame", client included; a quarter-turn adds 2–4 days;
- contraptions: 11–19 days.

**Next:**
- fold Alternate Current;
- find the boot race (`-PgametestDebugLog`);
- band block entities with turned Create tags;
- refuse piston and gantry movement into the band (`ContraptionCollider.isCollidingWithWorld`).

### 2026-10-03/04 — Volcanic biomes tied to real volcanoes (Ben's "Tie them to real volcanoes (Recommended)"; agent worktree agent-a3528f881aff2d206, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Asked (decisions log 2026-10-03):** where the pack has volcanic biomes (Terralith's yellowstone, volcanic peaks, volcanic crater, caldera, ashen savanna, basalt cliffs, thermal caves; Biomes O' Plenty's volcano, volcanic plains, hot springs) they go only at real volcanoes and are kept out everywhere else; without them the climate's biome stays.
- **Design chosen** (Java `worldgen/VolcanicZones`, `climate/VolcanicBiomes`, `climate/VolcanicCensus`; FORMAT.md "Volcanic biomes"; ledger BIO-104 to BIO-114):
  - *Kept out:* every biome of the tag `#deeptime:volcanic` (the seven role tags) is never the answer of a Deep Time level's climate search. The search stays the pack's own R-tree (the province's region tree with TerraBlender) with a distance metric that puts those leaves infinitely far, so the next-nearest biome of the same tree answers: no fixed filler, works for any mod's biomes. The plain search runs first and only a volcanic answer pays for the second search. One hole found and closed: Biomes O' Plenty puts volcanic plains in a slot whose next-nearest biome in its region is the lukewarm ocean (113 land columns on the 16k planet); with TerraBlender a kept-out land slot that would turn to ocean or river takes the vanilla region's (region 0) biome instead (beach there).
  - *Put in:* discs in blocks from the baked volcano list, the geothermal pools and the magma bodies, in priority order (first role whose disc holds the column and whose biome the pack has wins):

    | Role | Biome (first the pack has) | Condition |
    |---|---|---|
    | hot-spring field | terralith:yellowstone, biomesoplenty:hot_springs | every hot-spring pool (volcano or hot ground): its reach + 4 blocks |
    | caldera floor | terralith:caldera | crater with `caldera: true`: 0.9 of the rim radius |
    | summit crater | terralith:volcanic_crater, terralith:volcanic_peaks, biomesoplenty:volcano | other craters: rim + 4 blocks |
    | cone (summit, upper flanks) | terralith:volcanic_peaks, biomesoplenty:volcano | stratovolcanoes and shields: 0.45 R × reach |
    | fresh ash | terralith:ashen_savanna, biomesoplenty:volcanic_plains | stratovolcanoes and caldera complexes of activity ≥ 0.75: R × reach, where the climate point is inside the biome's own temperature and humidity ranges |
    | young lava | terralith:basalt_cliffs, biomesoplenty:volcanic_plains | shields: R × reach, same climate gate |
    | thermal caves | terralith:cave/thermal_caves | underground: 1.5 chamber radii, from the biome's own lowest depth parameter down |

    Every disc ≥ 8 blocks in radius (two biome cells), a field ring narrower than 8 blocks is dropped; surface roles hold where the biome depth parameter is under 0.2 (vanilla's cave band, read in OverworldBiomeBuilder: BIO-112), on land (terrain at or above the sea at the cell centre) and not on a river channel (variant input exactly 0, so rivers keep their biome). A role without a biome or not allowed gives way to the next disc's role, then to the climate search.
  - *Data:* the role lists are the tags `data/deeptime/tags/worldgen/biome/volcanic/<role>.json` (all entries optional, in order of preference; a pack adds, removes or reorders with tags), read in order from the server's biome registry and resolved once per level and tag load (`TagsUpdatedEvent`); only biomes the level's biome source can place count. The climate placement table (`placement.json`) is untouched apart from a note in its comment.
  - *Setting:* `underground.volcanic_biome_reach` (1.0, 0 to 3; 0: none placed), in the eight built-in presets, the editor (section adv_biomes, lang key) and FORMAT.md; scales the cone and the fields, not the craters, calderas, pools or caves.
  - *Plumbing:* `RegionSpawnTarget` now wraps every world-data level (with or without TerraBlender) and carries the level's volcanic state; the chunk-sampler mixin moved out of the TerraBlender-only package (`mixin/ChunkBiomesSpawnTargetMixin`) so generated chunks see it; new always-applied `mixin/VolcanicBiomeSourceMixin` (priority 1100, after TerraBlender's own) for plain multi-noise sources (vanilla, Terralith's list in MIC); `RegionBiomeSourceMixin` (TerraBlender) goes through the same code and, without a province table, uses TerraBlender's own region. Seven access-transformer entries (the R-tree's leaves and `findValueIndex`). Lithostitched, Tectonic, Citadel, Lithium and ModernFix in MIC were checked: none injects into `getNoiseBiome` or the chunk-sampler call. `TerraBlenderChecks` accepts a volcanic role biome in any region.
- **Evidence** (one quick 16k planet: `earthlike_quick_16k`, scattered continents, 500 Myr, built from master 0af3ff6e's CLI with `tools/review/volcanic-biomes.sh run vb`; 110 active stratovolcanoes, 45 of them oceanic, no shield or caldera; 50 hot-spring pools; `tools/review/volcanic-biomes.sh census <profile> vb` = `/deeptime probe biomes 16`, whose new `volcanic` section samples the same 51,574 land columns both as master placed them (the plain search) and as the branch does):

  | | MIC (Terralith) before | after | TerraBlender (BOP) before | after |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | volcanic-biome land columns (share of land) | 490 (0.95 %) | 591 (1.15 %) | 358 (0.69 %) | 557 (1.08 %) |
  | of them > 256 blocks from every volcano and pool | 285 (58 %) | 0 | 356 (99 %) | 0 |
  | of them > 8 blocks outside every zone | 459 (94 %) | 0 | 358 (100 %) | 0 |
  | hot-spring pools in the hot-spring biome | 2 of 50 | 50 of 50 | 0 of 50 | 50 of 50 |
  | lone volcanic surface cells (specks) | 10 of 525 | 26 of 9,797 | 0 of 5 | 37 of 9,538 |

  After: MIC volcanic peaks 341, yellowstone 154, ashen savanna 53, volcanic crater 43 columns; BOP volcano 384, hot springs 154, volcanic plains 19. What took the kept-out biomes' places (MIC): taiga 173, Terralith white cliffs 110, jagged peaks 37, savanna 36, forest 35, savanna plateau 25 (no ocean, river or cave biome); BOP: rainforest 176, beach 109 (the vanilla region's slot), floodplain 51, old-growth woodland 16. Standalone: 0 columns changed, the layer inactive. Zones on that planet: 50 hot-spring discs (mean 81 km²), 110 crater discs (19.6 km²), 109 cone discs (187 km²), 64 fresh-ash discs (1,180 km², of which only 53 sampled columns pass the climate gate) and 110 thermal-cave discs (38 km²). On the 4k test planet (MIC): pools 6 of 6 in yellowstone (plain search 2), volcanic columns 68 → 88, outside the zones 33 → 0, specks 0 of 355 cells.
- **Tests:** JUnit `VolcanicZonesTest` (9: each role's disc, the quiet cone without ash, shield and caldera complex, the hot-spring field over a caldera, the 8-block minimum, the seam, thermal caves, the reach setting and its parsing). ### 2026-10-03 — Orogenic collapse and the thickest crust: thickened belts give their area back (agent worktree agent-aeec1402fc6146955, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c, continued after two stops, re-measured 2026-10-04; not merged)
- **Ask.** Ben, decisions log 2026-10-03: "Merge, then give area back (Recommended)". Plate tasks 3-4
  cost continental crust (0.31 → 0.27 at 1000 Myr): crust crossing a collision front became belt
  thickness and never gave its area back. Kept as Ben said: PLT-253, resistance 200 mm/yr, stacking
  share 0.8, `arc_maturity_myr` 20.
- **What the model had.** At 500 Myr on master a fifth of the visible continental samples were thicker
  than 70 km (over 40 % of the crust's volume) under ground at a median 200-500 m; at 1000 Myr the
  median continental column was 83-104 km and the 99th percentile 450-480 km. Two causes, neither
  fixed here: the belt's cap (PLT-253) reads the elevation, which the surface stage owns and lowers
  (flexure, erosion) while the stacked thickness stays, so the belt keeps stacking; and a
  continent-on-continent overlap at a resampling adds the whole lower column to the upper one
  (PLT-228, `pools::accrete`).
- **Built** (`plates/collapse.rs`, run each plate step after belts and subduction; science page
  `docs/science/plates.md`, "Orogenic collapse and the thickest crust"; ledger PLT-254 to PLT-259):
  (1) *the thickest crust* (PLT-258): a visible continental column thicker than `crust_max_km`
  (70 km: Tibet and the Andes, Mooney et al. 2002; Lhasa 80 ± 2 km) loses the excess from its bottom
  to the mantle, no area back; (2) *collapse* (PLT-254): a visible continental sample no orogeny has
  raised for `collapse_quiet_myr` (10 Myr) and thicker than `collapse_thickness_km` (55 km) releases
  (1 − e^(−δt/τ))(T − 55 km), τ = `collapse_myr` 15 Myr, into the nearest samples of its plate
  thinner than the normal column (35.1 km), within `collapse_reach_km` (200 km, at least 1.5 sample
  spacings), filling them to 35.1 km; ocean floor filled turns continental. Heights follow Airy
  within each column's Airy height (a hidden root spreads without sinking its surface; a filled
  receiver rises to at most a continent's mean height). The driver is thickness, not height
  (the first version, height above 1.5 km, gave +0.02 crust at 500 Myr). Settings in the 12
  built-in presets and the test planet (`planet_world_4k`, which collapses now too), editor fields
  `collapse_time`, `collapse_thickness`, `collapse_quiet`, `collapse_reach`, `crust_max`, lang
  keys. The plates summary line gains `collapse_km3`, `collapse_gained_km2`, `foundered_km3`,
  `continental_thickness_km_p10/50/90/99` and a `crust_bins` diagnostic line.
- **Sources** (read by two Sonnet research sub-agents; bibliography section "Orogenic collapse"):
  Variscan crust 55-70 km by 315 Ma, thinned 315-290 Ma (Hillenbrand & Williams 2022, abstract);
  Bird 1991 (abstract): Moho relief not kept "for times greater than 10–20 m.y."; Urals root 50-56 km
  kept (Carbonell et al. 2000, abstract); channel flow 150 km in 15 Myr (Rey, Teyssier & Whitney 2010,
  full text); thickest crust 70+ km (Mooney, Prodehl & Pavlenkova 2002, full text). τ, the reach and
  the limit are taken from these; 55 km and the 10 Myr quiet time were chosen, inside the sources'
  range, by the 1000 Myr crust share (`calibrated` and `game-choice` in the ledger).

### 2026-10-04 — Wrap engine Phase 1: server core, band manager, entity crossing (Ben's "Folded access + band (Recommended)" and "TW slides, engine turns (Recommended)", 2026-10-03; agent worktree agent-a4445c63094be0023, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; master 297da4b6 merged; dev-only, not merged)
- **What.** The spike became the production core, package `wrapengine` (the old `wrap` package is Toroidal World's pole cap, unrelated), behind `-Ddeeptime.wrapengine=true` (`./gametest.sh -PwrapEngine`; `-PwrapBench` runs the benchmark with the engine off). Shipped default unchanged: without the flag no mixin is woven. Design doc `docs/design/wrap-engine.md` §9 (the stable API, for the Create-adapter agent) and §10 (as built).
  - A general edge table: translations, half-turns, quarter-turns, finite bands (`CellIsometry`, `WrapEdge`, `WrapTopology`); `WrapLayouts` builds Guyou (with or without the slides), Peirce, the survey's cube cross net (14 edges) and bounded test seams.
  - Folded access: `getBlockState`, `getFluidState`, `getBlockEntity`, `removeBlockEntity`, `setBlock`, neighbour updates, tick scheduling and queries; the `LevelChunk.setBlockState` choke point (a direct write into a band chunk goes to the stored block; one into a stored chunk replicates).
  - The `getBlockState` fast path: a grid over the bands' bounding box (`mayFold`), `@ModifyVariable` + `@ModifyReturnValue` so nothing is allocated off the bands.
  - `BandManager`: band chunks ticket their sources at their own level (`ChunkTicketLevelUpdatedEvent`), copy on load (only differing blocks; generated block entities and fresh mobs dropped), replication on every stored change; no random/weather/scheduled ticks, spawning or generation post-processing in band chunks.
  - Entity crossing with turned yaw, head, body, velocity and passengers; players teleported; `WrapCrossingEvent` (cancellable) for adapters.
- **Measured.** `./gametest.sh -PwrapEngine` on the VM: all 15 required tests passed. Each kind (half-turn seam, quarter-turn corner): building (stored turned, read back, band copy, solid both sides), collision (armour stand stops at oz + 0.2500), armour stand / item / mock player carried to the topology's fold with heading +180° / +90°, water 6,5,4,3,2,1,0 across (unglued control dry 7 of 7), redstone 15 14 13 | 12 11 and a repeater's turned band copy, block light 14 on the far side (21 and 40 blocks away in plain space), band consistency 0 wrong of 7,168 / 10,752 after 400 + 400 random edits and direct chunk writes, unload/reload 0 of 98,304 blocks wrong with the band chunk 31 / 16 chunks from its source. `WrapTopologyTest` 11 tests. Benchmark (ns per `getBlockState`, median of 20 interleaved rounds): engine off 23.8, woven with no topology 25.9, topology far away 25.8, whole-world Guyou interior 26.7, every read in a band 49.1 (medians of three JVMs each, alternated; JVM-to-JVM spread with the engine off 23.3–28.2).
- **Found.** The first run's reload tests failed: a band chunk whose level drops leaves the visible map and can come back without load or unload events, so replication skipped it and it stayed "synced" with stale blocks. Fixed (the manager tracks loaded band chunks and re-queues an invisible one's copy).
- **Gates.** `./gradlew build test`: tests=277 failures=0 skipped=2; `./gametest.sh`: all 71 passed; `tools/smoke/install.sh mic` (157 mods) then `./gametest.sh -PwithMic`: all 71 passed; `-PwrapEngine` 15 of 15. No Rust changed (no cargo gates). No physical constants (no ledger rows): band depth, copy budget and grid size are engineering choices.
- **Next.** Phase 2 (design doc §10.4): install a whole-world topology from the world data once Ben picks Guyou or the cube; block-entity data in the band and container range; fold `blockEvent`/sounds/level events; leashes, player vehicles and ghosts; world generation across seams; TW coexistence and DH.

### 2026-10-04 — Sphere-native grids: can the climate and surface maths run on the sphere without losing speed? (Ben's request, decisions log 2026-10-04; agent worktree agent-a68bfc6d58e378225, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; research only, no shipped code changed, not merged)
- **Note:** `docs/research/notes/sphere-native-grids.md` (indexed in `docs/research/README.md`); bibliography section "Sphere-native simulation grids" in `docs/science/bibliography.md`; no ledger rows (no constant enters code).
- **Answer:** solved by the climate models with patches of regular arrays (FV3's cube faces, NICAM's rhombi), not unstructured meshes; prior art for Deep Time's own algorithms on a sphere: fastscapelib's `HealpixGrid` (Braun–Willett on HEALPix), goSPL (global, HPC).
- **Benchmark:** `tools/research/sphere-grid-bench/` (own one-crate workspace; uses `deeptime-core`'s Fibonacci sphere and `SphereMesh`). Test VM, generic build, medians of 4 runs (L1, L2) and 2 (5.3M); the VM was loaded (load 13–25). L1, 333,824 cells, ns per cell, diffusion pass 1 thread / 8 threads; routing pass 1 thread: Lambert 0.88 / 0.29; 14.4. Cube 0.89 / 0.38; 14.1. HEALPix 0.95 / 0.37; 16.1. Icosahedral rhombi 1.77 / 0.40; 13.1. Fibonacci mesh: Fibonacci order 6.59 / 0.77; 18.9, Hilbert order 4.29 / 0.87; 14.6, random 8.34 / 1.31; 34.9. True-metric implicit diffusion (D·Δt/Δx² = 30, PCG to 1e-8): Lambert 785 iterations (1,273 ms) against cube 138 (249 ms), Lambert in block metric (as shipped) 129; at 5.3M 1,676 against 122. Commands: `tools/remote/mac.sh -- tools/research/sphere-grid-bench/run.sh build`; `tools/remote/mac.sh --no-sync -- tools/remote/detach.sh start sgbench --kind sim:quick:8t tools/research/sphere-grid-bench/run.sh run` (and `repeat`); `python3 tools/research/sphere-grid-bench/summarize.py review/out/sphere-grid-bench generic`.
- **Recommendation:** a cubed sphere for the climate (P1-26) now and for the surface solvers if the world becomes the equal-area cube (at quick 16k, 236 L1 cells per 3,776-block face edge: the same grid). Pending questions, "Sphere-native grids research".

### 2026-10-03/04 — Seamless projection survey: which projection for a portal-joined world (Ben's "Send off some research on what the current best projections would be for this"; agent worktree agent-a720027b758d66bc2, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; research only, not merged)
- **What.** `docs/research/notes/seamless-projection-survey.md` and its tools `tools/research/projection-survey/` (survey.py: any map as tiles plus a seam table, measuring area, shape, straight-walk drift and derivative jumps across every seam and face line; conformal.py: Schwarz triangle maps for the conformal cube, Peirce, Lee's tetrahedron; moser.py: a conformal map made equal-area by Moser's flow; bench.rs: inverse cost; run.sh runs them on the VM through the admission tool, results in review/out/projection-survey/). Two Sonnet sub-agents read the sources (formulas and licences; post-2015 cube-map work).
- **Found.** With quarter-turn seams the cube (8 corners of 270°) beats the pillowcase (4 of 180°) by a theorem: equal-area maps need shape ratio ≥ 4/3 near a cube corner against ≥ 2 near a Peirce point. Measured on 16 maps: the conformal cube made equal-area by Moser's flow (the note's own construction) has area 0.01 % rms, shape median 1.26 / max 1.42, no creases (derivative jumps ≤ 0.02, the table's floor); QSC = Roşca–Plonka (the same map, measured) median 1.32 / max 1.55, creased (diagonals ε 0.87, 41°); Petroff in the Guyou layout median 1.78 / max 2.67, smooth across its seams; HEALPix is a cube in disguise with 63° creases; Gringorten's crease lies on its seams. Inverse costs 4 ns (gnomonic) to 2 µs (Gringorten) per block; irrelevant at the bake (0.3 s for the table map on a 16k cube world).
- **Recommendation.** Equal-area smooth cube in a cross net (faces 3,776 / 7,552 blocks; 7 seam pairs: 1 translation, 4 quarter-turns, 2 half-turns); fallback face map QSC; runner-up Petroff in the Guyou 2:1 layout (1–2 crate days). Crate cost of the cube about 8–11 days, +5–10 days outside the crate over the Guyou plan.
- **Science docs.** Ledger SCL-078 to SCL-085 (all `not-yet-coded`); bibliography section "Seamless world projections" (Petroff2021, RoscaPlonka2011, CalabrettaGreisen2002, ONeillLaubscher1976, Rancic1996, Moser1965, Thurston1998, DimitrijevicStrobl2025; Lee1976 gains SCL-080); counts rewritten with `claims_counts.py --write`; research index row.

- **Design.** `docs/design/wrap-engine.md` (indexed in docs/research/README.md):
  - five architectures compared: rotated chunk views; folded access at the `Level` boundary; a
    replicated band; Toroidal World's client frame extended with turned packets; turned rendering on
    the client;
  - for each subsystem, the Minecraft and NeoForge hooks and the risks: block access, the band, light,
    world generation and caves, entities and AI, client and network, Distant Horizons, the MIC pack;
  - how Toroidal World 0.19.3 wraps (server canonical copy, unwrapped client frame, chunk-key aliasing,
    a `PacketTranslator` choke point, byte-identical chunk payloads), read on `mc/1.21` `5ded155` by a
    Sonnet sub-agent, and why a turn breaks it (`pos & 15` reverses).

  waited.
  - The cause: `admit.py`'s wait-loop signal handler (`_install_wait_signals` → `bail`) enters
    `with store` while the loop already holds `state.lock`. A SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP arriving
    inside the loop's locked section therefore deadlocks that process with the lock held.

### 2026-10-03/04 — Load-based admission on the test VM replaces the M6-era caps (Ben's "No set slots ... Guess load, run if load is less than what is available + 25%"; agent worktree agent-a2e1d18f0b1a34569, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; installed on the VM, not merged)
- **What it replaces.** The one-server lock (`deeptime-cache/server.lock`, `mac.sh --server`, preview.py,
  detached-server.sh, mic-climate.sh), "two simulations per agent, four of 2 threads on the box", and
  mac.sh's `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8` / `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=6` defaults. CLAUDE.md now states the new rule.
- **The tool.** `tools/remote/vm/admit.py` (stdlib Python; installed by `tools/remote/vm/install.sh` as
  `/usr/local/lib/deeptime/admit.py`, `deeptime-admit` on PATH; tests `tools/remote/vm/test_admit.py`,
  34 cases). `admit.py run --kind K [--server] -- cmd`: the kind's estimate (mean cores over a run,
  peak resident GiB) comes from a seed table, then from the kind's measured runs (weighted 90th
  percentile, each older run 0.85 of the next; the seed stays in the mix until three runs). The job
  starts when the estimate fits: CPU, 1.25 × (free − reserved − 4 cores kept for the play server,
  a workbench run and ssh), free cores = 32 − max(1-minute load, busy cores over the last 30 s from
  /proc/stat); memory by the rule in the **Memory rule** bullet below (first built as 1.25 × (free −
  reserved − 15 GiB), changed the same day); reserved = what admitted jobs have not used yet (CPU
  until a job first reaches 80 % of its estimate or for 3 minutes; memory for its whole life). Otherwise it waits in order, printing the reason; a smaller
  job may pass a bigger one until the bigger one has waited 15 minutes, then nothing passes it.
  Measurement: every 5 s the job's process tree, plus processes carrying its job id in their
  environment, plus the Gradle daemon its Gradle client is connected to (found through the client's
  TCP socket: a daemon runs one build at a time), minus nested admitted jobs; per-pid CPU deltas,
  with a reaped child's CPU not counted twice through its parent's cutime (a bug found in the demo:
  a 40-core peak on 32 cores; test `test_a_reaped_child_is_not_counted_twice` fails on the old code
  with 5.89 cores for a 1-core job). State in `deeptime-cache/admit/` (state.json, history.json,
  admit.log) under one flock; `deeptime-admit status` shows capacity, admitted, waiting with reasons,
  and the estimates. Settings in /etc/default/deeptime-admit. Quick looks (cat, grep, git, ...) and
  detached starts run at once; unrecognised commands are kinds of their own (`shell:<program>`) and
  start at once once two measured runs show them short and small.
- **Memory rule (Ben's answer, decisions log 2026-10-03; changed after the first build).** "Don't kill
  old things, just prevent new ones from launching if their usage isn't within it. I.E. On a machine w/
  4GB of ram we shouldn't force being under 3.5Gb at all times, If we are at 3.5Gb and a run is
  predicted to use 200mb it is green to run. If an agent predicts it will use 0.4 Mb [GB] then it will
  be red since that would use up 100% of the machine after margin is applied." Now: a job starts when
  its memory estimate × 1.25 is **under** free memory, free = MemAvailable − memory reserved but not
  yet used by admitted jobs (a job's reservation is its estimate minus what it has used so far, for
  its whole life). The 15 GiB standing headroom is gone, the margin is on the job's prediction instead
  of on the free memory (the first build admitted an estimate up to 1.25 × free, which would have run
  a 0.6 GiB job into 0.5 GiB free), and running jobs are never stopped. A 4 GiB box with 0.5 GiB free:
  0.2 GiB needs 0.25 and runs, 0.4 GiB needs 0.5, not under 0.5, and waits. An estimate is capped at
  90 % of the box's memory ÷ 1.25 so that no job waits forever on an idle box. The CPU rule is
  unchanged, including its 4-core headroom (the play server, a workbench run's burst and ssh; CPU
  overcommit only slows jobs down, and `deeptime-admit status` still shows it). The waiting message
  now reads "needs 0.40 GiB (+25% margin = 0.50), 0.50 free: it must be under the free memory";
  `deeptime-admit status` prints both rules with the memory free now and the largest estimate that
  would start. Tests (`test_admit.py`): Ben's 4 GiB example (3.5 used: 0.2 admitted, 0.4 waits), the
  margin on the job not on free memory, memory reserved but not yet used, two jobs in one pass, and
  running jobs untouched; the old 15 GiB test is rewritten. `RESERVE_MEM_GIB` is no longer a setting.
- **Many servers at once.** A server job gets a slot: ports 26000 + 10·slot (game, RCON, query, voice
  chat, spares), an X display (:200 + slot) and a folder `deeptime-cache/servers/<job>` removed when
  it ends. `tools/smoke/instance.py` copies a server set into it (libraries/ linked, mods/ and the
  rest copied; worlds and logs left out; ports written into server.properties and Simple Voice
  Chat's config), under the set's shared lock; `tools/smoke/install.sh` takes the set's world lock,
  then the set lock, exclusively. gametest.sh and run_planet.py run in `<job>/run-gametest|run-planet`
  (`DEEPTIME_GAMETEST_DIR`, `DEEPTIME_PLANET_DIR` in build.gradle) with a copy of the set's jars
  (`DEEPTIME_RUN_MODS`), and hold the checkout's Gradle launch lock until their JVM is up (Gradle
  writes a run's argument files into the shared build folder just before it starts the JVM).
  run.py and dh-client-check.sh keep the set's own world, linked in, under the set's world lock.
  preview.py boots a copy of the set instead of editing the set's server.properties and config.
  The play server (25765, voice 24464) and the workbench (8642) are outside the pool.
- **Callers.** mac.sh admits every command (`--kind`, or classified: `cargo:test`, `gradle:build`,
  `gametest:mic`, `sim:<preset>:<threads>t`, ...; `--server` only for scripts that boot Minecraft
  without the launchers); gametest.sh, gametest-planet.sh, run.py, preview.py (so the workbench's
  `/api/preview`), dh-client-check.sh admit themselves (a launcher inside an admitted server job takes
  over that job's slot); `detach.sh start` admits the detached job; detached-server.sh and
  mic-climate.sh use the tool instead of the lock. The idle watcher counts admitted and waiting jobs
  as busy (seen in its state: "admitted job ... (agent-..., pid ...)").
- **Rollout.** Installed on the VM from this branch (admit.py and the new idle watcher; the watcher
  restarted, the workbench and play server untouched). Nothing on master calls the tool yet, so the
  ~8 agents on the old scripts carry on with the lock; while `server.lock` exists the tool counts its
  holder as one admitted server job (`server:legacy`, its estimate reserved for 3 minutes after it was
  taken, its memory for 10). New servers never use the old fixed ports (25665/25675/25666/25676/24454),
  so old and new servers do not collide. No process of another agent was touched.
- **Demo** (the VM shared with other agents throughout; their load 18–43). Round 3, the measuring code
  final, six jobs submitted at 00:11:47 UTC from one call (`detach.sh start` × 5, `preview.py submit`):

  | Job | Kind | Waited | Estimate (cores, GiB) | Measured: cores mean / p90 / peak, GiB peak, wall | Result |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `./gametest.sh` | gametest:standalone | 0 s | 4.0, 8.0 (seed) | 1.75 / 4.45 / 7.56, 7.70, 602 s | 70 of 71 (finding 2) |

  | the same, scattered start | sim:earthlike_quick_16k:2t | 6 s | 1.8, 3.5 (4 runs) | 1.76 / 1.93 / 19.15, 3.16, 647 s | baked |
  | `cargo test --workspace` | cargo:test | 501 s | 10.0, 12.0 (seed) | 8.52 / 20.63 / 23.93, 5.37, 279 s | 766 passed, 0 failed |

  The first three got slots 0–2 (ports 26000, 26010, 26020; the MIC GameTest's voice chat 26013, its
  468 MB jar copy in its own folder; the preview's server "Starting Minecraft server on *:26020").
  sim 2 and the preview waited 6 s (free 9.3 cores at load 22.7, the GameTests' reservations still
  held); `cargo test` waited "needs 10.0 cores, 0.0 free (+25% = 0.0)" while other agents drove the

### 2026-10-03 — Two latent defects the ice branch's seed-11 test planet exposed: crater breccia at rim height, lake margins dry (agent worktree agent-ae203a8a910c7657a, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c, continued by a second agent after a stop; master 0261caf0 merged; not merged)
- **Asked (Ben, decisions log 2026-10-03, "Fix both bugs, then land (Recommended)"):** `aCraterIsABowlOverBreccia` and `riversHold` failed on the ice branch's test planet (66 of 68 GameTests); fix both in the impact and lake code, then the ice branch lands.
- **1. Breccia at rim height (impacts).** Root cause: `ImpactStage::finish` placed each small crater's lens body from the deep-time surface (`ground + kept × aged profile at 0`), but the amplifier changes the ground after that (erosion, glacial and thermal passes; up to 15 blocks at one crater on the ice planet), so the lens was centred at the rim's height with the floor 8 blocks above it. Fix: the stage records `lens_bodies` (crater id, body id); `impacts::settle_folder` (called from `session::finalize_write` once the folder is complete, as the placer pass is) reads the baked terrain at each crater's centre and re-seats the lens at `drawn height − cover` (`lens_floor_y`, `seat_bodies`), rewriting `bodies` and the manifest entry, `notes.bake.impact_bodies` records how many moved. Test: `bake::tests::a_craters_lens_is_seated_under_the_drawn_floor` (fails on the old code: 1,794 of 1,851 lenses off the drawn floor on a 40x-flux 4k planet, passes now). FORMAT.md "Impact craters" and `docs/science/impacts.md` step 7 say where the body sits; IMP-094 updated.
- **2. Lake margins flush with the waterline (lakes), two causes.** (a) The water pass filled a lake column only down to the *generated* ground, which between noise-cell corners can stand a block or two above `Water`'s bilinear `ground` (the density's scale differs from corner to corner): in a lake one block deep the column held no water, flush with the lake ("dry shore"). Fix: a lake column is cut to its bed like a river's channel (`WaterBodies` LAKE case: ground over `top` removed, ground between `bed` and `top` becomes water); FORMAT.md "Water columns", new ledger row HYD-077, `rivers-and-lakes.md`. `riversHold` now allows no dry shore (it allowed 1 in 20) and logs each one it finds (ground, surface, level, bed, blocks). Measured on one cold seed-11 planet (`DEEPTIME_TEST_PLANET_SET="planet.star_flux_rel=0.92 hydro.lake_freeze_mean_c=10"`, same planet before and after): dryShore 6 of 2,268 lake columns before, 0 after. (b) The ice pass replaced a frozen lake's ice (the water pass's `minecraft:ice` top block, which is not a fluid) with snow where the glacier cover reaches a lake, leaving a block of snow over the water: `IcePass.surfaceY` now leaves it alone (FORMAT.md "Ice cover", BIO-084); `icePassLaysTheCover` gets a frozen-lake column that fails on the old pass.
- **Not reproduced exactly.** The ice branch's own failing planet (seed 11, before master's 35 m scale and plate work) cannot be rebuilt on current master (the merged tree's seed-11 planet is a different one: no frozen lake at all, dryShore 0 before and after). The lake bug was therefore reproduced on a cold planet of the merged tree (above); the crater bug by the bake test.
- **Seen, not mine: `aCraterIsABowlOverBreccia` fails on `seed=12`** on the merged tree: crater 582 (6.2 km, fresh, 340 m of relief) has a bowl of 0.8 blocks where 3.2 are wanted; its lens is in place (breccia under the floor in 5 of 5 columns). It is a different failure (the drawn bowl, not the lens); this branch changes no terrain, so it is not caused by it, but it was not run on plain master. Not investigated; recommend a look at why a fresh 6 km crater has no bowl in the drawn terrain there.
- **Evidence on the ice branch's planet.** With the ice branch merged (uncommitted, then aborted: `32a9a39d`'s successor a2f51b75 with master 6f72f0dd) and the `seed=11` default test planet, `aCraterIsABowlOverBreccia` (crater 484, breccia in 5 of 5 columns), `riversHold` (dryShore 0 of 1,019 lake columns), `icePassLaysTheCover`, `lakeHolds`, `carversSpareWater` and `lakeIceAndSaltFollowTheClimate` pass; that planet has no frozen lake, so the lake fix was shown on the cold planet above.
- **Gates** (test VM, head 280d4aa9 less docs: master 7c14e4ab merged; the cargo and JUnit runs were on b23b38ec, the same code): `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo deny check licenses bans` clean; `cargo test --workspace` 557 core + 54 + 72 + 1 and the small ones, 0 failed; `./gradlew build test` 265 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped. ### 2026-10-03 — The GameTests that failed on master: each root cause (agent worktree agent-a7304a5adc996ef91, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c, continued by a second agent after a stop; master 78cffc7b merged; not merged)
- **How reproduced.** Master's test planet changed twice since the failures were seen (plate tasks 3+4 at 6f72f0dd, then the Lambert merge), and on both later planets the tests pass or read nothing (6f72f0dd: no active volcano, no wide river above the sea). So the failing planets were rebuilt from their own commits on the VM: the planet of 91b1550f (master df381d62 + the 35 m scale, where the four were measured) baked by that commit's `deeptime` and read by this branch's Java, and 6f72f0dd's whole tree for `climateConsistent`. Every failure reproduced exactly (same columns, same counts).
- **`magmaUnderActiveVolcanoes` (all sets). Cause: the shell of a broad lens was too thin.** The shell was the ellipsoid with radii rh + 1.5 and rv + 1.5; with a lens's half-height capped at 5, from a radius of 46 blocks up that leaves less than a block over the flanks, so a lava block faced the rock above it (checked over every radius 10–90; none with the new rule). Volcano 78 (an active shield, rh 15, 17 lenses down to y −507, the lower ones about 70 blocks in radius) had noise caves there, at y −473 to −479, in the part of the column the −512 floor added (cdfc907d): a latent bug of the crust-deep column (78bc6b50) that the merged planet exposed. **Fix (generator):** `Magma.inShell` takes 1.5 blocks off the offset's horizontal distance and height, so the shell is 1.5 blocks thick across and up everywhere, for chambers too (MAG-011). Master's Lambert branch fixed the same leak independently (a37fa3ee, `touchesLens`: any block with a face on the lens); the merge keeps both. **Evidence:** on the 91b1550f planet, with the fix 0 air faces of 828,114 molten blocks on all three sets; with the old formula 51 air faces, every open neighbour outside the old shell (`NONE`, in the altered rock). `MagmaTest.broadLensesAreSealedOnEverySide` (a 45 km shield's lenses) fails on the old formula.
- **`farTerrainMatchesGeneratedChunksAcrossTheSeam` (MIC). Cause: a Terralith canyon and coral reefs, not the seam or the projection; deterministic** (the same columns in every run: carvers are seeded by world seed and chunk). Terralith overrides `minecraft:canyon` (y −20 to 70, yScale up to 13.5); one cut through a sea bed two blocks under the water at (−1995, 519) down to y −2 and filled with water, and the next column (−1991, 519) to y 53. The other two misses were coral reefs of `terralith:deep_warm_ocean` up to 7 blocks over the bed at z 7, which the reader counted as ground. Standalone the same rows have neither (vanilla's canyon has other odds and range). **Fix (the test was wrong):** `FarTerrainCheck` reads under coral as it does under trees, and a column whose bed a carver cut below far terrain's ground (open and in the chunk's air carving mask) is counted apart, at most one in eight per tally (`carved_set_aside`). Far terrain draws the column rule, not the per-chunk carvers. On the 91b1550f planet with MIC: east 62 of 62 within two blocks, 2 set aside.
- **`riverBiomes` (TerraBlender). Cause: the test knew only vanilla's swamps.** The 12 of 14 wide-channel samples that standalone read `minecraft:swamp` (vanilla's valley slice on the flattest wet ground) read `biomesoplenty:wetland` under TerraBlender: BOP puts its own swamp in that slot and tags it `#c:is_swamp`. **Fix (test):** swamp means any biome of `#c:is_swamp`. 91b1550f planet, TB: 2 river + 12 swamp of 14.
- **`lakeIceAndSaltFollowTheClimate` (TerraBlender). Cause: an acacia's leaves over a playa column,** read as its ground; master already fixed it (3bff8305, reads under leaves, merged in 088d42a5 after the failing run). Passes on the 91b1550f planet with TB (24 of 24 playa columns salt).
- **`climateConsistent` (standalone and MIC, master 6f72f0dd; the coordinator's addition). Cause: the wetland rule did its job and the census counted it against the taiga tags.** On that planet all of the D-climate land is a wet coastal plain under 150 m: all 47 Dfc columns lie in the bake's wetland band (vanilla's E6, which only the wetland rule BIO-066 reaches on land), 66 % swamp and 28 % beach (Dfb 67 % and 30 %). Vanilla itself puts swamp at E6 in the cold and temperate bands, and the cells are genuinely wet (Dfc mean humidity band 3.95, P/PET about 1.9). On the way a real input bug turned up: the rule read the humidity band *after* the class's rule, which lifts Dfc, Dfd, Dsc, Dsd, Dwc and Dwd to 3.05 (taiga humidity) and Af to 4.1, so all of their flat lowland counted as wet whatever the rainfall. **Fixes:** (1) generator: the wetland rule reads the aridity index's own band (BIO-066); the bake note records `wetland_cells_by_class`; new test `wetlands_follow_the_climate_not_the_class_band` (a P/PET 0.6 Dfc plain has no wetland, P/PET 3 has; fails on the old rule). On 6f72f0dd's planet this changes Dfc nothing (179 wetland cells either way; 11 Af cells fewer) and the test still failed. (2) test: `BiomeCensus` leaves land in the wetland band out of the Köppen families, as it does the cold deserts, and logs it (`wetlands_set_aside`, with how many are swamp); the GameTest fails if that band holds more than the rule's flat share (0.35) of the land. On 6f72f0dd's planet: 112 of 1,385 land columns set aside (69 on swamp), Dsub and Dfc:taiga left with no columns, `climateConsistent` passes. No floor was lowered. Whether boreal wetland should be vanilla's swamp at all is Ben's (Pending questions).
- **Not this branch's:** `realPlanetRockMatchesTheParityFixture` (35 m; another agent).
- **Gates** (test VM; head 615fb1e7, master 78cffc7b merged; later commits STATUS only): `cargo fmt --check` clean (after `cargo fmt` of the wetland change), clippy `-D warnings` clean, `cargo test --workspace` 767 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored, `cargo deny check licenses bans` ok; `./gradlew build test` 266 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped. GameTests through the server lock, after `tools/smoke/install.sh` of each set: `./gametest.sh` 71 of 71, `-PwithMic` 71 of 71, `-PwithTerraBlender` 71 of 71, `-PwithEv` 71 of 71. On master's current (Lambert) planet `magmaUnderActiveVolcanoes` reads nothing (no active volcano) and `riverBiomes` samples nothing above the sea, so their evidence is the 91b1550f planet's runs above; `realPlanetRockMatchesTheParityFixture` passes on this planet.
