### 2026-10-03 — Distant Horizons curvature follows the planet (Ben's request in the decisions log; agent worktree agent-adffa6fb9561d851d, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Asked (Ben, decisions log 2026-10-03):** "btw, DH has world curvature settings, can you make it so those default to values that make sense for the given world a player is in (dependent upon the world size generated using our mod.)"
- **Research (DH 3.3.1, the MIC pin; licence LGPL-3.0, read with javap and by opening the jar's shaders and lang file on the VM; nothing copied):** the setting is `Config.Client.Advanced.Graphics.Experimental.earthCurveRatio`, an Integer in [-5000, 5000], default 0 (flat), a client setting stored in the player's DH config. The terrain vertex shader draws a sphere of radius 6,371,000 / ratio blocks (uniform `uEarthRadius`, read through `ConfigEntry.get()` every frame); 1 to 49 is rewritten to 50 *and saved* by `WorldCurvatureConfigEventHandler`. Only DH's LOD meshes bend, not Minecraft's chunks. The API is `DhApi.Delayed.configs.graphics().earthCurvatureRatio()` (`IDhApiConfigValue<Integer>`, null until DH starts): `setValue`/`clearValue` act on an in-memory override layer that `get()` prefers and that is never saved; `getTrueValue()` is the player's file value; while the override is set DH's screen shows "API LOCK" on the entry. Details and ledger BAK-043 to BAK-047 in `docs/science/world-scale-and-bake.md` "Distant Horizons world curvature".
- **Built:** `compat/dh/DhCurvature` (conversion, limits, and the `Controller` rule over a `Slot`), `DhApiBinding.earthCurvature()` (by name, same pattern as the far-terrain compat), `client/DhCurvatureClient` (once a second on the client tick, registered only when DH is installed; released on logout), `client/ClientConfig` (`config/deeptime-client.toml`, `dhAutoCurvature` default true, screen under Mods, Deep Time, Config) and lang keys `deeptime.configuration.*`. No new payload: `WorldInfoPayload.circumference` already reaches the client (`worldInfoFollowsThePlayer` shows 16384 on the test planet and 0 in the overworld). The value goes on the API layer only; a player's own non-default value is kept (and releases ours if set later), another mod's override is left alone, a vanilla level or a switched-off setting hands the layer back.
- **Numbers:** ratio = round(6,371,000 / (C / 2 pi)). 16k: R 2,607.6 blocks, ratio 2,443 (2,443.25 before rounding); drop at 256 / 512 / 1,024 blocks 12.56 / 50.10 / 198.5. 32k: R 5,215.2, ratio 1,222 (1,221.62); drops 6.28 / 25.11 / 100.2. DH's range covers circumferences 8,006 to 800,603 blocks; outside it the strongest curve (5,000) or flat.
- **Gates (this branch on master 613647a4; Rust untouched, so no cargo):** `./gradlew build test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 265 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped (13 new `DhCurvatureTest` tests; `DhApiBindingTest.theCurvatureSlotReachesTheRealConfigInterfaces` runs the controller through the real interfaces of the 3.3.1 and 3.3.3 jars); `./gametest.sh -PwithMic` through `tools/remote/mac.sh --pack --server`: 70 of 71, the one failure the known `realPlanetRockMatchesTheParityFixture` (35 m); DH is excluded from that run's mod set, so it exercises no DH code. The client side is not checked on a real client (the software-GL client has not made DH request LODs); how the bent LODs meet the flat chunks is unseen.
- **Next step:** merge; `tools/remote/mac-gc.sh`; when a client with a GPU is available, look at the LOD edge (pending question).

### 2026-10-03 — The Lambert equal-area world: the projection module's bodies are Lambert's, format 0.4 (agent worktree agent-a3186d42ee9449d3d, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; phase 2 of the projection task, on top of the refactor below; not merged)
- **Ask.** Ben, decisions log 2026-10-02: "Lambert for now" (Lambert cylindrical equal-area, true on the
  equator, wrapping east–west with Toroidal World, pole cap kept). The coordinator: phase 2 of the projection
  task, after the projection-neutral refactor (the entry below), reusing what fits of the parked
  `projection-lambert-wip`; the true-metric corrections of `docs/design/equal-area-projection.md` §4.
- **Built.** `deeptime_format::projection` is Lambert: R = C/2π, φ = asin(−z/R), poles at z = ∓R (2,607.6 at
  16k); metric cos φ east–west, 1/cos φ north–south, area scale 1. Grids run from −Zo, Zo the smallest multiple
  of the planet's quantum (64 blocks) at or past the pole, the same for every grid of a planet (the WIP's
  lcm(quantum, r) gave a coarse r = 128 a different Zo and the ladder stopped nesting; H = ⌈2·Zo/r⌉): L1 1024 ×
  328, L2 2048 × 656, L3 8192 × 2624 at 16k (L1 of 32k quick 1024 × 328). `GridDesc` gained `area_share`,
  `thinned`; cell areas, row weights, `true_cell_m` (north–south the arc of the row's band) and the band
  weights come from it. Map pictures are π : 1 (`picture_height`; keyframes 1024 × 326 in every preset and the
  default), rows uniform in sin φ. World-data format 0.4 (Cargo.toml, `FORMAT_MINOR`, Java `FormatVersion`).
  Java `worlddata/Projection` and the pages' `projection.js` are the twins (quantum, Zo, picture rows, the
  metric); the Java analytic test terrain and the Rust synthetic one use asin(z·2π/C).
- **True metric (design note §4).** The climate's geometry takes a per-row cell height and the ice distance
  transform's column pass runs at the rows' cumulative true positions (`dt_1d_at`, from the WIP); the ITCZ
  weighs rows by their cell areas; the satellite and world-map hill shades take a pixel's true size
  (`Projection::picture_pixel_m`, cos φ held at 0.15); the deposit footprints on the pages are drawn in block
  space (`ppbx`/`ppbz` instead of degrees); `climate-dem` resamples the Earth DEM (equirectangular input) onto
  the planet's grid. Left on purpose: the orographic rain's block metric (cylindrical: unchanged), the
  east–west marches (cos φ both ways), the section tool's km (game blocks × 300 m).
- **Pages.** The workbench map pane is π : 1; the final world's tile pyramid stays a 2 : 1 frame from z = −C/4
  (`Projection::tile_frame_z`) with the pixels past the poles drawn as the background (RENDER_VERSION 2); the
  graticule, readouts, box selections, globe texture and the section clicks go through `DTProj`.
  `tools/workbench/sections_shots.py` clicks through the page's projection; `tools/workbench/preview.py` and
  `tools/viewer/deposits-check.js` are Lambert.
- **Evidence (quick 16k, scattered continents, 500 Myr, seed 1, `deeptime stage volcanoes --threads 4` on the
  VM; before = the refactor's equirectangular build with the new ice line, after = this branch).** The
  planets differ in detail (the plate model reads a different raster, so the histories part), but the
  projection's property is exact: the map's share is the planet's share. Ice: before map 0.333 against true
  area 0.136 (land 0.084/0.039, sea 0.249/0.097), poleward of 60° map 0.334 against 0.1345; after map 0.1004
  against area 0.0975 (land 0.0463/0.0448, sea 0.0541/0.0527), poleward of 60° map 0.1346 against 0.1318 (the
  sphere 0.134). Land: the surface line's cell share 0.255 against true 0.268 before, 0.283 = 0.283 after.
  True-area hypsometry before / after: land mean 753 / 771 m, p50 581 / 549, p90 1,678 / 1,747, above 2 km
  0.055 / 0.069, sea median depth 4,037 / 3,810 m. Cost: 11 min 13 s / 8 min 44 s wall, 2.93 / 2.34 GB peak RSS
  (36 % fewer cells). Pictures and logs: `review/out/projection-lambert/` (not committed; satellite-before.png
  1024 × 512, satellite-after.png 1024 × 326). The before numbers equal the design note's §7 baseline exactly (the planet is
  deterministic).
- **Workbench, measured** (a private `deeptime watch` on port 8667 over a baked 500 Myr quick 16k Lambert run;

### 2026-10-03 — Cold deserts, schist at 525 °C, and the salt-flat GameTest (agent worktree agent-a0a9f9641ccc58e63, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c, continued by a second agent after a stop; not merged)
- **Asked (Ben, decisions log 2026-10-02):** "Move schist to 500-550 °C"; cold deserts "classify them properly and if a mod a player brings has a better biome then swap to it. - **Schist:** `formation_temp_c("schist")` 450 -> 525 °C (the middle of Baxter et al. 2002's 500 to 550 °C garnet-zone growth); amphibolite stays 500 and gneiss 650, so the key bands (RCK-052) are 0, 250, 300, 350, 500, 525, 650 and the grade order slate < phyllite < schist < gneiss holds (test `the_grade_order_and_the_key_bands_follow_the_formation_temperatures` fails on 450). `strata-check` now reports rock-class shares. Measured on one quick 16k run (scattered continents, 500 Myr, seed 1, master 00ef214c before, the branch after; `deeptime strata-check --columns 20000` and its 524,288 stored stacks): stored stacks holding schist / phyllite / gneiss 37.5 / 16.3 / 57.2 % -> 29.1 / 21.7 / 57.6 %, rock blocks 5.0 / 0.87 / 14.3 % -> 5.2 / 1.27 / 13.0 %; grade inversions in the stored stacks 0 of 524,288 before (master's own check) and after; land columns with folds applied 2 of 4,556 -> 10 of 5,448 (all thrusts, 0.18 %). The worlds are different planets (a rock class feeds the surface stage); two earlier seed pairs are on `docs/science/rock-and-metamorphism.md`. FORMAT.md's band list corrected. Ledger RCK-042, RCK-052.
- **Cold deserts:** BWk splits on its mean annual temperature in `placement.json` (above 10 °C hot desert; 0 to 10 °C the cold band at humidity <= 0.6, ramp `cold_desert`; at or below 0 °C barren frozen ground like EF), so vanilla draws plains / snowy plains and a biome mod's own cold desert or steppe (Terralith cold shrubland, steppe, gravel desert; BOP `cold_desert`) is picked by the same band coordinates, no special case. The placement table's switches now nest and humidity can switch too (`placement.rs`). Best vanilla fit argued in `docs/science/biomes.md` "Cold deserts" (the treeless dry cold biomes: plains and snowy plains). Measured on the same quick 16k world baked with the old table (a `climate_placement` content bundle) and the new (deterministic: other rasters byte-equal), `/deeptime probe biomes 16`, BWk 10,541 land columns: standalone desert 68.2 -> 40.5 %, plains 3.3 -> 36.9 %, snowy plains 0 -> 3.0 %; MIC desert 26.8 -> 9.2 %, Terralith cold shrubland 0 -> 14.2 %, temperate highlands 0 -> 9.8 %, badlands 14.9 -> 5.4 %; BOP desert 24.1 -> 12.5 %, `cold_desert` 0.3 -> 3.5 %, plains 0.9 -> 16.1 %. BSk hardly moves (plains 76.8 -> 78.3 % standalone). BWk is 7.6 % of that planet's 138,101 land columns; the new table changes the biome of 3.4 % of the land (4,750 columns, 45 % of the BWk) standalone and 3.5 % with MIC. Ledger BIO-101 to BIO-103; `BWk:cold_not_sand` census check (0 of 65 columns standalone and MIC, 0 of 1 TerraBlender).
- **climateConsistent:** with the cold deserts now plains on purpose, the `BW` and `BW:desert` shares fell below their floors (standalone BW 0.457 < 0.57 and BW:desert 0.297 < 0.37; MIC BW 0.543 < 0.57). Not a broken mapping: 65 of 266 columns are cold BWk. The two checks now leave out BWk columns colder than the cold band's top (`BiomeCensus.Check.notColderThan`, the cold ones have their own check). Floors unchanged; shares on the 4k test planet now BW 0.692 standalone / 0.766 MIC, BW:desert 0.502 / 0.592 (201 columns).
- **`lakeIceAndSaltFollowTheClimate`:** the leaves were read as the ground because leaves have a full collision shape and the old descent stopped on them. The column is a salt column (the playa pass runs before features, and replaces the ground's top blocks only), so the test now reads the ground under leaves and logs and counts the canopies (`underCanopy=`), and a log standing on the flat is a violation of its own (`tree-on-salt`), as is any non-salt ground. Evidence: the failing run (gradle daemon log, 18:48 on 2026-10-02) had lakeCells=10092 playaCells=25 saltRead=1, the same world as every later run of that tree; on that world, with the MIC pack of today, the new test finds underCanopy=0 and wrong=0, and a scan of all 100 salt columns finds 0 with leaves on top and 0 with a log on top. So the leaves were a transient canopy over the flat, not a tree growing on it (a tree in the column would put a trunk, then dirt, in the column, which the new check reports, and vanilla's tree features need a dirt-tag block below, which salt is not); no placement change. It did not reproduce, so "a neighbour's canopy" is the explanation that fits and was not caught in the act. Side finding: that scan counts 9 of 100 salt columns whose ground is not the salt block (it did not exclude ice and snow layers as the test does; not examined).
- **Gates (final head, master 6f72f0dd merged: 35 m scale, plate tasks 3+4):** cargo fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo deny check licenses bans` clean; `cargo test --workspace` 0 failures, 3 ignored; `./gradlew build test` 251 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped; GameTests through `tools/remote/mac.sh` (`tools/review/cold-final.sh`): `-PwithTerraBlender` All 71 required tests passed; standalone and `-PwithMic` 70 of 71, the one failure `climateConsistent` in both (`Dsub 0.043 < 0.380` and `Dfc:taiga 0.000 < 0.330` standalone, 0.213 with MIC, the same 47 Dfc columns). The BWk, BW and BW:desert checks pass. Tools: `tools/review/cold-schist-runs.sh`, `cold-desert-biomes.sh`, `cold-census.sh`, `cold-all.sh`, `cold-schist-gates.sh`, `cold-cargo.sh`, `cold-final.sh`, `detached-server.sh` (runs a command under the server lock detached on the VM, so a dropped ssh does not lose a queued job), `biomemap_shares.py`.

Supercontinent 1,000 Myr: sites 264 (20 m) / 291 (35 m before) / 291 (after); deposit ore 9.05 / 4.66 / 8.09 million blocks; median porphyry 2,351 / 1,964 / 4,876 ore blocks (7 porphyries: the median is noisy). Scattered 500 Myr: sites 143 / 149 / 149; deposit ore 6.46 / 3.57 / 5.77 million; median porphyry 1,694 / 983 / 1,685. Coal is 95–97 % of deposit ore. - **Parity GameTest, root cause.** The failing sample (−2026, 38, 521) is shale in the fixture, in Java's column and in the strata pass's prediction; shale's vanilla stand-in is `minecraft:stone` (P1-28), so the predicted block is stone. The placed andesite came after the strata pass: vanilla's `ore_andesite_lower` blob (y 0–60, replaces base stone) runs at the features step. `deeptime:claim_ores` removes rock blobs only when the server's overworld is Deep Time's (ClaimOresBiomeModifier, by design; `claimOffWhenOverworldNotGeologic` checks it), and the GameTest levels sit in a vanilla world, so they keep the blobs. A blob crossing a sample whose class is plain stone is rare, which is why it showed up only when the 35 m geometry moved a sample into one. Not a disagreement between the structure drawing and the column evaluators: a plug is an intrusion event inside the deformed stack, so all three would have said andesite. Today's test planet (plate work merged) no longer puts a sample in a blob (146 samples, 0 blob blocks, 0 wrong in both runs below), so the original sample could not be re-observed; the cause rests on the chain above. Fix in the test's judgement: a sample whose class and prediction agree but whose placed block is a block some rock-blob feature of the level's biomes places (`ClaimRules.dryRun` verdict ROCK) is counted apart when the claim is off, logged with how many of the 343 blocks around it are the same block; the test fails if over 1 in 20 samples are such. A real Deep Time world has no blobs (PlanetClaimGameTests).
- **Folds.** `DeformationParams::true_height_share`'s doc: the share keeps the structures' height in metres at any `m_per_block_v`, not their look in blocks (4× at 20 m, 2.29× at 35 m); the world-scale page says the same.

Master's listed failures `magmaUnderActiveVolcanoes`, `riverBiomes` and `lakeIceAndSaltFollowTheClimate` passed on this planet; this branch adds no failure.

### 2026-10-02/03 — P3-04 far terrain through Toroidal World's guard (agent worktree agent-ad7563a17d66b0c58, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
Ben, 2026-10-02: "Mixin around TW's guard" (decisions log). Branch `worktree-agent-ad7563a17d66b0c58`, master 3a11aa47 merged in.

- **Why TW guards.** Toroidal World 0.19.3 (MIT) wraps DH's `WorldGeneratorInjector.bind` and calls `DhGenerators.requireOwn(level, generator)`, which throws for any generator whose class is outside `com.seibel.distanthorizons.` on a level TW shapes (read in its class files on the VM). TW makes the seam seamless by reshaping the level's own chunk generator and folding DH's section keys into the lap (repository, retrieval queue, seam ranking and LOD-tree mixins); DH's own generator draws from that chunk generator, a foreign one would not know the seam. With DH 3.3.0 TW's DH mixins missed the renamed `_neoforge` classes and were inert; from 3.3.1 (MIC's pin since pack 57561c9) they apply and refused Deep Time's generator.
- **The patch.** `mixin/compat/toroidal_world/DhGeneratorsMixin`: `@Pseudo`, `@Inject` at HEAD of `requireOwn`, cancellable, `require = 0`, in its own config `deeptime.tw_dh.mixins.json` (`required: false`, `defaultRequire 0`) with the plugin `mixin/TwDhGuardMixinPlugin`. The plugin applies it only when TW and DH are installed and TW's jar has `public static void requireOwn(IDhApiLevelWrapper, IDhApiWorldGenerator)` in `com.toroidalworld.compat.distanthorizons.DhGenerators` (read from TW's class file before anything is applied); otherwise it logs why and skips (far terrain then falls back to DH's own LODs on wrapped levels). `postApply` checks the handler call is in the method and logs "patched"; the outcome is `-Ddeeptime.twDhGuard` and `/deeptime probe dh`'s `tw_guard_patch`. The handler (`compat/dh/TwDhGuard`) cancels TW's check only for Deep Time's own proxy generator (`DhLodGenerator.of`), and only when `TwDhGuardRule.verdict` holds: the generator was made for this level, the level's TW shape loops X with width equal to the world data's circumference C, and does not loop Z (BAK-041). Every other generator and every other case goes to TW's check unchanged; TW's key folding, retrieval, seam ranking and LOD-tree mixins are untouched. No code copied from TW or DH.
- **Dev runs and the GameTests.** `linkRunMods`' Fabric-only rule already kept a jar with `META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml` (DH 3.3.x's dual-loader jar). What left DH out of `-PwithMic` was `tools/smoke/profiles/mic.gametest-excluded`: DH 3.3.1 still casts the server to `DedicatedServer` in its server-starting listener (decompiled, `AbstractModInitializer_neoforge` line 111), which NeoForge's GameTest server is not. So it stays excluded there, every jar left out is now logged with its reason, and each run gets `-Ddeeptime.dh.expected` (true when the run's set has a DH jar it does not exclude); `farTerrainHasDistantHorizonsWhenExpected` fails when DH is expected and not loaded, and when loaded requires the API bound and the override registered. New GameTest `farTerrainMatchesGeneratedChunksAcrossTheSeam` (64 blocks either side of x = C/2, four rows, planet-wide thresholds per side). Distant Horizons itself is checked by the smoke run on a dedicated server.
- **Evidence (test VM).**
  - `smoke mic --dh` (`tools/review/p3-04-dh.sh mic`, 168 jars, DH 3.3.1, TW 0.19.3, `earthlike_quick_16k` 200 Myr, source 33f3a369): PASS. Patch `applied`, guard `passed`, override registered; `/dh pregen` fed 257 sections, 0 failures, 44.2 ms a section inside DH. Beside the spawn: DH holds 400 of 400 columns, its surface is far terrain's in 400 of 400; against chunks generated afterwards ground within 2 blocks 94.3 %, water or dry 100 %, biome 100 %. West of the seam (x 8032..8191): 400/400 held and same surface, within 2 blocks 91.5 %, water 95.8 %, biome 100 %. East of it (x −8192..−8033): 400/400, 97.8 %, 100 %, 100 %. Regions outside the span 0.
  - `smoke dh --dh` (standalone + DH 3.3.1, source 28e36616): PASS; 400/400 held and same surface in all three areas, ground within 2 blocks 96.9 / 96.5 / 98.2 %, water and biome 100 %. A first run on this branch failed (68 of 400 held) because a DH lookup ran past its 10-s limit with the VM at load 46 right after a pregen; the check now waits 30 s a lookup and stops at the third time-out (33f3a369).
  - GameTests (`./gametest.sh`, `./gametest.sh -PwithMic`, 160 MIC mods): All 70 required tests passed in each; the seam test west 53 columns (52 within a block), east 64 (64 within a block), C 4096; `farTerrainHasDistantHorizonsWhenExpected` expected=false in both (default set: no DH; MIC: `mic.gametest-excluded`).
  - Gates on the branch with master 3a11aa47 merged: `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (750 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored), `cargo deny check licenses bans`, `./gradlew build test` (JUnit 251, 0 failures, 2 skipped; `TwDhGuardRuleTest` 3, `DhApiBindingTest` on the real 3.3.1 and 3.3.3 jars). The smoke runs and GameTests above ran before that merge (master 00ef214c).
- **`/dh pregen` across the seam** (Ben asked; the video agent saw it stop at radius 75–76): it does not work with TW 0.19.3 + DH 3.3.1, whichever generator. DH's `PregenManager` keeps each pending section in a cache under its raw key and clears it under the position the data source reports; TW folds that position into the lap, so a section past x = C/2 is never cleared, and the two-minute expiry never fires because nothing touches the cache again. Measured on the dh set: a square centred five sections west of the seam stopped at 53.13 % after 136 sections and did not move in 200 s; a square ending at the seam finished all 257 in under 10 s; a square centred on x = C/2 never starts (TW's command coordinates reject 8192 as outside the world). The smoke run now records the crossing case (stalled at 53.13 %, 136 sections) and pregenerates inside the lap. Pending question updated.
- **Client: not verified, and the finding stands.** `tools/client/dh-client-check.sh dh` (real 3.3.1 client, software GL on Xvfb on the VM, joining the dh set's 3.3.1 server with Deep Time's generator registered through the guard). Getting a client to join took five fixes to the script: GL environment before Xvfb, DH's "update available" screen (update check off), Minecraft's first-launch accessibility screen (options.txt), a JVM abort in `pa_simple_write` from the session's half-working PulseAudio (a private PulseAudio server with a null sink), and the set's port taken by another worktree's server (wait for it). Run of 2026-10-03 04:44–05:02 UTC: the client joined, DH's networking came up ("Level init received", level key, the client's DH level started, OpenGL 4.6 Mesa, renderer set up), but in 3 min at the spawn and 5 min beside the seam it sent no generation request: the generator was asked for 0 sections, and the client's own database holds 91 sections, all within 512 blocks of its two positions (its own chunks), 0 beyond. This is what the video agent saw with a 3.3.0 server, now with matching 3.3.1 on both sides, so it is not a version mismatch and not the guard (the override is registered; the server is never asked). Untested causes: DH's client-side request queue starved by software rendering on a loaded VM (its LOD tree is driven from the render thread), or Toroidal World's client-side DH mixins (`WorldGenerationQueueMixin` re-targets the queue's centre through the seam). Next: one run on a machine with a GPU, or a client with DH's debug logging of the generation queue; until then far terrain reaching a player is unverified.
- **Ledger and page.** BAK-041 (the guard rule, game-choice, owner-decided) and BAK-042 (far terrain across the seam, game-choice); `docs/science/world-scale-and-bake.md`, section "Distant Horizons far terrain and Toroidal World's seam".
- **Not verified.** Singleplayer (the integrated server takes the same path, not run); how far terrain looks (nothing judged by eye); a MIC client (the client check used the standalone set); DH inside the GameTest server (impossible while DH casts to `DedicatedServer`).
- **Next.** Merge the branch (the server side is done and gated); after the merge batch's GameTests, put the `/dh pregen` question to Ben (or report it to TW's author); then find why a joined client requests nothing (a GPU machine, or DH's generation-queue debug logging).

### 2026-10-02 — Folds and faults: vertical scale and intrusion sizes (Ben's WP-8 answers; agent worktree agent-a14950a4d82be0c7b, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Decisions built** (decisions log 2026-10-02, "Setting, default 4x (Recommended)" and "Go somewhere in between"). Ledger DEF (DEF-007, -011, -019, -020, -048, -049, -054, -056, -061), STR-035, HNT-025/-027/-028/-031; page `docs/science/folds-faults-intrusions.md` (opening, what you see, equations, Earth table, open questions 1-2 settled, 3 now "wavelength from layer thickness, then true metres"); claims.md flag 14 settled. No new ledger ids; counts unchanged.
- **`structure.deformation.true_height_share`** (new; DEF-011): the share of their true height in metres that folds and faults are drawn at; default 4/15 (0.26666666666666666 in the presets), range 0.01-2, editor field `deform_true_height` 0.05-1 with stops Default / Half / True height. Built first as a block multiplier `vertical_scale` 4 (Ben's "4x"); re-expressed the same day at the coordinator's request, after Ben moved the world to 35 m a block, so its meaning holds at any `scale.m_per_block_v`: the block stretch is X = share × m_per_block_h / m_per_block_v (`DeformationParams::block_stretch`; exactly 4.0 at 300 m × 20 m, 2.29 at 300 m × 35 m, the same heights in metres; nothing assumes 20 m). Applied where structures are made (`deform/emplace.rs`: `stretch`, `Inputs::m_per_block_v`): fold amplitude × X; a dip-slip fault keeps its heave and its throw is × X, so dip → atan(X tan d), slip → s·√(cos²d + X²sin²d); strike-slip unchanged. The stored events carry it, so the Rust column rule and `worlddata/Structure.java` read the same numbers unchanged (no format or Java change): strata pass, far terrain, inspect, sections, parity all follow. At the default: normal faults 21-36° in metres and thrusts 5.5-12.6° at any block height (80-85° and 55-73° in 20 m blocks), folds and throws 4/15 of true metres. The scarp term in metres is relief × share × m_per_block_h per block of the 1:1 shape, so the ground relief does not change with m_per_block_v either.

### 2026-10-02 — Geothermal fields on hot continental ground: the heat flow is exported (agent worktree agent-a62d80aa30f831386, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Ask.** Ben, decisions log 2026-10-02: "Export heat flow (Recommended)": the bake exports the plate model's heat flow and geothermal fields also stand on continental ground above a threshold, besides the active volcanoes; every existing geothermal rule holds (rain test 400 mm, no pools under 3 degC, sizes, water safety).
- **The export.** New L1 layer `meta/heat_flow_mw_m2` (u16, 0.1 mW/m² per count, nodata 65535 on oceanic crust; FORMAT.md, bake table). It comes from a new L1 plate field `plates/continental_heat_flow_mw_m2`: the continental samples' stored heat flow interpolated over the continental corners only (NaN on oceanic crust and in gaps), because the L1 field `plates/heat_flow_mw_m2` mixes the sea floor's age law (up to 300 mW/m²) into every coast cell.
- **A fault found on the way, in `plates/ridges.rs`.** The final resampling's `interpolate` blended a sample's heat flow over all three corners of its cover triangle whatever their kind, so a continental sample on a coast took ocean-crust heat flow (the bake test planet showed a continental cell at 50.1 mW/m², under the model's continental floor of 55). It now blends only the corners of the sample's own kind, as the formation age already did. The next plate step sets every sample's heat flow again, so only what is read right after a resampling changes: the final snapshot, which the surface, structure and deposit stages and the bake read. A small change to the plate model, outside this task's files; the plates agents should know.
- **The placement** (`worldgen/Geothermal.heatFlowFields`): the world is cut into cells of 10,000 km² / `geothermal_heat_density`; each cell tries 6 random points and puts one field at the first where the baked heat flow reaches `geothermal_heat_flow_min_mw_m2` and the ground is dry land at least 5 blocks above the sea with no water column and no ice. The field is then built by the volcanoes' machinery as one away from the summit (hot springs where rain and temperature allow, else fumaroles; no cinnabar); its sites carry source id -1. Two new settings in the `underground` section (editor "Advanced · Hot springs and fumaroles", lang keys, all eight presets): `geothermal_heat_flow_min_mw_m2` (default **100**, range 50 to 400) and `geothermal_heat_density` (1.0, 0 to 4; 0 = volcanoes only). `geothermal_density` 0 still turns every geothermal feature off.
- **The threshold.** 100 mW/m²: Davies & Davies 2010 (Solid Earth 1:5-24, library `Davies2010`, full text read): continents 70.9, Cenozoic extensional geology 102.4, Quaternary 82.0, arc margins 73.8, fit 102 - 2.25 sqrt(t). The East African Rift, Iceland, Taupo and Basin and Range are not in that source and not claimed. In the model the continental heat flow is 55 + 35 e^(-t/60) (+40 arc, +40 hotspot, +30 divergent): 100 is reached by an arc, a hotspot or a young rift; a young orogen alone gives 90 at its start. Ledger GEO-052 to GEO-061 (10 rows; GEO-013 coded), page `docs/science/geothermal-features.md`, bibliography `Davies2010`.
- **Measured** (quick 16k planet, `earthlike_quick_16k` scattered continents, 500 Myr, seed 1, `structure.deformation.density=0`; census `GeothermalCensusTest` over the baked folder, the same code with `geothermal_heat_density` 0 and 1): **before (volcanoes only): 170 sites** (11 pools, 97 vents, 62 patches) around 24 of 63 active volcanoes; **after: 267 sites**, the 97 new ones from hot ground (11 pools, 51 vents, 35 patches). Dry land at or over 70 / 80 / 90 / 100 / 120 / 150 mW/m²: 0.715 / 0.628 / 0.092 / 0.047 / 0.015 / 0.0002. Building the sites takes 0.27 s with the heat flow, 0.24 s without. (The first measurement, before the resampling fix, had 5.8 % of the land at 100 or more: part of it was the ocean blend.)
- **Tests.** Rust: `a_planet_run_bakes_every_chunk_time_layer` (the layer, 54.9 to 200.1 mW/m², nodata where the crust has an age), `UndergroundParams` range test. JUnit `GeothermalTest`: `hotContinentalGroundTakesFieldsWithoutAnyVolcano`, `heatFlowFieldsKeepEveryGeothermalRule` (dry, cold, water, ice, coast), `theSameWorldGivesTheSameHeatFlowFields`, rules read and clamped; `GeothermalCensusTest` (a measuring tool, skipped without `DEEPTIME_CENSUS_WORLD`).
- **Gates.** On the test VM after the merge of master (f545c0bc) into the branch: `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo deny check licenses bans` clean; `cargo test --workspace` 735 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored; `./gradlew build test` tests=233 failures=0 skipped=2 (the census is skipped without its world). GameTests (`./gametest.sh`, `-PwithMic`, `-PwithEv`, run before the last merge of master, with all three commit groups of this branch in): 68 of 68 required tests passed in each. The geothermal export and the floor both reach the game, so the three runs cover both.

### 2026-10-03 — Margins and spires: the cause of each, submarine slope failure, the spires gone (agent worktree agent-acb3be522c393a248, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Asked.** Ben, 2026-10-02 ("Yes, find and fix both (Recommended)"): the one-column needle spires and the continental
  margins too steep in the simulation itself, both found by the vertical-scale study.
- **How measured** (test VM; scripts in the session scratchpad, not committed): every planet the quick 16k preset,
  seed 2, planet A supercontinent 1,000 Myr, planet B scattered 500 Myr, full runs with checkpoints; before = master
  f545c0bc (built from `git archive`), after = this branch on it. **Spires:** the baked terrain sampled at the L3 cell
  centres (`deeptime heightmap --step 2`), a land cell's height over the highest of its eight neighbours, in blocks at
  20 m. **Margins:** shore-normal transects in metres from every seventh open-sea coast cell of land masses over
  750 km² (|lat| ≤ 75°), along the downhill direction of the terrain smoothed over 10 km, sampled every 500 m out to
  400 km and 40 km inland; shelf break = first point deeper than 20 m whose 4 km gradient passes 1°; foot = first point
  1 km deeper than the break whose gradient falls under 1°; on each stage's elevation (plate model L1, surface L1,
  young L2, the bake's L3). **Earth:** the same code on ETOPO 2022's 60 arc-second surface (downloaded to the VM,
  coarsened to 2′; land masses over 50,000 km², |lat| ≤ 70°; 3,777 transects).
- **Spires: cause.** In the elevation layer, not the detail noise. Turning the amplifier's terms off one at a time on
  planet B's young checkpoint (land cells over 8 blocks; base 450): ruggedness 0 → 3, gullies off → 21, glacial off →
  67, folds, sharpening, terraces, the river fade: no change. Then, on the same young state: no trough fade → 64 (of
  777 on that state), gully direction from the smoothed terrain only → 540, both → 3. Two inputs of the mountain
  character varied cell by cell: the trough fade was each cell's own glacial cut (it jumps at the ice margin and over
  the bed's rills: single cells kept the full character between faded ones), and each gully octave took its direction
  from a one-cell gradient of the terrain plus the coarser octaves (undefined at summits, saddles and the coarser
  gullies' crests and axes, where neighbouring cells read unrelated stripes).
- **Spires: fix.** `amplify/tiles.rs` hands the character a trough fade that is the box mean over 3 cells of
  min(cut / 20 m, 1) (AMP-072; 20 m is the old full-fade cut); `character.rs` takes each gully octave's fall line from
  five gradients over ±¼ wavelength and fades the octave where they disagree (coherence 0.5–0.85, AMP-073). The halo
  grows with the reach. Test `a_glaciated_young_range_has_no_one_cell_spires` (what counts as meant: volcano summits and
  impact central peaks, not on its planet): no cell over 6 blocks above all neighbours; the old code gives 14. The
  amplifier test config's gullies are 64 blocks so its halo still leaves real tiles.
- **Spires: numbers** (land cells over 8 / over 16 blocks, tallest; 20 m per block): A 132 / 12 / 41.6 → 3 / 0 / 11.6;
  B 167 / 10 / 19.8 → 0 / 0 / 6.0. (Master 00ef214c, the study's code: about 450 / 50–60 / 31–33 per planet.)
- **Margins: Earth** (ETOPO 2022, medians): slope 500–2,000 m 2.1° (mean 3.1, p90 6.8); shelf break to foot 2.2°
  (p10 0.6, p90 5.2); steepest 4 km 5.5°; shore to the 200 m isobath 25 km (mean 51); break depth 108 m; land 3 / 10 /
  30 km inland 9 / 61 / 144 m. Pratson & Haxby 1996 (abstract): regional slopes 0.5–4.4°, NJ–MD 2.5°.
- **Margins: cause, stage by stage** (planet B, master 00ef214c, slope 500–2,000 m): plate model 10.6° at L1, surface
  11.3°, young 15.3°, L3 15.3°. The plate model's own elevation holds the wall (−1,790 m 10 km off the coast, +715 m
  20 km inland): its ocean–continent step is one sample wide and the Earth-normalized plate geometry is drawn 8.1×
  narrower on the map. Nothing under the sea relaxes it: marine diffusion vanishes below the 60 m wave base; the mouth
  fill raises every cell it reaches to the fill level, so a prograding shelf ends in a one-cell cliff; and
  `plates/pools.rs`'s oceanic dampening z −= (1 − z/z_floor)·ε_o·δt relaxes any load on old sea floor back to the
  age–depth curve with the curve's own time constant (47 Myr at the presets' 0.12 mm/yr), so a rise subsides away.
  The finer levels steepen what L1 has (the same drop in finer cells; the young stage's shallow diffusion builds a
  narrow shelf with a steep front). Flexure's boundary breaks and the amplifier's own passes did not add to it.
- **Margins: tried and withdrawn.** Oceanic crust subsiding at the curve's rate at its age (loads kept) filled the
  oceans: planet B land 0.23 → 0.62, the sea floor −2 km 100 km off the coast. The dampening is today the ocean's main
  sediment sink besides subduction; changing it needs the sediment budget recalibrated with it. No `plates/` edit is
  on the branch. A failure that also moves crust (not only sediment) gave planet B 5.0° at L1 but took the shelves
  (share of the sea under 200 m 0.050 → 0.017).
- **Margins: fix.** Submarine slope failure (`marine::slope_failure`): sediment on the sea floor steeper than
  `surface.submarine_slope_deg` (new setting, default 2.5° = Pratson & Haxby's steepest clastic margin; every built-in
  preset and planet_world_4k, editor field `submarine_slope`, lang key) slides down to the toe and the rise, 40 Jacobi
  iterations at rate 0.05 per LEM step, in the deep-time surface stage after the diffusion and in the young stage (its
  sediment read from L1's log). Only sediment (log, regolith and the step's deposits) fails, only between open-sea
  cells; mass conserved; `totals.slope_failure_km3` records it. Test `a_submarine_sediment_cliff_relaxes_to_the_critical_slope`.
- **Margins: numbers** (L3 medians; A before → after, B before → after; Earth): slope 500–2,000 m 9.5 → 4.2°, 10.0 →
  5.9° (2.1); shelf break to foot 6.8 → 3.6°, 7.5 → 4.3° (2.2); steepest 4 km 15.2 → 8.0°, 17.3 → 11.8° (5.5); shore to
  200 m 14.5 → 8.5 km, 13.0 → 7.0 km (25); break depth 84 → 56 m, 76 → 47 m (108); land 10 km inland 388 → 430 m,
  472 → 524 m (61). At L1 (surface): 8.5 → 5.2°, 9.0 → 6.8°. Median profiles, m at 10 / 20 / 30 km off the coast: A −90 / −877 /
  −1,871 → −339 / −1,081 / −1,672; B −103 / −1,139 / −2,207 → −541 / −1,597 / −2,308; Earth −79 / −134 / −221: the
  shelf ended in a wall 15–30 km out, now the slope starts nearer the coast and is gentler.
- **Hypsometry** (L1, cos-weighted; A before → after, B before → after): land 0.180 → 0.188, 0.266 → 0.277; land median
  445 → 517 m, 655 → 526 m; sea median depth 4,179 → 3,797 m, 4,170 → 3,686 m (Earth 4,062); share of the sea under
  200 m 0.049 → 0.039, 0.060 → 0.041. Four planets, 500 Myr, seeds 1–2 × both starts (`tools/review/p1-17-hyps.sh`,
  the merged code with the failure off / on / at 4°): land 0.291 / 0.266 / 0.274 (Earth 0.289); land median 581 / 616 /
  586 m (427); p90 1,756 / 1,634 / 1,698 m (2,022); sea median depth 4,143 / 4,250 / 4,205 m (4,062); continental crust
  0.386 / 0.383 / 0.383; share of the sea under 200 m 0.057 / 0.037 / 0.039; arc base p50 661 / 466 / 526 m. On master
  00ef214c the same pair gave land 0.271 → 0.283 and sea 4,097 → 3,699 m: the hypsometry moves by a few hundredths

- **The study's slope statistics** (`tools/review/vertical-scale.sh stats`, land only; before → after): at 35 m per

### 2026-10-02 — Plate tasks 3 and 4: collision belts, the wedge, resistance in the speed law and the weld on stall (agent worktree agent-a3b78040bb96d9aad, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **What it is.** Stage 1 of the force-balance plan (the fallback state): the review's three plate
  faults fixed on today's motion law. Design: `docs/design/plate-force-balance.md` section 3.5 and
  "As built: tasks 3 and 4"; science: `docs/science/plates.md`, "Collision belts, the wedge and the
  weld"; ledger PLT-241 to PLT-252; tables: `docs/design/plate-check-baseline.md`, "Tasks 3 and 4".
- **Built.** `plates/belts.rs` (new): each step the continental crust that crossed a collision
  front (task 2's real shortening × the front's length × the incoming crust's own thickness ×
  `collision_stacking_share`) is stacked by Airy into a wedge on the incoming plate (profile at
  `wedge_slope_deg` up to the overriding edge, filled first) and a belt `collision_belt_km` wide
  on the overriding plate (profile 1 − (d/W)²), with the consumed crust's own rock, its sediments
  metamorphosed; both stamped as a collision orogeny (the `collision` regime). The belt resists
  the convergence inside the speed law (`belts::resist`, a plastic cut over the law's own
  relaxation, shared by area). `shortening.rs`: a stall clock; a contact is handed over when it
  has stalled (`weld_speed_mm_yr` for `weld_after_myr`) or, for terranes under
  `collision_suture_frac`, shortened by `collision_threshold_km`. `collision.rs`: no surge; a
  continent welds only once stalled, the larger plate keeps its id; small terranes move alone.
  The foreland basin is the surface stage's flexure under the belt's load; the record reads it
  back from `surface/flexure_m`.
- **Removed.** The one-step surge; `collision_uplift_max_m`, `collision_coefficient_per_km`,
  `collision_orogen_core`, `collision_distance_km` (presets, editor field repointed, lang keys);
  the `collision_on_shortening` switch and `Contact::speed_count_km` (and `counted_km` in the
  record and the check). New settings, each in the 12 built-in presets and the test planet, with an
  editor field and a lang key: `collision_belt_km` 400, `collision_stacking_share`,
  `wedge_slope_deg` 1.5, `collision_resistance_mm_yr`, `weld_speed_mm_yr` 5, `weld_after_myr` 10.
- **Departures from the design, each measured** (the as-built note has the detail): (1) the
  resistance's front-length factor is against the incoming plate's own slab front, capped at
  `slab_pull_front_km`, not against 3,000 km alone (collision fronts are a median 400 km long;
  with the design's factor a plate with no other slab needed a belt tens of km high to stop);
  (2) the resistance reads the belt's height above the sea or its relief over the ground it was
  built on; (3) only oceanic slabs pull (the design's 3.3, brought forward) and the plate model's
  trench pull-down no longer drags continental crust at a collision front; (4) Cortial's
  subduction uplift acts at oceanic slabs only; (5) a collision's own stamped belt is not
  "locked" against it, a colliding contact is kept while its front lives, and a subduction
  initiation no longer splits off old floor that is mostly an enclosed continent; (6) belt width
  is measured across the front (the 3-D moments read a long curved front's sagitta as width).
- **Light calibration** (owner: light now, full after the switch). `collision_resistance_mm_yr`
  100 → 200 and `collision_threshold_km` 300 → 100 for the plate measures (with the design's
  defaults one 1000 Myr run consumed 0.53 of the sphere's area in continental crust at collision
  fronts and fell to 0.18–0.25 crust; now 0.25–0.40 crosses fronts, master about 0.21);
  `collision_stacking_share` 0.5 → 0.8 and `subduction_uplift_mm_yr` 0.42 → 0.55 (quick presets;
  0.34 → 0.45 on the full presets by the same factor, not re-measured) for the hypsometry. The
  plate-only presets and the test planet keep 0.5 and their own uplift. `arc_continental_m` was
  not touched (the crust regression is being repaired at its source).
- **Measured: plate-check**, `earthlike_quick_16k`, supercontinent, 1000 Myr, seeds 1–4, every run
  with `structure.deformation.density=0`; before = master 2c60ca3f (the master the branch was
  measured on; 750fc2cd is in the baseline doc too), after = this branch before merging 5c4d2ed3

### 2026-10-02 — Continental crust fix: resampling crust loss, arc emergence by crust (agent worktree agent-a53303ecbc2e62b94, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; two agents, the second continued the first's branch; not merged)
- **Task.** Ben's answer "Investigate, then fix arc emergence (Recommended)" (decisions log 2026-10-02) to the pending question
  from "Continental crust bisect". (1) Find out why each plate-grid resampling destroys continental samples. (2) Make island
  arcs turn continental from the arc crust they built, not from their momentary height. (3) Adjust no calibration knob.
- **Resampling crust loss (a conservation bug, fixed).** `ridges::resample` put a new point inside a plate only when a
  whole old lattice triangle of that plate held it. A point on a plate's boundary strip (a triangle spanning two groups)
  copied the nearest visible sample within 0.75 spacings, and only when no other group covered it. At a subduction
  contact the subducting plate's hidden crust covers the overriding plate's strip, so the overriding margin (often a
  continent's edge) lost its outer half-spacing at every resampling. Diverging edges grew into the gap by up to a quarter
  spacing. Audit (scratch instrumentation, not committed; `earthlike_quick_16k`, supercontinent, seed 1):
  - master, 300 Myr, 29 resamplings: continental area fell a mean 0.77 % per resampling (344 samples; the worst 694);
  - the old rule applied to the fixed run's states: 0.92 % per resampling, against 0.33 % for the new rule;
  - the new rule over 1,000 Myr (101 resamplings): 0.38 % per resampling. 82 % of that is continental crust under other
    continental crust and 18 % continental crust under an overriding oceanic plate: real overlaps, not lattice loss.
  Fix (PLT-228): a group's extent is its footprint. That is the old lattice's cells its samples owned, each triangle
  split between its corners by the largest barycentric weight, moved rigidly. Footprints tile the sphere at a
  resampling. Where they overlap, the crust on top is chosen in this order: visible, then the overriding plate of a
  contact, then continental, then higher. The pools of the subducting plate's crust accrete to the overriding plate,
  like hidden crust. Test `resampling_conserves_continental_area`: a static two-plate planet, and one with an ocean
  turned 0.1 rad under a continent, six lattices each; continental area is kept within 0.2 % (old rule -0.35 %, new
  -0.03 % at the converging margin). With the fix, one test history's initiation split off a plate 0.89 continental, so
  `rifting::initiate` no longer splits off a plate at least half continental (PLT-229).
- **Arc emergence by crust (PLT-047).** An oceanic sample turns continental once its island-arc magma (`arc_oceanic_m`)
  reaches `arc_magma_m_per_myr` × `arc_maturity_myr`, whatever its height; hidden crust does not convert. Before, the
  setting was `arc_continental_m` (80 m, tuned in P1-27 against the resampling loss), and the sample had to be an active
  arc above sea level that step.
  - Setting `tectonics.arc_maturity_myr` = 20 Myr in every built-in preset and the test planet; the Rust default too
    (it was `arc_continental_m` 0 there and in the plate-only presets). Editor field and hint updated (HNT-092, numbered HNT-090 on its branch; the lang
    key `arc_maturity` is unchanged).
  - Source: Cloos 1993 (abstract): only arc crust over about 15 km jams a trench, and arcs on ocean crust "typically must
    be active for more than ~20 m.y." to reach it.
  - The model's arc magma, 20 m/Myr at the axis at v_0, is 25-90 times smaller than Earth's arc growth: several hundred
    m/Myr (Stern 2010, read in full) and 90-180 km³/km/Myr (Stern & Scholl 2010, read in full). So the rule counts
    Cloos's time in it, at the full arc rate. Slower trenches and off-axis samples take longer.
  - Height is not the test: intra-oceanic arcs "are generally mostly below sea level" (Stern 2010, p. 9).
  - Jicha & Jagoutz 2015 has no open copy; its abstract gives no numbers. It is in the bibliography and no value rests
    on it.
  - Ledger: PLT-045 (comparison), PLT-047 (`abstract-only`), PLT-228, PLT-229, PRS-016, HNT-092 (HNT-090 on its branch); four bibliography
    entries; science page `docs/science/plates.md`, section "The continental crust budget".
- **Evidence: plate-check.** `tools/review/plate-check.sh 1000 1,2,3,4 supercontinent base` on `earthlike_quick_16k`
  with flexure on (the presets' default). Each build ran from its own binary on the test VM, in
  `/Volumes/Graphide/ban/deeptime-runs/crust-resample/`. The table gives the mean, then per seed 1/2/3/4:

  | Build | Crust at the end | Lowest step (after 10 Myr) | Highest step | Land, median | Largest continental piece, median | Pieces of 1 % or more | Arc samples turned continental per run | Targets met |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | master (c52eb97b) | 0.34 (0.31/0.31/0.41/0.34) | 0.33 | 0.45 | 0.31 | 0.59 | 5.5 | 51,836 | 14 of 42 |
  | resampling fix only (2fe9c129) | 0.55 (0.60/0.56/0.55/0.51) | 0.43 | 0.57 | 0.37 | 0.83 | 3.25 | 45,070 | 15 |
  | arc rule only (master's resampling) | 0.15 (0.18/0.16/0.13/0.12) | 0.15 | 0.43 | 0.25 | 0.37 | 7.25 | 8,532 | 17 |
  | both (5bf8ef97 = this branch's code) | 0.31 (0.33/0.30/0.36/0.27) | 0.31 | 0.43 | 0.31 | 0.42 | 7.25 | 6,535 | 15 |

  The lowest piece share and the other plate-check rows are in the run tables (`<build>/base-supercontinent-1000.table.txt`,
  not committed). The "arc rule only" build is this branch with master's `ridges.rs` and `rifting.rs`, a scratch build.
- **Evidence: where the crust goes.** Scratch per-step counters of the visible continental samples (100,000 samples;
  42,254 continental at the start), summed over 1,000 Myr:

  | Run | Hidden under another plate (`subduction::resolve`) | Welded back in collisions | Arcs turned continental | Resampling | At the end |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | both, seed 1 / 2 | -15,543 / -16,549 | +11,253 / +10,753 | +7,893 / +6,017 | -13,065 / -12,576 (104 / 123 resamplings) | 32,792 / 29,899 |
  | arc rule only, seeds 1-4 | -11,461 to -13,831 | +7,374 to +9,991 | +6,655 to +10,855 | -31,489 to -32,451 | 12,326 to 17,780 |

  For comparison, "Continental crust bisect" counted, for master, 49,350 arc conversions against -56,578 at the
  resamplings (seed 1, 500 steps).
- **Evidence: flexure off.** The same build with counters, seeds 1-2, `surface.flexure.strength` 0 against
  the default: crust at the end 0.28 / 0.37 (flexure off) against 0.33 / 0.30 (on). Arc conversions are 7,094 / 9,388
  against 7,893 / 6,017, and the largest continental piece is 0.56 / 0.55 against 0.45 / 0.27. Before the fix the same
  switch moved the crust from 0.39 / 0.40 to 0.27 / 0.25 ("Continental crust bisect"). Flexure no longer decides the
  crust budget. It still leaves the continents in more, smaller pieces on these two seeds.
- **Evidence: hypsometry at 500 Myr.** `tools/review/p1-17-hyps.sh 500 "1 2 3" "supercontinent scattered_continents"`,
  6 runs per build; mean [min, max]:

### 2026-10-02 — Continental crust bisect: the flexure merge cuts the crust (agent worktree agent-aee75761ddffd745f, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; measurement only, nothing fixed, no code committed)
- **Question.** `deeptime plate-check` on `earthlike_quick_16k`, supercontinent start, 1000 Myr: continental
  crust at the end 0.42 on 38ca6b0 (baseline doc, mean of seeds 1-4) and 0.29 on 1eac09f.
- **Commit.** The flexure merge, 5ce5af4a (1eac09f differs from it in STATUS.md and the decisions file only).
  Of the seven first-parent merges between, the code of 60fc3418 and 1aa0579a is docs, aa78aadc touches only
  `plates/check.rs`, `plates/dynamics.rs` (the recording) and the CLI, and e057a041 adds geothermal features
  after the plates. Built and run on the test VM with `tools/review/plate-check.sh 1000 <seed> supercontinent
  base:structure.deformation.density=0`, `density=0` on every run because seed 2 as well as seed 1 now panics
  in the structure stage on e057a041 and 5ce5af4a (history limit, fixed after 1eac09f in 38e0102a; the stage
  reads the plates and writes nothing they read):

  | Commit | Seed | Crust at the end | Lowest step | Highest step | Land, median |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 38ca6b0 + recording (baseline doc) | 1 / 2 | 0.44 / 0.42 | 0.39 / 0.40 | 0.45 / 0.49 | 0.30 / 0.29 |
  | e057a041 (impacts, 1b, geothermal; before flexure) | 1 | 0.39 | 0.39 | 0.47 | 0.31 |
  | 5ce5af4a = 1eac09f (flexure on) | 1 / 2 | 0.27 / 0.25 | 0.27 / 0.25 | 0.44 / 0.45 | 0.29 / 0.29 |
  | 5ce5af4a, `surface.flexure.strength=0` | 1 / 2 | 0.39 / 0.40 | 0.39 / 0.40 | 0.47 / 0.49 | 0.31 / 0.33 |

  e057a041 seed 2 was not run (it panicked and the figures above already separate the cause). The flexure-off
  run of seed 1 equals e057a041's to the digit on every figure above, so the impacts, plate-check and geothermal
  merges change nothing here. Seed 1 ends at 0.39 against the baseline's 0.44 with or without flexure: the
  baseline's four seeds span 0.38-0.45, so that is seed noise from the impacts stage, not examined further. The
  plate-check "land at the end" is not a measure it prints; the median land share is given.
- **Confirming run.** Switching flexure off on the bad commit returns 0.39 and 0.40 (table above).
- **Mechanism (seed 1, per-step counters of the visible continental samples, scratch patch on 5ce5af4a not
  committed; runs are deterministic, two builds gave the same figures).** The plate model's continental crust is
  a near-cancellation of two churns, each as large as the crust (about 44,000 samples at the start):

  | Over 500 steps | flexure on | flexure off |
  |---|---|---|
  | arc samples turned continental (`finish_samples`, `plates/mod.rs`: oceanic, ARC, `arc_oceanic_m` at least `arc_continental_m` = 80 m, and elevation > 0) | 49,350 | 55,110 |
  | continental samples lost at resampling (`ridges::resample`, 110 / 105 resamplings) | -56,578 | -51,488 |
  | continental samples hidden under another plate (`subduction::resolve`) | -22,126 | -20,802 |
  | continental samples welded in collisions (`collision::collide`) | +14,347 | +14,085 |
  | net / visible continental samples at the end | -15,007 / 27,247 | -3,095 / 39,159 |
  | mean height of mature oceanic arc samples | -1,788 m | -1,525 m |
  | continental pieces of 1 % or more, median / largest piece's share | 7 / 0.46 | 3 / 0.67 |

  The channel is the surface feedback: `surface/mod.rs` hands the plate model the whole height of the ground
  (`feedback = sc.h - pf.elevation`, the flexed height with `flexure.strength` 1), and
  `PlatesStage::apply_surface_feedback` (`plates/mod.rs`) writes it into the samples. Flexure replaces the local
  isostasy blur and bends the plate under every load, which puts the arcs about 260 m lower, so about 10 % fewer
  mature arcs rise above the sea in time to become continental crust, and the resampling loses 5 % more. Flexure
  also leaves the continental crust in more, smaller pieces. Ablation: flexure on, but the plate model fed
  `feedback - surface/flexure_m` (the flexural part removed): crust at the end 0.34 (seed 1) and 0.36 (seed 2),
  lowest step 0.34 and 0.35: about 60-70 % of the loss comes back, the rest is the different heights the
  surface itself reaches without the old blur.
- **Bug or model?** No sign, unit or double-count error found: the flexure code only changes heights, and the
  heights are what the plate model's emergence rule reads. It is a coupling consequence. Not explained: why
  `ridges::resample` loses about 500 continental samples at every resampling in both runs (it is as large as the
  arc gain), nor why flexure raises it; a decomposition of that loss was not made.
- **Limits.** Two seeds, one per mechanism run; single trajectories diverge after about step 100, so the counter
  table is an example, not a mean. The early merges were not each built (code reading and the e057a041 run
  stand in).
- **Housekeeping.** VM scratch (`crust-bisect` runs, the five `bis-*` copies) and the scratch worktrees removed.
  My worktree was removed while the session was cut off; this entry is on a new branch of the same name.
- **Next step.** Ben answers the pending question (row "plate-motion task 2 (found), bisected").

### 2026-10-02 — Force-balance task 5: the forces computed and recorded, not applied; slab length on contacts (agent worktree agent-a48d34ca4617223c6, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **What.** New `plates/forces.rs`: each step, right after the fronts are found and only while the dynamics record is on,
  every plate's slab pull (trench length × √age × slab length / `slab_depth_km`), slab suction, edge energy (ridge push and
  belt weight from the columns' gravitational potential energy), basal drag with continental keels, the drag of a weak
  degree-2 mantle flow, slab resistance, boundary resistance against the real neighbour and collision resistance from the
  belt's energy; one SPD system over all plates (3 unknowns a plate) solved by Cholesky; per plate the torque of each term,
  the mean in-plane stress and the answer's speed and rotation change are recorded (dynamics record version 4:
  `StepRec::forces` as 14-number arrays, `slabs_km`, `breakoffs`; state `Dynamics::slabs`, `prev_balance`). Not applied:
  the old speed rules still move the plates. Slab length per subducting contact (keyed by its plates and onset step, kept in
  the record so `subduction.rs` stays untouched) grows by the oceanic front's convergence and breaks off after continental
  crust has held half its front for `slab_breakoff_myr`. `DEEPTIME_NO_PLATE_FORCES` leaves the balance out (for timing).
  `plate-check`: the four waiting force rows now fill (pull share, mega-plate stress and tension, slab length) plus 18
  reported rows: break-offs, the balance's RMS, percentiles raw and scaled per step to 45 mm/yr, above 150/250, oceanic/
  continental and slab/free ratios, slab and area rank correlations, rotation change, and its rank correlation and median
  ratio against today's speed; new definitions `balance_rms_mm_yr` 45, `balance_guard_mm_yr` 250 (CHK-058, CHK-059).
  Settings `plate_speed_scale_mm_yr` 45, `slab_pull` 1, `slab_depth_km` 700, `slab_breakoff_myr` 10, `slab_resistance` 3,
  `slab_suction_share` 0.3, `edge_energy` 0.1, `keel_drag` 3, `boundary_resistance` 3, `mantle_flow_mm_yr` 5,

  "Not active yet") and lang keys.

  so a reference plate, the average starting plate with a 3,000 km trench of full-length 80-Myr slab, moves at
  `plate_speed_scale_mm_yr`), not renormalised each step; the sea floor's potential energy is Turcotte & Schubert's ridge push
  in terms of subsidence (the design's "Airy column from its depth" gives a ridge push five times too small), trenches take

### 2026-10-02 — Science stage 2, WP-8: folds, faults and intrusions checked against sources (agent worktree agent-a5a641d341ccfe59e, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Ledger DEF** (74 rows): `verified` 17, `abstract-only` 1, `game-choice` 56 (was `cited-unverified` 16, `game-choice` 54, `uncited` 4). Every row says what was read, where, and in which library file. **No value in the code changed**; comments now carry `// ledger: DEF-0nn` ids (deform/, the Noddy crate, the format's column rule, the Java twin) and say what was read.
- **Read in full** (library, test machine): Mouthereau et al. 2007 (HAL copy: 15.8 ± 5.3 km wavelengths, 500–1,000 m amplitudes, 200 km belt), Alavi 2007 (200–300 km belt, 16–30 % shortening, anticlines to 150–200 km, foreland vergence), Schmalholz & Mancktelow 2016 (Biot–Ramberg dominant wavelength, natural wavelength/thickness 2–16), Lathrop et al. 2022 (D = 0.03 L^1.06 after Schlische), Elliott 1976 (thrusts K ≈ 7 %), Anderson 1905 (the theory; 45° ± 15° at μ = 0.577; wrench planes vertical), Waldron & Snyder 2020, Delaney & Pollard 1981, Krumbholz et al. 2014, Bunger et al. 2013, Earle 2019 §3.5, Jessell 1981, Jessell et al. 2022, and the noddyverse source at the pinned commit. Abstracts only: McQuarrie 2004, Schlische et al. 1996, Collettini & Sibson 2001. Not obtained: Anderson 1951, Biot 1961, Sherwin & Chapple 1968, Blanc et al. 2003, Cowie & Scholz 1992, Kim & Sanderson 2005, Gawthorpe & Leeder 2000, Jessell & Valenta 1996.
- **Findings.** (1) Flag 13 (slip ratios against 0.03) is not an error: the ratios are slips along the dip in block space whose heave is true in metres, so in metres normal faults displace 0.017–0.029 of their length and thrusts 0.031–0.075, inside Schlische's 0.03 and Elliott's 7 %; it is the throw that is short, about a ninth (normal) and a sixteenth (thrust) of real at the medians. (2) Flag 14 (dips): Anderson's angles verified; applying them in blocks is a declared design (params.rs module doc), not a units error, so no code change: question for Ben with pictures (Pending questions). (3) Flag 15, DEF part: the "stock < 100 km²" definition is about the exposed area (Earle 2019); the coded radius is the body's half-width at the world's floor and a stock's outcrop is only its cupola, so there is no contradiction; the comment is corrected. (4) The fold-shortening comment's (πA/λ)² is first order: the coded amplitudes shorten beds 7–20 %, not 8–30 % (comment corrected). (5) The port's fold profile is the exact sine; Noddy's own default "sine" is 21 points joined by straight lines (up to 2.2 % off): comment corrected, kept. (6) Every Noddy constant and convention the port names was found in the original source and in Jessell 1981. (7) Foreland belts are 250 km on the plate model's Earth-sized sphere, 31 km on the 16k map, while the folds keep their Earth size: a belt holds about two wavelengths across (open question for the plate work).

### 2026-10-02 — Plate-motion task 2: real shortening and the collision state (agent worktree agent-aaf46227fde85f19a, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **What changed in behaviour: nothing in the built-in planets.** Every built-in preset gets
  `tectonics.collision_on_shortening: false`, which keeps the trigger used before this task, so the worlds are master's.
  Measured: plate-check on seeds 1–4 gives the same value for every measure that does not depend on when a collision
  starts, to the last digit, seed by seed. The hypsometry run checked against master is bit-identical too (below).
  The collision state, the real-shortening count and their records run alongside and decide nothing. Setting the
  switch to `true` makes real shortening fire transfers and welds.
- **Real shortening** (`plates/shortening.rs`). A contact's **collision front** is the stretch of the overriding plate's
  edge where continental crust of the subducting plate stands now (the nearest sample of another plate within 1.75
  spacings is that plate's, continental, not freshly sutured). The **convergence across it** is the flux of the relative
  velocity through the edge's Voronoi edges (cotangent lengths), divided by the front's length (the summed length ×
  outward-normal vector, and at least half the summed edge). On a straight front this is the speed across the boundary.
  Pure strike-slip gives under 2 % of the speed, an oblique contact its normal part, and a parting one a negative
  value. A first version used each edge sample's mean normal and read 19 % of a strike-slip speed as convergence,
  because the Fibonacci lattice's normals lean one way along a boundary. **Shortening** is that convergence integrated
  over the collision (parting steps add nothing), and the crust crossed is shortening × front length (km²).
- **The collision state** (`state::Collision`, on `Contact::collision`). It begins on the first step a live contact's
  front has 3 or more samples and converges at 10 mm/yr or more. That is `subduction::CONFIRM_MM_YR`; counted from
  above zero, the onset convergence was a few mm/yr and the 20-Myr slowdown ratio a median of 3–8. The state carries
  its onset, last step, shortening, crust crossed, convergence now, at onset, peak and 20 Myr after onset, the front's
  length and peak length, its centroid and outward normal, and the share of the front that is continental on the
  overriding side. It survives 3 steps with no front, since a resampling consumes the overlap and it comes back. It
  ends in one of five ways. A transfer or weld writes a `CollisionRec`, whose `start_myr` is now the state's onset and
  `end_myr` the transfer, plus a `BeltRec` with the convergence at onset and 20 Myr later. The other four write a new
  `PartingRec`: parted (no front for over 3 steps), reversed, closed (the contact timed out or a plate died), emptied
  (the terrane was gone) or open (the run ended). The `collision` event gains `onset_myr` and `shortening_km` (EVENTS.md).
  `Counters::collision_onsets` counts states, and the run test checks that every state ends exactly once.
- **The `depth_km` bug** that the plate-check agent noted is real: it added the *magnitude* of the relative velocity at
  the overlap's centroid, so sliding plates counted in full. `depth_km` is gone. The real count is above, and the old
  count is kept on purpose, unchanged, as `Contact::speed_count_km` (it fires while the switch is off). In the default
  runs it reads 351 km at the transfer or weld while the front had shortened by a median of 167 km (p90 320).
- **Interim weld and uplift: the old trigger still fires, by measurement.** The new setting is

  `deeptime.editor.field.collision_on_shortening`, in all 13 presets and the test planet. Task 4 removes it together

### 2026-10-02 — Flexure follow-up: the margin zigzag and the polar stripes, causes and fixes (agent worktree agent-afae960b6db068f94, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c; not merged)
- **Asked.** The coordinator, after flexure landed (5ce5af4): find the cause of the cell-to-cell alternation along
  active margins and the rise in land roughness (99th percentile 294 → 391 m in one pair), and of the stripes near
  the poles, show each with a controlled test, fix it there, re-measure on the merged tree. Ben's answers to the
  five flexure questions are in the decisions log (2026-10-02, logged in 4918af3).
- **Measured how.** A temporary diagnostic split each step's flexure response linearly by source (solving the same
  operator for each part of the residual) and counted cell-scale zigzags (a cell and its next neighbour both strict
  extrema of opposite kind, by more than 5 m a step) at margins (within three cells of a plate boundary) and
  elsewhere; `tools/review/flexure_artifacts.py` does the same on a run's final fields (20 m threshold, margins,
  interiors, poleward of 70°). Design note `docs/design/flexure.md` section 13 has the whole account.
- **Cause 1, the main one: the carried state acted as a force.** Every step re-solved the whole load against the
  deflection and frozen moment carried from the last step. Carrying them on the raster interpolates them (near the
  pole a plate's rotation shifts rows by many cells); new crust and arriving crust restart at zero beside cells that
  carry kilometres. In a whole-load solve that mismatch is a residual, and the solve moved the ground to remove it:
  **up to 4.6–6.2 km in a step from the carried state alone** (200 Myr, scattered seed 1), split about equally
  between restarted crust, cells whose stiffness jumped fourfold, and interpolation. Controlled test
  `carrying_a_bent_plate_moves_nothing`: the old formulation moves a carried, unloaded bent plate by 1.15 m a step,
  the new one by under 1 cm. **Fix:** each step solves only for the step's load increments; the carried plate is in
  equilibrium; the solve's unfinished residual is carried and solved with the next step; the plate carries its
  bending moment (kept when it stiffens, released as a force when it weakens). Ledger ISO-068, ISO-056 changed.
- **Cause 2: the plate-boundary break was a staircase.** Applied after the stiffness smoothing, it stepped with the
  raster. Controlled test `a_moving_margin_bends_smoothly` (an ocean plate moving 0.37 cells a step under a craton
  advancing 0.23 cells a step along a wavy boundary, a sediment fan, an arc): with the staircase the deflection
  zigzags beside the boundary by 3–70 m; fixed, nowhere by more than 10 m. It was the polar artifact: polar-band
  zigzag 3.5 % [1.4, 5.0] with the staircase, 0.87 % [0.49, 1.27] fixed, 1.48 % with flexure off (four planets).
  **Fix:** the boundary cells are blurred and the stiffness share taken from that (0 on the boundary rows, then 0.17,
  0.72). Ledger ISO-055 changed.
- **Cause 3: the plate model's sample lattice reached the ground.** Its uplift is interpolated from samples 71
  Earth-normalized km apart onto 39 km cells; the uplift field itself zigzags in 4.8 % of margin cells by more than
  5 m a step (aliasing). Local isostasy passed that at its own height; a stiff plate passed the thickening behind
  it, 5.5 times higher. Controlled test `the_plate_models_sample_lattice_is_not_a_load`: a 500 m column-by-column
  uplift on a craton now steps the ground by 500 m (over 1,500 m unfiltered). **Fix:** only the part of the plate
  model's root that it resolves bends the plate (binomial (1,2,1)/4 passes set by the sample spacing, two on the
  quick presets); erosion, deposition and spreading are not filtered. Per step, the uplift part's margin zigzag fell
  from 4.2–6.0 % to 1.3–3.6 %. Ledger ISO-069 (new), `StepIn::plate_spacing_m`.
- **Ruled out:** the preconditioner's leftover residual (its response zigzags in under 0.1 % of cells); latitude
  terms in the operator or preconditioner (none: block metric throughout; a ring load bends the plate the same at
  every longitude, tested). The regime field is populated on resampling steps, unlike `plates/flags`.
- **What remains at margins** (per step, final code): erosion and deposition 1.6–4.1 % of margin cells (marine
  fill of kilometres in trench cells: real at this resolution), uplift with water and ice 1.3–3.6 %, moment released
  where a moving boundary weakens the plate 1.0–3.1 %. On the final fields the worst margin window of each planet,
  with and without flexure, is old ocean floor whose own local-isostatic level wiggles by ±50 m.
- **Re-measured on the merged tree** (master 412d517; quick preset, test VM):
  - Artifacts, 200 Myr, seeds 1–2 × both starts: elevation zigzag at margins 11.1 % off, 13.1 % final (first build,
    one planet, 19.3 % against 10.8 % off); polar band 1.48 % off, 0.87 % final; land roughness p99 237 m off,
    274 m final.
  - **Roughness:** on the pair of the first complaint (500 Myr, supercontinent seed 1) land p99 289 → 372 m, but land

### 2026-10-02 — P2-01 fix: the structure stage panicked on long-lived belts (agent worktree agent-a49703993341aa701, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c)
- **Bug.** `earthlike_quick_16k`, supercontinent, 1000 Myr, seed 1 panicked: "a history holds at most 128 events"
  (`deeptime-noddy/src/history.rs`). **Cause:** only the end-of-run check (`deform/lattice.rs` `noddy_check`, which
  compares the column rule with the Noddy port on every 53rd L2 column) built a Noddy history, one per sampled column
  from all its candidate structures; the port keeps the original's limit of 127 events a history (its 4-bit-per-event
  sequence code), and a belt active for most of 1,000 Myr puts more structures over one place. The column rule the
  game runs (Rust and Java) never had a limit, so nothing the game reads changed. Master's interim guard (5ce5af4)
  skipped such columns silently.
- **Fix.** `noddy::Chain`: any number of events undone as a run of histories of at most 127 each, youngest first; the
  same restored position exactly (unit test against undoing event by event). The check uses it, skips no column, and
  the note carries `noddy_check.max_history` and `noddy_check.long_histories` (sampled columns that needed a chain).
  `History::is_full` lets a caller ask before `push`. The density itself (option c) was left alone: `max_overlap` 3 per
  kind with overprinting already bounds each kind, and 218–340 candidates over a column is what three kinds over
  1,000 Myr of belts give; nothing showed it to be wrong in the rock.
- **Tests.** `a_place_with_more_structures_than_one_noddy_history_holds` (420 structures over one place: panicked on
  the old code, skipped every column with the guard), `the_stage_never_panics_however_dense_the_structures` (seeds 1–4,
  both starts, dense settings; asserts the longest history met passes 127), `a_full_history_says_so_and_a_chain_takes_any_number`.

### 2026-10-01 — P1-10 TerraBlender regions follow provinces (agent worktree agent-a7e713f9fdd326fb4, sub-agent of session f981c0d3-5144-49ec-8686-2946d755872c)
Branch `worktree-agent-a7e713f9fdd326fb4`, master e8668ca merged in (then 5e601d9, folds and faults stage B, format 0.3), not merged back, not pushed. Plan §10 P1-10 "As built" and §7.3 carry the design; FORMAT.md, "The geologic provinces and TerraBlender's regions", the contract.

- **The plan's mechanism was not needed.** TerraBlender 4.1.0.8 (decompiled on the VM) has no `terrablender:uniqueness` density function and no uniqueness on `Climate.TargetPoint`/`Sampler`; it picks a region in `MixinMultiNoiseBiomeSource.getNoiseBiome` (HEAD, cancellable) from `IExtendedParameterList.getUniqueness(x, y, z)`, a layered noise of (x, z) alone, on a parameter list that every level on the overworld preset shares. So ReTerraForged's four mixins and `RegionIndexDensity` were not ported (no ReTerraForged code used; NOTICE.md unchanged). One mixin, `mixin/compat/terrablender/RegionBiomeSourceMixin` (priority 900 so its handler runs before TerraBlender's), answers first **only for a Deep Time level's sampler** and runs the same tree search with the column's province region (`compat/terrablender/RegionTrees`). How it knows the level: `GeologicChunkGenerator.bindSettings` wraps the noise settings' `spawnTarget` list in `worldgen/RegionSpawnTarget` (carries the level's `RegionSource`: `meta/province` at the column → region index), and `RandomState` hands that list to `Climate.Sampler` unchanged. Anything else (other levels, no table, TerraBlender not initialised) falls through. Compile-only dependency `maven.modrinth:terrablender:6e8GCrLb`, plus five access-transformer lines (the ones TerraBlender's own AT has) so Deep Time compiles without TerraBlender applied.
- **No fallback depth** (the plan's "points below the fallback depth use TerraBlender's own index"): TerraBlender's uniqueness ignores y, so a province keeps its region at every depth and cave biomes come from the region's tree as before.
- **The bake's provinces are the USGS classes** (log 2026-09-29, "Yes, for P1-10"). `bake/meta.rs` runs `provinces::derive_with` (the view layer's classifier, now with the preset's thresholds) and cuts the classes into connected regions, small ones absorbed as before. `meta/province` keeps its name, type and contiguity; `notes.bake.meta.provinces` lists `classes`, `params`, per-province `class`/`cells`/`km2` and `shares` (`classified` and `provinces`, planet and continental, plus `absorbed_cells`). Settings added: preset section `provinces` (`min_area_km2` 50,000, `orogen_max_age_myr` 500, `andean_max_age_myr` 50, `andean_min_elevation_m` 1,500), four editor fields in Advanced · Biome placement and regions (`region_size`, `orogen_age`, `range_age`, `range_height`), lang keys, all eight built-in presets. The view layer keeps the default thresholds. `planet_world_4k.json` (test planet) sets `min_area_km2` 1,500: it has 1/66 of the Earth-scale planet's area and with 50,000 it baked 2 provinces (sea floor and one extended-crust continent); with 1,500, 34 to 35. This changes no simulation figure, only `meta/province`.
- **Province → region** (`climate/ProvinceRegions`): stratified by weight (rank by a hash of province id and the preset seed, ranks dealt over the regions by cumulative weight), stored by region *name* in `climate_mapping.json` `regions` the first time a start has TerraBlender and the world has provinces; kept afterwards; unknown names fall back to the default region with a warning. Without TerraBlender nothing is written and nothing changes (MIC).
- **The orogen share, measured** (`earthlike_quick_16k`, scattered start, 500 Myr, preset seed, this tree; checkpoint `7-amplify`; `tools/review/p1-10-orogen.sh`). Classified shares of the continents, default thresholds: shield 0.157, platform 0.123, **orogen 0.421**, basin 0.085, LIP 0.045, extended 0.168 (matches P1-27's 0.40). Orogen by reason: active collision/arc regime 0.125, collision belt within 500 Myr 0.166, Andean range 0.134. Thresholds (orogen share): `orogen_max_age_myr` 400 0.421, 300 0.389, 200 0.366, 100 0.355, 50 0.238; `andean_min_elevation_m` 2,000 0.402, 2,500 0.385, 3,000 0.375; `andean_max_age_myr` 25 0.414, 10 0.396; 200 + 25 + 2,500 together 0.327. The active-regime part (0.125) is the plate model's, so thresholds cannot reach Earth's 0.17. Defaults unchanged (question in Pending). **After absorption** (the bake: 40 provinces on this planet, 68,000 to 2,200,000 km², `absorbed_cells` 412,247 of 524,288) the share of the continents is orogen 0.09, extended 0.44, basin 0.19, LIP 0.12, platform 0.11, shield 0.04: thin belts lose to the long coastal extended-crust ring. The notes record both.
- **Tests.** Rust: `bake::meta::tests` (3: absorption, two regions of one class, shares classified vs provinces); `provinces::ProvinceParams` through the preset and editor tests. JUnit: `ProvinceRegionsTest` (7: weights, small planet reaches every region, determinism, runs, JSON round trip through `climate_mapping.json`), `ProvinceBakeTest` (2: the real test planet's classes, ids = layer, shares, parameters).
